author: jinhokim46
body:
## Summary

Ticket 05 (`docs/specs/2026-10-03-length-voice-design/tickets/05-alignment-a11y-pass.md`): the ticket 02 design system now covers every page, followed by an accessibility audit (`design-review` + `web-design-guidelines`, with `frontend-design` as the quality bar). I took screenshots of every page at 1440 px and 420 px, in light and dark, before and after the changes.

**Layout (shared helpers only, no one-off sizes)**
- Start form: three `panel`s, and the four interview settings sit in a 2 x 2 `form_row` grid. Segmented controls are now exactly as tall as the select boxes, so labels and boxes line up to the pixel (checked in the browser: both 68 px, same top and bottom). Start interview goes in a `button_row`.
- Interview screen: the session header is a panel. Continue/Retry, Keep my answer, Send again/Discard, Try again, End this interview, Start a new interview and Get my feedback report use `button_row`. Continue/Retry used to stretch across the full 1440 px width; they are now the width of the longest label. Both buttons are drawn before either click is handled. I removed the double divider in the sidebar.
- Report: the headline is a panel with an aligned `form_row`, and the score breakdown is one grid. Strengths and improvements are natural-height panels in a top-aligned row. I tried equal-height cards here first, but with zero strengths against three long improvements they left a ~500 px empty box.
- History: the three score numbers are equal cards. The trend chart is in a panel, the filters are half width, and Delete / Open / Go-to actions use button rows. The "Open an interview" box now shows "Choose an interview…" instead of Streamlit's generic placeholder.
- Settings: the defaults sit in a panel grid that matches the start form, and the Length caption now sits right under Length. The developer settings have their own panel, Save is in a button row, and usage shows as cards with an aligned table row.
- Home: application card footers are always two lines (count, then score or "No score yet"), so they stay level even when a badge would wrap.

**Accessibility fixes (CSS, still static)**
- Selected segmented/pill options (Length, Difficulty, Channel, Reasoning effort) had accent text at 3.5:1 on dark. They now keep the normal text colour (13:1) and are marked with weight 600, an accent ring and a light tint, so colour is not the only cue.
- Focus rings were missing or only a 1 px border-colour change on select boxes, text inputs, text areas, toggles/checkboxes, the Voice audio player and data tables. All now get the 2 px accent ring (≥ 4.2:1 against the background). I tabbed through every page to check.
- Light-theme badges: gray was 3.5:1, orange 3.2:1, red 4.6:1 and the green "Hire signal" exactly 4.5:1. All are now 5.8–7.0:1. Dark-theme badges already passed.
- The divider gap inside the Applications expander was ~2× the spacing scale and is now one step.

**Deferred (with reason)**
- Data tables scroll sideways inside themselves at 1440 px (History) and at 420 px. The page itself never scrolls sideways (`scrollWidth == viewport` on every page and width). Column widths belong to Streamlit's canvas grid.
- At 420 px the long application/model names in select boxes are cut off in the closed box. The open dropdown shows them in full, and Streamlit select boxes can't wrap.
- At 420 px the History metric cards stack into three short cards. That is Streamlit's column stacking below 640 px and is acceptable.
- The disabled Delete button/checkbox shows 2.4:1 (light) and 3.3:1 (dark). WCAG exempts disabled controls from contrast.
- Badge overrides match Streamlit 1.64's inline tint values. If a later version changes them, the rules stop matching and the badges fall back to Streamlit's colours. The CSS comment says this.
- The dark `:primary-badge` would be 2.8:1, but the app doesn't use it.

No `unsafe_allow_html`. The CSS has no placeholders, and untrusted text still goes through `safe_md`. Engine, evaluation and voice behaviour are unchanged, and the core never imports Streamlit.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -m "not live"`: 504 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check`: clean
- [x] AppTest suite green. One assertion changed on purpose: the Home footer now reads "Latest score **64**" with the count in its own caption.
- [x] New tests in `tests/test_design_system.py`: selected options aren't marked by accent text alone, and every kind of focusable control has a 2 px focus ring.
- [x] Code map regenerated; `tests/test_code_map.py` green

The master vulnerability job stops before scanning because `govulncheck@latest` now requires Go 1.26, while this project uses Go 1.25. The compatible scanner then finds six reachable standard-library vulnerabilities in Go 1.25.12.

Pin govulncheck to v1.7.0, the highest published stable release compatible with Go 1.25, and raise the project's Go patch to 1.25.13, which fixes all six reported findings. Existing `go-version-file` steps follow the patch. The mandatory `govulncheck ./...` command, current public vulnerability database and workflow dependencies stay intact; no findings are suppressed and no application dependency or lockfile changes.

Validation: the actual pinned scanner passes against the current database with Go 1.25.13; `make check-quick` passes Go tests/vet, 228 frontend tests, three Compose validations and the strict product boundary. Official module metadata, Go archive checksum, all six advisory records, and the original failed CI/scan are retained in local evidence. Independent review covers both changed lines.

body:
The owner asked for everything learned while ruling on a studied source to go into `study-a-source`: useful to a session, general, with no source named and no detail that costs time.

## What the study standard missed, and what each new line makes a session do

The evidence is in #1260: the rulings comment and the measurement comment of 2026-10-03.

| learned | the line | what a session now does |
|---|---|---|
| A unit field said "per tile" on products the cart charged per m². A store setting said "display excluding tax" while three carts added no tax. | Pass 5: **the cart is the measurement, and the label is a claim** | asks him before a guest-cart test, tests one product from each label group, reads quantity × price = line and subtotal + shipping = total, and stops at the cart |
| The study saw "a calculator" and did not read it. Its script wrote boxes × box size into the cart's quantity, which was the unit, and fell back to a fixed 1.5 when a product had no carton area. | Pass 4 line **16**: the page's own logic between the buyer and the cart | reads the script, takes its per-product constants as fields, and never stores its fallback default as a stated value |
| A 200-row sample gave "Aruba" as the commonest country. The 1,384-row census showed real values in the category that mattered. A derived carton area matched the stated one on 93.5% of rows, and the misses were the site's own entry errors. | new section, **When the site disagrees with itself** | counts agreement over the census, tests a formula on the rows that state the value before deriving it, keeps both values, and recommends with evidence where they disagree. That last part is his ruling. |
| Three 250-item GraphQL pages came back HTTP 200 with the body cut off at ~15 s. | the budget: **a 200 is not a complete response** | parses every response and re-asks in smaller pages |
| A staff-name field was offered as "take everything". | after line 16: a field that names a person | reports exactly what it holds and recommends it out. Taking it stays his decision. |

"Done means" gains two checks and moves the count of hidden-field lines from fifteen to sixteen.

## Guard
`tests/test_the_documents_cite_what_they_claim.py` verifies every `path:line` in this skill. The addition cites none, and the guard plus `tests/test_the_docs_gate_is_complete.py` pass locally (23 passed, 1 skipped). This is documentation only, under `.claude/`, and not `CLAUDE.md`, so the review skill exempts it from the review loop.

body:
## Why

The task projector already accepts voluntary release, but the CLI and shared task API cannot request it. Workers need a direct way to return unfinished work to the queue without reporting a shipment or abandonment.

## Changes

- Add `release` to the existing CLI, task tool schema and HTTP manifest.
- Require the observed `expected_started_at` and check that same claim generation inside each transaction attempt.
- Return explicit rejection for missing/inactive tasks, changed custody or changed generations.
- Reuse the existing RELEASE projection and matching legacy-holding mirror; never take another task as part of release.
- Preserve operation-ID replay and document the command.

## Execution

Ran the actual CLI with a local Git remote copied from the retained `state/claims` branch; shared fleet custody was not changed by these runs.

- Valid release: exit 0, task OPEN, worker UNKNOWN, next null.
- Exact operation replay: exit 0, replayed true, changed false.
- Mismatched generation: exit 2, claim_generation_changed, original ACTIVE worker preserved, next null.
- Loaded the shared tool schema with release and expected_started_at exposed.

Composes with #30253 source normalization and #30265 legacy-holding release, plus current README and command-center feed changes. Runtime.sync, collectors, provider cache and routing remain with their existing implementations.

author: olivervillson
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"OliverVillson"} -->
_Requested by **Oliver Villson** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NkFa1vu2SVL68CYqnBeiQr?thread=cmsg_01NkFa1vu2SVL68CYqnBeiQrHqxEmpydRigsYK7aGF8c2L)_

**DO NOT MERGE before #99 (per-person keys) AND #101 (roles).** Red-team H1/N1: a ticket file can carry `by-bob` even when someone else signed it. #99 and #101's `acceptTicket` strip remote `by-*` labels and add one from the verified sender (shared-key tickets get none, so they count as authorless). The seat check below trusts that label, so it is only sound once both are in. #104 (lending) has the same dependency.

Before: the scheduler judged every ticket against one meter (the machine's own login), so a project with several seats could not use the room on a second seat.

After: with `salu sched on`, a ticket in a project with seats starts on the seat that has room. If it does not fit seat A, it starts on seat B, and `salu sched` shows each seat's meter, the seat each queued ticket would take, and why the other seats did not (`not on alice-team: needs about 30% of the 5-hour window, 80% is used`). If no seat has room the queue is held until the earliest reset, naming every seat.

How: `src/sched/seats.ts` places a ticket on the usable seat with the most room, judged with that seat's own windows and its own percent-per-dollar. Dead, no-login, switched-off and used-up seats are skipped. Tickets started a minute ago count against their seat before the meter shows them, so two tickets do not pile onto one seat. Finished runs record their seat and read that seat's meter. Projects without seats behave as before. `salu sched` keeps the last real decision instead of wiping it when the queue goes empty.

**Whose seat (red-team F2):** borrowing is off (W6), so a ticket may only use a seat that is the project's (no owner), its author's own (the member named by its `by-<name>` label), or, for a ticket with no author, an admin's. A `by-` label naming nobody on the team gets project seats only. A seat already on the ticket (`seat_id`) is checked the same way, so a pinned seat is never a way onto a teammate's seat; the ticket is held and `salu sched` says "it is alice's seat and alice has not lent it". The scheduler never reads a seat from a ticket file or tag. Tests in `test/sched-seats.test.ts`.

**Where the label is read:** `seatClosedTo` in `src/sched/seats.ts` reads `by-*` from the ticket row in the database, on every path. Other writers of that label: local `salu add -l`/`salu change` (passed to #101 to decide) and sync.ts's message-created tickets.

**Still needed once #101 lands:** `setTicketSeat` and any `salu change` that writes `tickets.seat_id` must call `whyNotSeat(sender, seat)` (admin any seat, member only their own, shared key none). Not stacked on #101 on purpose.

**Merge order:** #95 (W0), #98 (W4), #97 (W5), #99 and #101 first, and #96 (W10) before this PR (it is merged into this branch).

Tests: `test/sched-seats.test.ts` (11 new); full suite passes except the 3 `salu box init` tests, which need openssh-client.

author: thomhurst
body:
Failed Redis, Valkey, or Sentinel initialization previously lost daemon logs when cleanup removed the container. The fixture now captures each daemon's last 4 KiB before removal, attaches the result to the original exception at `Data["RespireFixture.DaemonLogs"]`, and automatically reports it to standard error after cleanup.

Collection has an independent two-second deadline and a 32,768-character aggregate limit divided between ports. Portable per-file tail commands preserve each daemon's label and tail, including unavailable-log diagnostics. Reporting has a separate two-second bound, isolates synchronous writers, and permits only one outstanding write. A stalled sink cannot prevent cleanup, replace the failure, or accumulate blocked workers. Concurrent healthy reports serialize within their deadlines; exception data remains available when reporting times out.

Tests cover capture before cleanup, reporting after cleanup, normal/throwing/stalled writers, concurrent reports, caller cancellation and startup expiration, unavailable and oversized logs, ignored cancellation, cleanup failures, port-collision retries, and real Redis/Valkey logs. An internal clock seam makes startup expiration and diagnostic cancellation deterministic without changing production deadlines. The branch also corrects the fake Sentinel's acknowledgements for three individual SUBSCRIBE commands.

Validation: Release builds and all 52 fixture/startup tests pass on net8.0 and net10.0, including real Redis/Valkey checks. After rebasing onto current main, all 73 dedicated-routing tests pass on each runtime, including the zero-allocation assertion. The website production build and diff checks pass. All .NET runs used the standard 600-second/2,048-MB guard. Previous Linux Cluster fallback failures are tracked separately in #789 and its fix PR #790.

Closes #781

author: linyows
body:
This builds on #264 and reuses its in-memory server helper in the tests.

## timeout

`timeout` was read into the request and documented as the "connection and operation timeout", but nothing used it. The dial had no deadline, and a command waited on the server for as long as it took, so a server that went silent left the step hanging until the step's own five-minute limit.

It now bounds the whole session:

- The dial goes through a `net.Dialer` with the timeout, which also covers the TLS handshake.
- Once connected, a timer closes the connection when the rest of the time runs out. Closing the connection is what stops a command that is waiting on the server.
- The step then fails with an **action error** that names what it was doing, for example `IMAP session timed out after 30s while running commands`, and exits `3`. A silent server is the environment's failure, unlike a command the server refuses, which still sets `res.code` to `1`.
- A zero `Timeout`, which only the Go API can produce, means no limit rather than an immediate cut-off.
- When a command fails, the logout after it is checked too. If the session runs out there, the step fails with the timeout, and the message keeps the command's own failure (`… while logging out … (after the command failed: …)`).

A number used to reach the `time.Duration` field as nanoseconds, so `timeout: 30` meant 30 ns. It now means seconds, as does a numeric string. A value that is neither a duration nor a positive number is rejected, and so is one too large for a `time.Duration` (about 292 years). The range is checked before converting, since multiplying first would wrap a huge value such as `20000000000` around to some other positive duration.

## strict_host_check

`strict_host_check` was read and never used, and it has no meaning for IMAP, so it is removed. A workflow that still sets it keeps working, because unknown keys are ignored; a test covers that.

**Breaking change for Go callers:** the exported field `imap.Req.StrictHostCheck` is removed. Code that builds or reads `imap.Req` and sets that field no longer compiles; drop the assignment. Workflows are unaffected. This should be called out in the release notes.

## Verification

- `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass.
- `TestRequest_TimeoutBoundsTheSession` runs a server that never sends its greeting, one that logs the client in but never answers `SELECT`, and one that refuses `SELECT` and then never answers `LOGOUT`. With `timeout: 300ms`, each fails in about 0.3 s with the expected message. With the timer disabled, the test hangs until `go test -timeout` kills it.
- `TestRequest_TimeoutAsNumberIsSeconds` succeeds with `5`, `5.0` and `"5"` against the in-memory server, and the request reports 5 s.
- `TestParseTimeout` covers durations, numbers, numeric strings, and the rejected values, including overflowing numbers, `NaN`, and the largest accepted value. The overflow cases and the logout timeout fail against the code before this change.
- The imap reference documents the behavior in English and Japanese. The Japanese page had no `timeout` section; one is added.

author: dammianmiller
body:
## What this adds

The durable goal layer above `uap deliver` — a prompt, small or large, becomes a mission the system owns until its frozen acceptance criteria are verified met. Survives reboots, crashes, session teardown, and context exhaustion. Inspired by Choir (Weber-GeoML, arXiv 2609.31903): the loop clock and the state are durable and external to any agent process.

## Surface

- `uap mission create|list|show|pause|resume|replan|salvage|poll` (+ hidden alias `uap orch poll` — deliberately distinct from `uap orchestrator on|off`, the in-deliver blackboard toggle)
- `uap-orchestrator.service` systemd unit (`uap mission poll --loop --interval 300`), doctor-probed via capacity-policy
- New ledger `.uap/missions.db` (SQLite WAL, user_version 1, FK on)

## Mechanics (ADR-0003 has the full record)

- **Frozen acceptance** (sha256 at create; replan supersedes through recorded revisions and resets the run link)
- **Provenance-checked run linkage**: marker `[mission:#N:<hash8>]` + pid must match the launch the orchestrator spawned — planted run-state files cannot steer the daemon
- **Atomic launch claims** (60s window) — daemon poll and `create --launch` cannot double-spawn
- **Struggle metric**: attempt rows dedupe per (run, outcome, observedAt); 3+ failures turn salvage proposals into escalation asks
- **Approval-gated salvage** — the orchestrator proposes, the overseer rules
- **Backoff**: first relaunch immediate, then 15·2^n capped at a day

## Docs

- `docs/guides/MISSIONS.md` (operator guide)
- `docs/architecture/adr/0003-mission-orchestrator.md`
- `docs/visual/mission-orchestrator.html` — visual-explainer page (Blueprint register, self-contained)

## Validation

- 51 new tests (ledger, decision table, executor incl. provenance/claims/dedupe/escalation, CLI parsing, interval clamp) — all green
- Build, `tsc --noEmit`, review prepass clean for all new code
- 3 parallel reviews (code-quality, security, architect) — all FIX-FIRST findings applied, P1s included: struggle-escalation reachability, salvage dedupe, fd leak, provenance gate, replan staleness, marker collisions, naming, schema versioning, ADR
- Full suite: 5598 passed / 1 failed — the failed test is the pre-existing, load-induced T1 flake in `optimization-sweep-2.test.ts` (verified: identical failure on master in this environment; passes 33/33 in isolation). Version bump pending on the same flake — bump commit lands on this branch before merge.

## Remaining (documented, deliberate)

- PR 2 (next worktree): deterministic merge gate consuming `verifyAcceptanceHash` + the attempt ledger
- Deferred P3s noted in ADR-0003 (pid-reuse corroboration via /proc, singleton path-map hardening)

body:
> **#38（#11）の上に作っています。** #38 をマージすると、この PR の差分は #12 の分だけになります。先に #38 をマージしてください。

## 概要
AI エージェント（Claude Code など）が、作った資料をそのまま Galley に登録・更新できる MCP サーバーを `/mcp` に実装する。

Closes #12

## 変更内容
- **ツール**（`crates/server/src/mcp/`）：`list_projects`、`list_documents`、`get_document`、`create_document`、`update_document`
  - 資料は「プロジェクトの slug」と「資料の slug」で指定。結果は JSON のテキスト。版番号は `revision_number` に揃える
  - 登録・更新の結果に「第N版として登録しました」と資料ビューアの URL（`/<プロジェクト>/<資料>`）を入れる。`get_document` で過去の版を取ったときは `/v/<番号>` 付きの URL
  - 画面と同じ検査を通す。外部リソースで断ったときは、該当箇所（行番号・種類・コード）と作り直しの依頼文をツールのエラーで返す
  - 更新者名は `X-Author-Name`（UTF-8 として読む）。無ければ登録を断る。source は `mcp`
  - 説明文とサーバーの instructions に「外部リソースを含まない1ファイルの HTML」を明記
  - エラーの文言は利用者向けと分かっているものだけ返し、DB・ストレージのエラーは隠してログに出す
- **`MCP_TOKEN`**：設定したときだけ `Authorization: Bearer` を必須にする（401、`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`）。トークンはログに出さない
- `/mcp` のリクエストの大きさは HTML の上限の2倍＋1MB まで（413）。rmcp の `allowed_hosts` には `ALLOWED_HOSTS` を渡す
- `app.rs`：アプリのルーターの組み立てを `main.rs` から分け、テストで同じ組み立てを使う。adapter は `main.rs` で作って trait として渡す

author: thegoodengineer
body:
Refs #835

## The phase

QPLIB_9030 (QIL: 10,000 integer columns in [0, 10], 5,000 `>=` rows, a Hessian of 39,986 lower-triangle entries) at `--time-limit 60` on main ac41865 ran 170.8 s on this laptop (the #835 container killed it at 180 s as `hung`). The verbose log splits it into node QPs of the MIQP branch and bound, each run by Condat-Vu:

| node QP | what | ended at (its own clock) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | root relaxation | 48.3 s, optimal |
| 2 | re-solve after the root cut round (2 MIR cuts) | about 60 s, time_limit ("Root cuts induced failure: time_limit; rolled back") |
| 3 | the next QP solved at the root, before branching | about 60 s, time_limit |
| 4 to 23 | strong-branching probes (10 candidates, two sides, 50 iterations each), after the deadline | short |

The convexity test itself is not the slow phase on this instance: each of the 21 late node QPs, convexity LDL^T and step-size norms included, cost about 74 ms.

## Root cause

Two things, both in front of the clock rather than inside a loop that ignores it.

1. `BranchAndBound::solve_node_with()` wrote the time that is left into the node options only on the LP path (#803). The QP branch returned before that line, so every node QP of an MIQP was handed the caller's whole `time_limit` afresh. Each node QP honoured the clock it was given; the tree only looks at the clock between node solves, so the overrun was up to one full limit per node solve in a row with no tree check between them (cut re-solve, the next solve, strong branching, dives).
2. With that fixed, 9030 still ended at 61.58 s: the 21 node QPs that ran after the deadline (all handed `time_limit = 0`) each paid for `check_convexity()`'s LDL^T, and the step-size norms, before the Condat-Vu loop read the clock, about 74 ms each. `check_convexity()` never passed a deadline to `SparseLdl::check_semidefinite()`, although that function takes one.

## The fix

- `solve_node_with()` sets `time_limit` to what is left before every node solve, LP or QP. The `miqp_node_ipm` path copies it into `node_ipm_options_`, and its two fallbacks (the feasibility LP and the Condat-Vu re-solve) each get what the solves before them left.
- `check_convexity(model, should_stop)` passes the engine's deadline into the ordering, the symbolic analysis and the factorization. A stopped test sets `ConvexityResult::stopped` with the verdict `kUnverified`: never convex, never a refusal with a witness. Both QP engines (`solve_convex_qp`, `solve_convex_qp_ipm`) build the predicate from their own `ResourceLimits`, timer and `SolveControl` interrupt, and a stopped test returns `time_limit` (or `interrupted`) with the message "convexity not established within the time limit: the sparse LDL^T of Q + shift I over N nonzeros was stopped before it finished; stopped at the time limit ...". Soundness is unchanged: only a factorization that completes with every pivot positive accepts Q.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 8 says both.

## Tests that fail on the old code

`tests/unit/test_qp_time_limit.cpp`, 2.5 s in all:

- `QpTimeLimit.AnMiqpNodeQpRunsOnTheTimeThatIsLeft`: a generated 9030-shaped MIQP (20,000 integer columns, banded PD Hessian with a diagonal over four decades). The progress callback spends 0.9 s at the tree's first clock check, before the root QP, under a 1.2 s limit. Old code: 2.12 s (Condat-Vu nodes) and 2.14 s (`miqp_node_ipm=true`), failing `elapsed < limit + 0.5`. New: 1.21 s each, status time_limit.
- `QpTimeLimit.TheConvexityTestEndsAtTheTimeLimitInBothQpEngines`: a 4,000-column strictly diagonally dominant Hessian on a random sparse graph, whose LDL^T fills in to nearly dense. Under a 0.05 s limit the old code returned after 2.85 s (Condat-Vu) and 3.91 s (interior point). New: 0.1 s for both, status time_limit, the message names the convexity test.
- `QpTimeLimit.AConvexityTestStoppedByItsDeadlineDecidesNothing`: with a deadline that has already passed, both a convex and an indefinite Hessian come back `stopped`, `kUnverified`, with no witness; unstopped, the same matrices are decided convex and indefinite. (New API, so it does not compile on the old code.)

## Numbers

All on this laptop (Windows 11, i7-1355U, GCC 13.2, Release), time limit 60 s.

QPLIB_9030, `sankhya solve QPLIB_9030.qps --time-limit 60`:

| | wall | solve seconds | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| main ac41865 | 171.8 s | 170.82 | time_limit |
| node QPs on the time left only | 62.5 s | 61.58 | time_limit |
| this PR | 60.2 s | 60.03 | time_limit, bound 327522.47, no incumbent |

20 other QPLIB instances, `bench/runners/qplib_all.py --time-limit 60 --jobs 2`, main and this PR side by side: every status, objective, reference match and verifier verdict is identical. Largest wall time past the limit: main 15.8 s (QPLIB_3913, a CBL MIQP, 75.8 s), this PR 0.15 s (QPLIB_3913 now 60.1 s).

| instance | type | status (both) | objective (both) | matches ref | verified | wall main | wall PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QPLIB_0018 | QCL | model_error | - | no | - | 0.0 s | 0.1 s |
| QPLIB_10040 | QBL | model_error | - | no | - | 0.1 s | 0.1 s |
| QPLIB_10050 | CBL | time_limit | none found | no | yes | 60.1 s | 60.1 s |
| QPLIB_10069 | CBL | optimal | 0 | yes | yes | 2.8 s | 2.9 s |
| QPLIB_2482 | LCD | read_error | - | no | - | 0.1 s | 0.1 s |
| QPLIB_3678 | LMD | read_error | - | no | - | 0.1 s | 0.1 s |
| QPLIB_3913 | CBL | time_limit | none found | no | yes | 75.8 s | 60.1 s |
| QPLIB_3980 | CBL | time_limit | none found | no | yes | 60.1 s | 60.1 s |
| QPLIB_4270 | CML | time_limit | none found | no | yes | 60.1 s | 60.1 s |
| QPLIB_8495 | DCL | optimal | 42857.4964 | yes | yes | 5.9 s | 4.2 s |
| QPLIB_8515 | CCL | optimal | 319.9999952 | yes | yes | 0.3 s | 0.4 s |
| QPLIB_8559 | CCL | time_limit | 73819678.85 | no | no | 60.2 s | 60.1 s |
| QPLIB_8616 | DCL | optimal | 245.0685978 | yes | yes | 0.3 s | 0.3 s |
| QPLIB_8785 | DCL | optimal | 7867.491149 | yes | yes | 30.7 s | 30.0 s |
| QPLIB_8790 | CCB | optimal | -0.0001562421091 | yes | yes | 1.1 s | 1.2 s |
| QPLIB_8792 | CCB | optimal | 3593.516294 | yes | yes | 0.5 s | 0.5 s |
| QPLIB_8845 | CCL | optimal | 10907992.49 | yes | yes | 0.6 s | 0.6 s |
| QPLIB_8906 | CCL | feasible | 2699111.515 | no | yes | 0.8 s | 0.7 s |
| QPLIB_8938 | DCL | optimal | -35.77945295 | yes | yes | 0.3 s | 0.2 s |
| QPLIB_8991 | CCB | optimal | -0.001667867378 | yes | yes | 0.4 s | 0.3 s |

Of the 11 named as solving optimal, 10 are optimal here on both binaries; QPLIB_8906 comes back `feasible` on both (it is not a change of this PR).

Maros-Meszaros, `bench/runners/maros_meszaros.py --time-limit 60`, all 138:

| binary | optimal | at the published objective | verified | passed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | 107/138 | 106/138 | 119/138 | 106/138 |
| main ac41865, same session | 106/138 | 105/138 | 118/138 | 105/138 |

The two instances that differ, cont-300 (optimal in 42.5 s in the PR run, time_limit in the main run) and stadat1 (iteration_limit at 45 s against time_limit at 60 s), sit at the limit and are decided by the clock: re-run twice more on each binary, both came back time_limit on both binaries every time. No other instance changed status, pass or verifier verdict.

`ctest --test-dir build -j4`: 100% tests passed, 0 failed out of 1481 (the CUDA tests skip on this CPU-only build). Clean with -Wall -Wextra -Werror; clang-format 22.1.8 on the touched files.

No CSV is committed; the runs above wrote to the build directory.

author: tacticaldoll
body:
The base Definition of Done ended with `cargo +1.88 build --workspace`, so every local run built
the whole workspace a second time on a second toolchain. Tianheng made the same move in 0.8.0
("The MSRV build is CI-only"): the pinned build is a second full build that costs a workstation
more than it catches, while CI's msrv job already runs it and the merge waits on it.

What changes:
- Both references drop the pinned build from the base list, so profile-check still finds them
  identical. The shared opening paragraph of the Definition of Done now says builds and checks on
  a pinned toolchain other than the default are not in the list: CI runs them, main accepts a pull
  request only once every CI check has passed, and a report of the list says they were left to CI.
- docs/development-flow.md (shared whole file) says CI also runs those builds.
- The skeleton's owned closing paragraph names the msrv job.
- FAMILY.md records the decision, and a repository's lower floor for its published crates becomes
  an extra CI gate.

Decision: nothing about the MSRV promise moves. The msrv job, the declared rust-version, and the
required-check settings are unchanged; family-check still requires every base gate, and a
repository that keeps the line passes as an extra gate until it adopts this change.

Verification: the skeleton's Definition of Done; a brick and an application instantiated from the
references conform under family-check, pass their own Definition of Done, and family-check detects
a planted drift in each; profile-check reports the references shared.

Before: Ohne eigene `<author>`-Regel in der Domain-Config kam der Autor nur aus `article:author`, JSON-LD oder Readabilitys Byline-Heuristik. WordPress-Block-Themes (`wp-block-post-author-name`) wurden nicht gezielt erkannt, Yoast-JSON-LD mit `{"@id": …}`-Verweis lieferte keinen Namen, und ein `article:author` mit Facebook-URL landete als „Autorenname“ im Artikel. Profil-Links wurden nirgends gespeichert.

After: Fehlt ein Name, greifen generische Signale: WordPress-Blöcke (`wp-block-post-author-name`, `wp-block-post-author-name__link`, `wp-block-post-author__name`), schema.org-Microdata (`itemprop="author"`), hCard (`.author.vcard .fn`) und `<a rel="author">`. „Von“/„By“-Präfixe werden entfernt, URLs gelten nie als Name, JSON-LD-`@id`-Verweise werden aufgelöst. Bei genau einem Autor wird der Profil-Link als `authorUrl` gespeichert, und im Reader sowie in der Share-Ansicht ist der Autorenname damit verlinkt. Content-Filter können den Link mit `<metadata><author-link xpath="…" | json="…"/>` explizit festlegen.

How: `resolveAuthorMetadata()` läuft am Ende von `extractDomainMetadata()`. Reihenfolge für den Namen bleibt Domain-Regel > `article:author` > JSON-LD, danach `GENERIC_AUTHOR_XPATHS`. Der Profil-Link kommt aus einer `<author-link>`-Regel, sonst dem `<a href>` der gewinnenden Domain-`<author>`-Regel (Knoten, Vorfahre oder Link darin), sonst JSON-LD `author.url`, sonst einem generischen Signal mit gleichem Namen, sonst aus einer URL in `article:author`. Nur http(s)-Links, nie die Artikel-URL selbst; bei Co-Autoren bleibt er leer. Neue Spalte `merlin_articles.author_url` (Migration 26), `authorUrl` in Artikel-API, Public Share und Filter-Testlauf. `author-link` steht im `ContentFilterSchema`, Validator und Admin-Editor übernehmen es von dort.

Tests: `php tools/test-author-detection.php` (24 Prüfungen, alle grün); die übrigen `tools/test-*.php` liefern unverändert dasselbe Ergebnis wie auf `main`. `vite build` läuft durch. Hinweis: Die Migration läuft erst mit dem nächsten Versions-Bump in `appinfo/info.xml`.

### عناوين الأدعية
- اختصار عناوين الأدعية الـ٥٨ كلها إلى موضوعها مصدَّراً بكلمة «دعاء» («دعاء التحميد لله عزوجل»).
- عرض العبارة الفاصلة فوق متن كل دعاء: «وَكَانَ مِنْ دُعَاؤُهُ (عليه السلام) فِي يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ».
- توحيد كتابة «دعاؤه» **في العناوين والعبارة الفاصلة فقط** — المتن المنقول والشروح تبقى بحرف المصدر.
- حصر ترقيم «الدعاء ن» بفصل الأدعية وحده: كتاب الصحيفة سبعة فصول، وكان الترقيم يكتب «الدعاء ١» أمام «مقدمة» الملحقات.
- عرض رقم الدعاء بدل عدد الفقرات في القائمة وبطاقة ترويسة القراءة.

### واجهة
- توحيد كل العناوين على الخطّ الافتراضي (Inter + خطوط عربية احتياطية) ومحاذاتها يميناً، مع حراسة ذلك باختبار مصدريّ يمسح `lib/`.
- شريط التنقّل السفلي ينزل تلقائياً عند تبديل التبويب بعد رفعه.
- حبّة «المفضلة» بصفوف البحث تفتح المحفوظات فعلاً بدل الرجوع، وزر رجوع حقيقي بشاشة الزيارات.

### محتوى وبيانات
- كتب الإصدارات المقسَّمة لأجزاء تُعرض بعنوانها وتكشف أجزاءها بالضغط.
- استبعاد الشهداء ذوي السيرة المبتورة بعتبة مقيسة لا بأسماء مكتوبة.

author: bestmaa
body:
## Problem and scope

Native C interop had no executable compiler path. This draft adds the source-bound verification pipeline and a Linux x86-64 scalar export path that emits real Zryna ELF definitions, generates their C header, links typed invocations and executes the independently authored reverse C client.

Related to #417; this is a partial implementation and does not close the issue. Imports and private resource-bearing entries remain verified plans. Generated safe wrappers, execution-instance foreign accounting, physical exactly-once cleanup, hostile foreign-result execution and exact foreign-library/recipe linkage are unfinished. No public CLI profile or support activation is added.

## Architecture

The separate native C source/declaration and body/private authorities retain original source, captured header/policy material and genuine dual-layout/runtime issuers. The registered native C IR and native MIR each independently admit complete untrusted claims; their verifiers do not call the matching producers. The saved graph-test correction uses TOML document deserialization. Strict Rust corrections split cohesive validation responsibilities and use checked ordinals without weakening malformed-input or budget assertions.

The backend accepts only the immutable native C MIR seal and existing exact target capability. A distinct scalar-export artifact retains the complete program and admits only the closed ELF sections, fixed file metadata and exact total public export definitions; imports, relocations and private entries are absent. The driver selects an exact logical export with typed arguments before staging and uses the existing retained GNU toolchain, bounded link/process runner, executable audit, four-byte result framing and consuming cleanup. The existing scalar link helper is moved intact into its own module for reuse. Backend/driver native C IR edges are dev-only for genuine recapture tests; production consumption stays through native MIR.

## Verification

Candidate: `13cf78fb9e208418c76a5894f7d37c435aae4cc0`. Saved checkpoint `8c84df6a18c3e5e598df1e25db269b3e79d284e1` and original `1ddc16dddc5fca34347f86774791374b183b434b` remain ancestors. Verified base main `e63460b599312ab59677080795ff6843ad4d87fe` was merged into the continuation branch. Node 22.22.1, pnpm 11.18.0, Rust 1.97.1, GCC 14.2.0 and GNU ld 2.44; locked dependencies, two Cargo jobs, two test threads, unchanged gate inventories and limits.

Main later advanced to `77e43fef882f6a9e992755253c8056982ec1be94` with the independent #424 beta documentation update. That documentation/test-only delta is not incorporated into this verified branch. A read-only merge-tree preview succeeds; it is not execution evidence for a merged candidate. #416 draft #511 retains separate C interop ownership and no shared layout/IR/ABI change.

| Final candidate check | Observed result |

This PR adds a complete marketing website and admin dashboard for Unknown Host, a secure hosting and infrastructure management platform.

## Summary
A full-featured Next.js application including a public marketing site, authentication flows, and a comprehensive admin dashboard for managing servers, security, users, and infrastructure.

## Key Changes

**Marketing Site & Pages**
- Landing page with hero section, service cards, security features, and Telegram bot showcase
- Documentation page with guides for API, authentication, servers, Telegram bot, security, and webhooks
- Status page with 90-day incident history
- Legal pages (privacy policy, terms of service)
- Contact form with validation and toast notifications

**Authentication**
- Multi-step auth form supporting login and signup modes
- OTP verification with 6-digit input component
- Email verification flow
- Password visibility toggle and validation
- Account lockout after 3 failed attempts (30-second cooldown)

**Admin Dashboard**
- 8-view navigation: Overview, Servers, Security, Users, Telegram Bots, Logs, Notifications, Settings
- **Overview**: Server status, uptime metrics, security score, activity charts
- **Servers**: Server management with status badges, resource usage, region filtering, restart/stop/start actions
- **Security**: Login history, active sessions, device management, security events chart, 2FA/passkey settings
- **Users**: Team member management with role-based access control (Owner, Admin, Operator, Viewer)
- **Telegram Bots**: Bot configuration, chat management, activity metrics
- **Logs**: Audit log viewer with filtering by level and date range
- **Notifications**: Real-time notification center with read/unread states
- **Settings**: Profile management, login security, API key generation and management, workspace settings

**UI Components**
- Reusable component library: Button, Card, Badge, Input, Select, Modal, Switch, Toast, Skeleton
- SecretField component for secure credential display with masked/reveal toggle
- Charts: Sparkline, AreaChart, BarChart, RadialGauge, Meter for data visualization
- Accessible modal with focus trapping and keyboard navigation
- OTP input with auto-advance and paste support

**Styling & Design**
- Tailwind CSS v4 with custom theme (green accent #00ff88, dark background)
- Glass-morphism effects with custom shadows
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach
- Framer Motion animations for transitions and reveals
- Custom grid and particle background effects

**Data & State Management**
- Mock dashboard data (servers, users, sessions, audit logs, notifications)
- React Context-based store for dashboard state management
- Form validation with error handling
- Toast notification system

**Developer Experience**
- TypeScript strict mode
- Comprehensive component documentation
- Utility functions for formatting (IP masking, number formatting, secret masking)
- Custom hooks (useDisclosure, useActiveSection)
- Accessibility features (ARIA labels, focus management, semantic HTML)

## Notable Implementation Details
- API keys are generated client-side using Web Crypto API with secure random values
- Secrets are masked by default and can be revealed for 15 seconds before re-masking
- Dashboard uses a Zustand-like context pattern for state management
- Charts use SVG with Catmull-Rom spline smoothing for smooth curves
- Modal focus is trapped and restored on close for accessibility
- Form validation happens on blur and submit with field-level error messages

body:
Step 4 of 4 of Witzman/pinball-workshop#10 (closes the planned scope of #10). Design: the architect comment on #10.

- `sim/game.ts`: `createGame(def, {rules?, seed?})`; every tick the rules hear `ballAtPlunger`, button edges, switch events (names via `switchNames`, kinds hit/gateAB/gateBA/trigger/capture, in buffer order) and drains; then their commands are applied (magnet, fireSolenoid = kickTrigger, lockBall checks the ball is held, feedBall puts a ball on the plunger) and queued in `outbox` (`takeCommands`). Drained balls are removed (descending index), the rules decide. `main.ts` takes the commands each frame.
- Ball manager in the engine: `ballAtPlunger` and `drain` change `inPlay`; `ball.feed()`, `ball.lock(lockId)` (the ball of the current switch event; lock id = sinkhole trigger id), `ball.release(lockId)` (fireSolenoid for that id), capacity guards, shot progress cleared on a new ball, `onBallStart` called.
- `freePlay` rules (feed on drain) are the default: same behaviour as the old placeholder. Replacing a drained ball happens in the same tick.
- Replay: `runReplay(r, tables, rules?)` seeds the rules from the header seed, returns `rulesHash`, clears the outbox each tick. Goldens: three new `replay/*/rules` keys; every existing world hash is unchanged.
- Zero allocation on an idle tick in the sim (scratch lists reused).

Tests: sim wiring (events, edges, names and kinds, drains, partial drains, outbox, magnet and kick commands, unknown ids, lock check), a launched ball captured by a sinkhole, held 300 ticks, released with a kick, replay determinism of both hashes, seed effect, rules left out changes the result; ball manager unit tests. Mutation-checked: 19 breaks in the wiring and the manager each turn a test red (one gap, the magnet command, found and closed). Bench 2.1 us per ball-step, bundle 12.3 KB gzip.

author: tong-bit-art
body:
# O que este PR faz

Quarto recorte do mesmo prazo, e o que você apontou na revisão do #2169:

> "a barra do prazo nas telas de detalhe ainda conta em milissegundos ou em dias
> locais. Na da administração (`SlaTimelineInline`), às 09h do dia do prazo, ela
> pode dizer '1d em atraso' ao lado de 'Vence em 05/10'."

**Medido, e é maior do que "pode dizer":** ao lado da data certa, a cópia da
administração dizia "1d em atraso" às 09h do dia do prazo; a cópia da organização
dizia "vence hoje"; e **as duas discordavam entre si em 92 de 169 horas seguidas**,
porque cada uma fazia a conta de um jeito (uma com `differenceInDays`, outra com
`Math.floor(ms / dia)`). A barra chegava a **100% às 21h da véspera**, um dia antes
de o prazo acabar.

Agora as duas leem `diasAtePrazo` e `fimDoPrazo` — a mesma âncora do e-mail ao
DPO, do selo e da coluna. O último marco também só ficava "current" no dia
seguinte ao prazo, por comparar `isBefore(dueAt, now)` contra o **início** do dia
guardado.

`Refs #2100` — segue parcial: a lista da organização, o `kpis/route.ts` e os marcos
em dias corridos continuam na `DIVIDA_CONGELADA`, que encolheu de 4 para 2.

---

## Evidence

`due_at = 2026-10-05T00:00:00.000Z`; o dia guardado acaba em
`2026-10-06T00:00:00.000Z` = **21:00 de 05/10** em São Paulo. Medido com as quatro
expressões de hoje lado a lado (`npx tsx sonda4.ts`):

| quando (São Paulo) | org HOJE (`differenceInDays`) | admin HOJE (`floor(ms/dia)`) | proposta | barra HOJE | barra nova |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 04/10 09:00 | vence hoje | vence hoje | **1d restantes** | 98% | 93% |
| 04/10 21:00 | vence hoje | vence hoje | **vence hoje** | **100%** | 95% |
| 04/10 22:00 | vence hoje | **1d em atraso** | **vence hoje** | 100% | 96% |
| 05/10 09:00 | vence hoje | **1d em atraso** | **vence hoje** | 100% | 98% |
| 05/10 20:00 | vence hoje | **1d em atraso** | **vence hoje** | 100% | 100% |
| 05/10 21:00 | 1d em atraso | 1d em atraso | **1d em atraso** | 100% | 100% |
| 06/10 09:00 | 1d em atraso | **2d em atraso** | **1d em atraso** | 100% | 100% |
| 20/10 09:00 | 15d em atraso | **16d em atraso** | **15d em atraso** | 100% | 100% |

```console
=== as duas cópias discordam? ===
em 169 horas medidas: 92 horas em que o tenant e o admin dizem coisas DIFERENTES
```

## Root cause

Duas cópias do mesmo componente, e duas âncoras erradas em cada:

- `app/app/lgpd/requests/[id]/SlaTimeline.tsx` — `differenceInDays(dueAt, now)`
  (dias de calendário, no fuso do navegador) e `total = dueAt - receivedAt`;
- `app/admin/(protected)/lgpd/requests/[id]/_client.tsx` — `Math.floor(msUntilDue / dia)`
  e o mesmo `total`.

`due_at` é o **início** do dia do prazo; as duas mediam até ele, e o prazo vai até
o **fim** do dia. A duplicação é o que fez as duas divergirem em direções opostas
— mesmo produto, duas telas, respostas contrárias.

## Files Changed

| arquivo | o que |
|---|---|
| `lib/lgpd/sla.ts` | +37 — `fimDoPrazo(dueAt)`: a âncora, num lugar só. `horasAteOFimDoPrazo` passa a usá-la |
| `lib/lgpd/balde-de-sla.ts` | `computeRiskLevel` usa `fimDoPrazo` em vez de `+ 86_400_000` (**no-op** — ver abaixo) |
| `app/app/lgpd/requests/[id]/SlaTimeline.tsx` | `diasAtePrazo` + `fimDoPrazo`; `milestoneStatus` recebe `prazoPassou` |
| `app/admin/(protected)/lgpd/requests/[id]/_client.tsx` | `diasAtePrazo` + `fimDoPrazo` |
| `tests/unit/lgpd-prazo-e-dia-civil.test.ts` | +159 — a barra, a régua das duas cópias, `fimDoPrazo` e a partição das listas |
| `.changes/prazo-lgpd-barra-das-telas.md` | fragmento: `nada_mudou` / `corrigido` (→ patch) |

**6 arquivos, +240/−40.** Sem migration, sem schema, sem RLS, sem frase nova.

## Tests

**49 passed** nos dois arquivos de LGPD (eram 41). O que entrou:

- `fimDoPrazo` **com asserção direta** (o primitivo não tinha nenhuma): o dia
  seguinte, o fim de 05/10 às 21h em São Paulo, e o ilegível devolvendo `null`;
- a barra não fecha 100% na véspera, fecha no fim do dia, e não fecha um minuto antes;
- a régua das duas cópias: cada arquivo precisa **importar** o helper e usar as
  duas funções, e **não pode** voltar a `differenceInDays(due, …)` nem a `msUntilDue`;
- o último marco: `diasDeAtraso` é 0 no dia do prazo e 1 depois dele;
- a **partição das três listas** (`LEEM_PELO_HELPER` / `REPASSA_O_VALOR` /
  `DIVIDA_CONGELADA`): um arquivo em duas listas é vermelho.

### Sabotagem — agora com `git show origin/main:<arquivo>`, e não com mutação escrita à mão

Você achou no #2169 que a minha armadilha procurava uma forma que nunca existiu, e
que ela ficava verde contra o código real. Esta rodada troca o método: cada
sabotagem **repõe o arquivo real da `main`**.

```
BASELINE (sem sabotagem)                                rc=0   0 failed
SlaTimeline.tsx volta ao código da main                 rc=1   3 failed | 34 passed
_client.tsx (admin) volta ao código da main             rc=1   2 failed | 35 passed
balde-de-sla.ts volta ao código da main                 rc=0   0 failed   ← e deve mesmo
um arquivo em DUAS listas (o defeito do #2169)          rc=1   1 failed | 36 passed
```

**O terceiro resultado é um `0 failed` honesto, não um buraco:** a mudança em
`balde-de-sla.ts` é um **no-op** — `new Date(dueAt).getTime() + DIA_MS` virou
`fimDoPrazo(dueAt).getTime()`, o mesmo instante. Repor a `main` não muda
comportamento nenhum, então nenhum teste deve ficar vermelho mesmo. Se ficasse,
o teste estaria medindo o texto e não a regra.

E o primitivo, sabotado à parte (`+ DIA_MS` → `+ 0`): **seis casos vermelhos**, de
duas suítes diferentes.

### Os dois ajustes que a sua revisão do #2169 pediu, aplicados no método

1. **A partição das listas** — no #2169 a tela da organização ficou em
   `LEEM_PELO_HELPER` **e** em `DIVIDA_CONGELADA`. Agora há caso próprio, e ele fica
   vermelho quando eu injeto exatamente aquele defeito.
2. **A armadilha aponta para a forma real** — as novas usam as expressões que
   existiam na `main` (`differenceInDays(due…`, `msUntilDue`, `new Date(due_at)`), e
   a prova é a reposição do arquivo da `main`, não uma mutação minha.

### Gates

| gate | resultado |
|---|---|
| `vitest run` nos 2 arquivos de LGPD | **49 passed** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | **18 erros antes, 18 depois** — todos de 7 pacotes ausentes neste checkout. **Zero** nos arquivos tocados |
| `eslint . --quiet` | **0 erros** |
| `prettier --check` nos **novos** | ok. As duas telas já não eram prettier-clean na `main` e ficaram como estavam — `--write` nelas reformataria linhas que não são minhas |
| `tsx scripts/cortar-release.ts` | fragmento aceito |
| `vitest run --project cercas` | **nenhuma falha nova** comparando a lista de arquivos. A única diferença é `sem-marcador-de-conflito.test.ts`, o timeout por carga já medido na rodada anterior (2,3 s isolado, igual aqui e na base; passa no CI) |

## Risks

- **A barra passa a chegar a 100% ~24 h mais tarde.** É o conserto: ela chegava
  cheia quando ainda faltava um dia.
- **A contagem em dias muda de valor** em ~1 dia no intervalo do prazo. Antes, uma
  das telas subestimava e a outra superestimava; agora as duas usam a régua do resto
  do módulo.
- **Na véspera à noite, depois das 21h de São Paulo, o módulo diz "vence hoje"** —
  porque o dia civil do prazo, no eixo UTC em que o motor conta, já começou. Não é
  deste PR: é a mesma hora em que o selo já é `at_risk` e a organização já é
  `critical`. Mudar isso é mudar `computeDueAt`.
- **Nenhuma linha de `lgpd_requests` muda.**

## Compatibility

- **Schema: nada.** Sem migration, sem `baseline.sql`, sem MANIFEST.
- **Contrato da API: não muda.** `risk_level` e `sla_bucket` ficam iguais — o
  `balde-de-sla.ts` deste PR é no-op, e os 49 casos provam.
- **Produto instalado: nada a fazer.** `impacto: nada_mudou` → **patch**.
- **`computeDueAt` intocada.** As três horas do eixo UTC seguem declaradas como
  limite do motor.
- **Nada de layout.** As mesmas células e os mesmos `<div>`; o que muda é o número
  que entra neles. Nenhuma frase nova no dicionário.

## Why Maintainers May Accept It

1

author: rikutoyamada01
body:
## 概要 (Overview)

本PRでは、点字学習装置における単音節音声認識の**汎用精度・女性話者（新規話者）・スピーカフォン環境（実機残響）におけるロバストネス向上**を目的に、複数の学習・モデル戦略を体系的に実装・評価・統合しました。

さらに、学習済み戦略モデルを **Hugging Face Hub (`braille-mate/braille-mate-hiragana-recognizer`) の戦略別ディレクトリ（`strategies/<strategy_name>/`）に一元管理**し、Raspberry Pi や別 PC などのエッジ端末で**手動ファイル転送なしに個別自動ダウンロードして即座に実行できる仕組み**を構築しました。

---

## 主な成果とベンチマーク結果 (Leaderboard)

同一の評価データセット（汎用検証セット、実機スピーカフォン録音セット、AI女性話者テストセット）および Raspberry Pi 想定の CPU 推論環境（ONNX INT8）にて比較計測を実施しました。

| Strategy | カテゴリ | 汎用検証 Acc | スピーカフォン Acc | 女性話者 Acc | CPU レイテンシ | モデルサイズ | 評価サマリー |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`wav2vec2_phoneme_multi`** 🏆 | **Representation & Loss** | **90.3%** | **88.5%** | **76.9% (+9.6%)** | **41.3 ms** | **116.6 MB** | **【最高精度・推奨】子音・母音マルチタスク。女性話者で大幅向上、推論も最速クラス** |
| `wav2vec2_baseline` | Baseline | 92.8% | 90.4% | 67.3% | 70.1 ms | 116.6 MB | 標準 Wav2Vec2 ファインチューニング |
| `wav2vec2_ipa_kd` | Knowledge Distillation | 90.2% | 89.1% | 71.2% (+3.9%) | 44.6 ms | 116.6 MB | XLS-R 国際音声記号(IPA)ソフトターゲット蒸留 |
| `wav2vec2_whisper_kd` | Knowledge Distillation | 90.1% | 87.8% | 63.5% | 40.8 ms | 116.6 MB | Whisper-large-v3 中間特徴量アライメント |
| `wav2vec2_rir_simulation` | Acoustic Augmentation | 89.2% | 85.3% | 69.2% | 44.2 ms | 116.6 MB | 部屋インパルス応答(RT60) & マイク歪みシミュレーション |
| `wav2vec2_phoneme_ipa_hybrid` | Hybrid | 87.5% | 85.9% | 59.6% | 71.4 ms | 116.6 MB | マルチタスク音素分解 + XLS-R IPA 蒸留の複合 |
| `wav2vec2_arcface` | Representation & Loss | 24.9% | 11.5% | 9.6% | 50.4 ms | 116.5 MB | 角度マージン損失（少サンプル単音節では過学習・ノルム崩壊） |

### 🏆 チャンピオン戦略: `wav2vec2_phoneme_multi`
- **日本語 105 文字分類 + 子音 16 クラス分類 + 母音 5 クラス分類** のマルチタスク学習モデル。
- 課題であった女性話者の認識精度が **67.3% → 76.9% (+9.6% 向上)** へ大幅改善。
- 音響前処理を内包した ONNX INT8 モデルにより、CPU 推論レイテンシ **41.3 ms**（目標の 70ms 未満を余裕で達成）を記録。

---

## 実装・変更内容 (Changes)

1. **学習ストラテジーの実装**:
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/phoneme_multi/`: 子音・母音マルチタスク学習実装
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/ipa_kd/`: XLS-R 多言語 IPA 事後確率蒸留
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/whisper_kd/`: OpenAI Whisper 特徴量蒸留
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/arcface/`: Additive Angular Margin Loss
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/rir_simulation/`: 実機部屋音響畳み込み & クリッピングシミュレーション
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/phoneme_ipa_hybrid/`: ハイブリッド検証

2. **ストラテジー・レジストリ & ファクトリ統合**:
   - `src/voicerecognizer/strategies/registry.py`: `DEFINED_STRATEGIES` による一元管理、`create_strategy_recognizer` 実装
   - `src/voicerecognizer/core/factory/recognizer_factory.py`: `RecognizerFactory.create()` で全戦略名を直接受け付け可能に拡張

3. **Hugging Face Hub 戦略別管理 & 個別自動ダウンロード**:
   - `src/voicerecognizer/utils/model_uploader.py`:
     - `upload_strategy_weights_to_hf`: `strategies/<strategy_name>/` へモデル成果物をスマートアップロード（ハッシュ一致時はスキップ）
     - `download_strategy_weights_if_needed`: 未所持または古い場合に HF Hub から個別自動取得し、必要に応じてローカル ONNX エクスポートを実行
     - `list_remote_strategies`: リモートでホストされている戦略一覧の取得
   - `script/upload_to_hf.py`: `--strategy <name>` / `--strategy all-active` による柔軟な一括アップロード CLI を提供

4. **推論 UI & CLI の拡張**:
   - `main.py`: `--strategy` (または `--model`) で任意の戦略を指定可能に拡張
   - マイクリアルタイム対話採点モードにて、Top-3 予測候補と確信度バーを常時表示

5. **ドキュメントの拡充**:
   - `benchmarks/LEADERBOARD.md`: 全戦略の横並びスコア一覧を新規作成
   - `docs/MODEL_HUB_GUIDE.md`: 戦略の HF リモート管理構造と個別自動ダウンロード仕様を追記
   - `README.md`: クイックスタート、Top-3 表示、戦略指定オプションを最新化

---

## 使用方法 (Usage)

### 1. CLI からの推論実行
手元にモデル重みが存在しない場合でも、**Hugging Face Hub から該当モデルのみが個別自動ダウンロード**されて即座に実行されます。

```powershell
# 最高精度モデル (子音・母音マルチタスク) で推論
uv run python main.py dataset/mikeryu/a/001.wav --strategy wav2vec2_phoneme_multi

# リアルタイムマイク推論 & 連続人間丸付けモード (Top-3 候補表示)
uv run python main.py --strategy wav2vec2_phoneme_multi
```

### 2. Python コードからの動的切り替え
```python
from voicerecognizer.core.factory.recognizer_factory import RecognizerFactory

# 未ダウンロード時は自動的に HF Hub から取得・配置
recognizer = RecognizerFactory.create("wav2vec2_phoneme_multi")
text = recognizer.recognize("sample.wav")
print(f"認識結果: {text}")

# 利用可能な全戦略一覧を取得
print(RecognizerFactory.available_strategies())
# => ('cnn', 'wav2vec2', 'wav2vec2_baseline', 'wav2vec2_ipa_kd', 'wav2vec2_phoneme_multi', ...)
```

### 3. 戦略モデルの Hugging Face Hub アップロード (開発者向け)
```powershell
# 特定の戦略をアップロード
uv run python script/upload_to_hf.py --strategy wav2vec2_phoneme_multi

# ベンチマーク済みの全アクティブ戦略を一括同期
uv run python script/upload_to_hf.py --strategy all-active
```

---

## テスト・品質管理 (Verification)

- `pytest tests/test_model_uploader.py tests/test_strategy_hf_sync.py`: 全 15 件のテストがパス。
- `ruff check` / `ruff format`: コードスタイルおよび型整合性をパス。
- Hugging Face Hub リポジトリ（`braille-mate/braille-mate-hiragana-recognizer`）の `strategies/` 配下に全アクティブ戦略が正常にアップロード・同期されていることを確認。

Title: Stock page: location, category and size, locked stock-in from a row, ledger filters

Stock in modal

## Summary
This PR adds support for a new insurance product type: personal accident insurance (PA - "ประกันอุบัติเหตุส่วนบุคคล"). Users can now select between car, motorcycle, and personal accident insurance, with a simplified selection flow based on age range and occupation class.

## Key Changes

- **New Insurance Product Type**: Added "pa" (personal accident) as a third vehicle type alongside "car" and "moto"
  - New tab in the finder UI with icon and label
  - Simplified 2-step selection process (age range → occupation class)
  - No vehicle/brand/model selection needed

- **Data Structure**: Created `assets/data-pa.js` containing:
  - Three PA products: PLV, PA 700, and Bone (fracture insurance)
  - Age bands (1 month - 70 years) with different pricing tiers
  - Occupation classes (1-4 plus student) with class-specific pricing
  - Comprehensive occupation list for search functionality
  - Coverage details and policy conditions per product

- **State Management**: Extended application state to track PA-specific selections:
  - `paAge`: Selected age range ID
  - `paOcc`: Selected occupation class ID
  - `paOccName`: Custom occupation name from search

- **UI Components**:
  - New `renderPaSearch()` function with dedicated search interface
  - `vtypeTabs()` extracted for reuse across search types
  - Occupation search sheet with filterable occupation list
  - PA-specific summary card showing age and occupation

- **Offer Generation**: Implemented `paOffers()` and `paBlockReason()` to:
  - Filter available products based on age and occupation
  - Handle student restrictions (PLV doesn't accept students)
  - Generate plan options with appropriate pricing

- **Quote Display**:
  - PA-specific coverage rows (death, injury, medical, fracture, funeral, etc.)
  - `paCoverageValue()` for formatting PA-specific benefit amounts
  - `highlights()` adapted to show PA plan key features
  - Quote table with PA-specific product badges and coverage details

- **UI Polish**:
  - `clsBadge()` function to display product names (PA) or class numbers (car/moto)
  - Updated vehicle icon logic to show person icon for PA
  - Conditional text for "check premium for new car/person"
  - Tax note display in quote showing VAT/stamp duty inclusion

## Implementation Details

- PA products use a `bands` object mapping age IDs to price indices, allowing flexible age-based pricing
- Coverage values can be undefined (product doesn't have this benefit), null (benefit not covered in this plan), or a number/object
- Student occupation is treated as class 2 for pricing but flagged separately for product eligibility
- All PA pricing is per-person per-year as specified in product brochures
- Cache version bumped to v7 and service worker updated to include new data file

author: claycantrell
body:
Two causes, both measured:
- The surface mesh wasn't watertight: each cell chose its own corner heights,
  so the same grid point could be drawn at two heights (3,000-6,200 cracks per
  area, up to 9.7 units). Now every grid point has one surface height shared
  by all cells around it (dry points tuck under the bank at the highest wet
  neighbour, looking across chunk borders), so where levels differ the
  surface slopes between them; steep drops are drawn as white water (rapids)
- Containment ran per chunk and couldn't see neighbours, so a lake spanning a
  border could sit at two levels (370-780 seam splits per area, up to 7.8).
  Containment now reads neighbouring chunks, shared border points get one
  level, and drops spread chunk to chunk through a queue; affected neighbours
  are redrawn

Now: seam splits 0 in all four test areas, cracks 6-14 (mostly < 2 units),
hovering corners 0 in three areas and 6 (1.6 units) in one.

Approach informed by Minecraft aquifers (one fluid level per region, barriers
between different levels) and procedural river work (levels drop at
rapids/falls).

author: aniketmaithani
body:
Part 5 of #63. **Stacked on #67 (model capabilities).**

- **`domain.llm_pricing`**: a call is priced on the model that **served** it, in **integer micros** of US dollars per million tokens (AGENTS §3: no floats):

  | Model | Input | Output | Cache reads |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Opus 5.5 | $4 | $20 | $0.20 |
  | Sonnet 5.5 | $2 | $10 | $0.20 |
  | Haiku 4.5 | $1 | $5 | $0.10 |

  Cache writes cost 1.25× input. Each call is rounded **up** to a whole micro, an unpriced model raises, and negative counts are refused. **Please check the Haiku 4.5 prices.** The Opus and Sonnet prices come from the current model docs; I couldn't find Haiku 4.5's there, so its figures are from memory.
- **`ports.llm_client`** (`LLMClient.complete(LlmRequest) -> LlmResponse`):
  - A request names its **task**, its **prompt version** (which must belong to that task) and its **variables**. The adapter renders the versioned prompt file (AGENTS §7), so no business code assembles a prompt, and untrusted mention text arrives only as variables.
  - It carries the checked `RequestShape`, the JSON schema of the structured output, prompt caching, refusal fallback, a timeout and the reasoning-summary opt-in.
  - The response has the served model, the stop reason, the raw structured output (none on a refusal) and the usage. The gateway validates, prices and records the call.
  - `LlmCallFailed` carries a **code** and whether a retry may help, never provider text.

Unit tests cover:
- the cost for each model, including cache reads and writes and rounding up
- refusal of an unpriced model and of negative token counts
- the request's task rule
- the failure code
- a client conforming to the port

Commits: `feat(domain)`, `feat(ports)`, `test(domain)`.

author: hstoecker
body:
**Problem:** GitHub Pages serves \`/assets/css/main.css\` with \`cache-control: max-age=600\`. A visitor who loaded the site shortly before a deploy keeps the old stylesheet for up to 10 minutes. A page with a **new figure** then renders its SVG without the figure's CSS – paths are filled black instead of drawn as lines. I saw exactly this in the local preview of the early-atmosphere article (PR #28) until I reloaded.

**Fix:** \`_layouts/default.html\` appends \`?v={{ site.time | date: '%s' }}\` (the build time) to \`main.css\` and the five scripts (\`nav\`, \`lens\`, \`graph\`, \`code\`, \`guide\`). Every deploy changes the URL, so browsers fetch the new files immediately; between deploys caching works as before.

- \`check_site.py\` ignores query strings when it resolves links – checked: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- Browser test: stylesheet and scripts load with \`?v=\`, the graph page draws its 51 nodes, no console errors
- Rule documented in the \`wildbionics-design\` skill; plugin version **1.10.2** (PR #29 uses 1.10.1 – whichever merges second, I'll resolve the one-line version conflict)

## What changed

Hands-on UI QA found that Observer Send submitted the click event as `[object Object]`, narrow layouts buried the Coder composer beneath the entire settings sidebar, and Lite Coder requests failed before reaching a provider. The TUI also lost drafts when credentials were missing, misrouted pointer input after focus changed the pane split, and scrolled long wrapped messages incorrectly.

This PR fixes those interaction failures and gives both interfaces a shared pale lavender/blue palette.

- **GUI:** correct Observer click submission; preserve IME composition and Shift+Enter; associate settings labels; trap/restore modal focus; keep settings reachable through a mobile toggle while bringing the composer into the first viewport. Fix default thread naming and Markdown export newlines, expose server disconnect/reconnect state, and prevent reloads from repeating the same automatic Observer recovery request.
- **TUI:** share drawing/hit-test geometry, count rendered wrapped rows, keep picker selections visible, preserve drafts while blocked or busy, implement bracketed multiline paste without dispatching pasted commands, and make Ctrl+O review the latest completed Coder response. Keyless interactive setup can reach `/keys`; noninteractive authentication checks stay strict.
- **Configuration:** preserve workspace/approval/Observer preferences when switching presets. Clear explicit credentials when their effective destination changes, allow pane fallback only for matching provider and endpoint, and exclude legacy secret fields from browser config persistence. TUI preferences and `/base_url` also re-resolve credentials for the destination.
- **Local workflows:** generate scaffolds for the host shell, refuse existing directories, and ignore inherited CDPATH when entering the new directory. Fix Lite prompt interpolation so JSON tool examples remain literal.
- **Visuals:** align Coder, Observer, Chat, controls, review panels, and code highlighting around blue/periwinkle/lavender; retain readable warning/error meaning colors. Remove the loop effect that shifted the entire page's hue.
- **QA:** add interaction/rendering regressions and make UI smoke results fail on page errors, console errors, and failed HTTP responses even if scenario assertions pass.

## Validation

`bash scripts/check-local.sh` passed locally and in both Linux/macOS CI for `62a7ef3` ([run](https://github.com/RyoSpiralArchitect/Spiral-Coder/actions/runs/37104977114)):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Rust unit / server asset integration | 595 + 1 passed; 1 existing HF test ignored |
| TUI orchestration replay | 3/3 |
| JavaScript | 53 passed |
| Python, including Lite Coder and SSE regressions | 12 passed |
| Repo-map evaluation | 14/14 |
| Formatting, JS/shell syntax, Lite assets/status/git smoke | Passed |

Actual Rust and Lite GUIs ran in the in-app Browser with a local key-free provider fixture. Verified Japanese multiline input, exact Observer pointer submission and draft clearing, streaming stop/retry, simulated HTTP 503 recovery, server disconnect/reconnect, repeated reload without duplicate assistance, search, settings/preset retention, label focus, and Help/Reader dialog focus and dismissal. Desktop 1280×800 and narrow 390×844 / 320×740 layouts had no horizontal overflow; the narrow Coder input remained in the first viewport. Final screenshots showed the intended page and usable content without an error overlay; final Browser error/warning logs were empty.

The final rebuilt TUI also emitted the expected blue/lavender truecolor ANSI values in a PTY (with `NO_COLOR` removed only in the test child). Actual TUI processes ran in a PTY with keyless Mistral/Anthropic setup, `/provider`, `/keys`, Japanese multiline paste, terminal resize, and clean exit with raw/alternate-screen/bracketed-paste restoration. Ratatui TestBackend and production input-handler regressions separately cover drawing, pointer routing, scrolling, and draft preservation.

## Verification limits

- Desktop computer use rejected Terminal access, so TUI evidence is PTY + TestBackend, not desktop pointer automation.
- Native OS IME composition and completed native Markdown downloads were not verified; their submission/export logic has regression coverage.
- Windows scaffold execution was not available on this macOS host. POSIX creation, literal content, duplicate-directory refusal, and CDPATH isolation were executed.
- Browser QA used mock responses and does not establish live model quality. Model selection policy was not changed.
- Browser interactions were run through the in-app Browser. The standalone Playwright `ui-smoke.mjs` suite was not rerun here; its diagnostics gate has focused unit coverage.

author: yottayoshida
body:
<!-- triage-batch: b_4999e2056da7 -->

## Summary

Property, from `docs/limits.md` (added here): "With a key set, a question that names a value — a number, a checksum, a code, with three digits or more in one of them — has its values looked for in the whole of each moved-out result, a line at a time. Where one result alone has a line holding them all, each as a word of its own, Jev is told so beside that result's first lines, and still chooses: a result is not given because a line of it holds a value."

`find` shows Jev the call that made each result and its first 400 characters, so asked for a value further down a result it said that none was about it: 13 times of 14 in the benchmark. It now looks for the values in the whole of each result and adds one sentence to the option of the one result that holds them. This is the change asked for in #55, which stays open until I comment on it and it is shut by hand.

**The property is not the one the plan started from.** The first form answered without asking Jev when one result held the value; its review found three ways that gives an unrelated result silently. A second form told Jev of every result that held a value; told the same of four, Jev gave the first as the answer (`bench/results/2026-10-03-values/told-of-each/`). The form here tells Jev of one result or of none, and Jev chooses.

## Verified

- Jev alone (`pick`, 7 conversations, Workers AI): by a value, the right result given 17 times of 17 (1 of 17 before); by meaning, 18 given and 8 listed, as before. `bench/results/2026-10-03-values/picks.json`.
- 30 other questions, each asked of Jev once (21 written before any rule, 3 after the first review, 6 written to mislead: the value they name is another result's): no wrong result given. On the 6, Jev gave the result asked for 5 times and listed it first once. Asked once: this does not show that Jev never takes the result it is told of, and `docs/limits.md` says so.
- Through an agent (Haiku 4.5, key set, 3 runs; Claude Code 2.1.288 for `opaque` and 2.1.287 for `results`, the versions their bases were built with): a code in the middle of a document, 8 of 9 right (1 of 9 with #51). `find` was called for 8 and was right on all 8; for the ninth the agent called no tool. `results`: 8, 8 and 7 of 8 right (6, 8 and 5 with #51). Not run: the arm with no key, which has no `find`; Sonnet and Opus (#57).
- All of it was measured on the code as it is in this PR: `src/`, `hooks/`, `package.json` and `.claude-plugin/` of the measured commit are the same files as here (`diff -rq`). The units name that code by `plugin` (`b6736911384a`); their `pluginCommit` is a local commit made to measure, not pushed.
- `npm test`: 345 pass. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:hooks`, `npm run validate`, `npm run check:host` (9 checks, Claude Code 2.1.288): pass.
- Each of 23 one-line breaks of `src/find.ts` fails a test. Each of 50 changes of a figure in a document, or of a published record, fails the test that binds them.
- Reviews by readers with none of the context, two of the diff and one of what is sent out:
  - Round 1, on the first form: three ways it gave an unrelated result with `[found]`. The form was rebuilt, twice.
  - Round 2: a value joined to another word (`job-4821`, `status:500`) was not found, and the answer said no line held it — a word now needs only that no letter or digit stands right beside it. A number written with commas (`9,821.50`) gave `821.50` as the value — it now gives none. Four statements of the documents were corrected.
  - What is sent: in the added sentence a value with the shape of a secret went to Jev unblanked, and past the 2,000 characters a question is cut at — the values are now taken from the question as it is sent. A test that failed before that change holds it.
- simplify: applied 4, passed over 3.
- CI: pending.

## Same-class scan

- A text match alone deciding the answer. `grep -n "found(files" src/find.ts`: two calls. `:342` is Jev's choice. `:275` is a quoted phrase of twelve characters or more that one result alone holds: not a hit — the asker quoted it, and it has been the documented behaviour since 0.3.0. That match does look through kept parts of the conversation, where an earlier question of the agent may stand: not filed — such a part does hold the phrase, and no wrong result was observed.
- Text sent to Jev that does not pass `redact`. `grep -rn "choose(" src hooks`: one caller, `src/find.ts:286`. Its options are the call (blanked), the digest (blanked) and the added sentence: corrected here, as above.
- Not filed: a file's name with two digits (`log42.txt`) counts as a value and stands on no line of a result, so the answer says no line holds the values together — no wrong result. A result whose first lines hold the words `One of its lines holds "…"` could lean Jev towards it — as any text in the first 400 characters could before.

## Open points

None that needs a decision. Known, and written in `docs/limits.md`: where a question about one result names a value of another, Jev is told of the other and may take it.

## Recommendation

Merge. The change is in what `find` does with a value; where the agent does not call `find` at all (one code of nine here) is #54, and the same measurement with Sonnet and Opus is #57.
