body:
Drain-Review-Verdict: APPROVE
Drain-Review-Head: 11532d51a417296538d8a7d03bc92cb2549d1ec7
Drain-Review-Artifact: https://github.com/TinyAssets/TinyAssets/pull/4361#issuecomment-5966630240

## Main is red and this unblocks it

`preview-security` / "Preview trust-boundary contract" fails **on main**, not on any one PR, so it is currently red on every open PR.

| sha | result | when |
|---|---|---|
| `9c0fd4c69` | **failure** | 06:52Z |
| `b024c872c` | success | 06:27Z |
| `405116067` | success | 06:00Z |
| `5e3fc0170` | success | 05:30Z |

Exactly one commit between the last green and the first red touches these files: **`8c404911e6` (#4352, "Skip five heavy PR workflows while a PR is a draft")**. It added

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
```

and did not update the test that pins this workflow's shape, which still asserted `on.pull_request === null`. `git show 8c404911e6 --name-only | grep -c preview-worker-security.test.mjs` → `0`.

## #4352 did not weaken anything — the guard measured the wrong thing

The old assertion used `=== null` as a proxy for "unfiltered". But a `types` list is not automatically a narrowing, and this one is the **three GitHub defaults plus `ready_for_review`** — strictly more triggering than before. So the boundary is intact; the guard just happened to be pinned to the absence of a key rather than to the property it cared about.

## What this pins instead

- **The types must contain every default** (`opened`, `reopened`, `synchronize`). That catches a real narrowing — verified by dropping `synchronize`, which fails with `on.pull_request.types drops the default 'synchronize', so the job would stop running on some ordinary PR events`. The old assertion would have caught that only by accident.
- **The types must contain `ready_for_review`**, because the draft skip is only correct with it: it is not a default type, so without it a PR marked ready keeps the draft run's skip until its next push. The trigger and the `if:` are one contract, so the test now holds them together.
- **A conditional on the job must lead with the event-name check.** Nothing enforced this. Without it, `merge_group`, `push`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` runs read `pull_request.draft` as `undefined` and get skipped too. The workflow's own comment warned about exactly this; no test held it.

The test keeps triggering-shape assertions tolerant of `null` as well, so reverting #4352's trigger would also pass — this does not lock in the draft skip, it only forbids a narrowing.

## Header comment corrected, not left to mislead

#4352 made the existing header inaccurate: the job no longer runs on "every pull request", it runs on every **non-draft** one, and "unfiltered" here means by **path**, not by event. The branch-protection caveat is restated where someone acting on "required-check candidate" will actually read it, since a skipped job reports `conclusion=skipped` and branch protection accepts that as satisfied — the hole #4352's own commit message flagged.

## Scope

Two files, +41/−6 at `11532d51a4` (the figure was +49/−6 before the Codex fold shrank the test). **No change to what runs.** Deliberately separate from #4357 (my model-shortlist feature PR): a workflow file does not belong on a feature PR — the shape `CLAUDE.md` flags from #1491 — and putting it there would have invalidated that PR's review receipt again.

Local: `npm test` in `WebSite/site-react` → **233 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped**. `actionlint` is not on this host's PATH; CI runs it on every workflow-touching PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Codex cross-family refute: ADAPT, folded (head `11532d51a4`)

`gpt-6-astra`, read-only, asked to refute. **ADAPT**, four `DISAGREE_EVIDENCE`. The valuable finding: **#4352 did add a guard** — `tests/test_ci_runner_budget.py`, a Python test I had not found. So my JS additions duplicated it while my comments claimed coverage that actually lives there.

Codex disproved three of my claims by in-memory mutation:

| Mutation | My test said | Reality |
|---|---|---|
| `pull_request: null`, draft `if:` kept | "holds both halves together" | **passes** — comment was false |
| `if: false` | "must pass non-PR events first" | **passes**, skips every run |
| workflow `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` | "prevents coverage reductions" | **passes** |

It also confirmed claim A from the brief against GitHub's docs (defaults are exactly `opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`, so #4352's list narrows nothing), confirmed the diagnosis (finding 7), and confirmed the parsed workflow objects are identical at base and head — no behaviour change.

**I removed the duplication instead of chasing each hole with a stronger assertion.** `test_ci_runner_budget.py` pins the exact draft condition, the three default activity types, `ready_for_review`, *and* the branch-protection-context rule this file cannot see — strictly stronger on every one. Two authorities for one fact drift apart; one of them should not assert it.

What this file keeps is what Codex confirmed is covered nowhere else: **no `paths`, `paths-ignore` or `branches` under `pull_request`**. That is what "unfiltered" means for a trust boundary — by path, not by event.

Verified both directions after the fold: adding `paths-ignore` fails here; `if: false` fails in the Python test. `npm test` 233 pass / 0 fail; `pytest tests/test_ci_runner_budget.py` 8 passed.

Net result is **smaller than before the review** — the test is −30/+22 rather than +42 — with the broken `=== null` assertion still fixed, which was the actual red on main.

Codex also caught that my brief told it `git diff main...HEAD` while local `main` is stale at `52ae4657dd` (a 3,118-file span). It reviewed the correct `9c0fd4c693..HEAD` range anyway and said so.

author: hcw-architect
body:
Closes #816
Closes #837
Closes #834
Closes #822

This PR holds six items, so there is one PR and one `hcw-azure` run. Only B and C touch `infra/`. The run needs one owner step by hand after the apply; it is at the end.

## A. Every provider the site routes can be chosen on the review board

Docker, VMware and Ansible are included. This is the bug left by #775, widened at the owner's request.

**The problem.** Docker has had `/docker/blog/<slug>` since #776, and VMware and Ansible have had blog routes for longer. But `normalizeProviderName` knew six providers: aws, azure, gcp, github, terraform and finops. So `Docker`, `VMware` and `Ansible` all normalised to `''`:
- `updateContentItem` refused them.
- `validatePublishMetadata` refused the publish.
- `inferProviderFromTags` returned `null`.

The review board offered only Azure, AWS, GCP, GitHub, Terraform and FinOps. "Send to Publish Queue" stays disabled until a provider is set.

**The fix: derive from the registries instead of keeping copies.**
- **Server.** `normalizeProviderName` is now derived from `PROVIDER_ALIASES` in `functions/src/lib/public-reads.js`, the server's provider registry. `public-section-counts.test.js` already holds that registry to `VALID_PROVIDERS`.
  - The stored value is the route key with its first letter capitalised, exactly as `Aws`, `Gcp` and `Finops` always were. The new ones are `Docker`, `Vmware` and `Ansible`.
  - Every spelling the registry lists still normalises (`Google Cloud`, `GitHub`, `VMware`).
  - `public-reads.js` has no imports, so there is no cycle.
- **Frontend.** `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` in `frontend/src/config/admin.js` is built from `CANONICAL_PROVIDERS` in `frontend/src/lib/providers.js`, the frontend registry, which its own tests hold to `VALID_PROVIDERS`.
  - A small `PROVIDER_LABELS` map supplies the button text (`AWS`, `GitHub`, `VMware`).
  - It feeds the review board's picker (`BlogReviewBoard`) and the Publish-Ready Builder's provider and landing-zone dropdowns (`StageOneCard`). The Builder could already infer Docker from a URL but not show it.
  - The editor's provider filter (`EditorListPage`) had its own list, with Docker but not VMware or Ansible. It now reads the same list.
  - The public submission forms keep their own lists **on purpose**: each offers only the providers its page can file under, and `docker-submissions.test.jsx` pins that. Nothing is duplicated.
- **Tests that fail when a registered provider is missing from the board:**
  - `frontend/src/config/admin.test.js` requires the options to equal `CANONICAL_PROVIDERS`, every provider to have a label, and the Builder lists to match.
  - `BlogReviewBoard.test.jsx` renders the board and requires a button for every registered provider. It also checks that choosing Docker posts `cloudProvider: 'Docker'`, and that the queue button is disabled with no provider and enabled with Docker.
  - `docker-cms.test.js` reads `CANONICAL_PROVIDERS` and requires `normalizeProviderName` to store each one the way `admin.js` does.
- **The publish path, end to end:** `publish.test.js` publishes a Docker, a VMware and an Ansible post. It checks `curatedSubpagePath`, `publicUrl` and `Cloud Provider` for `/docker/blog/compose-basics`, `/vmware/blog/...` and `/ansible/blog/...`.
  - `publish.js` lower-cases the stored value into the path.
  - `PROVIDER_ALIASES` already matches `Docker`, `Vmware` and `Ansible`.
  - The manifest's `providerOf` lower-cases into `PROVIDERS`, which has all three, so pre-rendering places them.
- **`inferProviderFromTags`** knows every provider. Docker comes **last**: `['docker', 'compose']` gives `Docker`, but `['docker', 'azure']` gives `Azure`, the rule `docker` being last in `providers.js` states. The server's `inferProviderFromUrl` and the recording drafter's `KNOWN_CLOUD_PROVIDERS` gain Docker on the same terms, matching the client's `pageMeta.js`.
- **The public submissions API refused Docker,** and it also had its **framework and coder_corner provider lists swapped** against their pages since it was written.
  - The Frameworks form offers AWS/Azure/GCP, and the API accepted Github/Terraform.
  - The Coder Corner form offers Github/Terraform/Docker, and the API accepted AWS/Azure/GCP.

  So every submission from either form was refused. Each list in `functions/src/lib/submissions.js` is now exactly its page's list, with Docker on blog and Coder Corner. `submissions.test.js` reads the four pages to hold them together.
- `ci.yml`'s functions row also runs when `admin.js`, `lib/providers.js` or a submission page changes, since functions tests now read them.

## B. #816 part 2: the cp_sortDate healer is deleted

Part 1 (#829) applied on 2026-10-03.
- **Deleted:** `.github/workflows/heal-computed-properties.yml`, and `infra/roles/cosmos-container-writer.json`. Nothing else read the JSON.
- **`infra/oidc.tf`:** `azurerm_role_assignment.github_deploy_cosmos_container_writer` and `data.azurerm_role_definition.cosmos_container_writer` are removed, and a removal record replaces them. The deploy identity no longer holds a Cosmos control-plane write.
- **The role definition was owner-created outside Terraform** (a `data` lookup, like the SWA deployer role), so it is deleted by hand (below).
- **`scripts/apply-computed-sortdate.mjs`:** `--apply` and its ARM helpers are removed. **`--inspect` stays.** It is the one check the apply cannot make: whether the date aliases in the *data* are ISO-sortable. It is the precondition for `PUBLIC_LIST_SQL_ORDER=1` and the first diagnostic if the list mis-orders, and it now runs locally. `--apply` exits 2 with usage (new test in `entrypoint-guards.test.mjs`), and the ARM body tests went with the code.
- **`scripts/assert-expected-plan.mjs`:** `DECLARED` gains the assignment's `delete` and drops part 1's three applied entries. The shape test now requires a declared whole-resource delete to name a block `infra/*.tf` no longer declares. A new test passes the baseline plus this delete against the shipped list.
- **Docs and comments:**
  - The runbook (`deployment-runbook.md` §2 and §6).
  - Required-Inputs: `CLIENT_ID`; `COSMOS_ENDPOINT` and `COSMOS_RESOURCE_GROUP` marked "read by nothing", like `STORAGE_ACCOUNT`; §4.6b down to three roles.
  - `cosmos.tf`, `functionapp.tf`, `outputs.tf`, `variables.tf` and `oidc.tf`.
  - `public-reads.js` and `cosmos-sort-date.mjs`.
  - Three workflow comments.

  Dated records (`docs/history/`, the 2026-08 review, ADR 0025, scanner-triage, `.azure/infrastructure-plan.json`) are left as written.

**Now consumer-less, left for an owner decision (not changed, so the plan stays as stated):**
- The deploy identity's container-scoped data-plane grants `azurerm_cosmosdb_sql_role_assignment.github_deploy_cosmos_content` and `..._blogs`. Their only reader was the workflow's `--inspect`.
- Its branch federated-credential pair, `github_branch` and `github_branch_immutable`. No workflow now signs in with `CLIENT_ID` without `environment: production`.

`oidc.tf` says so at each one.

## C. #837: tostring() on the passed-through app settings

`azapi_update_resource.function_app_settings_without_webjobs_storage` now writes `key => tostring(value)` inside the `merge(...)`. Its comment no longer calls the hardening pending. **No plan effect:** the resource is already one of the baseline's three replacements, and every value is already a string. If the plan shows anything else on it, stop and find the non-string value first (#837).

## D. #834: the SWA deployment token is kept, as an accepted risk

Owner decision 2026-10-03. There is a new row under *Accepted risks* in `TODO.md`, in that table's style:
- **Risk:** the deploy still uses the deployment token.
- **Reasoning:**
  - OIDC sign-in as the federated `github_deploy` identity.
  - A just-in-time read through the custom `HCW Static Web App Deployer` role (`listSecrets` on the one site).
  - The token is used for one run. There is no stored secret, deploys are `main` only, and a productio

author: prakashsewani
body:
## What

First slice of the D1 import-efficiency work (approved plan, 2026-10-03): the audit's decisions, the architecture doc's target state, and migration `0005` — schema only, no behavior change.

- `observations.record_key` + `observations.content_hash` (nullable) with a `(user_id, record_key, created_at)` index
- `identities.normalized_name` (nullable) with a `(user_id, normalized_name)` index
- Drops `observations_user_id_idx` and `observations_normalized_name_idx` — no product query uses them, and each costs a written row per observation insert
- Backfills `record_key` for existing `external_id` rows (`<kind>:x:<externalId>`)
- `docs/decisions.md` records D-023 (batched, scan-free, statement-budgeted slices) and D-024 (one observation per distinct source state); `docs/architecture.md` moves to the target state

## Why

The audit found the free plan's D1 limits (5M rows read / 100k rows written per day) were exhausted by imports: every 5-contact slice re-scanned all identities and the import's observations so far (O(M × T/C + T²/C) per import), and each contact cost ~6–10 unbatched statements. A re-import of 493 unchanged contacts wrote ~7k rows and read ~150k. This PR prepares the schema; the batched reconcile lands next, idempotency + instrumentation after that (stacked, D-008).

## Verification

- `pnpm check` green: typecheck, Biome, 66 Workers-pool tests (applying migration `0005`), all builds.
- Note: an intermediate revision widened `identity_values_lookup_idx` to cover `identity_id`; that changed SQLite's row order for equal keys and flipped the "oldest identity" tie-break in `process-import.test.ts` (two identities in the same second). Reverted — this slice is strictly behavior-neutral, and the next slice will order candidates deterministically in memory instead of relying on SQL row order.

## Stack

This branch is the base for the next two slices (`imports/batched-reconcile`, then `imports/idempotent-imports`).

author: elevateforhumanity
body:
Add explicit Mobile view, Desktop view, and Full screen controls to the existing browser workspace. Keep every tab and popup at the selected viewport, and return actual viewport geometry so image coordinates stay accurate.

Extend signed live acceptance with actual encrypted writes/restores on the mounted provider volume and viewport switching. Native attachment and blob downloads use ephemeral synthetic HTTP responses from the existing worker instead of DevTools-fulfilled attachment responses; fixtures expire and expose no user files or account state. Both download paths must independently verify saved bytes.

Validation: focused worker regression checks pass, including viewport propagation and invalid dimensions. Studio/navigation/planner/media-resume checks and component lint run before merge. Previous live acceptance passed ten checks but cancelled the mocked attachment download; real HTTP transfer, durable volume I/O, and popup resizing must pass before readiness is claimed.

author: nightfall-wizard
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an experimental, non-consensus prototype for cut-through-compatible spend authorization for Nightfall's one-sided stealth outputs.

The design is informed by Litecoin LIP-0004, but adapted to Nightfall's existing Ristretto-based cryptography, canonical UTXO model, aggregation rules, value-kernel orientation, and persistence/reorg architecture.

## What this PR adds

- receiver spend authorization bound to canonical `Ko`, `Ki`, and the spent commitment
- additive stealth authorization balance for aggregation
- kernel-bound authorization prototype
- versioned cut-through transaction candidates
- validation against authoritative UTXO state
- builders and aggregation
- retention-horizon handling
- atomic application and reorg-safe undo state
- horizon-expired metadata pruning
- crash-safe sidecar persistence
- recovery from ambiguous post-rename persistence errors
- adversarial, aggregation, exploit, restart, persistence, and reorg tests
- `docs/RFC-CUTTHROUGH-SPEND-AUTH.md`

## Protocol boundary

This PR is deliberately experimental and does **not** activate a new consensus version.

It does not intentionally change:

- `PROTOCOL_VERSION`
- `WIRE_VERSION`
- existing v8 block serialization or hashing
- genesis
- emission or supply accounting
- existing v8 validation
- existing UTXO-root semantics

The new machinery remains isolated from the active protocol path.

## Validation

The branch passes:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- strict Clippy (`-D warnings`) for `nightfall-ledger` and `nightfall-storage`
- 121/121 ledger unit tests
- 7/7 cut-through spend-authorization research tests
- 8/8 exploit-regression tests
- full storage tests and reorg-persistence tests during development checkpoints
- `git diff --check`

The complete desktop workspace cannot be reproduced unchanged under Termux because the untouched `nightfall-core` GUI dependency path reaches `winit/android-activity`. Linux GitHub CI should therefore remain authoritative for the complete workspace.

## Security status

Passing these tests is not proof of cryptographic security.

Before any consensus activation, this design still requires:

- independent cryptographic review
- review of the Nightfall adaptation of the LIP-0004 algebra
- aggregation/cancellation and rogue-key analysis
- chain-history and persistence integration design
- active node/reorg lifecycle integration
- actual historical cut-through beyond retention/undo metadata pruning
- protocol-version and migration design
- wallet/mempool/RPC integration
- broader property and differential testing

## Review focus

Review is especially requested for:

1. canonical-UTXO binding and receiver-only spend authority;
2. stealth-balance and kernel-binding algebra;
3. aggregation/cancellation and rogue-key risks;
4. retention, rollback, pruning, and persistence semantics;
5. the isolation boundary before any future consensus activation.

This PR is intentionally opened as a draft.

author: jperner11
body:
## Problem

`ChatScreen` in `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/my-pt.tsx` fetches messages and marks them read in a `useEffect` using bare `.then()` chains with no `.catch()`. If either Supabase call rejects (transient network error), it becomes an **unhandled promise rejection**.

`MessagesScreen` in `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/clients.tsx` has the same underlying gap: `fetchMessages(id)` is called fire-and-forget inside the effect's `.then()` callback. The outer `.then(...).catch(() => Alert.alert(...))` chain only covers `getOrCreateConversation()` — it does not catch rejections from the unawaited `fetchMessages(id)` call, since that promise is never returned into the chain.

This is the same bug class already fixed elsewhere in this repo (e.g. #180, #174, #627, #279, #886) — just two instances that were missed.

## Fix

- `my-pt.tsx`: wrap both the message-fetch and mark-as-read Supabase calls in `Promise.resolve(...)` (needed because the Supabase query builder's `.then()` returns a `PromiseLike`, not a full `Promise` with `.catch`) and add `.catch()` handlers — an `Alert` for the message fetch (user-visible impact), and a silent no-op for mark-as-read (non-critical, matches the existing no-op convention used for similarly low-stakes background calls).
- `clients.tsx`: attach `.catch(() => Alert.alert(...))` directly to the `fetchMessages(id)` call, matching the `Alert.alert('Error', 'Could not load exercises')` pattern already used later in the same file for the exercise-list fetch.

## Verification

- `npm run lint` in `apps/web` — passes (no warnings/errors).
- `npm run build` in `apps/web` — passes.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `apps/mobile` — passes (confirms the `Promise.resolve` wrapper is needed and correctly typed; the raw `.then().catch()` chain on `my-pt.tsx`'s Supabase builder otherwise fails to typecheck).

No test framework is configured in the repo; verification was lint + build + typecheck as outlined above.

author: git-nostr
body:
The site ships as a container image rather than through Pages (which is disabled for this repo), but nothing was building it — the ghcr package held a single `latest` tag with no provenance, meaning published docs came from whichever machine last ran the build by hand.

This builds on every push to `main`, plus manual dispatch, and publishes `:latest` and `:<sha>`.

Notes on the choices:
- It publishes the **`caddy`** stage. That stage already carries `org.opencontainers.image.source` pointing at this repo (which is what links a ghcr package to it) and serves the built site, unlike the `dev`/`serve` stages which run a Docusaurus server.
- The Dockerfile here is lowercase `dockerfile`, so `file:` is set explicitly — buildx looks for `Dockerfile` by default and would otherwise fail.
- GHA layer caching is on, since a cold Docusaurus build is slow.

Verified by building `--target caddy` locally first; the image builds and exports cleanly.

Heads-up: once merged, pushes to `main` will move `ghcr.io/flokiorg/docs:latest`, replacing the hand-built image. That is the intent, but it does mean deployments pulling `latest` will pick up `main` automatically from now on.

author: nitinkumar004
body:
## Plan

Rows: GVPC-06, and GVPC-09's `peerings[]` half (`subnetworks[]` shipped in #1425).

- Root cause: `server/gcp/vpc/handler.go` `routeNetworks` sent every network action to the CRUD switch, so `addPeering`, `removePeering` and `updatePeering` returned 405, and `toNetworkResponse` had no `peerings[]`.
- Real GCP: `POST networks/{n}/addPeering` and `removePeering`, plus `PATCH networks/{n}/updatePeering`, each return an Operation. Each side of a peering is its own entry in its network's `peerings[]`. An entry is INACTIVE until the peer network adds the reverse entry, then both read ACTIVE. `exchangeSubnetRoutes` and `autoCreateRoutes` are always true, `exportSubnetRoutesWithPublicIp` defaults to true, and `stackType` defaults to IPV4_ONLY.
- Fix: `server/gcp/vpc/peerings.go`.
  - Peerings are stored as JSON in a tag on the network's VPC record, so snapshots cover them.
  - `addPeering` accepts either `networkPeering` or the older top-level `name`/`peerNetwork`. A duplicate name is 409, a missing peer network is 404, and a network peering with itself is 400.
  - `updatePeering` changes the route flags, `stackType` and `updateStrategy`.
  - State is computed when the network is read, from whether the peer network has the reverse entry.
  - Network get and list return `peerings[]` with absolute network links.
- Tests: `TestNetworkPeeringLifecycle` covers INACTIVE, then ACTIVE after the reverse add, the 409 and 404 cases, updatePeering, and removePeering sending the other side back to INACTIVE. It fails on development (405).

## Verification

- `go build ./...`; `go test -race` on `server/gcp/vpc` and `server/gcp/compute`; lint 0 issues.
- Binary TF e2e (OpenTofu 1.10, hashicorp/google): two custom networks.
  - Apply `google_compute_network_peering` a-to-b only: net-a `peerings[]` reads a-to-b INACTIVE.
  - Apply b-to-a: both networks read ACTIVE. Plan exits 0.
  - Update `import_custom_routes` (updatePeering): apply, then plan exits 0.
  - Destroy succeeds, and both networks then return 404.
- Docker: pending Gate 2.

author: gioabq
body:
Closes #102, #132, #152, #157

Not fixed: #68 and #101 (see below). One commit per issue, plus follow-up commits from the independent review.

## #152 HttpOutbox drops 408/429
- **Wrong:** every 4xx except 401 was treated as a permanent rejection, so a throttled or timed-out write was deleted.
- **Fix:** 408 and 429 are kept like 401/5xx: the entry is saved with the error and attempt count, and the flush stops.
- **Retry-After:** not honoured, because the outbox has no backoff concept; adding one would be a new public option.
- **Test:** `HttpOutboxTests.TransientClientError_KeepsTheEntryWithTheError_AndStopsTheFlush` (408 and 429).
- **Revert check:** both cases fail with the fix reverted.

## #157 Sentry:TracesSampleRate out of range or NaN
- **Wrong:** Sentry's own options setup binds the `Sentry` section during `Build()`, before the `UseSentry` callback. Values outside [0,1] still crashed there, NaN was applied, and `abc` crashed too.
- **Fix:** `AddFExSentry` validates the key first. An unusable value (unparsable, NaN, infinity, outside [0,1]) logs one warning and the key is overridden with null through a later in-memory configuration source, so the binder leaves the SDK default. `ConfigureOptions` keeps the same guard for direct callers.
- **Test:** `AddFExSentry_UnusableSampleRate_BuildsWithTheSdkDefault_AndWarnsOnce` goes through `AddFExSentry` + `Build()` + `IOptions<SentryAspNetCoreOptions>` for `10`, `1.5`, `-0.1`, `NaN`, `abc`. `AddFExSentry_UsableSampleRate_IsAssigned_WithoutAWarning` pins `0`, `1` and `0.25`.
- **Revert check:** reverting the fix fails all 5 unusable cases. Changing the guard to `> 0 and < 1` fails the `0` and `1` cases.

## #132 FExEncryption.Priority never assigned
- **Fix:** `Priority => -1`. `FExServiceContainer.Initialize` runs lower values first, `Splash` uses -2, unprioritised initializers are at 0. The cipher now initializes behind the splash and ahead of default-priority initializers.
- **Test:** `Priority_RunsBehindTheSplash_AndAheadOfTheDefaultPriority` asserts -2 < Priority < 0.
- **Revert check:** fails for the old 0 and for -5.

## #102 IsErrorPath uses two comparison rules
- **Wrong:** `Contains` was ordinal and `StartsWith(string)` was culture-sensitive.
- **Comparer:** `ErrorPaths` is a plain `ConcurrentHashSet<string>`, so path equality in this file is ordinal and case-sensitive. The fix matches that: one `fullPath.StartsWith(errorPath, StringComparison.Ordinal)` check covers the exact match and descendants. An earlier revision of this PR used `OrdinalIgnoreCase`; the review showed that folds case-variant siblings on case-sensitive file systems, so it is gone.
- **Scope:** the Windows case-insensitivity concern in the issue text is not addressed. Doing that would mean changing the set's comparer too, which is a separate decision.
- **Test:** `DirectoryWalkerErrorPathTests`: exact match, descendant, case-differing directory not recognised, sibling sharing a name prefix not recognised, and a soft-hyphen name that a culture-sensitive `StartsWith` would wrongly match.
- **Revert check:** with `develop`'s code the soft-hyphen test fails; with `OrdinalIgnoreCase` the case test fails.

## Left out: #101 DbSet SaveChanges extension has no concurrency retry
Dropped from this PR after the independent review. The service-layer retry it would reuse is client-wins: it overwrites the original values with the database values and turns a Modified entity whose row was deleted into an insert.
- Probe 1: another writer deletes the row, then `ValidateAndSaveChangesAsync()` modifies it. At the PR's earlier head the row was resurrected (`await check.Docs.CountAsync() should be 0 but was 1`); on `develop` it throws `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`.
- Probe 2: another writer bumps a `[ConcurrencyCheck]` version, then the stale edit saves. At the PR's earlier head it was silently overwritten (`should throw` but did not); on `develop` it throws.

So the extension keeps throwing as on `develop`, and `PooledDbService` is untouched. The maintainer is handling #101 and the `PooledDbService` policy separately.

## Left out: #68 NuGetManager downloads NuGet.CommandLine on every construction
Nothing in this repo uses NuGet.CommandLine: the only reference is the init-time restore, so there is no operation to restore it lazily for.
- Removing the restore changes what consumers get, and choosing which operation triggers it is a design call.
- `GetResourceAsync` in the same init also hits nuget.org, so "no network call on construction" needs lazy resources too.
- `FEx.NuGetx` has no test project.
- The empty-sequence `Max()`/`First()` crash in the private `RestorePackageByIdAsync` overload is real and not addressed here.

## Breaking changes
None. All signatures are source-compatible. Behaviour changes: `FExEncryption.Priority` is now -1 instead of 0, and an unusable `Sentry:TracesSampleRate` now warns and keeps the SDK default instead of crashing or being applied.

## Verification
All run on Linux, `net10.0`; the test projects were also built once without `-f` (all TFMs), 0 errors.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `dotnet test test/FEx.Offline.Tests/FEx.Offline.Tests.csproj -f net10.0` | 33 passed |
| `dotnet test test/FEx.Telemetry.Sentry.Web.Tests/FEx.Telemetry.Sentry.Web.Tests.csproj -f net10.0` | 36 passed |
| `dotnet test test/FEx.Encryption.Tests/FEx.Encryption.Tests.csproj -f net10.0` | 110 passed |
| `dotnet test test/FEx.FileSystem.Tests/FEx.FileSystem.Tests.csproj -f net10.0` | 29 total, 28 passed, 1 skipped |
| `dotnet build <each test project above>` (no `-f`) | 0 errors |
| Revert of each fix, tests re-run | the new tests failed every time, as listed per issue |

CI (Windows, all TFMs, full suite) is the full gate.

Closes #29.

I removed stale schedule routing and made the billed skill-behavior lane an explicit manual opt-in that fails when no provider scenario completes. Local missing-key skips remain unchanged, and CI now selects the relevant suites when embedded command metadata changes.

I expanded strict oracle replay to Linux, macOS, and Windows. The case-folding probe is skipped on Linux, where case-insensitive `PRODUCT.md` discovery is unavailable; it continues to run on macOS and Windows. ## What

The center relationship materializer re-upserted the `PI` edge of a faculty research area it linked, replacing the whole `rosterProvenance` subdocument, so the lane that owned the lead lost its `sourceName` on every center pass.

- `syncProfileBackedFacultyResearchAreaMemberFromIdentity` now looks for any existing `PI` role assignment on the target row, archived or not, and returns `skipped: 'lead-edge-held'` without writing when one exists.

- `skills/scrapers/SKILL.md` records the rule.

`researchEntityRelationshipSourceUrl.integration.test.ts` adds a case where a row's lead edge carries another lane's provenance and a center pass must leave it unchanged and not duplicate it, and asserts that a newly created edge carries the lane's `sourceName`.
Both fail on the pre-fix materializer.

## Data operation

Stored-data fix: the edges where `role` is `PI`, `archived` is not true, `rosterProvenance` exists and `rosterProvenance.sourceName` is empty keep their state until the owning lane re-stamps them.
Verification on Development runs after the current sweep: rematerialize the owning lane for those rows, then re-run the center relationship pass and confirm the count of such edges does not grow.

## Что это

Два дополнения к стороне eXpress (#152).

**Выключатель eXpress с телефона.** В TeleMotoMax, в настройках учётной записи, появился флажок «Сети моста → eXpress». Снятый — мост останавливает сторону eXpress (закрывает Chromium, её чаты уходят из контакт-листа); поставленный — поднимает обратно. Выбор уходит мосту парой в `01/F2` (ключ 14: 1 — включена, 2 — выключена) при входе и сразу при сохранении настроек; мост запоминает его в базе (`meta.express_on`) и после перезапуска не запускает eXpress, пока телефон не включит.

**Вход по QR-коду.** `python3 run.py login express` на вопрос о номере принимает `qr`: на снимке `express.session/login.png` показывается QR-код (обновляется каждые 30 с), который сканируется из мобильного приложения («Чаты» → профиль → «Войти на компьютере»). Без SMS, капчи и кода на корпоративную почту — корпоративный сервер подключается сам. Нужен для корпоративных аккаунтов: при входе по номеру у них есть ещё шаг с кодом на рабочую почту, и сервер может на нём отказать.

**Браузер глазами.** Новый параметр `devtools_port` в `[express]` открывает отладочный порт Chrome на localhost сервера. По туннелю ssh (`ssh -L 9222:localhost:9222 сервер`) обычный Chrome через `chrome://inspect` показывает живую картинку браузера моста с мышью и клавиатурой — капчу и QR-код при входе можно пройти прямо там, без VNC и X-сервера. Работает и у `run.py login express`, и у запущенной службы.

author: squattingmonk
body:
Closes #159.

## What changed

- **`accumulates*(self: Arg): bool`** is a new base method in `backend.nim`, defaulting to `false`. It returns `true` for `ValueArg[T, true]` (`args`/`opts`) and `FlagArg[T]`, i.e. args that build their value from more than one match (Match Accumulation in `CONTEXT.md`).
- **`autoFillUsage`** uses it as a hint. An accumulating positional argument is auto-filled as `<name>...`. A hand-written usage line still decides, so `<text>` there takes exactly one value even for an `args`.
- **More than one accumulating positional argument** in an auto-filled line raises a `SpecDefect` asking the author to write a usage line, since how the values split between them is the author's call. A hand-written `<foo>... <bar>...` is still allowed.
- **Docs:** the fill-in rule in `docs/guide/usage-strings.md` and the `autoFillUsage` section of `docs/architecture.md`.

The `[options]` catch-all doesn't consult `accumulates`. Whether it should follow a per-arg rule is #162.

A spec with two `args` positionals and no usage line used to build, taking one value each. It now fails with the `SpecDefect`. That only affects specs that were already broken, so this is `fix:` rather than breaking.

## Tests

New tests in `tests/test_argumint.nim`, written test-first and checked against mutations of the fix:

- `<file>... <dest>` is auto-filled and parses several values.
- `[options] <text>...` keeps the options prefix.
- Two accumulating positionals raise the `SpecDefect`.
- Hand-written `<foo>... <bar>...` is still allowed.
- Hand-written `<file>` still rejects a second value.
- `accumulates` returns the right value for each kind of arg.

`nimble test` and `nimble examples` pass. Ran `/code-review` (standards plus spec) before committing. Its findings are applied: the method's name, CONTEXT.md vocabulary, a comment pointer, and the `[options]` test.

author: noctua84
body:
## What

`app/core/errors.py` mapped `sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError` but not its sibling `sqlalchemy.exc.DataError`. Any request whose parameters were rejected at the data level fell through to a bare plain-text `Internal Server Error` with no JSON body, so a client could not parse `detail` from it.

Reproduced before the fix with `TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)` — a NUL byte (`"\x00"`) in `POST /api/v1/ingest`'s `repo_name` gave `500`, `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, body `Internal Server Error`. The exception was `sqlalchemy.exc.DataError` wrapping `psycopg.DataError` (*"PostgreSQL text fields cannot contain NUL (0x00) bytes"*).

This adds a `DataError` handler returning **`400`** with `{"detail": "Request contains data the database cannot accept"}` and **no** `Retry-After`.

## Why 400

**Not 503.** `OperationalError`'s `503 + Retry-After` means "try again later", which is false here — the same bytes fail on every attempt.

**Not 422.** 422 is already owned by FastAPI/Pydantic request validation, whose body is `{"detail": [ ... ]}` — a *list*. Reusing it with a string detail would make `detail`'s type depend on which failure produced it. 400 keeps `detail` a string everywhere in this file.

**No `Retry-After`**, for the same reason `EmbeddingBackendMisconfigured` omits it.

`detail` comes from a module constant, never `str(exc)` — the file's existing invariant, pinned by a test asserting psycopg's own wording never reaches the client.

## The tradeoff, stated rather than hidden

`DataError` is SQLSTATE class 22xxx, which is **not** exclusively caller-caused — numeric overflow or division by zero can come from our own SQL, in which case a 400 blames the caller for our bug. The handler documents this as an accepted tradeoff, with a warning log carrying the traceback as the mitigation.

The `exc_info` is load-bearing and was added after review. Without it the handler would be strictly *less* debuggable than the unhandled 500 it replaces: Starlette's `ServerErrorMiddleware` used to re-raise so the server could log a traceback, and SQLSTATE alone (`22000`, `22023`) identifies neither the failing value nor the code that produced it.

**Note on log content:** SQLAlchemy's exception text includes bound parameters, so the traceback can contain caller-supplied document text. This is *not* new exposure — on `main` the unhandled exception reached uvicorn, which logged the identical traceback at ERROR. It is restored here at WARNING. Flagging it so the log-sink implications are a conscious choice.

## Scope

Branched off `main`. `ingest` and `search` are the only routes the service exposes, so the two covered here are **all** of them.

This work was originally spun out of a QA audit of an egress path in #37. That PR has since been re-scoped to search-context expansion and no longer adds `/api/v1/documents*` — its `router.py` is now identical to `main`'s — so there is no second route family pending. The handler is registered app-wide by `register_exception_handlers`, not per route, so any route added later is covered without further change.

**Conflict surface with #37 as currently scoped:** it does not touch `app/core/errors.py` or `tests/test_error_responses.py`, so the files carrying this fix are conflict-free. It does change `README.md` (+105/-10), which may conflict textually with the "Current limitations" edit here. It also reshapes `app/repositories/learning.py` and `app/api/v1/search.py`; `test_a_nul_byte_in_the_search_repo_filter_is_a_400` depends on `repo_filter` reaching the WHERE clause, so if that test goes red when #37 lands it is a real signal rather than a flake.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `uv run pytest` on `main` | **94 passed**, exit 0 |
| `uv run pytest` on this branch | **103 passed**, exit 0 |
| Test functions removed / assertions removed | **0 / 0** — no existing test's expected status changed |
| OpenAPI drift (`export_openapi.py`) | none |
| `openapi-spec-validator openapi.json` | OK |
| `uv sync --locked` | lockfile not stale |

## Follow-ups found during review — deliberately not in this PR

- **A degenerate embedding is now blamed on the caller.** `_validated()` in `app/core/embeddings.py` checks type and length but not finiteness, and `isinstance(float("nan"), float)` is `True`. pgvector rejects NaN/Inf with SQLSTATE 22000, which this handler now turns into a 400 — so a broken embedding backend would fail every ingest and search while keeping 5xx alerts green. Reachable: `json.loads` parses bare `NaN`/`Infinity` literals by default. Fix is `math.isfinite` in `_validated`, which routes it back to the existing `EmbeddingBackendBadResponse` → 503.
- **`STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` has no upper bound.** `app/config.py` guards only `<= 0`; an oversized value makes `set_config` raise 22023, turning 100% of `/search` into 400s.
- **No edge validation of `repo_name` / `file_path` / `content` / `repo_filter`.** Rejecting control characters at the Pydantic layer would give a field-level message and shrink this handler to a backstop.
- **The OpenAPI spec declares only `200`/`422` per route.** The pre-existing `503`/`500` are undeclared too, so the new `400` is consistent with current practice rather than a regression — but the spec under-describes error responses generally.
- **`alembic/env.py`'s `fileConfig()`** uses the default `disable_existing_loggers=True`, so three tests now need a `logger.disabled = False` workaround.

body:
## Why

The EV **Start Session** form had an editable "Date" picker (`Oct 3, 2026`). Its value was never sent anywhere: the server stamps each session itself. It also showed no time. Staff could change a date that did nothing.

## What changed

- Replaced the date picker with a read-only **Date & Time** in **Nepal time** (`Asia/Kathmandu`), on a **12-hour clock** (`Oct 3, 2026, 5:45 AM`).
- Nepali mode shows Devanagari numerals and पूर्वाह्न / अपराह्न (`२०२६ अक्टोबर ३, ०५:४५ पूर्वाह्न`).
- It updates on each minute boundary, so the shown minute is never stale.
- New small shared component `NepalDateTime` (`components/NepalDateTime.jsx`), min 44px tall, using the existing `common.dateTime` / `common.currentDateTime` strings (no new translations needed).
- Removed the now-unused `date` state and the `useBusinessDate` call from `EVEntryPage`.

Not changed: the manual EV entry page (it already has its own Date & Time display), the backend, and how the date of a session is recorded.

## How to test

1. Open the EV page, Start Session tab: the Date field is now a grey read-only "Date & Time" showing Nepal time with AM/PM.
2. Switch the language to Nepali: Devanagari digits.
3. Watch it tick over on the minute. It follows Nepal, not the device's time zone (for example a phone set to the US still shows Nepal time).
4. Start a session as usual: it works, and no date is sent.

## Tests

- New `NepalDateTime` tests (8): AM/PM, read-only, Nepal vs UTC around midnight (23:59 on 2 Oct to 12:00 AM on 3 Oct), ticking each minute, Nepali numerals, 44px height, timer cleanup.
- `EVEntryPage` tests: replaced the old "auto-fills the date and keeps it editable" test (the behaviour being removed) with checks that no date input remains, English and Nepali. The existing start-request test already checks the payload has no `date`.
- Playwright EV flow: asserts the Date & Time field and that no `input[type=date]` exists.
- Local run: admin unit tests 463 passed (2 skipped), lint 0 errors, Playwright 17 of 17.

author: oliviermadre
body:
## Problème
Depuis le CLI Claude Code **2.1.284** (SDK ≥ 0.3.280, bump du 28/09), une session reprise renvoie dans `total_cost_usd` et `modelUsage` le **total de la session**. Fleex le stockait comme coût du run : chaque mention refacturait tout l'historique de la session.

Les CLI plus anciens renvoyaient un usage **par requête**. Leurs coûts sont justes et ne doivent pas être touchés.

Vérifié sur la prod contre les transcripts :

| CLI | Le total brut correspond au transcript | L'écart correspond au transcript |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 2.1.270 | 43/58 | 5/58 |
| 2.1.284 | 0/83 | 78/83 |

> La première version de cette PR réécrivait tout l'historique dans la migration 035, ce qui aurait faussé avril → septembre. Elle est remplacée par celle-ci.

## Règle (runtime)
`coût_du_run = total_SDK(fin du run) − total_SDK(fin du run précédent de la même session)`, appliquée **seulement si** toutes ces conditions sont réunies :
1. le run vient d'un CLI ≥ 2.1.284. La version est lue dans le message `init` du SDK et stockée sur l'exécution. Les versions 2.1.280 à 2.1.283 sont traitées comme inconnues ;
2. le point de départ est le run **immédiatement précédent** de la session qui a dépensé quelque chose, il a un total brut enregistré, et il vient lui aussi d'un CLI ≥ 2.1.284 ;
3. aucun compteur ne redescend. Sinon (`/clear`, transcript sans total sauvegardé), on prend le total brut.

Dans tous les autres cas, on stocke le total brut avec `cost_basis = 'unverified'`, plus un warning dans les logs.

L'écart ne suppose rien sur le cache : le total du SDK inclut déjà la réécriture du cache, après une longue inactivité comme après un changement de modèle. Vérifié : le run de 08:42 du #636, après 7,6 h d'inactivité, donne 2,228 $ en écart comme dans le transcript, et c'est aussi le cas pour les 2 changements de modèle dans une même session.

## Schéma : migration 035, colonnes seulement
`sdk_total_*` (valeurs brutes du SDK), `cli_version`, `cost_basis` (`per_run` | `per_run:backfill` | `unverified`, NULL pour les lignes anciennes).

La migration est idempotente : `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` en pg, try/catch en sqlite. **Aucune réécriture de données.**

> La migration 035 a été modifiée depuis le premier commit de cette PR. Elle n'a jamais été mergée ni exécutée hors des tests.

## Historique : `scripts/fix-sdk-session-costs.ts`
- **Par défaut : dry-run.** Le script n'écrit rien et sort un rapport par ligne.
- **Ordre des preuves pour chaque ligne :**
  1. **Transcript** (y compris les transcripts des subagents). On garde l'hypothèse, total brut ou écart, qui correspond à la dépense calculée sur la fenêtre du run. Si aucune ne correspond, la ligne est ignorée.
  2. **Version du CLI** (colonne, ou fichier d'événements local).
  3. **Rien de connu** : la ligne est ignorée.
- **Idempotent** : seules les lignes avec `cost_basis` NULL ou `unverified` sont traitées. Les lignes écrites passent en `per_run:backfill` et gardent leurs valeurs brutes dans `sdk_total_*`.
- **`--revert`** restaure les valeurs brutes.
- **`--verify`** contrôle l'invariant de chaîne (pour chaque run, `cost = brut − brut précédent`) et le taux de correspondance avec les transcripts, par version de CLI et pour les changements de modèle.
- **Machines** : les transcripts et les journaux d'événements sont locaux. Il faut lancer le script sur les deux machines.

**Dry-run sur la prod (machine principale, avant migration) :**

| Décision | Lignes |
|---|---|
| Confirmées par le transcript | 309 |
| Confirmées par la version | 681 |
| **Réécrites, prouvées par le transcript** | **85** (83 en 2.1.284, 2 en 2.1.280) |
| Ignorées, le transcript ne correspond ni au brut ni à l'écart | 45 (dont 4 en 2.1.284) |
| Ignorées, rien de connu | 419 (toutes avant le 28/09, sauf une à 0 $) |

Aucune réécriture n'est datée d'avant le 28/09, hors les 2.1.280 prouvées par leur transcript. Le coût des lignes traitées passe de 6 247 $ à 4 595 $.

**Baseline `--verify`** : en 2.1.284, le coût stocké correspond au transcript dans 0 cas sur 87.

## Tests
- `sdk-run-usage.test.ts` : régime par version ; règle runtime (ancien régime, régime inconnu, point de départ d'un autre régime, ligne ancienne sans total brut, session neuve) ; classification de l'historique. Ce dernier test couvre notamment le piège de la v1 : une session ancienne dont les coûts montent ne doit **jamais** être réécrite. Il couvre aussi : priorité du transcript, régimes mélangés, idempotence.
- `execute-agent-workflow-cost.test.ts` : écart avec un point de départ du même régime ; total brut marqué `unverified` quand le point de départ vient d'un autre régime.
- `sdk-session-totals.bun.test.ts` (sqlite réel) : point de départ = run immédiatement précédent ayant dépensé ; persistance de `cli_version` et `cost_basis` ; migration idempotente qui ne réécrit rien.
- `transcript-cost.test.ts` : dédoublonnage des messages ; refus de calculer un coût en présence d'un modèle inconnu.
- `bun run lint` OK · `vitest run` 3298/3298 · `test:bun` 319/319.

## Limites connues
- **Contrôle croisé sur les tokens du flux : abandonné.** Les messages assistant du flux ne portent qu'un `output_tokens` partiel (301 tokens dans le flux, pour plusieurs milliers facturés). Le garde-fou au moment du run repose donc sur la version du CLI. La vérification a posteriori se fait avec `--verify`, contre les transcripts.
- **Tarifs dupliqués** : `scripts/lib/transcript-cost.ts` duplique la table de prix de `backfill-agentic-costs.ts`, qui ne peut pas être importé car il s'exécute à l'import. À regrouper.
- **`backfill-agentic-costs.ts`** ne dédoublonne pas les lignes de transcript (plusieurs lignes par message). C'est un risque de double comptage. Non modifié ici.
- **Base testée** : les requêtes pg/supabase n'ont été vérifiées qu'en lecture (dry-run et verify sur la prod). Les écritures ne sont testées que sur sqlite.

author: max-miller1204
body:
## Summary

This PR makes pi-teach a plugin for Claude Code and Codex. Pi works as before. All three hosts use the same classrooms on disk and the same web UI.

- **MCP server `classroom`** (`src/mcp.ts`, `mcp/launch.mjs`). It serves the four shared tools and four session tools: `begin_teaching`, `open_classroom`, `list_classrooms`, and `wait_for_learner`.
- **Delivery through `wait_for_learner`.** An MCP server cannot wake its client. The agent calls `wait_for_learner` after it gives a lesson. The call returns when the learner asks a question or submits a quiz. Prompts that arrive while nobody listens stay in a queue. A cancelled wait (Esc) takes nothing from the queue.
- **Skills** `teach` and `classroom`, with manifests and marketplaces for both hosts.
- **One set of tool definitions.** The tools use plain JSON Schema. Pi's validator compiles it as-is, so the `typebox` peer dependency is gone. The lockfile root was edited by hand, as CLAUDE.md requires.
- **No build step.** Claude Code and Codex run the TypeScript with Node type stripping (Node 22.18 or later). Relative imports now end in `.ts`. `tsconfig.json` enables `erasableSyntaxOnly` and `verbatimModuleSyntax`. On its first start, the launcher runs `npm ci --omit=dev` to install `marked`.
- **No always-on cost.** The MCP server sends no `instructions`, so sessions that never teach pay nothing (rule 3).

## Install

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add max-miller1204/pi-teach && claude plugin install pi-teach@pi-teach
codex plugin marketplace add max-miller1204/pi-teach && codex plugin add pi-teach@pi-teach
```

## End-to-end test

`scripts/e2e.ts` drives a real session through a full lesson round trip:

1. Seed a lesson in a temporary classrooms directory.
2. Tell the agent to open the classroom and listen.
3. Read the server URL from the harness's JSON event stream.
4. Post a question, as the browser does. Wait for the answer on the card.
5. Submit a quiz. Wait for the grade.
6. Check that the agent called every required tool.

It calls a real model, so it is not part of CI. Run it with `npm run e2e:claude` and `npm run e2e:codex`.

### Claude Code (`npm run e2e:claude`)

```text
[e2e:claude] starting claude --plugin-dir /Users/maxmiller/.t3/worktrees/pi-teach/t3code-2a1f8a40 ...
[e2e:claude] classroom server: http://127.0.0.1:64473
[e2e:claude] asked question cd23c11a-7d33-48ca-a01d-377813595f54
[e2e:claude] answer on the card: "Since the value is dropped when its owner goes out of scope, having exactly one owner means there's exactly one clear moment when it gets dropped. If two owners could both drop the same value, it would be freed twice (a \"double free\"), so with a single owner Rust can clean up memory safely without needing a garbage collector."
[e2e:claude] submitted quiz e66f3f25-9fd1-45c4-aedf-043e4799b2ab
[e2e:claude] grade: 100%, "Full marks: you've got the core rule that a value's lifetime is tied to its owner's scope. Next, look at what happens when ownership *moves* from one variable to another."
[e2e:claude] tool calls: open_classroom → wait_for_learner → answer_lesson_question → wait_for_learner → grade_lesson_quiz
[e2e:claude] PASS: question answered and quiz graded through claude
```

### Codex (`npm run e2e:codex`)

```text
[e2e:codex] starting codex exec --json ...
[e2e:codex] classroom server: http://127.0.0.1:64621
[e2e:codex] asked question 85257014-f7a3-467b-9d6c-7cb295019407
[e2e:codex] answer on the card: "Having one owner gives Rust a clear rule for when to drop a value: it is dropped when its owner goes out of scope. This prevents two owners from trying to free the same value, while other code can still borrow it without becoming its owner."
[e2e:codex] submitted quiz 885eb0a3-0b6e-46cd-be1d-003c61620e4e
[e2e:codex] grade: 100%, "You correctly identified when Rust drops a value. You earned 100% on this quiz."
[e2e:codex] tool calls: open_classroom → wait_for_learner → answer_lesson_question → wait_for_learner → grade_lesson_quiz
[e2e:codex] PASS: question answered and quiz graded through codex
```

## Other checks

- `npm run check`: clean. Before this PR it failed on `main`, because `typebox` was not installed at the top level.
- `npm test`: 159 tests pass. New: `test/mcp.test.ts` drives the JSON-RPC dispatcher against the real HTTP server, and `test/plugin.test.ts` checks the manifests.
- `npm run format:check`: clean.
- `claude plugin validate .`: passes. It warns that the Claude manifest has no `version`. That is deliberate: Claude Code then follows commits, which matches "main is what you get".
- Pi: `pi -ne -e .` loads the extension, and a tool call with an optional parameter validates.

## Notes for review

- Codex passes no environment variables to MCP servers unless they are listed. `.codex-plugin/mcp.json` lists `PI_CLASSROOMS_DIR` and `PI_CLASSROOM_AUTO_OPEN`.
- Keep `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` `version` equal to `package.json`. Codex caches plugins by version. A test checks this.
- Browser text that said "Pi session" now names no host.

author: duongnq2798
body:
Found while testing reminders (#165) in testnet-2. No migration.

## 1. A payable to a client waits for a person

**What happened.** The invoice form's Direction started at Payable whatever the counterparty. A receivable for the client "Ho Client" went in as a payable (#1075), and the agent decided to pay the client (#1079). Only the day's spending limit stopped it, and it would have been paid once the limit had room again.

- **Guardrail.** New rule `counterparty.client_payable`: a payable whose counterparty's role is `client` is held, pay or schedule. It sits after the duplicate check and the screening verdicts, and before the address and the limit. A person can still approve it (a refund).
- **What the card says.** "*Name* is a client: it pays you. If this is a refund, pay it in Approvals; if it is money *name* owes you, reject it and add it as a receivable."
- **The form.** Choosing a client sets Direction to Receivable; anyone else, Payable. The line under Direction says what it means, and warns about a payable to a client.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-client-payables-design.md`.

## 2. Code bounds the treasury's moves

**What happened.** #1063: DeepSeek redeemed 58.1 USDC, nearly the whole USYC reserve, to cover 0.10 USDC due in two days. The written policy redeemed 0.114999. Code moved whatever amount the model chose, and the entry said `agreedWithReference: true`, because only the action was compared.

- **Sweep:** at most the cash above the 7-day buffer.
- **Redeem:** at most what falls due within 14 days needs (with the 15% cushion), and at least the written policy's amount.
- **The model is told the bounds** in its prompt (`sweepAtMostUsdc`, `redeemAtMostUsdc`, `redeemAtLeastUsdc`).
- **The entry records what changed.** `decision` is the move that happened. `boundedByCode` keeps the model's choice and the reason, and the reasoning ends with "[Code limited this: …]".
- **`agreedWithReference` now weighs the amount** (within 5%, or 0.01 USDC). The research script judges every treasury entry the same way. All published windows held only holds, so the note's figures don't change.

On #1063's figures the model's 58.1 would now redeem 0.114999. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-03-treasury-bounds-design.md`.

## 3. Reminder toast

After the reminders test, the toast said "a link sent before no longer works" even when the receivable had no link. `ar_reminders_on` now records `replacedLink`, and the toast mentions an old link only when one was replaced.

## Docs

- Collections spec: the rollout record of the testnet-2 test (#1082–#1089, tx `0xd973…3ab8`).
- First-payment guide: Direction, and a client payable as a stop. The invoice form screenshot is re-shot.
- Go-live guide: bounded moves.
- Research note: method updated.
- Changelog and README.
- **Privacy page**, which had fallen behind #165: it now names the reminder emails to clients, the billing email, and what a reminder decision sends the model. Last-updated date bumped.

## Tests

`npm run verify`: 357 files, 6406 tests, typecheck and lint clean. Covered:
- the client rule's order and outcome, through the AP stage, with nothing sent;
- the form note;
- the bounds on #1063's real figures;
- amount-aware agreement;
- the research count;
- the stage's wiring;
- the toast copy;
- the privacy field list.

author: johnxu22786
body:
## What this PR does

### Before this PR:
The encoded stream is forwarded through an unbounded WebSocket channel. A slow sender can retain an increasing backlog of stale frames. The sender task is detached, so failure is not promptly propagated to the viewer relay.

### After this PR:
- Bound the relay's shared ordered send FIFO to 16 MiB retained payload capacity and 512 queued messages, including in-flight payloads in the byte budget.
- Apply a 2-second absolute relay enqueue-to-Actix-handoff deadline, including time spent waiting behind other packets. All multiplexed packets use the same limits because non-video packets can otherwise retain memory and block queued video.
- Supervise the sender and close the viewer stream on backlog/deadline/sink failure rather than dropping dependent frames or sending increasingly stale video.
- Bound graceful viewer-disconnect cleanup without quitting the running host application.
- Add deterministic paused-clock tests, including a non-video send preceding video near its original deadline.

This is a **Draft** for upstream discussion. Limits are deliberately conservative constants, not throughput claims or a guarantee of smooth playback on a stalled link. Closing the affected viewer is the explicit overload behavior. No authentication, incoming input controls, browser UI, host encoder settings, or deployment configuration changes are included.

### Type of change
Video transport backpressure and resource-lifecycle fix.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked -j1`: 91 passed, including 12 queue regressions.
- A separate release build was not run. Clippy was stopped during dependency checking to avoid excessive host load; no Clippy result is claimed.
- No real-device WAN frame-rate or latency improvement is claimed by these tests.

## Known limitation / follow-up
The byte and age budgets cover the relay queue and its in-flight handoff, **not** Actix, kernel/TLS buffering, network delivery, or browser playback. Actix can retain accepted frames beyond this deadline. A stalled-Actix integration test and an end-to-end transport-age policy remain follow-up work before marking ready; the 12 queue tests do not establish an end-to-end latency cap.

## Summary
Second route behind the same `PipelinePorts.generate` port: `createMessagesApiGenerate` on `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 0.131.0 (exact pin), so the owner can pick either route at the sitting. **Stacked on #258** (base `agent/dossier-provider`); retarget to main after #258 merges. Grants no read, egress or write.

The body equals the generator bytes plus profile-set limits and nothing else: `model`, `max_tokens`, `system` (string), one `messages` user entry (the stage input string), `output_config.effort`, `stream: true`. No tools, metadata, thinking or context field, no subprocess, no probe request. `acceptMessagesApiRequest` compares each field by value and rejects any extra body field or unlisted header name. Profile-set: model, effort, `maxOutputTokens` (permit allowances can only lower `max_tokens`). Retry only on 429/529 inside a run budget, SDK retry off, per-try `attempts()` receipts, token usage `agent-sdk-tokens-v1`-style sum, abort via signal (connection closes). `PROVIDER-EGRESS-BYTES.md` gets a section for this route.

body:
## Bug
In the fullcheck of 03/10, 110 records of the German national selection (`IPhO_MC_Aufgaben*` and similar; country `Germania`, comp_code `IPhO`) came out of `quesiti.json` with `flag_name: "International"` and no flag. The atlas report counted 113.

The cause is `nationInfo()`. Its `pathIntl = /\/ipho\/|\/eupho\//` test matched the pdf path `gare di altri paesi/Germania/IPhO/...` and overrode the mapped country.

## Fix
- `COUNTRY` and `nationInfo()` move to `scripts/nation.mjs`, exported so they can be unit-tested.
- The vault note's `country` is the source of truth, because the vault facets already set `International` on every real IPhO/EuPhO paper. A mapped country now always passes through.
- comp_code IPhO/EuPhO and the `ipho/`/`eupho/` pdf path now only decide the flag when the country is missing or unmapped. In that case the behaviour is the same as before.

author: eamonmason
body:
## Summary

Addresses three Dependabot security alerts for `brace-expansion` in the npm dependency tree, and brings `aws-cdk-lib` and `aws-cdk` to their latest releases.

### Security fixes

| Advisory | Severity | Description | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| [GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p) | High | DoS via uncontrolled recursion in `parseCommaParts` (stack exhaustion) | Override raised to `>=5.0.12` |
| [GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7) | High | DoS via uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups (stack exhaustion) | Override raised to `>=5.0.12` |
| [GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr) | Moderate | Quadratic-time expansion of `{a},b}` rewrite (CPU DoS) | Override raised to `>=5.0.12` |

The existing `overrides.brace-expansion` entry in `package.json` was raised from `>=5.0.9` to `>=5.0.12`; the lock file now resolves the top-level `brace-expansion` to `5.0.12`.

### Known limitation — bundled copy inside aws-cdk-lib

`aws-cdk-lib@2.272.0` ships with an internal copy of `brace-expansion@5.0.9` marked `inBundle: true`. npm overrides cannot patch bundled dependencies. The CDK team will need to publish a new `aws-cdk-lib` release that bundles `brace-expansion>=5.0.12` before that copy can be updated. `npm audit` will continue to report one high-severity finding scoped to `node_modules/aws-cdk-lib/node_modules/brace-expansion` until that upstream release lands.

### Dependency bumps

- `aws-cdk-lib`: `^2.270.0` → `^2.272.0` (latest)
- `aws-cdk` CLI: `^2.1143.0` → `^2.1144.0` (latest)

author: isentropik
body:
The int8 main-dial model produces distant tied maxima in two saved-image tone probes, moving the highest dial from approximately 0.25 to 6.04. Cross-dial checks withhold those totals. Dev20 selects the existing, unretrained floating-point main model and preserves the secondary int8 model, frozen native features, alignment, separate pivots and circular decoder. It avoids the large jumps in the tested probes.

Validation: 430 Windows checks pass out of 433 run (three explicit Linux-only skips), including private protected full-frame replay. The candidate retains 3/3 blind user labels and 11/12 historic positions from five photos; the existing borderline miss remains visible. Twenty-eight derived probes show cache/kernel parity and safe rejection of eight obscured needle/marker cases. Six synthetic ledger tests and an actual-reader persisted upgrade/restart rehearsal pass. Linux amd64 CI passes 427/433 backend/package checks, with six explicit private-fixture skips, and all 157 UI checks. Required Linux filesystem/process and packaged startup/restart checks run without skips; private protected image replay passes separately on Windows.

The reader identity changes. Old images, inference, reviews and ledger segments remain immutable; current readings are withheld until the number format is explicitly rebound. Rebinding preserves unit/scales and creates a separate consumption segment rather than inheriting an old anchor. Documentation explains this step. No automatic migration of user reviews or silent total correction is added.

Derived probes are not independent accuracy observations. Local saved-frame timing increases from 15.52 to 17.40 ms median on Windows; this excludes camera transfer, persistence and HA publication. Broader real-image accuracy and sustained cadence remain unverified. This draft neither updates HA nor changes the camera, and capture/MQTT/archiving remain off. No images, private labels or credentials are published.

author: lightsabit
body:
Fixes #4

With `enableServiceLinks` on (the default), Kubernetes injects
Docker-link variables for every Service in the pod's namespace. A
Service named `cleanrr` puts them inside the `CLEANRR_` config prefix,
where strict extraction fails and the pod exits at startup.

Filters those keys out of the `Env` provider in `load_from`, after the
`CLEANRR_` prefix is stripped: `PORT`, `SERVICE_HOST`, `SERVICE_PORT`
and anything starting with `PORT_` / `SERVICE_PORT_`. No config key has
any of those shapes, and unknown `CLEANRR_*` keys still fail extraction
(second new test).

The new tests run under `Jail` via figment's `test` feature
(dev-dependency only); the lockfile grows just the
`tempfile`/`parking_lot` test-only tree.

Testing: `cargo test --locked --all-targets` (27 passed; the
service-link test fails on unmodified main), `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The
published v0.1.7 image with the eight injected variables exits 1; a
build of this branch starts normally.

body:
# Relates to

Operator-authorized bug hunt on `elizaOS/eliza` `develop` (`502e068eb2b31cf0bf963b90802b5ad05ed3dec0`). No existing issue. Knowledge document upload stores uppercase markdown with an empty MIME type as base64 instead of the file text.

# Change

`shouldReadDocumentFileAsText` now compares markdown extensions case-insensitively, matching `isSupportedDocumentFile`. `README.MD` and `Notes.Mdx` with an empty MIME type take the UTF-8 text path used by `KnowledgeDocumentsView` instead of being base64-encoded.

The upload route already treated `.md`/`.mdx` as text-backed regardless of case for byte decoding. It still compared `filename.endsWith(".mdx")` when rewriting a fallback MIME to `text/markdown`, so `Notes.Mdx` with `application/octet-stream` stayed an octet-stream document. That rewrite is now case-insensitive, matching `hasTextBackedFilename`.

# Testing

On `502e068eb2b31cf0bf963b90802b5ad05ed3dec0` (exact `origin/develop`):

Dropped `README.MD` with empty MIME and body `# owner notes` through `KnowledgeDocumentsView`. The bulk-upload payload content was `IyBvd25lciBub3Rlcw==` (base64 of that markdown).

```text
cd plugins/plugin-knowledge
bun run test src/components/documents/documents-upload.helpers.test.ts \
  src/components/documents/knowledge-documents-upload.dnd.test.tsx
```

- Unfixed source: **2 failed / 15 passed** (`README.MD` predicate false; drop payload `IyBvd25lciBub3Rlcw==`)
- After the client fix: **17 passed**
- Revert only `documents-upload.helpers.ts`: **2 failed / 15 passed** again
- `bun run test src/components/documents`: **63 passed** (10 files)
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check` on the three touched files: pass
- `bun run typecheck` in `plugins/plugin-knowledge`: pass

Leftover on the same PR after rebase onto `origin/develop` `88fa1bc65b`. `Notes.Mdx` with `application/octet-stream` was stored as `contentType: application/octet-stream` because the upload route used `filename.endsWith(".mdx")`.

```text
bun --bun ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config plugins/plugin-knowledge/vitest.config.ts \
  plugins/plugin-knowledge/test/routes.test.ts \
  plugins/plugin-knowledge/src/components/documents/documents-upload.helpers.test.ts
```

- Unfixed route: **2 failed** (`Notes.Mdx` single and bulk stored as `application/octet-stream`)
- After `filename.toLowerCase().endsWith(".mdx")`: fallback-MIME matrix **4 passed**; those two files **62 passed**
- Revert only the production line: **2 failed** again
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check` on `routes.ts` and `routes.test.ts`: pass (pre-existing `import type` warning on `routes.ts` left unchanged)

- [x] Targets `develop` and has no conflicts with the latest `origin/develop`.
- [ ] Ran `bun install` and `bun run verify` after syncing; record blockers below.
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation.

`bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` was already present in this checkout. Full `bun run verify` was not rerun for this knowledge upload encoding change.

# Evidence Gate

Evidence must match the reviewed commit. `packages/scripts/pr-evidence.ts rows`
sets the marker from the live PR head; rerun after each push.
<!-- evidence-head:ef309395f47e99fcec2ea1d248ef2cf9503b7806 -->

Keep every row. Attach artifacts inline or write `N/A - <reason>` where
inapplicable. UI changes require desktop/mobile before-and-after screenshots,
a walkthrough, logs, and OCR review. Use MP4 videos and preferably JPG images.
Keep generated artifacts out of source control.

- [ ] N/A - no live Knowledge UI session; drop path proved by KnowledgeDocumentsView root-drop harness
<!-- evidence-row:after-screenshots -->
- [ ] N/A - no live Knowledge UI session; same proof as before-screenshots
<!-- evidence-row:walkthrough-video -->
- [ ] N/A - no live documents UI session in this environment

<!-- evidence-row:ocr-review -->

# Evidence Details

Reproduction on `develop` `502e068eb2b31cf0bf963b90802b5ad05ed3dec0`:

`new File(["# owner notes"], "README.MD")` has an empty MIME type. `isSupportedDocumentFile` accepts it because it lowercases. `shouldReadDocumentFileAsText` compared `file.name.endsWith(".md")`, so `KnowledgeDocumentsView` read the file as an ArrayBuffer and sent `content: "IyBvd25lciBub3Rlcw=="`. The documents upload route treats `.MD` as text-backed and persists that base64 string as the searchable body.

After the client change the same drop sends `content: "# owner notes"`. Lowercase `notes.md` with empty MIME and `notes.txt` with `text/plain` stay on the UTF-8 path. Images remain binary.

The leftover: bulk/single upload of `Notes.Mdx` with fallback MIME `application/octet-stream` still skipped the `.mdx` → `text/markdown` rewrite, so `addDocument` stored `contentType: application/octet-stream`. Lowercase `note.mdx` already became `text/markdown`. The rewrite now lowercases the filename.

Duplication: no open PR touches `plugins/plugin-knowledge/src/components/documents/documents-upload.helpers.ts`. Distinct from calendar span #33151 and the UTC-day / malformed-JSON series.

author: wertikooo-web
body:
## Evidence
The admin diagnostic ring from [PR #129](https://github.com/wertikooo-web/wine-ai/pull/129) captured the founder's 3-minute Russian Free Conversation (`session_ff9f4326f4f065ab`):
- two Gemini connections, both with `sessionLanguage: null` and `languageCode: null`;
- **zero** language detection events.

`GEMINI_SPEECH_LANGUAGE_CODE=ru-RU` is set in Railway, but it never applied.

## Root cause
`noteUserLanguage()` and `rememberTurn('user')` ran only when the input turn had ended (`generation.inputEndedAt`). In Free Conversation the server keeps one input turn open between utterances, so `inputEndedAt` is never set. As a result:
- the conversation language was never detected, so neither the speech anchor nor the RU↔RO switch rotation ever happened;
- the guest's lines never reached the recent-turns context used when a connection is reopened.

## Fix (`src/realtime/realtimeServer.js`)
- **Utterance bookkeeping.** In Free Conversation the utterance is noted once, when the model starts answering (`transcript.model`) or calls a tool. The full user transcript goes to `rememberTurn` and to language detection. The PTT path is unchanged and marks the same flag.
- **Initial anchor.** When the first detected language has an anchor and the current Gemini connection was opened without one, the connection is reopened with the anchor before the next utterance. This uses the existing language-switch path (`pendingLanguageSwitch` → `rotateProviderSession`). Logged and recorded in the diag ring.
- Read `docs/architecture/STATE_OWNERSHIP.md`. Language and recent turns stay owned by the realtime session. No change to VAD, barge-in, the microphone/audio pipeline or provider audio handling.

## Verification

Listings were pinned in the wrong neighbourhood: the geocoder took Google's first result, and its fallback dropped the area entirely, so "Kifisias 88" (Marousi) landed in Ampelokipoi, "Socrates 17" (Zografou) near Omonia, "Dimokratias 15" (Peristeri) on the Aigaleo side. L'enum `PersonalRecordType` garde quatre cas hérités (`'1RM'`, `'strength'`, `'cardio'`, `'volume'`) que plus aucun code n'écrit. Les retirer alors qu'une ligne les porte ferait lever une `ValueError` à chaque relecture par le modèle : tableau de bord du compte en 500, reconstruction des records en échec. author: theyashasvipandey
body:
## What

`STALE_FILE` now counts only the commits that touched what a scaffold file describes, instead of every commit in the repository.

- **Scoped commit signal.** It counts commits made since the file last changed that touched one of its referenced paths: the file's path claims and the files of its grounded code. A grounded file comes from the committed `file`, or else the node's file in the graph, plus inline `mex://` anchors. The count is a single `git rev-list --count --stdin` with the pathspecs on stdin, so a long list never hits the Windows command-line limit.
- **No references, no commit signal.** A file that references no paths is judged only by its age and `last_updated`.
- **Excluded paths.** Some references would count unrelated commits again, so they are left out:
  - other scaffold files (`ROUTER.md`, `context/*.md`, anything under `.mex/`), since another document changing is not a change to the code this one describes
  - URLs
  - `.`, `..`, absolute paths, and pathspec magic
- **Bare filenames.** A bare filename such as `tsconfig.json` is matched at any depth, mirroring the path checker's recursive lookup.
- **Template-owned files.** `SETUP.md`, `SYNC.md`, `patterns/README.md` and `patterns/INDEX.md` are not checked for staleness. mex ships them, and `INDEX.md` is kept current by `mex pattern add` and the index-sync check.

Thresholds, severities, the single combined issue per file, and the `last_updated` signal are unchanged. Callers of `checkStaleness` that pass no `referencedPaths` keep the old whole-repository count.

## Why

Closes #237. On an active repository, the whole-repository commit count crossed the threshold for nearly every scaffold file. Those warnings outnumbered real findings and drove the score to 0, without saying whether anything a file describes had changed.

Measured with `mex check` on mex's own scaffold:

| | Issues | `STALE_FILE` | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 29 | 16 | 0 |
| After | 14 | 1 | 2 |

The files that reported 50–289 repository commits now count 0–6 commits to the paths they reference. The one remaining finding is a `last_updated` that is 30 days old.

This PR takes the issue's first and third directions. The second, making `STALE_FILE` informational and unscored, is left for a separate decision, since scoping removes most of the noise.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] CI/Tooling

## How to test

1. `npx vitest run test/staleness-scoped.test.ts`. The 12 tests run against real temporary git repositories and cover:
   - commits to unreferenced code are ignored
   - commits to a referenced path and to a grounded file's committed `file` are counted
   - a file with no references is judged by age only
   - template-owned files are skipped
   - an old `last_updated` still reports
   - the pathspec helper handles directories, `*/name`, never-existing paths and untracked files
   - path derivation drops scaffold, URL and whole-repo pathspecs
2. Run `mex check` on mex itself, or any active repository, and compare its `STALE_FILE` findings with `main`.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tests pass (`npm test`). The full suite was not run locally. Typecheck passes, and the staleness, checker, public-API and grounding-drift suites pass (177 passed, 1 skipped), plus the 12 new tests.
- [x] No breaking changes (or documented below)
- [x] Tested locally with a real project

## Code-graph changes

Not a code-graph change.

author: camonz
body:
Adds `vtb::tasks::delete` and `vtb::artifacts::delete` to Rhai execute scripts (ticket 9a202bdc).

## Behavior
- `vtb::tasks::delete(id, opts)` takes only `cascade: Bool` (default false) and always passes it to Sacrum, whose own default is to cascade. Without cascade, the children are detached, as Sacrum already does.
- Deleting a task also deletes its TaskRuns and step executions. So the call refuses with `invalid` when the target is the executing task, has an active TaskRun (`run_controls.active_run`), or, with cascade, has either below it. The check is read-then-act and can race with a run that starts in between. If the blocking task below the target is in another project, the error doesn't name it.
- `vtb::artifacts::delete(subject, name)` looks the artifact up on that subject by name, then deletes it by ID.
- A missing target, or one in another project, raises `not_found`. The documented samples catch only that kind, so reruns converge.
- Deleting a task leaves its artifacts behind. The docs say to delete them first.

## Docs
- New `docs/agent-context/workflows/steps/execute/host-deletes.md` with a sample that deletes scratch children and their artifacts.
- Links from `host-writes.md`, `host-artifact-writes.md` and `index.md`; updated `artifacts.md`, `vtb-guide/steps.md` and `testing.md`.

## Tests
- Unit tests in `task_writes.rs` and `artifact_writes.rs`: cascade vs non-cascade, reruns, every refusal, bad arguments, other-project/missing targets, transport errors.
- `execute_deletes.feature` (daemon acceptance), including:
  - a second task whose run a sleeping mock provider holds open;
  - the documented sample run twice;
  - an artifact still readable by ID after its task is deleted.
- Docker `@execute` daemon acceptance: 192/192 scenarios passed. That run used the sample from `host-writes.md`; the commit moves it unchanged into `host-deletes.md`.
