author: analisaperlengkapan
body:
## What broke

After #626, main's **WebKit** e2e failed almost every test, about 9 s each (for example "element not found" on `academic-integrated`). Before #626 the same job passed 515/515 in 19.7 minutes.

The cause is the new CSP. Every production build sent `upgrade-insecure-requests`, and WebKit, unlike Chromium and Firefox, applies that directive to `http://localhost` as well ([WebKit bug 171934](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=171934), [250776](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=250776)). CI serves the production build over plain http, so the page fetched its own `/_next` chunks from `https://localhost` and never hydrated. The real site is https throughout and was never affected.

A second consequence: with three attempts per failing test, the informational WebKit job ran past its 45-minute `timeout-minutes`. A timed-out job ends the whole E2E run as **cancelled**, a cancelled run does not trigger *Deploy staging*, and so #626 never reached staging.

## Fix

- **CSP:** `upgrade-insecure-requests` is removed. Every host the app loads from is https and HSTS covers navigation, so on the real site the directive rewrote nothing. It is dropped rather than made conditional, because the build does not know its own scheme: staging and production build with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` empty.
- **`apiOrigin()`:** an empty `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` now means the API is the portal's own origin, which `'self'` already covers. Before, it fell through to the localhost default, so the deployed policy named `http://localhost:3001` in `connect-src` and `media-src`.
- **Pipeline:** the Firefox/WebKit job now runs with `--max-failures=30`. A broken engine ends early as a red, reported job instead of cancelling the run and holding back the deploy.

## Tests

- `security-headers.test.ts`: no `upgrade-insecure-requests`; with the API on the portal's own origin, the policy names no localhost and `connect-src` / `media-src` are `'self'` (+ Turnstile / `blob:`). 17/17 pass.
- Web tsc and ESLint clean; Prettier clean.
- **WebKit itself:** the E2E workflow was dispatched on this branch ([run 37118069539](https://github.com/ypcipansor/cipansor/actions/runs/37118069539)), which runs Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

  | | main after #626 | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | WebKit | nearly every test failed; job hit its 45-min timeout, run **cancelled** | **528 passed**, 2 failed, 7 flaky (21.4 min) |
  | Firefox | 525 passed, 2 failed | 534 passed, 1 failed |
  | Chromium | passed | passed |

  The failures that remain:
  - `e-simaan-recorder` on Firefox and WebKit is fixed by #649.
  - `page-state-helper`'s first case on WebKit asserts that `page.content()` throws in the middle of a redirect. On WebKit the redirect now finishes before the first read, so the race it pins never occurs there. It is a test of the test helper, not of the app.
- Lessons: `.claude/memory/lessons/webkit-seen-only-after-merge.md`. Firefox/WebKit run only on `main`, and an informational job that times out cancels the run and holds back staging.

author: jan-kubica
body:
Background runs that act for a member (document translation, bilingual, report export, document review) read their inputs through a scope that applies the requester's current membership when the run executes, and write their own rows through a separate scope pinned to the run's workspace. Content readers refuse a pinned scope at compile time, and construction of pinned scopes is confined to the modules that write run rows. A run whose requester no longer has access ends as failed without reading the source.

Tests cover each queue with access intact, matter access removed, and organization membership removed.

author: cedricziel
body:
## Problem
If Hermes blocks a cron job before it starts (`last_status: blocked_config`, for example because an attached skill is missing its credentials), no run session is created. The detail pane then showed "Failed … [blocked_config:silent] …" in the status card and "No runs yet" under Run history, which contradict each other.

## Approach
`CronJob` now strips Hermes' `[blocked_config]` / `[blocked_config:silent]` tag from `last_error` when it parses the job, and exposes `isBlocked`. The run history's empty state is a new plain-model widget, `RunHistoryEmpty`, with a Widgetbook use case. For a blocked job it says Hermes blocked the task before it could start, that Hermes retries at the next scheduled time, and why. Every other job still says "No runs yet". The scheduled-tasks spec gains a scenario for this case.

## Tests
- `flutter test --concurrency=2 test/schedule_models_test.dart test/schedules_screen_test.dart test/widgetbook_test.dart test/workflows/schedules_workflow_test.dart`: 1308 passed. The new model and screen tests failed before the fix, because `isBlocked` was missing and the pane showed "No runs yet".
- The new workflow test `schedules-phone-detail-blocked` takes screenshots of the detail. I checked them: the status card shows the reason without the tag, and the run history explains the block.
- `flutter analyze`: clean. `openspec validate --specs`: 21 passed. CI runs the full suite.

## Security Impact
None.

## Risk
Low. The change is limited to the schedules detail pane and to how `last_error` is parsed for blocked jobs.

Closes #317

## What
Adds ADR-0039 and ADR-0040, the decisions that unblock the pi 1.0.0 upgrade, and points ADR-0015's status at ADR-0039.

## Why
pi 1.0.0 writes and locks `auth.json` and `models-store.json` in its agent dir on every credential read, and locks `trust.json` when the checkout has project pi config. That fails on the read-only agent dir ADR-0015 and ADR-0033 require, which blocked #247. Upstream closed the matching issue (earendil-works/pi#6406), so forge has to handle it.

## Changes
- ADR-0039: pi runs with `--no-approve` in the fixed contract flags, and the runner warns in the run output about checkout pi config pi ignores. This closes the `.pi/settings.json` gap ADR-0015 accepted.
- ADR-0040: forge's pi package patches pi to use `ReadOnlyAuthStorage` and an in-memory models store, so the agent dir stays read-only. A writable throwaway agent dir and staying on 0.75.4 were rejected.
- ADR-0015's status now reads "amended by ADR-0033 and ADR-0039".

## Testing
Docs only. The pi 1.0.0 behaviour the ADRs describe was traced against the built pi 1.0.0 with an empty agent dir. The patch itself is not built yet, which is #247's work.

## Notes
#246 and #247 are updated to match. Refs #246, #247.

## Summary

Full MyFatoorah integration per the user-pasted shipping samples: **GetCountries, GetCities, CalculateShippingCharge, SendPayment (hosted invoice link), ExecutePayment, DirectPayment, GetPaymentStatus** — replacing PayFort entirely, including marketplace checkout wiring on web + mobile.

## API

- `lib/fatoorah.ts` — typed gateway client with the official Python-style error mapping (ValidationErrors/ErrorMessage/Data.ErrorMessage), Bearer auth, fail-closed config, `FATOORAH_SIMULATE` dev stubs, and `resolvePaymentState` that never infers PAID from unknown statuses (Paid/Succss → PAID; Canceled/Failed → FAILED; else PENDING).
- `lib/storeCheckout.ts` — shared cart validation + per-vendor StoreOrder placement, extracted from `marketplace.buyCart` (behavior unchanged).
- `payments` router: `authorize` (online) now returns a MyFatoorah invoice link; `statusCallback` (server-side GetPaymentStatus verification) replaces the PayFort signature webhook; new public queries `shippingCountries`/`shippingCities`/`shippingCharge`; new `payCart` (atomic wallet debit or invoice link, idempotent via `StoreCheckout.idempotencyKey`, P2002-race safe) and `verifyCartPayment`.
- DB: new `StoreCheckout` model (shipping + payment fields), `StoreOrder.checkoutId`, `TransactionSource.STORE_PURCHASE` — hand-written migration `20261003000000_fatoorah_checkout` (applied to dev DB; a stale failed migration from a previous session was resolved --applied after verifying all its indexes already existed).
- env: `PAYFORT_*` → `FATOORAH_API_TOKEN` / `FATOORAH_BASE_URL` / `FATOORAH_SIMULATE`.

## Checkout UI

- **Web**: ShippingForm (country select, city list, consignee fields, DHL/Aramex, live charge), pay button → `payCart` (wallet → success card; online → hosted gateway redirect), server-side status pages `/checkout/status` and `/payments/status` (Next 15 async searchParams).
- **Mobile**: shipping section (country chips, debounced city search, inputs), `payCart` + `Linking.openURL`, AppState-active invoice verification + manual check-status button.
- ExecutePayment/DirectPayment ship as tested lib functions (PCI scope — no raw card entry in our UI).

## Verification

- 80/80 targeted tests pass: fatoorah (15), store-checkout (7), payment-flow, money-integrity, router-inventory, trpc-procedures (266-router gate untouched; inventory re-baselined: −webhook, +6 procedures).
- All four packages type-check (api, web, mobile, shared, ui); api/web/mobile lint clean (0 errors).

## Notes

- Real gateway E2E pending the MyFatoorah API token — until then `FATOORAH_SIMULATE=true` serves dev stubs (test token: https://myfatoorah.readme.io/docs/test-token).
- Production server env needs `FATOORAH_API_TOKEN` (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md updated).

author: behnamazimi
body:
## What changed

Adds a hand-drawn doodle illustration set to the landing page. Each scene acts out its section's message, with CSS-only animation:

- **Hero, Read / Review / Quiz:** replaces the term-card mockup. One character reads a giant term card through a magnifier, one quizzes itself by flipping a flashcard to a check mark and cheering, and one reads a card overhead and throws it onto a pile of reviewed cards.
- **No due dates:** side by side. On the left, someone is buried under a growing pile of overdue cards with an alarm clock rattling. On the right, someone calmly reviews a card with a coffee.
- **Same queue, everywhere:** a thumb tap on a phone flips the laptop, desktop widget and Telegram chat to the same next card at the same moment.
- **Final CTA:** a character peeks out of an envelope, looks around, then climbs out holding a card. The section is now a two-column grid on desktop, matching the other illustrated sections.

`term-card-mockup.tsx` and its data file are deleted, since only the hero used them.

## Why

The redesigned landing page had almost no imagery. The illustrations give it a friendly, human tone and show each section's point visually.

## How it's built

`components/illustrations/` is its own module, so other parts of the app can reuse it:

- `Illustration`: the svg shell. It adds the shared marker-wobble filter and the hatch patterns, with per-instance ids so several illustrations on one page don't clash.
- `Shape`, `Line`, `Hatch`, `Clip`: the drawing primitives. `Shape` draws the colour fill slightly offset from the outline, like a misregistered print.
- `marks.tsx`: sparks, squiggles, dotted paths (optionally with moving dots), scribble "text" lines and eyes.
- `geometry.ts`: seeded path builders, so every render draws the same wobble.
- `palette.ts` and `illustrations.css`: colours as `--ill-*` tokens with dim-theme overrides, imported from `globals.css`.
- `<Motion kind=…>`: the CSS keyframe moves. It can set phase, amount, duration, mirroring and a pivot point. All motion stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Scenes are server components and ship no client JS.

## Reviewer notes

- `AGENTS.md` gets a short style guide (look, characters, scene, motion) so new illustrations stay consistent.
- `.oxlintrc.json` raises `max-lines` to 500 for `components/illustrations/scenes/**` only. Scenes are coordinate data, and the formatter puts every point on its own line.
- Checked in the in-app browser at desktop and 375px widths and in the dim theme, with no horizontal overflow and no console errors. I froze key animation frames to confirm limbs stay attached and the actions line up. The page held about 120fps at an earlier stage of the animations; I haven't measured after the later changes or tested on a real phone. `pnpm check` passes.

body:
Closes #44 (together with Backend's #91, merged, and #101, content). **Merge #101 first**: this branch contains it by merge; I merge main in again afterwards so the diff is only my files.

**What the student sees (Chapter 1 Q3 octal, Q4 hex):** each step is its own goal.
- **Step 0 — mark the groups:** a row of bit cells (36 × 44 px tap targets). Tapping a bit starts a new group there, shown as a 2 px divider in a gap; "Add 0" / "Remove 0" pad on the left. The correct groups are never shown in this step. A number that is a single group can be submitted with no cut.
- **Steps 1…G — one digit per group**, left to right; only the active group has an input, later groups show nothing; focus follows the step. Two characters allowed so "13 for D" is recognised; hex accepts lower case.
- **Done:** the joined result as a confirmation, e.g. (32)₈.

**Wiring**
- `QuestionView` renders `bit-grouping` in practice and Explain Slowly (content stages `groups` / `attention` / `done`; a digit appears only after its prediction), reading groups and digits from the step contract (`steps.ts`).
- Runner passes `hintsForStep(variant, step)`, so `hintsByStep` ladders (`group`, `digit`) are live.
- `useScrollFade` shared hook (BitGrouping row and CircuitDiagram).

**Tests** unit: component (keyboard, padding keeps cuts in place, wrong groupings reported as marked, single group), runner (each goal its own step, wrong grouping retried with its nudge, ladder per step kind, "10 for A"), rendered walk 26 → (1A)₁₆ through QuestionView. e2e: octal and hex walked step by step on desktop and Pixel 7 (wrong grouping stays on the goal, one input at a time, no page overflow).

Checks: tsc, lint, 182 unit, build, e2e 16/16 locally.

body:
Continues the Strings topic (after #184). Each problem runs the owner's accepted submission as written; all are the standard optimal approaches.

| Problem | Owner's approach |
|---|---|
| Reverse Words in a String (151) | `trim().split("\\s+")`, then append back to front. |
| Longest Palindromic Substring (5) | Expand around each centre, first absorbing the run of equal letters, which handles even lengths. |
| Count and Say (38) | Recursion: term n read off term n−1. The chain shows on the call stack. |
| Sum of Beauty of All Substrings (1781) | O(26·n²) counts. |
| String to Integer (atoi) (8) | Spaces, sign, leading zeros, digits into a `long` with an early stop past MAX, sign, clamp. |

- **atoi**: each early `return 0` is highlighted on the check that decides it, so every highlight is reachable. `Character.isDigit` accepts non-ASCII digits, which `ch - '0'` would misread, so the input is now LeetCode's set: letters, digits, ' ', '+', '-' and '.'. A refusal test covers this.
- **Guards**: 7 answer rows: "+-12" → 0, "00000-42a1234" → 0, both int limits, only spaces, n = 1, and "ab".

**Verification**
- Only the 5 content-changed goldens are committed, each read.
- The full backend suite passes.
- Checked in Chromium: the Count and Say walkthrough (dark, 1440), Longest Palindrome (light, 390) and the atoi editor (dark, 390). No errors, no overflow.

author: jeffreynijs
body:
Proposed first beta: toolkit **0.1.0-beta.0**, `hey-api-builders` **3.0.0-beta.0**, still on npm's `next` channel. This PR is the candidate record for `docs/beta-readiness.md`. **Merging does not publish.** Publication is a separate approval: after merge, create the `toolkit-v0.1.0-beta.0` prerelease at the merge commit.

## Version transition
- Changesets leaves `alpha` and enters `beta`; all 19 packages are versioned, the CHANGELOGs are generated and the lockfile refreshed. `check:workspace` passes (19 packages, core 0.1.0-beta.0, exact internal dependencies).
- Changesets v3 continues the prerelease counter across tags, so `alpha.4` would become `beta.5`. The generated versions are renamed to the documented `beta.0`. Later betas count up from it as usual.
- The train ships the fixes since alpha.4: #50, #53 and the docs work in #51, #52 and #54, all listed in the package CHANGELOGs.

## Entry checklist
- [x] **Candidate.** This branch's head, built on main `8c8315b`. The SHA at merge will be the squash commit.
- [x] **API and compatibility scope.** A beta scope review covered all 19 packages: export maps, peer ranges, cross-cutting contracts and known gaps.
  - Fixed and documented before the candidate: two shipped READMEs pinned alpha versions; 14 diagnostic codes were undocumented (#51); 27 error-class codes are now a documented contract (#52); public exports are documented; README links now work on npm; adapter limits are documented (#54).
  - Compatibility targets are unchanged.
  - Planned migrations remain Hey API v2 → v3 and Effect 3 → 4.
- [x] **Final-head checks.** All 18 jobs pass at `332ae3c` on the first attempt: source and types, coverage, tarballs, dependency audit and review, browsers, platforms, runtimes, the vendor version matrix (zod, typebox, typebox-legacy, arktype, faker), examples and website.
- [x] **Checkout example** at this candidate (`332ae3c`), installed from the tarballs:
  - The tarball consumer installs all 19 tarballs with matching integrities and imports them; 21/21 recipe tests pass, including the checkout bug, fix and replay; the generated Zod and ArkType facades, `doctor` and `inspect` work.
  - `pnpm validate`, `pack:check`, `test:examples` and `release:prepare` pass.
- [x] **Candidate artifacts.** `release:prepare` produced 19 tarballs plus `manifest.json` and `SHA256SUMS` (commit `332ae3c`, tag `toolkit-v0.1.0-beta.0`, `next`). They were installed in a fresh consumer, not workspace imports.
- [x] **Application trials.**
  - Molenheide (native Zod forms with Temporal; wisemen-digital/molenheide#634) and Linio (Hey API-generated Zod schemas; wisemen-digital/linio-web#200) were refreshed to alpha.4 on 2026-10-03 and stay unmerged drafts.
  - Generated v3 builders are covered by packaging and e2e generation tests, not an application trial.
- [x] **Pseudo-repository trials.** These cover the packages no application trial uses. Four realistic local apps (about 210 tests) were built against the candidate tarballs: a Hey API shop with generated v3 builders and the CLI; Effect 4 billing; Valibot, ArkType, both TypeBox adapters, JSON Schema and Faker; and OpenAPI, GraphQL, Protobuf, Avro, consumers and property tests with replay.
  - Their bugs are fixed in #53. Against this candidate's tarballs, all four `run.sh` scripts pass after the known-bug tests became normal assertions: hey-api-shop 77, effect-billing 36, schema-zoo 49 and logistics-protocols 49 tests, with no regressions.
  - Two tests still pin open issues as expected failures (`inspect` reference blame; GraphQL missing-scalar error text).
  - One fixture was corrected: it relied on the old `readOnly` bug to hide a missing required field.
- [x] **Feedback plan.**
  - Native-schema tasks use the beta feedback kit (Zod fixture with variation; failing property replayed from a record) and its GitHub issue form.
  - Channels: the Reddit posts (r/javascript Showoff Saturday, r/typescript, r/coolgithubprojects, r/SideProject), the JavaScript Weekly / Node Weekly pitch, and Bluesky.
  - Review point: two weeks after publication, or earlier on any blocker. Triage follows the exit criteria.
  - The beta feedback kit pins move to beta.0 in the post-publication docs PR.

## Known limits carried into the beta
Documented, or tracked for after beta:
- The `@mimlet/api` body is typed `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>`, which TypeScript 6's DOM `BodyInit` rejects.
- `mimlet inspect` prepares every supplied reference and blames the root schema.
- Generated `hey-api-builders` setters accept `undefined` for exact-optional keys.
- Valibot `isoDateTime`/`isoTime` generation fails validation (documented).
- Hey API's Faker plugin data may not satisfy the spec (documented).
- `reportStatus` is exported only as a type.
- Some errors don't name the offending field.

## Publication (separate approval)
After merge and approval: create the `toolkit-v0.1.0-beta.0` prerelease at the merge commit; verify all 19 registry artifacts (bytes, `next` tags, SLSA provenance) and a clean registry install; attach the 21 assets; then update the docs to beta.0 and move `latest`.

Regenera `requirements.lock` y `requirements-dev.lock` con `make lock` después de las cuatro PR de Dependabot de hoy (#20–#23), que subieron las cotas inferiores en `requirements*.txt` sin tocar los locks. author: liolu
body:
## E0 — Fondations de l'éditeur de modèles (0.12, `ROADMAP-0.12-editeur.md`)

**Module `src/editeur/` et état du jeu**
- `AppState` : **Jeu** ou **Éditeur**. Dans l'éditeur, le jeu ne lit plus le clavier ni la souris (caméra, vaisseau, vol bas, menu) ; Échap ou « Retour au jeu » ramène au jeu.
- Ouverture :
  - toute seule à la **création du personnage** : au premier lancement (aucune sauvegarde), sur le type Personnage, avec un message de bienvenue ;
  - depuis le **menu du jeu** (Échap → bouton « Éditeur de modèles ») ;
  - par **`/editeur`** (`/editeur vaisseau`, `/editeur autre`).
- Écran E0 : choix du type (Personnage, Vaisseau + catégorie, Autre) avec la taille de grille, bibliothèque des modèles, « Nouveau modèle » (modèle vide enregistré), « Importer Pixel World ». **L'édition elle-même arrive en E1.**

**Format `.ssvox`** (règles 1 et 2)
- Une archive zip (deflate) : `meta.json` (nom, type, race ou catégorie, taille, palette, zones, étiquettes), `voxels.bin` et `zones.bin`.
- Palette de **255 couleurs** au plus, chacune avec sa **matière** (mate, métal, verre, lumineuse) ; un octet par voxel (0 = vide).
- **Stockage creux par chunks de 32³** : absent (vide), **uniforme** (un octet) ou plein (32 Kio, codé en RLE). Une coque pleine de 512³ pèse moins de 1 Mo en mémoire et moins de 200 Ko sur disque (testé).
- Grilles : personnage 16 × 32 × 32 (Q6), vaisseau 64 à 1024 selon la catégorie, autre jusqu'à 64³.
- **10 Mo** au plus par fichier (Q4), enregistrement refusé au-delà ; empreinte FNV pour le réseau (E7).
- Fichiers dans `saves/modeles/`, jamais écrasés (« nom-2.ssvox »).

**Import de Pixel World** (`import.rs`) : un modèle ou un catalogue JSON (`VoxelModelSerializer.cs`). Chaque `BlockType` reçoit sa couleur de `BlockData.cs` et une matière (verre pour l'eau, la glace et le cristal ; métal ; lumineuse pour Glow). On dépose les JSON dans `saves/import/`, puis « Importer Pixel World ». **Les 64 vrais modèles de `Pixel world/VoxelModels/` s'importent sans aucun bloc inconnu** (36,5 Ko au total).

**Tests** : 242 réussis (+ format aller-retour, chunks qui se replient, coque géante, palette limitée, fichiers cassés refusés, import modèle et catalogue, bibliothèque). Lancement vérifié deux fois : premier lancement (aucune sauvegarde) → l'éditeur s'ouvre sur Personnage ; lancement normal → il ne s'ouvre pas. PROTOCOL inchangé.

**À tester** : Échap → « Éditeur de modèles », changer de type et de catégorie, « Nouveau modèle », copier des JSON de Pixel World dans `saves/import/` puis « Importer Pixel World », Échap pour revenir au jeu.

author: bal7hazar
body:
LIB-06 M2-T3 (brief `docs/briefs/LIB-06-M2-T3-operators.md`): the arithmetic of `Hex`.

## What lands
- `hex/impls.cairo`: `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Rem`, `Neg` of `Hex`, the homogeneous assignment operators, and `HexOpsTrait::{add_scalar, sub_scalar, add_direction, sub_direction, add_diagonal, sub_diagonal, div_scalar, rem_scalar}`.
- `div_scalar` on exact rationals with `Hex::round`'s rule. Exhaustive off-chain comparison with the crate (`tools/refgen`): **44 of 157,464** pairs of `[-40,40]²` by `[-12,12]\{0}` differ (0.03 %, all hexround ties moved by the `f32` rescale), and 3,931 of 4,096 seeded pairs with `2^20 ≤ L < 2^31` differ. Every pair is listed and explained in `docs/deviations/div_scalar.md`; the generator stops on any non-`f32` difference or on more than 1 %.
- `hex/swizzle.cairo`, `hex/euclidean.cairo` (squared only), `hex/convert.cairo` (`from_u64`, `as_u64`, `Into<(i32, i32), Hex>`, `Into<[i32; 2], Hex>`).
- `conversions.cairo`: `DoubledHexMode`, the doubled and hexmod conversions (with their `as i32` deviations documented).
- Golden vectors for 5 modules, budgets, benches, the `HexxOps` call sites, and the regenerated snapshots and documents (Linux VPS, single-threaded builds per #106).

## Stop (crossed, accepted) and what was deferred
- **The stop was crossed and accepted by the orchestrator (review of #107):** `Div`/`Rem` of `Hex` measure 8,563 per call, above 2U = 8,076. The task went on past the stop instead of stopping at that measurement. The figure is accepted: the target was mis-derived (about 1,100 assumed per signed `i32` division, about 4.3k measured). It is recorded in `gas/accepted.md`, and `docs/GAS.md` is regenerated.
- `div_scalar` (42,720) and `rem_scalar` (45,749) are between U and 2U, budgeted on the measurement.
- `Sum`/`Product` are **deferred** (`PLAN.md`, "Deferred (orchestrator)"). They need corelib's `associated_item_constraints`, an experimental feature of `crates/hexx/Scarb.toml`.
- `scripts/api_parity.py` now reads the homogeneous two-argument assignment impls (`AddAssign<Hex, Hex>` …) as Rust's `impl AddAssign for Hex`, with one test per form; a heterogeneous form raises. The five rows read `ported`.

author: kevinkickback
body:
Media loads could apply after their editor closed or changed, and provider downloads and YouTube titles were trusted without a checked contract. Centralize image validation and session-owned loading so only the current selection reaches the UI, with cancellation and cleanup for stale local video URLs.

Local and downloaded images now share raster signature, MIME, and 2 MB checks. Preserve IGDB size fallbacks and HTTP/HTTPS image source compatibility; validate character search URLs. Match exact YouTube hosts and supported video IDs, validate title responses, and clear a previous title when its URL changes. New notebook resources require HTTPS to match desktop opening rules; existing HTTP resources remain in backups and editable with a visible explanation.

Validation: lint, TypeScript, release metadata, web production build, all 840 unit tests with coverage (78.90% lines), and all 65 browser tests pass. Regressions cover delayed and superseded requests, close/reopen and entity changes, malformed provider payloads, spoofed URLs, cover fallbacks, and video URL cleanup.

## Purpose
Clean the production repository around its actual goal: a reliable daily candidate pool.

## Removed
- Portfolio construction layer and generated portfolio snapshot.
- Execution-plan layer and generated execution plan.
- Stateful constrained-execution backtest and dedicated workflow.
- Obsolete production-layer tests tied only to the removed execution stack.
- Stale execution comparison/cloud-provenance artifacts and documentation.

## Kept
- Daily market-data update.
- Private/main strategy loading.
- Candidate generation and independent candidate validation.
- Immutable daily candidate history.
- Candidate-focused historical backtest, walk-forward and factor research.
- GitHub Pages candidate-pool display.

## Web
- The page now reads factor weights from the candidate snapshot.
- Production strategy metadata is displayed as Momentum 35%, Liquidity 15%, Value 30%, Safety 20%.
- Candidate capacity is shown as the actual Top-3 production cap.

The Private main strategy remains the sole source of production scoring/admission.

author: samubura
body:
Includes the commits of #975 (needs its `askAllTo` fix), which is not in `develop` yet: review the last four commits.

**Asking several agents**
- `askOneTo(receivers, query, timeout)` and `askAllTo(receivers, query, timeout)` send the question to every receiver and wait until each one replies.
- `broadcastAskOne(query, timeout, replies = 1)` and `broadcastAskAll(query, timeout, replies = 1)` broadcast the question and wait for the first `replies` answers. The timeout is required, as the number of agents that will answer is not known.
- All of them return the answers by sender, and on timeout the answers received so far. `askOneTo` to several receivers and `broadcastAskOne` also bind the query to the first reply received, as the single-receiver `askOneTo` does. They replace the commented-out broadcast asks and their TODO.

**`Reply` performative (breaking)**
- Answers are sent with `replyTo(receiver, questionId, beliefs)` as a `Reply`. The `tellTo` overload taking the question id is removed, and `Tell` no longer has `replyingTo`.
- `handleKQMLPayload` returns `null` for a `Reply`: only the ask waiting for it receives it, and replies arriving after the ask stopped waiting are dropped (as Jason does for synchronous asks). Before, every reply was also added as a belief.
- Updated the contract-net example.

**Tests**: the ask tests move from `TestKQMLMessaging` to `TestKQMLAsk`, which adds `askOneTo` to two agents (bound to the first reply), `askAllTo` to two agents with one silent (partial answers on timeout), `broadcastAskOne` with the default single reply (bound to the query, and no belief left by any reply, which fails if replies are handled as `Tell`), and `broadcastAskAll` waiting for 2 replies out of 3.

author: alexander-shamray
body:
Four issues, taken in priority order: #58, the only open bug, then #50,
which its own issue puts first in the Inventory and Payments catch-up, then
#63 and #83, which have no preconditions. Ten commits, each self-contained.
Two more follow when a patch is applied, because `.github/workflows/` and
`README.md` are edit-denied to the session. The rest of the catch-up (#51 to
#57) does not start here: #51 says no console PR in that series starts before
the workspace `run-locally.md` gains Inventory and Payments, and that file is
still dated 14 Sep.

| | |
|---|---|
| Class | C+D |
| Touch set | `src/Admin.Host/**`, `src/Admin.Web/**`, `tests/**`, `docs/superpowers/specs/**`, `docs/testing.md`, `README.md`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Closes | #58, #63; issues 50 and 83 with the pending commits |

## What changed

### #58: Stop ends the host's `logs -f`

**`fix(jobs):` keep the ps and exec reads out of the job registry**

The Stack screen's 3 s `ps` poll pushed 50 exited jobs through `JobRegistry`
in 150 s, so a dead `npm start` stopped being reopenable within two and a half
minutes. `ProcessSpec.Listed` defaults to true. `ComposeService` reads (`ps`,
`exec`) clear it, so they are still jobs, with the bound and the kill, but
the registry does not keep them.

**`feat(logs):` stop the follow job by name**

`POST /api/logs/follow/{id}/stop` ends the named job only while it is still
`LogFollower`'s current one, and answers 204 either way. It goes by name
because a Stop and the next Follow can reach the host in either order. A
generic `POST /api/jobs/{id}/stop` was refused: it would reach `up`, `down -v`
and `npm start` halfway through.

**`feat(logs):` end the host's follow on Stop and when the screen is left**

Stop and the destroy hook now call the host. The page keeps at most one
follow request out. A Stop pressed while that request is out lets it answer
and stops the job it names, because a cancelled request cannot stop a job
the host already started.

**`feat(broker):` auto-refresh re-reads exchanges and permissions too**

Once reads are unlisted, the reason auto-refresh read only queues is gone.

**`docs:` say Stop ends the host's follow and reads are not kept as jobs**

Spec Â§5.2, Â§5.3, Â§5.10 and Â§6, and README's known limits, amended to match.
Executes the known-limits jobs plan, Tasks 1 to 5.

### #50: the owner-drift gate, and the drift it found on its first run

**`fix(api):` copy the gateway's payments-admin route into GatewayRoutes**

The gateway gained `payments-admin` and the copy never followed. No caller
changes behaviour: the proxy has no Payments surface yet (#51).

**`fix(logs):` list every service the backend composes**

`COMPOSE_SERVICES` stopped at the four units the console knew, so the Logs
screen could not follow Inventory, Payments, Shipping or Notifications.

**`test(drift):` read every fact copied from blueprint-backend against the clone**

`tests/Admin.Host.Tests/Drift/` reads each copied fact at its owner:

| Fact | Read against |
|---|---|
| A URL per surface, its port | the Compose unit and its host port binding |
| `GatewayRoutes` | the gateway's `ReverseProxy:Routes`, every method |
| `GoldenSignals` | the three dashboard panels, `$service` at All |
| `RunLocallyExamples` | `run-locally.md`'s `-Body` hashtables, parsed |
| Header, length, alphabet, scope key | `CorrelationIdExtensions` |
| `ProjectionQueue`, `OutboxTable` | Ordering's queue constant, `OutboxTable` |
| Realm users and the fake's grants | `realm-export.json` |
| Logs' `COMPOSE_SERVICES` | every included Compose file |

Units with no surface (inventory and payments #51, shipping #59,
notifications #65) and the fake realm's two missing grants (#52) are named
exceptions citing the issue that removes each. An exception that is no
longer needed fails too. `DriftCoverageTests` needs no clone: a source file
naming `blueprint-backend` without a drift check or a stated reason fails
the build.

### #63: run-locally.md's commands

**`test(drift):` every fenced line in run-locally.md is accounted for**

Each fenced line must be one of four things:

- a docker or npm command the host's own `ComposeService`, `BrokerService`
  and `FrontendSupervisor` can be shown to run, through a recording runner;
- a request to a host `AdminOptions` configures;
- a listed non-run (`npm ci`), with its reason;
- PowerShell that only builds a value.

On a scratch copy, a `compose restart`, a `curl.exe` line and a request to
Inventory's port each failed.

### #83: Stop and the client's Playwright run

**`feat(stack):` say beside Stop frontend that it can end a Playwright run's server**

One sentence beside the button, with a spec assertion. Nothing is detected:
whether a run is attached is not observable from the host.

## Pending: two commits a patch will add

The session cannot edit `.github/workflows/**` or `README.md`, and a script
is staged for the user to apply. It adds:

- **`ci.yml`, a `drift` job.** It checks the backend out with
  `persist-credentials: false` and runs the Drift namespace with
  `ADMIN_DRIFT_REQUIRED=true`, so a clone that fails to appear fails the job
  instead of skipping 24 tests. That commit carries the closing line for
  issue 50.
- **README, one known-limits line for #83.** That commit carries the closing
  line for issue 83.

Until they land, nothing in CI runs the drift checks against the backend:
the `host` job has no clone and skips them.

## The honest cost

- **No new test project.** #50 asked for one. A `.csproj` and its `.slnx`
  entry are edit-denied to the session, and a namespace filter gives the CI

author: michelamin47
body:
## Problem
The sync window started at `laterOf(latest stored datum, today − 6)`. Once a newer day was stored, an earlier day that had been skipped for "no data" was never read again. 2026-10-02 (~14k steps) was lost this way: Samsung Health wrote it to Health Connect late, after 2026-10-03 had already been stored.

## Changes (`voeding-app/src/lib/stepSync.js`, web-only)
- After the first-run 30-day backfill, **every sync re-reads today − 6 … today**, regardless of what is stored. The `step_log` query only checks "is the table empty?" (`select=datum&limit=1`).
- The upsert is unchanged: a re-read overwrites the stored count with Health Connect's current value. That includes **lowering** it: HC deduplicates across sources, so its current value is the source of truth.
- "No data" is still "skip". The plugin only emits a bucket whose aggregate is non-null (`HealthManager.kt`), so a date with no data is left out of the upsert and its existing row stays untouched. It is never written as 0 or nulled.
- **DST:** the plugin's `bucket: 'day'` is a fixed 24h, so 2026-10-25 (25h) returns two buckets. All buckets are now summed instead of taking `samples[0]`.
- CLAUDE.md: range, DST and `bronnen`/`sourceId` notes.

Not touched: Coach.jsx, coach-chat, morning-checkin, close-day-cron, `_shared/`. No schema change.

## Verification
- eslint + `npm run build` pass.
- A scratch script ran the real helper functions from `stepSync.js`. For 2026-10-03:
  - Not-empty table: 09-27 … 10-03, 7 dates, **including 10-02**. The old logic would have read only `[10-03]`.
  - Empty table: 30 dates, 09-04 … 10-03.
  - DST: two buckets (13000 + 412) are summed to 13412, and an empty result returns `null`.
- No test rows were written to `step_log`; this session only ran read-only SELECTs.

author: arambucak
body:
## Problem
Im Events-Feed stand bei Veranstaltungen, die ein Nutzer nur **in die Community eingetragen/geteilt** hat (z. B. ein Theaterstück im Jagdschloss Grunewald), **„Gastgeber Aram B."**. Das ist irreführend — die Person veranstaltet das Event nicht, sie hat es nur eingetragen.

## Änderung
- Label-Logik in `EventHostIdentity` ehrlich gemacht:
  - geteiltes Angebot (`interest`) → **„Geteilt von"** (unverändert)
  - sonst → **„Eingetragen von"** (neuer Key `event_submitted_by`, in allen 16 Picker-Sprachen)
- `event_host` („Gastgeber") bleibt erhalten — es wird weiterhin korrekt im Einladungs-Screen für selbst ausgerichtete Events genutzt.
- Entscheidungslogik als testbare Pure-Function `eventHostLabelKey()` extrahiert + Tests (4 grün).

## Formulierung — kreative Wahl, begründet
„Eingetragen von" ist in **beiden** Fällen wahr (privates Treffen wie Community-Tipp), ohne eine Veranstalter-Rolle zu behaupten. Weniger anmaßend als „Gastgeber", wärmer und ehrlich.

## Nicht in diesem PR (bewusst)
- Das Fehlen der **KI-Funde** ist ein separates, technisches Thema (Gemini-Verfügbarkeit/Filter), kein Formulierungsproblem — sollte eigenständig untersucht werden.
- „0 bestätigt" bei Fremd-Events ist verwandt, aber eine tiefere Semantik-Änderung — bewusst ausgeklammert, um diesen PR fokussiert zu halten.

author: elhoim
body:
## BLUF
- **Priority:** medium
- **What:** new rule `rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_cloud_imds_credential_request.yml` detecting command lines requesting cloud instance metadata (IMDS) role credentials or managed-identity tokens (AWS/ECS/Azure/GCP/Alibaba) (ATT&CK T1552.005)
- **Why:** No Sigma rule references 169.254.169.254 / metadata.google.internal on any OS.
- **Validation:** Atomic Red Team T1552.005 #3 "AWS - Retrieve EC2 IAM Role Credentials via IMDSv2" + local SigmaHQ CI gate passing

### Summary of the Pull Request

Adds the rule **Cloud Instance Metadata Credential Or Token Request Via CLI - Linux** (`level: medium`, `status: experimental`).

Detects a command line querying a cloud instance metadata service (IMDS) endpoint that returns temporary credentials or access tokens of the role or managed identity attached to the instance.
Covers AWS EC2 IAM role credentials, the AWS ECS container credentials endpoint, Azure managed identity tokens, GCP service account tokens and Alibaba Cloud RAM role credentials.
Adversaries with code execution on a cloud workload, or abusing an SSRF, query these endpoints to steal credentials and pivot into the cloud control plane.

### Changelog

new: Cloud Instance Metadata Credential Or Token Request Via CLI - Linux

### Example Log Event

N/A (new rule). No regression data is added: no real telemetry from an ART run is attached, and none was fabricated. The rule carries `simulation` metadata pointing at the validating Atomic Red Team test(s).

### Fixed Issues

N/A

### SigmaHQ Rule Creation Conventions

- If your PR adds new rules, please consider following and applying these [conventions](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma-specification/blob/main/sigmahq/)

## Details

- Logsource: `{"product": "linux", "category": "process_creation"}`
- Tags: `attack.credential-access`, `attack.t1552.005`
- False positives: Cloud bootstrap or configuration management scripts that read instance role credentials; Administrators troubleshooting instance roles or managed identities
- Duplicate check: searched `rules*/` on current master for the key strings and `gh pr list -R SigmaHQ/sigma --state all` for related terms; no existing rule or open/merged PR covers this detection.

## Validation

Local reproduction of the `Sigma Rule Tests` and `Validate Sigma rules` workflows (Python 3.11, pySigma + sigma-cli + `pySigma-validators-sigmahq==0.21.*`), on master with this rule added:

```
yamllint -s <rule>                                   -> OK (strict)
python tests/test_logsource.py                       -> OK
python tests/test_rules.py                           -> OK
sigma check --fail-on-error --fail-on-issues --validation-config tests/sigma_cli_conf.yml rules*
                                                     -> 0 errors, 0 condition errors, 0 issues
JSON schema (sigma-specification v2.1.0)             -> valid
duplicate-id check (rules* deprecated unsupported)   -> no duplicates
```

Baseline: all of the above also pass on unmodified master.

Converted query (`sigma convert -t splunk --without-pipeline`):

```
CommandLine IN ("*100.100.100.200*", "*169.254.169.254*", "*169.254.170.2*", "*fd00:ec2::254*", "*metadata.google.internal*") CommandLine IN ("*/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts*", "*/meta-data/iam/security-credentials*", "*/meta-data/ram/security-credentials*", "*/metadata/identity/oauth2/token*", "*/v2/credentials*") NOT (ParentImage IN ("*/amazon-ssm-agent", "*/cloud-init", "*/google_guest_agent", "*/google_metadata_script_runner", "*/ssm-agent-worker", "*/waagent"))
```

Logic check: the rule was converted with the SQLite backend and run against command lines taken from the Atomic Red Team test(s) (true positives) and benign look-alikes (true negatives):

| Expected | Result | Event |
|---|---|---|
| match | match | Image=`/usr/bin/curl`; ParentImage=`/bin/sh`; CommandLine=`curl -s --connect-timeout 2 -m 5 -H X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: AQAE http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` |
| match | match | Image=`/usr/bin/curl`; ParentImage=`/bin/bash`; CommandLine=`curl -H Metadata:true http://169.254.169.254/metadata/identity/oauth2/token?api-version=2018-02-01&resource=https://management.azure.com/` |
| match | match | Image=`/usr/bin/wget`; ParentImage=`/bin/bash`; CommandLine=`wget -qO- --header Metadata-Flavor:Google http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token` |
| no match | no match | Image=`/usr/bin/curl`; ParentImage=`/bin/bash`; CommandLine=`curl -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600` |
| no match | no match | Image=`/usr/bin/curl`; ParentImage=`/usr/bin/cloud-init`; CommandLine=`curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/role` |

author: bfnoc
body:
Fixes #363. Likely also #293.

### Cause

Editing an existing account that has a date range (*Since specific date* or *Download recent emails only*) cannot be saved. For example, changing only the **Download Schedule** and clicking **Save changes** does nothing, and there is no toast or validation message.

The API returns the unused half of `date_since` as `null` (e.g. `{ "fixed": "2026-09-01", "relative": null }`). `mapAccountToFormValues` passes it into the form unchanged, and `dateSelectionSchema` rejects `null` for `fixed` / `relative`. The `null` half has no rendered field to display the error, so `handleSubmit` silently never calls `onSubmit`.

### Change
- In `dateSelectionSchema` (`components/schema.ts`), accept `null` for `fixed` and `relative` (`.optional()` → `.nullish()`), matching what the API returns. Validation of the half that is set is unchanged.
- Add `__tests__/date-since-null.test.ts`: the API shapes `{ fixed, relative: null }` and `{ fixed: null, relative }` pass; an empty fixed date and an invalid relative value are still rejected.

Saving sends the null half back as returned; the backend treats it as unset (verified via `POST /api/v1/account/:id` with both shapes).

### Blast radius
Frontend only: the account settings page when loading an existing account. No backend, API, or data format changes. Account creation is unaffected.

### Backward compatibility
Fully backward compatible. No stored data, config, or API contract changes.

### Testing
- New tests: 4/4 pass.
- `src/features/accounts` suite: 8 failures in `schema-edge.test.ts` (e.g. "accepts fixed date_since", "accepts use_dangerous: true"). The same 8 fail on unmodified `main`, so they are pre-existing and unrelated to this change.
- Manual: built `bichon-server` from this branch, edited accounts set to *Since specific date* and to *Download recent emails only*, changed only the cron schedule, saved. Got "Saved", and the change persisted after reloading.

AI-assisted; I reviewed the change and tested it manually.

body:
Browser worker/transport failures can store only task.error, with no result payload. The delegation summary then became empty, leaving Overwatcher unable to distinguish an unavailable host from a timeout.

For failed Browser tasks without a formatted result, project fixed messages for HostUnavailable, host timeout, and other pre-result failures. Preserve the existing durable error for diagnostics without exposing raw exception text or secrets in the public summary. This improves reporting; it does not restart an offline Browser Host or establish a successful live lookup.

Validation: 63 tests passed across durable Overwatcher follow-through, coordinator, Browser subtask routing and Browser Chat bridge. New regressions prove worker-only failures return the correct category without disclosing the stored secret-shaped error text.

author: smeltzzz
body:
Three releases' worth of work on top of the published **8.1.0** (8.1.1 and 8.2.0 were never tagged, so this tag carries all three).

## 8.1.1 — seven chain-fidelity defects

Audited every decision the toolkit makes against the hardware it is tuned for (Chromecast G454V → Hisense AX3125H HDMI IN → Samsung UN60F6350AF), re-verified against the manufacturers' own documents. The hardware *profile* was already correct and well sourced; all seven bugs were in how the tools applied it. Two could permanently delete audio or queue a pointless re-encode.

1. 1920×1088 macroblock-padded 1080p was flagged oversize, queueing a pointless re-encode.
2. The cleaner f-string-joined its probe blob, so an absent `codec_id` shifted fields and a playable **DTS core** track was promoted to unplayable DTS-HD — the two tools disagreed about the same track.
3. "Atmos" was credited from the track *title*, so a stereo AC-3 named "Dolby Atmos 5.1" outranked real surround.
4. **Destructive:** the ranking led with the codec sub-tier, so AC-3 2.0 beat FLAC 7.1 and the remux permanently deleted surround to keep stereo.
5. `VIDEO_UNKNOWN` was unreachable — unreadable dimensions/codec failed **open** as direct-play.
6. The audiofit step title advertised "(AC-3 5.1)", stale since 8.1.0.
7. `render_diagnostics` indented a multi-line `detail` once, so the chain summary's Sink/Display/Wiring rows went flush-left.

## 8.2.0 — keep the best track the chain can **end up with**

8.1.1 ranked audio by playback band first: right about *playability*, wrong about *possibility*. The remux is irreversible, so a TrueHD Atmos 7.1 master lost to a stereo AC-3 that plays today — and the 7.1 master was deleted for good, when `audio_standardizer` could have turned it into chain-native DD+ 7.1 on any later run.

Ranking is now `(achievable layout, band, atmos, codec sub-tier, bitrate, sample rate, original)`. Band survives as the **tiebreak**, so Direct-Play-first is unchanged where it still applies: 5.1 AC-3 still beats 5.1 TrueHD. New: `playbackchain.achievable_channels()`, plus a `Kept audio needing audiofit` report bucket so a retained master that still needs converting is never silent.

## 8.3.0 — every cut of a movie is the same movie

Downloading the Extended cut of a film already held in the Theatrical cut was declined as a conflict, because the canonical name carries no edition tag. Title and year now decide identity on their own: Extended, Theatrical, Director's Cut, Unrated, IMAX, Criterion, 3D and any resolution all replace the existing copy under the same `Title (Year)/Title (Year).mkv` name — the newest download wins, with no size or quality judgement. `part` is the one marker that still has to agree, because a split movie is one film across several files.

Also fixes a latent bug: two cuts in one release folder were two "distinct movies" that both mapped to the same canonical destination, so one silently overwrote the other and the run logged a box set that does not exist.

## Verification

Every gate the release workflow runs was pre-flighted locally and passes: tag `v8.3.0` == `organizekit.VERSION` · `twine check` on wheel and sdist · clean-venv install running `organize --version` and `organize doctor --json` **outside** the source tree · the extracted sdist's own suite · the zipapp build.

Suite **1278** tests OK (skipped=5) · ruff clean · coverage 86% vs floor 85 · self-tests 8/8. Tests 1247 → 1278 across the three releases; the tests that pinned superseded behaviour were rewritten to pin the new rules rather than deleted.

## Remaining steps (need a permission this branch does not have)

Per [`docs/merge-and-release.md`](docs/merge-and-release.md): merge with a **normal merge** (not squash — the commits carry the story), then tag the merge commit on `main`:

```
git tag -a v8.3.0 -m "8.3.0" && git push origin v8.3.0
```

author: meymchen
body:
## Summary

Both endpoints used to rebuild the inbound pipeline from about 20 small Protocol session methods, and the two copies had drifted. Now the [[Protocol session]] owns that pipeline, and each endpoint pulls events from it (ADR 0037, which revises ADR 0028).

```diff
 Server engine / Client endpoint
-  loop next_input
-    trace.message
-    classify reader error → close cause
-    reserve_inbound / reject duplicate / reject capacity
-    $/cancelRequest → cancel_inbound → complete_cancelled
-    Response → outbound_registry.complete
-    spawn + HandlerTimeout + run_handler_with_deadline + completion_gate
-  close → final_close_cause → trace.connection_closed
+  loop session.next_event
+    Request(AdmittedRequest) → respond(..) | session.spawn_request(..)
+    Notification { method, params }
+    Closed → break
+  session.finish() → SessionEnd<C>
```

An **Admitted request** has passed admission and must be answered exactly once. The endpoint either answers it with `respond`, or hands it to `spawn_request`, and the session then runs it to completion. Dropping one unanswered sends an internal error and fails debug builds.

```text
src/
├── session.rs          # inbound pipeline: admission, cancel, correlation, deadline,
│                       #   panic backstop, rejection telemetry, close-cause selection
├── engine.rs           # Server lifecycle precedence, initialize transaction, built-ins
└── client_endpoint.rs  # Client lifecycle gate, reverse-handler routing, progress create
```

`SessionEnd<C>` holds the connection-level endings: `ReaderEof`, `ReaderFailed`, `WriterFailed` and `Endpoint(C)`. The endpoint close-cause enums keep only their own reasons, so `ClientCloseCause`'s `unreachable!` goes away.

Where the two endpoints disagreed, the Server's behaviour now applies to both:

| Situation | Client before | Both now |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate ID or exhausted capacity | rejected silently | `Rejected` telemetry and failure report |
| Notification handler panics | lost when the task is joined | isolated, logged, reported as `PanicIsolation` |
| Malformed `$/cancelRequest`, unknown response ID | `debug!` only | failure report and `debug!` |
| Reader error | not classified | classified as Framing or Transport and reported |

The Client still has no `on_error` hook, so its failure reports remain no-ops. The Server's `PanicIsolationService` Layer is unchanged (ADR 0019); the session's catch is only a backstop on the Server.

## Evidence

Commit 1 adds the notification-panic fix test-first:

- **Before:** `client_notification_handler_panics_are_isolated_and_logged` fails with `notification panic is logged as isolated: Elapsed(())`.
  **After:** it passes.

I ran the new Client regression tests against the pre-refactor `src/`:

```text
client_admission_rejections_emit_rejected_telemetry            FAILED  → ok
client_initialize_reports_reader_endings_as_transport_errors   ok      → ok   (connect errors unchanged)
```

These new tests in `session.rs` drive the pull interface directly:

- admission rejections are answered without reaching the endpoint
- `$/cancelRequest` answers a spawned request exactly once
- a panic while constructing or polling a handler is answered, and its admission is released
- a notification-task panic is isolated
- the first cause requested is the ending
- a reader failure ends the connection with its error
- a late required-send failure overrides an earlier cause
- an unanswered admitted request fails debug builds

They replace the session tests that lived in `engine.rs`, together with its test-only copy of `final_close_cause`.

Local runs on Windows:

- `ci/native-feature-command.sh test-workspace`: all 70 test binaries pass.
- `test-workspace-docs` passes.
- The fuzz driver regressions pass.
- clippy with `-D warnings` is clean on native maximal features, `stdio`, `tcp`, `websocket`, default features and wasm `worker-channel`.
- `ci/check-public-api.sh` reports compatible on all four targets.
- `ci/check-public-docs.sh` passes.

`stdio_child` (Unix-only) and the wasm test run were not exercised locally.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change is crate-private and the public API is unchanged, so a revert restores the old wiring.

**Blast Radius:** connection-wide

Every inbound message on both endpoints now goes through the new path. These differences are observable:

- **New telemetry:** the Client now emits `Rejected` completion telemetry.
- **Capacity during initialize:** if inbound capacity is exhausted while the Client is still initializing, the peer gets `ServerCancelled` instead of `ServerNotInitialized`.
- **Close-cause label during initialize:** a Client that fails initialize because its reader or writer ended now reports `reader_eof`, `reader_failed` or `writer_failed` instead of `initialize_failed`.
- **Log wording:** the EOF warning reads "transport closed by peer before the connection ended". The Client now logs it too. Client request panics log "panic isolated while dispatching request".
- **Request spans:** spawned Server request tasks are now also instrumented with their request span.

## 개요

HTB 승인제 풀이 에이전트에 (1) **명령 옵션 조합 변형(경우의 수)** 기능과 (2) 사용자가 제공한 **HTB 공식 라이트업 39종**을 학습데이터로 지식베이스화했습니다. 모두 **사용자가 직접 올린 자료만** 사용했으며 외부 라이트업을 검색·참조하지 않았습니다(P1 준수).

## 변경 내용

### 1. 명령 옵션 조합 변형 (`24b3b1d`)

### 2. 학습데이터 지식베이스화 (5개 팩, 96개 규칙)

| 팩 | 규칙 | 머신 |

author: juan-fernandez-gotherlabs
body:
## Why

AP integration must start from the active phase's recorded consumption, including HOLD invoices that were subsequently posted. An empty baseline can reuse GR/SES; filtering by the initial decision misses real journal effects.

## What changed

- Added a read-only ERP baseline joining PO positions, receipts, AP invoices/logs and every AP journal, with source SHA-256 values and scope validation.
- Connected the conservative historical quantity engine; ambiguous splits and reversals without restoration proof remain UNKNOWN. No FIFO or journal-date processing clock is inferred.
- Preserved unlinked AP journals as incomplete identities, without invented doc_ids. Kept invoice currency separate from the journal header and historical 407 currency.
- Strengthened the transaction guard: a recorded company/document identity cannot be reposted by changing supplier or currency.

## Why this approach

The adapter reuses the existing PO, duplicate, history and allocation engines. Original inputs remain untouched and Golden/provider access is unnecessary. This establishes the phase baseline; it does not claim the monthly document pipeline is complete.

## How to review

Read `ap_erp.py`, its integration tests and `docs/ap-erp.md`; inspect the company/document guard in `ap_transaction.py`. Refs #140; no issue is closed by this partial integration step.

## Validation

Original July source read: 1,520 PO positions, 21,699 receipts, 4,208 AP journals and 4,207 registered posted documents. One unlinked direct AP journal is preserved. Without an inferred processing clock, 10,461 receipts are demonstrably consumed, 67 available and 11,171 UNKNOWN. This is ERP reconstruction, not a July AP delivery or September validation.

Evidence saved locally in `outputs/m1-integration/erp-original-july.json`, `erp-id-guard-before.txt`, `erp-id-guard-after.txt`, and `erp-ap-suite.txt`.

## Testing

- 11 new ERP integration tests passed: resolved HOLD, unlinked/direct AP, accrual exclusion, currency, uncertainty, source mutation/path escapes and phase independence.
- The historical-ID regression reproduced a second posting with a changed supplier before the fix, and now rejects it before factories.
- 231 AP tests passed with original ERP enabled, zero skips. `git diff --check` passed.
- The backend CI workflow is absent; validation is local and no remote CI success is claimed.

body:
[Spec: icon legibility (#31)](https://github.com/yahyabedirhan/scoop/issues/31) | [#36 feat: ship the scale-up icon in white on green](https://github.com/yahyabedirhan/scoop/pull/36)

## Why the change

Now that Scale-up has shipped, the comparison tooling from the icon review is dead weight, so this puts the generator back to one pair of masters and releases the new icon as 0.0.8.

## Special things to note

- Every shipped PNG (the four extension icons and both README logos) and all 34 archive renders are byte-identical before and after `npm run gen-icons`, checked with `shasum -a 256`.
- `ICON_TILE` is still the one switch between `GREEN_TILE` (white on green, shipped) and `WHITE_TILE` (green on white).
- Loading the built extension in Chrome is manual and was not done here.

## Change outline

Scale-up's masters take over the top-level paths, and the review material leaves the tree.

```diff
 assets/
 ├── images/logo/
 │   ├── archive/                 # unchanged
-│   ├── scoop.svg                # was the icon before spec 05, variant `current`
-│   ├── scoop-16.svg
-│   └── variants/scale-up/{scoop,scoop-16}.svg
+│   ├── scoop.svg                # Scale-up's full master
+│   └── scoop-16.svg             # Scale-up's 16 px cut
 └── screenshots/
-    └── icon-legibility/         # review sheets for current and scale-up
```

The generator goes back to spec 04's shape. The masters' viewBox is the tile, so the span constants go too.

```diff
 main
   load_master(scoop.svg), load_master(scoop-16.svg)
+  fail if the two viewBoxes differ
   write icons/icon{16,32,48,128}.png in ICON_TILE
   write scoop.png (GREEN_TILE), scoop-on-white.png (WHITE_TILE)
-  --variant NAME  -> draw another variant
-  --review        -> toolbar.png, logo.png, overview.png
-Variant, variant_names, Sheet, FONT, SHIPPED, CURRENT, FIGURE_SPAN
```

`npm run icon-review` is removed from `package.json`. The icon tests drop the variant and review-image checks, and the logo-folder test no longer expects `variants/`. The README, `docs/scoop-v01.md`, spec 05's outcome and the changelog follow suit.

The release commit moves `manifest.json`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to 0.0.8 and turns the changelog's Unreleased entries into `[0.0.8] - 2026-10-03`, as the 0.0.7 release did.

## Things to be aware of

- **Decided alone:** I dropped the never-released "Icon variants" bullet from the changelog, since the feature no longer exists. I also renamed the moved masters' SVG `<title>` to drop "scale-up variant".
- **Surprises:** 0.0.7 had no git tag or GitHub release, so 0.0.8 gets none either.
- **Not in this PR:** The icon before spec 05 is not added to the archive as a render. It lives in git history and in the 0.0.7 README logo.
- **Follow-ups:** Todo for the maintainer: reload the unpacked extension from `dist/` in `chrome://extensions` to see 0.0.8.

## Summary
- Adds a macOS platform layer (`src/platform/macos/`): a Quartz event tap intercepts keys, IOHIDManager tells keyboards apart, and `CGEventPost` / AppKit inject keys, media keys and open the browser.
- Plain mappings to or from Caps Lock (`tab = capslock`, `capslock = tab`) are handed to the HID system with `hidutil`, because macOS toggles Caps Lock before the tap sees it. author: weichen-lf
body:
## Summary

Add an independent, read-only Historical Overview for exploring a household's accounts, cash, holdings, debts and allocation on a closed date. Compare another closed date or a captured current state, inspect valuation evidence, and filter changed rows.

## Rationale

A net-worth chart point does not explain the household's composition on that date. This view reconstructs past economic state from facts retained today; it does not claim to reproduce what the app knew at the time. Later corrections and historical price backfills can change the reconstruction.

## Main changes

- Read both sides from one immutable historical input batch, reusing replay and valuation without snapshot writes, provider refreshes or schema changes. Current comparisons remain fixed until explicit refresh.
- Compute totals and row differences in Go using exact decimals. Preserve native differences when FX is missing, keep unknown separate from zero, and never treat an absent account as a zero balance. Excluded archived FX gaps cannot invalidate eligible zero holdings.
- Resolve civil-day boundaries across skipped/repeated midnight while retaining market-date pricing. Reject skipped dates and explicitly error if the runtime cannot advance an extrapolated timezone interval.
- Add bounded date shortcuts, visible invalid-date states, total-change summaries, same-date guidance and changed-row filtering that retains offsetting child movements. Prevent duplicate refreshes and hide stale totals after a failed refresh or changed selection.
- Keep currency tokens intact in summaries and differences; choose metric columns from card width, with untruncated scrolling for oversized amounts. Add explicit horizontal table controls and arrow-key handling. Each step overlaps the unobscured area using the measured fixed-column width, preventing skipped content; release fixed labels when the viewport is too narrow.
- Add read-only detail sheets with parent-account context, exact amounts, household-zone source/cutoff timestamps and original UTC instants. Restore keyboard focus on sheet close and page exit; provide a horizontally scrollable comparison table with sticky account names and three-language copy.
- Keep the sheet viewport a non-scrollable clipping frame (`overflow: clip`). Native geometry tracing reproduced focus-induced `scrollLeft=448` on the previous hidden-overflow wrapper during slide-in; it persisted after animation and shifted the panel offscreen. Preserve the popup's own scrolling, viewport coordinates, Close and focus behavior.
- Anchor shared sheets to the visual viewport during native magnification and panning, preserving zoom, scrolling and dismissal. Retain a CSS viewport fallback and clean up resize/scroll listeners when the portal closes. Keep Close in the non-shrinking sticky title region in normal flow, with an icon and visible label, instead of a separately positioned child of the scrolling popup.
- Preserve default form focus after moving Close into the header: select the first usable content control while keeping Close in tab order. Respect explicit focus, autofocus, touch behavior and read-only fallback; use pinned `tabbable` 6.2.0 for candidate eligibility.
- Unmount current pages during historical browsing. Document current-metadata limitations and native acceptance cases. Names/classifications use current metadata; historical metadata versioning, member attribution, fixed-FX comparison and new return/contribution attribution are outside scope. Balance changes are not returns.

## Validation

- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go build ./cmd/nestworth` with output directed to a temporary validation binary.
- [x] Frontend lint, typecheck, production build and tests: **85 files / 730 tests passed**.
- [x] Generated Wails bindings verified; generated artifacts excluded per the repository workflow.
- [x] `gofmt -l cmd internal` is empty; `git diff --check` passes.
- [x] Full race suite passed during implementation; all Historical Overview application tests passed with race detection after the final backend changes.
- [x] Temporary SQLite tests cover read-only enforcement, consistent capture, corrected economic time, quote/FX gaps, archive/clearing, exact sub-cent amounts, neutral transfers/principal repayments and civil-date boundaries.
- [x] DOM regressions cover invalid/cleared dates, bounded shortcuts, native/unknown/absent deltas, duplicate and failed refreshes, late responses after exit/reopen, same-date comparisons, offsetting child changes, source-time context and focus restoration.
- [x] Shared-sheet regressions cover magnified/panned bounds, resize, Actual Size, reopening, fallback, focus restoration, dismissal and listener cleanup, plus the Close/header layout contract, disabled-state propagation, explicit focus and form autofocus. Fix an existing asynchronous loading assertion that also fails with the previous sheet implementation.
- [x] Reproduced three real directory creation focus failures before the fix. Regressions now cover default Name focus and direct typing without test-supplied overrides, account settings, instrument creation, keyboard access to Close, hidden/disabled controls and explicit opt-out/touch behavior.
- [x] Two new non-scrollable-frame regressions failed before the fix and pass at the measured 640/1280 CSS-pixel widths. The compiled production CSS contains `overflow: clip`; DOM tests guard the contract and do not claim WebKit pixel validation.
- [x] Exact-head [GitHub Actions run 37192615067](https://github.com/MnemosyneLab/NestworthGo/actions/runs/37192615067) passed: `test` and `race`, for `0df3c43178b9b942dbad4679d0c95315940a555d`.

## Screenshots or recordings

author: sheyda-fathi
body:
## What this PR adds

- `StandardScaler` (fit, transform, fit_transform, inverse_transform) with tests
- `notebooks/demo.ipynb`: learning rate experiment and feature scaling experiment
- `notebooks/real_data_comparison.ipynb`: gradient descent, normal equation and scikit-learn compared on a real dataset
- Figures in `docs/figures`

## Design decisions

- The scaler uses `ddof=0` (same as scikit-learn) and `np.ptp` to detect constant columns, so rounding errors cannot cause a division by almost zero
- The scaler is fitted on the training set only, to avoid data leakage
- The learning rate in the experiments is computed from the Hessian (`2 / lambda_max`), not guessed
- Gradient descent on the real data uses `tol=0.0`: the loss is flat near the minimum, so a stopping rule on the loss change can stop too early when `kappa` is large
- `sklearn` is used only in the notebook as a reference, never in `src/`

## Results

- Gradient descent, normal equation and scikit-learn agree on the coefficients (max difference below 1e-4, checked by an assert in the notebook)
- Standardizing the features reduced `kappa` from about 6e6 to about 1.2 in the synthetic experiment, and gradient descent went from a negative test R2 to the same R2 as the normal equation

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #112

Too many wrong passwords lock sign-in for a few minutes, and trying again during a lock no longer makes it longer. A lock on a connection shuts out everyone on it for a few minutes, administrators included, and then ends. Solvent keeps no address readable: a failed sign-in leaves a scrambled trace of the connection, deleted after about a quarter of an hour.

<details>
<summary>Technical part</summary>

- `solvent/ratelimit.py`: a refused request writes no row, so a lock runs from the failure that tripped it. The address limit counts failed sign-ins only and keys each address by a truncated HMAC-SHA256 under an HKDF subkey of `SECRET_KEY`. Username and address locks are rows of their own.
- Expired rows are pruned by a daemon pass, and legacy `ip:` rows are deleted at startup. Every connection sets `secure_delete`.
- `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` (default 0) applies `ProxyFix(x_for=N)`. `LOGIN_REQUESTS_PER_IP_HOUR` is refused at startup.
- gunicorn logs at error level with an access format carrying no peer address. Lockout log lines carry no address.
- Spec: `spec/architecture.md`, `spec/features/login.md`, `spec/features/app-shell.md` and related product, screen and compiled files.
- Regression test: `tests/test_attempts.py::test_an_administrator_signs_in_when_the_lock_ends_despite_retries_during_it`.
</details>

body:
## What & why

The New-Job modal and the Edit-recurring-rule modal each had their **own** "how often" control, and they didn't match — the edit screen was missing **Daily** entirely and figured out the cadence a different way. Past the mismatch you noticed, that hid a real bug: open a *daily* series to edit it and it showed **Weekly** selected, so saving quietly turned a daily clean into a weekly one.

Now both screens use **one shared picker** with the same seven options (Daily → Every 8 weeks, Monthly).

## How it behaves
- Same options, same look, in both places.
- The highlighted option is worked out from the *actual* cadence, so an older rule saved as "weekly, every 3 weeks apart" correctly reads back as **Every 3 weeks**, and a daily rule reads back as **Daily** (not Weekly).
- Picking **Daily** means "every day" unless you tap specific weekdays.

## Safety
Nothing about how series are stored or generated changed — this is purely the on-screen control. The edit screen also stops quietly seeding "Monday" onto a daily every-day rule (which would have narrowed it on save).

author: yashascoding
body:
## Description Fixes a bug where runs stopping at static breakpoints (`interrupt_before`/`interrupt_after`) on the legacy v1 streaming path were incorrectly reported as "success" with thread status "idle" while the thread remained paused. The v2 streaming path already behaved correctly. The root cause was in `graph_streaming._process_stream_event()`: when `updates` mode was not explicitly requested (default v1 case), interrupt updates were only forwarded if `__interrupt__` contained non-empty data. Static breakpoints emit `("updates", {"__interrupt__": ()})` with an empty tuple/list, so these events were dropped before reaching `run_executor._stream_legacy()`, leaving `has_interrupt` false and causing the run to be finalized as success. This change treats the presence of `__interrupt__` as an interrupt signal regardless of emptiness, matching v2 behavior and LangGraph's semantics for static interrupts. Dynamic `interrupt()` calls are unaffected since their `__interrupt__` payloads are non-empty. ## Type of Change - [x] `fix`: Bug fix - [x] `test`: Tests added/updated ## Related Issues Fixes #668 ## Changes Made - **Changed:** `graph_streaming._process_stream_event()` now forwards updates containing `__interrupt__` even when empty (treating presence as the interrupt signal) - **Updated:** Unit tests for graph streaming to reflect corrected behavior for empty interrupt lists/tuples - **Added:** Regression tests for empty interrupt handling in: - `TestProcessStreamEvent` (graph_streaming) - covers empty tuple/list cases - `TestStreamLegacyInterruptDetection` (v1 path) - verifies `_stream_legacy()` detects interrupts with empty `__interrupt__` - `TestStreamNativeV2InterruptDetection` (v2 path) - verifies empty interrupt handling ## Testing - [x] Unit tests added/updated (78 service unit tests pass including new regression tests) - [x] All existing unit tests continue to pass (1883 unit tests total) - [x] All existing integration tests continue to pass (2339 integration tests total) - [x] Linting, formatting, and security checks pass ## Checklist - [x] Code follows project style (Ruff formatting) - [x] All linting checks pass (`make lint`) - [x] Type checking passes (`make type-check`) - [x] All tests pass - [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits format (`fix(api): ...`) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Empty interrupt markers are now recognized consistently in streamed responses, including empty lists and tuples. * Interrupt updates are forwarded as values events, with subgraph namespaces preserved, including when interrupt filtering is enabled. * Previously accumulated output is retained when a legacy stream emits an interrupt-only event. Events that include other values continue to update the output. * Interrupts that arrive alongside state updates continue to apply those updates to the displayed output.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge; no new actionable issue was identified since the previous review.

Summary

The PR forwards empty static-breakpoint interrupt markers through legacy streaming and preserves partial run output when an interrupt-only values event arrives. - Adds unit coverage for empty interrupt markers and a real-graph static breakpoint. Follow-up to #91, which was merged before the review fixes landed. Built on main after P2d.4 (#95) and P2d.5 (#92). Supersedes #94.

## Visual review (six items)
1. **Stray bars at the transcript's right edge.** P2d.4's borderless transcript already removed them. Their cause was the `⚙` tool mark, which has an emoji form drawn two columns wide.
2. **Emoji tool mark.** P2d.5 (#92) already replaced `⚙` with `›` in the glyph set; that change is kept.
3. **Box drawing in the ASCII set.** P2d.5 had already removed box drawing from the ASCII set and folds what is left to `+ - |`; that is kept. In addition, in the ASCII set the phone header, the resources and PR strips, the inbox and the leader popup draw as **OpenCode-style panels without lines**. Tests now require the 45-column frame to be pure ASCII.
4. **Placeholder under the cursor.** In `ui::input`, a focused, empty prompt now draws its placeholder one column after the cursor, with the glyph set's ellipsis.
5. **account · model · mode shown twice.** On the chat tab the tab row leaves them to the prompt's meta line.
6. **"< leave".** That hint went away with P2d.4's composer. The phone's prompt now offers `esc done`, the spec's wording.

## Session de-duplication
A client paired with a host and with a vault that replicates it listed and counted every session twice. Now there is one copy per session id:
- the host's own copy while the host is paired here and connected;
- otherwise the vault's read-only copy, marked `vault` when the host is paired here but unreachable.

The tree (both groupings), project rows, roll-up counts, the attention list, the inbox, the phone summary and the session position all skip the copy that is stood in for. Covered by the reducer test `nav::tests::a_session_a_vault_replicates_is_listed_once_from_its_live_host`, with a fixture of a host plus a vault. It checks both groupings and that counts, inbox and summary count each session once. Then it drops the host and checks that the vault's copies take over, without the host's stale ones.

author: leothesouthafrican
body: A Marrow user can hold more than one live MCP bearer token. Issuing a new token no longer replaces the current one. Migration `057` copies each existing `user_settings.external_api_token_hash` into `external_api_tokens` without overwriting that hash. The copied row is named `existing token` and keeps authenticating. The old columns stay in place as a frozen snapshot. Creating a token does not write them. Revoking the copied token clears the snapshot so a later copy cannot resurrect it. Revoking any other token leaves the snapshot alone. MCP auth (`BearerTokenVerifier`) accepts any of the user’s live token hashes. Revoking one token leaves the others valid. Each new token has a name the user chooses. Settings → Integrations → External access tokens lists tokens by that name (and created time when one exists). The secret is shown once, above the list, and is not repeated on the row. The already-issued token appears as `existing token` because only the hash is stored. ## Test plan - [ ] Existing hash still authenticates after the copy - [ ] A second named token authenticates while the existing token still does - [ ] Revoking one token leaves the other valid - [ ] Settings list shows token names, not a second copy of the secret
