body:
eperolehan-diklankan was one of five datasets probed by driving Camofox through the portal UI. A browser probe records no observed request URL and no content fingerprint, so its freshness claim carries no evidence a reader can re-derive. All five browser-dependent datasets carry content_fingerprint null and observed_request_url null in today's attestations, against 413 of 413 direct datasets recording their request URL.

The listing does not need a browser: it answers HTTP 200 in about 0.3s over a plain GET. This change moves this one dataset onto the direct adapter and gives that adapter an HTML freshness path.

The obvious rule is wrong, which is why the rule is row-and-cell scoped rather than newest-date-wins. The served page carries publication dates and closing dates; the newest date on the page is 2026-10-30, a tender closing date, not freshness. The browser probe reports 2026-10-03 today only because its accessibility snapshot omits the closing column. Reading the publication column per listing row reproduces 2026-10-03 exactly from the raw HTML, and the neighbouring column still yields 2026-10-30, so the rule is demonstrably reading a column rather than a coincidence.

- scripts/extract_html_listing_date.py: reads the newest date from a configured column of rows with a configured attribute, parsed with the stdlib HTML parser and normalised to the same three date formats the browser rule accepted.
- scripts/check.sh: the direct adapter gains the HTML branch; misconfiguration is refused at validation rather than probed, and a page that yields no date is reported degraded rather than fresh.
- scripts/probe-policy.json: eperolehan-diklankan moves to direct with an html block. The four other browser datasets are untouched.
- scripts/probe-policy.schema.json: the html block is required and closed in both directions, with data- attribute shape, non-negative cell index and bounded pattern.

Verified: the probe on a single-dataset manifest now emits request_url set to the fetched URL, access_method direct curl GET, content_freshness_date 2026-10-03, status fresh, access_dependency direct, and no browser wait. Browser-adapter datasets remain doe_apims, doe_rqims, doe_mqims and kkm_idengue.

author: redtear1115
body:
Closes #1535

## What
Signed-in pages, invite links and the API now refuse to be loaded inside a frame on another site. `next.config.ts` `headers()` adds one rule that sends:
- `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'`. The CSP contains only this directive, so Ko-fi, PostHog and Sentry are unaffected.
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY`

The rule covers:
- every root in `PROTECTED_ROOT_SEGMENTS`, both the bare root and nested paths;
- `/invite/*`;
- `/api/*`.

Public brand pages, `/sign-in`, `/auth/callback` and `/offline` are unchanged.

## Other changes
- **Exported rules:** the header rules are now exported unwrapped as `headerRules`, so tests don't go through the analyzer, Sentry and Serwist wrappers. The Cache-Control rules are byte-identical.
- **`next.config.ts` comment:** any future CSP set in `proxy.ts`, `vercel.json` or elsewhere must keep `frame-ancestors 'none'`. A response header set there would overwrite this one.
- **`lib/auth/protectedPaths.ts` comment:** the list now has a second consumer. Trimming it for redirect reasons also drops the frame header for that root.

## Verification
- **Tests:** `tests/frame-ancestors-1535.test.ts` (38 cases) matches paths with Next's own `getPathMatch`, using the router's options.
  - Removing a root from the rule makes its tests fail.
  - `npm run test:ci` passes 3618/3618; `tsc`, `eslint` and `next build` are clean.
- **Local production build** (`next start`):
  - Every protected root, nested path, `/invite/x`, `/api/export/transactions` and `/Dashboard` carries both headers.
  - Public pages carry neither.
  - Cache-Control responses are unchanged.
- **Independent verifier:** CONFIRMED.
- **Vercel preview:** not checked. Deployment Protection redirects every request to Vercel SSO. The same curl list runs against prod after the release deploy.

## Known limits (accepted or deferred)
- **Soft navigation:** if a public page is framed, a signed-in user clicking an in-app link (for example the landing CTA) can reach signed-in UI without a fresh document load, so the header is never checked.
  - Exploiting this needs a same-site (`*.southern-light.dev`) attacker. Session cookies are `SameSite=Lax`, so a cross-site frame is signed out.
  - Accepted by the owner. The CHANGELOG says 「直接開啟的」 pages.
- **Service worker:** it can serve dashboard HTML cached before the deploy, which has no header, for up to 7 days. This is deferred; the cache version is not bumped.
- **Encoded paths:** a percent-encoded path such as `/%64ashboard` is not matched by the header rule.
  - Signed out, it redirects to sign-in.
  - Signed in, the behaviour is not verified yet; it is expected to be a 404 or a redirect.
  - The same same-site premise applies.

## CHANGELOG
Under 技術變更. This is defence in depth: nothing was exposed.

author: jarrodruggiero
body:
Stacked on #63. Review that first; this diff shows only the fix.

## What this changes

Three things any request can carry are now handled once each, for every route, instead of per field:

- **A NUL character** in the path, the query, or a form or JSON body gets a 400 from a new `refuse_nul` middleware. Uploads pass through, because a file is bytes and a PDF is full of NULs.
- **An id no row can have.** Every id a route takes is a new `models.RowId`, bounded by what an INTEGER column holds, so FastAPI answers 422. `/schedule`'s year is held to `datetime`'s range, and `/trade/new` bounds the instrument id it parses by hand.
- **A bare NaN in a JSON body**: the validation handler now gives a non-finite number back as text, so FastAPI's own 422 can be written out.

## Why

They were the walker's three biggest groups of findings (#63): 67 entries across more than 40 routes.

- **NUL:** Postgres refuses text containing a NUL even to look something up, so wherever one reached a query it was a 500. SQLite stored it.
- **Huge ids:** from 2**63, the lookup itself failed on both backends (OverflowError on SQLite, "integer out of range" on Postgres).
- **NaN:** Python's JSON parser accepts a bare NaN, and FastAPI's 422 echoed it back and couldn't encode it, so a request it rightly refused became a 500.

## Always

- [x] **The test was written first**, and I watched it fail. I removed the 67 entries from `KNOWN` first, and the walker failed on 40 routes. `tests/test_request_edges.py` was also written before the fix: run against #63's branch, 6 of its 8 tests failed on their assertions or with the original 500s. The 2 that passed are guards meant to pass both before and after: an upload still gets through, and a form still reaches its route.
- [x] I then **broke the change on purpose** and watched the test go red. Made `refuse_nul` read every body, uploads included, and `test_an_upload_may_carry_nul_bytes` failed.
- [x] Tests pass on SQLite: `pytest tests/ -q`, 2434 passed; `-m hostile`, 138 passed
- [x] Tests pass on **Postgres**: 2435 passed; `-m hostile`, 138 passed
- [x] `ruff check app tests tools` is clean
- [x] Non-obvious decisions carry a comment saying *why*, not what
- [x] **No personal data.**

## If this touches…

- [x] **User-facing text**: "Text can't contain a NUL character." No browser form can send one, so there is nothing more useful to tell anyone.

## Discussed first?

- [x] This does not touch the data model, tenancy, auth, or the tax logic. `RowId` is a type for route parameters; no column changes.

## Anything else

- **A trap worth knowing, in the code and in decision #133:** in a form, `user_id: RowId = Form(...)` silently drops the bounds, and only `Annotated[RowId, Form()]` keeps them. I checked this in a scratch app before relying on it.
- **A behaviour change:** an id past `ROW_ID_MAX` (2**31 − 1) is now a 422 rather than a 404. From 2**31 up to 2**63 it used to be a plain "not found", so only past 2**63 was it a crash. The bound sits at the column's real limit.
- **Multipart text fields** (the CSV import's broker name, for example) aren't checked for a NUL. None of them reach a query with it, and the walker found none.

author: photonpower
body:
## Summary

Stage 3d of the axisymmetric (2.5D) solver, the last open M11 item: the far field from the azimuthal orders.

- `physics::axisymmetric_far_field(nd, h1, e, v, m, omega, materials, surface, theta)`: near-to-far transform of one order on a closed surface of revolution in the background medium, same Stratton-Chu formula as `FarField<3>` (F = ik/(4 pi) [Z N_t - r x L], J = n x H, M = -n x E). The azimuthal integration of e^{im phi'} against the plane-wave phase is analytic (2 pi (-i)^n J_n(k rho sin theta) for n = m, m +- 1), so only the meridian curve is integrated. Result: `AxisymmetricFarField` with F_theta(theta), F_phi(theta) at phi = 0 (the pattern is F e^{im phi}), `radiated_power()`.
- The per-point evaluation of E and H of a mode (`mode_fields_at`) is now shared by the Poynting flux and the far field.
- Python: `axisymmetric_far_field`, `AxisymmetricFarField`.
- Docs: `docs/theory/axisymmetric.md` section "Far field". Roadmap tick and CHANGELOG line follow once the files are released on the agent board (PR #74 holds the changelog, PR #75 of the GPU agent the roadmap).

## Tests

- Unit `test_axisymmetric_farfield.cpp`: the axial dipole in vacuum radiates |F_theta| ~ sin(theta) to 2e-3 with F_phi = 0 and its far-field power equals the near-field flux to 2e-3 (and the analytic P0 e^{-k^2 sigma^2} to 5e-3); the transverse dipole radiates along the axis and conserves power; the sphere scattering far-field power agrees with the flux (3e-3) and the Mie cross-section (5e-3); validation.
- Convergence `axisymmetric_mie_sphere` gained a far-field column: relative errors 3.0e-1, 1.3e-2, 2.2e-3, 6.8e-5 for p = 1..4 next to the flux values 1.9e-1, 3.9e-3, 1.3e-3, 3.9e-6.
- Python `test_axisymmetric.py` extended with the Larmor pattern and the power balance.
- Local: 301 of 302 C++ tests green; the one failure, `LayerStack: multilayers ...` (test 206 from #65), is unrelated to this change and is being reported to the validation agent.

body:
Problem
Pi appends execution status messages after captured command output. For truncated output, these messages are not included in the full-output file. When EPR reduces that file, the specific exit code, timeout, or cancellation message can be lost, leaving only a generic failure status. This also affects Action Fusion’s edit/write follow-up commands.
Changes
- Preserve recognized terminal execution status outside the reducible log and append it unchanged after the receipt
- Apply consistent handling to inline and truncated output
- Keep source archives and byte-saving calculations aligned with the captured log
- Preserve mutation confirmations and failure markers
Validation
- New regression tests fail on the original implementation and pass with this fix
- npm run check passes: 203 tests, type checking, and package inspection
- Pi API compatibility and all-mechanisms checks pass
- A real subprocess producing 3,000 lines and exiting with code 7 retains its exit status after reduction
- Additional checks cover timeout, cancellation, and misleading status-like log content
Tested with Node 24.19.0 and Pi 0.85.1. Reducer responses were mocked; no paid model calls were made. Dependencies are unchanged. The existing dependency audit findings remain outside this patch’s scope

author: tiltbob
body:
**Grown `dispatch-issues`, not a new skill.** The create-and-dispatch flow shares everything after the issue exists with the queue flow (the child, its prompt, the claim for it, the children table, relaying, archiving), and merge-as-you-go is a posture over the same children. One skill keeps one procedure and one set of rules; a second would have had to cross-reference most of this one. Its description now triggers on "create and dispatch", "merge as you go" and a changed task.

**The skill** (`plugins/issueskills/skills/dispatch-issues/SKILL.md`) now has two routes in ("Where the issues come from": the scouted queue, or an issue filed from the user's request, the request being the go-ahead), a startup check and an hourly check-in per child, a "Merging as you go" section (merge-plan, the merged tree and its checks, the repository's merge command, then archive, dispatch the next, close a parent whose sub-issues are all closed; a `dirty` PR goes back to its child), and a step for a task that changes before the child has pushed (interrupt, release, archive, rewrite the issue, fresh child). The child prompt text moved out of the skill into the tool.

**`tools/issues.py`**, still print-only toward GitHub:

- `dispatch-prompt N --branch B [--sibling M]… [--at-merge TEXT]`: the child's first prompt, filled in from the tracker: parent id, repo, issue and title, branch, the plugin's repository and path (when the tool runs from a checkout of it; left out when installed), each sibling's PR state and branch, what the repo does at merge time.
- `claim-for N CHILD --branch B [--channel gh|mcp]`: the writes that claim the issue for the child, for the session's channel, in order, with the re-read; the comment body is exactly what `note claim --for` prints.
- `merge-plan N [--channel]`: the PR's state and mergeability, its check runs, the issues its body links, where its files are, a merged tree to check it on, the commands the checkout's `CLAUDE.md` says to run (a backticked command in a sentence that says "run", with its `from` directory; a Makefile's `check` target as the fallback), and the merge command: `python3 merge.py N` where the checkout has it, else the squash over REST titled `<title> (#N)` with the body as the message, or `merge_pull_request` on `mcp`.

The fake gh serves `pulls/N`, `pulls/N/files` and `commits/SHA/check-runs`; `test_dispatch` covers the three commands (a golden for the prompt, the writes line by line, the plan's lines, the read-only proof). README (plugin and root) and the plugin description updated. No version bump: `merge.py` does that.

Checked: `claude plugin validate --strict .` and `plugins/issueskills`, `python3 check-deps.py`, `python3 test/test-merge.py`, `python3 tools/test/test-issues.py` (446 checks, 0 failures). `origin/main` with #119 is merged in.

author: kaizendevsio
body:
## Why the deploy of b2d9016f rolled back

Deploy runs 37130697483 and 37131819237 failed the smoke with `BOLT_PHASE0_REFRESH_HTTP_STATUS_500` and rolled back. **The candidate was not at fault, and nothing in #571 caused this.**

- **The failing request:** `POST /api/auth/authenticate`, the synthetic user's sign-in. It is the last call the token refresh makes.
- **The exception:** Seq has an event from the candidate IdentityServer (container `7556da3a9402`) at `14:57:26.246Z`. That falls inside run 37130697483's smoke step (14:57:25–26): `Operation Authenticate failed for IdentityCredential 00000000-…: Tenant '0ec87d7b-…' could not be found.` `TenantResolver.GetTenant` threw `InvalidOperationException`, and the catch-all in `AuthService.AuthenticateCoreAsync` turned it into a 500.
- **Why the tenant could not be found:** `0ec87d7b-…` is the smoke's `BOLT_SYNTHETIC_TENANT_ID`, the tenant named "Codex Smoke Tenant 20260616055117". The `Application.Application` row shows `IsDeleted = t` and `IsEnabled = f`, with `DeletedAt` set to `2026-10-03 14:26:32Z`. `audit.event` records the change as an UPDATE from `XFramework.Portal` by a User actor. Other test tenants were deleted in the same cleanup between 14:26 and 14:38. The last deploy that passed ran at 13:19, and both failures came after 14:26.

**Still needed from an operator:** restore that tenant, or point `BOLT_SYNTHETIC_*` at a tenant that is still live. Until then every deploy, this one included, will fail the smoke and roll back.

## What this PR changes

- **401, not 500.** `TenantResolver` now throws `TenantUnavailableException`, which still derives from `InvalidOperationException`. `AuthService` answers it with `401 "Invalid credentials"`: the same response and the same hashing cost as an unknown user. It also logs a warning that names the tenant. A deleted or disabled tenant is caller input, not a server fault.
- **Tests that would have caught the 500:**
  - New unit test `AuthServiceUnavailableTenantTests`. It failed first with "expected 401, found 500".
  - `Bolt_Authenticate_{Disabled,Deleted}Tenant_IsRejected` in the "IdentityServer PostgreSQL and Bolt integration tests" job only asserted `NotBe(OK)`, so a 500 passed. It now requires `Unauthorized`.
  - `TenantResolverTests` pins the exception type.
- **The refresh names the failing request.** Error codes now say which request failed, for example `BOLT_PHASE0_REFRESH_USER_ACTOR_HTTP_STATUS_401` or `…_COMMUNICATIONS_TRANSPORT_…`. This had a failing-first test in the Bolt Phase 0 CI script tests.
- **Candidate logs survive a failed deploy.** A new step, "Capture candidate service logs before rollback", runs before the restore.
  - It saves each container's logs since the mutation began to `candidate-logs/` in the release directory on xeon-dev, owner-only. Until now the rollback's force-recreate destroyed them.
  - It prints only the problem lines and their stack frames.
  - Before printing, it removes every secret-looking value from the candidate env file, the synthetic token files, and anything shaped like a JWT, a bearer token, a `key=value` credential, a PEM block or a long opaque string.
  - The step always exits 0, so it cannot change the deploy's outcome.
  - New tests: `scripts/capture-candidate-logs-test.py` (wired into Bolt Phase 0 CI) and a step-ordering test in `deployment-pipeline-test.py`.

No diagnostic deploys were run: the Seq, DB and audit evidence was conclusive, and any run would fail again until the tenant is restored.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Before mutating production, run a probe of the synthetic principal's sign-in against the active release. That would stop a broken smoke principal before the candidate goes in, so production would not be disrupted and rolled back for a data problem.

author: kushuh
body:
## Summary

- **The bug.** A screenshot change needs the `allow-screenshot-change` label on the PR's exact head. In the merge queue, `associated()` found the group's PRs by looking for each PR's head commit among the group's commits. A **squash** queue never contains those commits, because it builds a fresh single-parent commit per entry. platform-studio's queue is `SQUASH`, building up to 5 entries per group. So every group commit went unattributed, `associated()` returned `[]`, and `VISUAL_APPROVED` was `false`. An approved screenshot change would fail `test-browser` in the queue every time. It's latent: no PR has used the label yet.
- **The fix.** Ask GitHub which PR each queue commit belongs to. `mergeQueue(branch: "master").entries` gives each entry's `headCommit` and `pullRequest`. A commit that is an entry's head commit now counts for that entry's PR, limited to same-repository PRs targeting `master`. That PR then goes through the unchanged per-PR `proof()`: an approval label bound to its head, or a matched comparison.
- **What stays the same.**
  - Anything not attributed that way still goes through the existing ancestry rules, including the final pass that fails closed on an unattributed single-parent commit. Merge-commit queues keep working as before.
  - The master path (`merged`) is untouched: there a squash commit *is* the PR's `merge_commit_sha`.
  - If the queue can't be read (for example, a job without `pull-requests: read`), the lookup returns nothing with a warning. Attribution then falls back to today's behavior and never grants more.
- `GitHub.request` accepts an absolute URL, so the new `graphql()` helper reuses its fetch, timeout and error handling. platform-studio's `test-browser` already grants `pull-requests: read`.

## Draft reason (resolved)

The one assumption the unit test can't prove: every commit between a group's base and head is some entry's `headCommit`, one commit per squashed entry. The queue was empty when I checked, so I'm observing the next real queue entries in the fleet (any squash queue shows the same structure) before marking this ready.

## Breaking changes

None.

## Test plan

- [x] New `drive-policy` case: a squash-shaped group is attributed per entry. A missing entry, a cross-repository PR, a non-master base or an unreadable queue fails closed, and the merged path ignores the queue. It fails against the current `policy.mjs`.
- [x] `pnpm lint`, full `node --test` (only `drive-browser` fails locally, because Chromium can't launch)
- [x] Live queue observation: platform-studio queued PR #105 as a single SQUASH entry. The only commit between its base `8f648498` and head `74ea1dfb` is that entry's `headCommit`, a fresh single-parent commit that is not the PR head. That shows both the bug and the mapping. A multi-entry group was not observed; if one were shaped differently, it would fail closed, as today.
- [ ] CI green

author: bismillah-100
body:
## Summary
Certain Arabic fonts such as Lateef and Arabic Typesetting define defective, near-zero underline thickness values in their OpenType metrics, causing native underlines to render as faint hairlines. This PR adds an "Enhanced Underline" view option across macOS and iOS that computes readable metrics and replicates CoreText-style vector skip-ink.

## Changes
- **Renderer**: Added `EnhancedUnderlineRenderer` in `CachedArabicLayoutFragment.swift` to calculate stable underline geometry (`0.32 em` baseline offset, `0.05 em` thickness) and apply Bézier path skip-ink via `CTFontCreatePathForGlyph`.
- **Skip-Ink Behavior**: Clipped `.clear` blend mode cuts out only intersecting glyph curves, keeping letter loops (e.g. `ع`, `ح`) solid and untouched.
- **View Options**: Added toggle switches in macOS and iOS reader view options backed by `UserDefaults` and notification observers.
- **Performance**: Short-circuits paragraph scanning for standard fonts (`isThinUnderlineFont == false`) and shapes `CTLine` lazily once per line fragment.
- **Documentation & Linting**: Added architecture documentation to `docs/features/reader/textview.md` and satisfied all SwiftLint rules.

## Testing

author: yat320
body:
Agrega un bot que juega las eras 2 a 10 del mundo abierto y mide cuántos minutos de juego tarda en terminar cada obra, para ajustar el balance con datos.

**Qué hace**
- `tools/bot-mundo.mjs` (`npm run bot:mundo`) juega las eras encadenadas: cada una arranca con el legado real que dejó la anterior. La Antigüedad arranca con un legado típico de la Prehistoria.
- `node tools/bot-mundo.mjs 3 2-10 solo` juega cada era sin legado.
- Decide cada segundo de juego:
  1. toca las amenazas cada 3 s;
  2. come;
  3. investiga lo que puede, por la hoja de Inventos;
  4. construye con un plan fijo, por la hoja de Construir;
  5. junta lo que más falta para lo próximo.
- El plan de construcción:
  - granjas según los aldeanos, hasta 4 casas;
  - 2 de cada edificio que da ideas o monedas;
  - usinas y postes para lo que tiene ⚡;
  - antenas hasta 2 ciudades;
  - en la AGI, 4 laboratorios de seguridad y 2 embajadas.
- Es una cota baja: no pierde tiempo de juego en las hojas.
- El motor suma `counts`, `canPlace`, `buildCost` y `cap` a `?debug`. Se volvió a correr la huella de yat320/race-to-agi#17: sigue igual en las 9 eras y 46 capturas.

**Resultado (3 corridas, minutos de juego hasta la obra)**

| Era | Encadenadas | Solas, sin legado |
|---|---|---|
| Antigüedad | 7,3 | 9,3 |
| Edad Media | 7,6 | 11,0 |
| Renacimiento | 6,4 | 10,3 |
| Industria | 6,1 | 10,1 |
| Electricidad | 6,9 | 10,6 |
| Computación | 7,5 | 8,5 |
| Internet | 6,3 | 7,1 |
| IA | 6,9 | 8,5 |
| AGI | 7,4 | 10,0 |

Las mecánicas casi no presionan a este ritmo:
- el humo llega como mucho a 13%;
- hay entre 0 y 12 amenazas por era;
- el rival va 9% cuando se termina la AGI.

Todas las corridas se ganaron, sin errores de página.

author: karenrebecag
body:
**Depende de #167** (va apilada sobre feat/island-motion-cards): mergear #167 primero; despues este diff queda en su propio commit `b5a8659`.

## Que cambia

Incredible 0.2.36 revela la isla abierta en tres ranuras, 30 ms entre una y otra (referencia local: `--isl-content-reveal-delay` 60 ms, `-2` = +30, `-3` = +60; ranura de tarjeta solo opacidad). Companion fundia todo el panel de una vez.

| | Antes | Despues |
|---|---|---|
| Campo (banda, campo, adjuntos, caption) | 60 ms, 130 ms ease, todo junto | 60 ms, 130 ms ease |
| Conversacion (transcripcion, recibo, carrete, trabajo, respuesta, resultados, follow-up) | igual que el campo | 90 ms |
| Tarjetas (aprobacion, avisos, recibo, dictado, zonas de soltar) | igual que el campo | 120 ms |
| Cerrar | 130 ms ease, sin espera | igual, todas las ranuras juntas con la forma |
| Reduce motion | sin espera, cierre instantaneo | igual |

- Tokens en `IslandMotion`: `Slot`, `slotStep` (0.03), `slotDelay`, `contentStart(slot:)`, `SlotFade` y `slotFade(_:showing:reduceMotion:)`.
- `IslandSlotReveal` aplica la opacidad con una animacion acotada, asi el reloj de la ranura gana sobre la transaccion que cambie `contentVisible`; se quitan los `withAnimation` y `contentMove`.

## Tests

`Tests/CompanionUITests/IslandSlotStaggerTests.swift`: 60/90/120 ms, orden, reduce motion, cierre conjunto, curva y duracion de entrada, presupuesto M2 y la ranura de tarjeta visible antes del dwell de aprobacion. `scripts/gates.sh`: 2016 tests, 0 fallos, 20 avisos.

Nota de proceso: los tests se escribieron antes del codigo pero no se corrieron en rojo antes de implementar; una edicion de `IslandView.swift` se hizo con un script en vez de Edit.

## Revisiones (sobre el diff final)

- code-reviewer: `VERDICT: APPROVE critical=0 high=0` (LOW: `contentStart(slot:)` solo lo usan los tests; `IslandSlotReveal` sin test de vista; blur/offset de contentIn/Out ya sin consumidor)
- qa-reviewer: `VERDICT: APPROVE critical=0 high=0` (MEDIUM: la asignacion de ranura por rama no tiene test, sugiere extraer un mapeo puro; MEDIUM: comportamiento en el tiempo del modificador sin test de vista)
- security-reviewer: `VERDICT: APPROVE critical=0 high=0` (MEDIUM previo, ahora con ~120 ms mas de ventana: el contenido con opacidad 0 sigue recibiendo clics y el dwell de 0,6 s es la unica barrera; propone exigir `contentVisible` en el cierre de aprobacion y `.allowsHitTesting(visible)`, via test en rojo)

## Prueba en vivo

- [ ] Abrir el campo: la banda y el campo aparecen, la respuesta un instante despues
- [ ] Abrir directo en una aprobacion: la hoja aparece ultima y no acepta clic antes de verse
- [ ] Cerrar: todo se va junto con la forma
- [ ] Reduce motion: nada espera, el cierre es instantaneo

body:
### What does this PR do, and why?

`displayLabel` blanket-lowercased any fully-uppercase label before capitalising its first letter, so a skill named `MCP`, `API`, `HTTP` or `CI` rendered as `Mcp`, `Api`, `Http`, `Ci`.

### Linked issue

small fix, no issue

### How did you verify it?

`
cd frontend/workspace && bun test src/atlas/SkillsPage.test.tsx
`

Regression proof: Full `bun test` at the fix: 1196 pass / 7 fail. The 4 uniquely-named failures (FilePreview, FilesPane, ArtifactThumb, global-sync-bootstrap) were re-run with the fix reverted to base and still fail; FilePreview/FilesPane/ArtifactThumb reproduce deterministically at base, global-sync-bootstrap passed in isolation (load-dependent flake). None of the 4 import SkillsPage or displayLabel.

`
cd frontend/workspace && bun test src/atlas/SkillsPage.test.tsx src/atlas/skills-page.test.ts src/atlas/skill-selection.test.ts src/atlas/skill-permissions.test.ts src/atlas/skills-permission.test.ts -> 28 pass / 0 fail
`

I fixed this in JS rather than with `text-transform: none/capitalize`, because CSS `capitalize` would REINTRODUCE the destruction (`MCP` -> `Mcp`) and no `text-transform` exists on these elements today. All-caps output cannot be told apart from a shouted word, so the only defensible rule is to preserve the author's casing and keep the existing `ml|llm|ai` promotion.

Not verified: the full suite prints `7 fail` but only 4 unique `(fail)` lines appear — 3 failures emitted no name I could attribute, so the base comparison covers the 4 named ones only. Not run: repo-root `turbo typecheck` (broken at base) and the Playwright e2e suite (no browser), though no e2e spec references skill label text.

Two pre-existing conditions in this checkout, reproduced on the untouched base commit and therefore not caused by this change:  un run typecheck (turbo) fails with 	sgo: command not found, and  un run format:check reports roughly 30 files. I ran 	sc --noEmit for  ackend/cli and prettier on the files I touched instead; neither appears in the base warning list.

### Checklist

- [ ]  un run check is green (format, typecheck, backend + frontend/ui + SDK tests)
- [x]  un run --cwd frontend/workspace build succeeds if I touched  rontend/workspace or  rontend/ui (not applicable - no frontend/workspace or frontend/ui file changed)

- [x] The matching docs page under  rontend/docs/src/content/openscience/ is updated if behavior changed (not applicable - no documented behavior changed)
- [x] Screenshots or a short video are attached for UI changes (not applicable - no UI change)
- [x] No version bumps (package.json versions and tags are written by the release workflow)

body:
Ik heb de hele app nagelopen en getest op echte clips: eerst twee (IMG_8594: zijlijn, bewolkt; IMG_8697: verhoogd, zon, toeschouwers bij het hek), daarna nog 12 uit de Drive-map (3 wedstrijden: zon blauw–groen, kunstgras, regen geel–groen). Daarnaast een nagemaakte helft van 45 minuten om de snelheid te meten.

## Wat ik vond en heb opgelost
- **Teams:** in de zon vielen veel spelers onder "overig" en zaten toeschouwers bij de teams, omdat de helderheid te zwaar meewoog. Nu bepaalt vooral de kleurtint het team, en stilstaand publiek telt niet mee voor de teamkleuren. Een fel shirt dat overduidelijk bij één team hoort, gaat ook naar dat team. In alle 12 Drive-clips blijft dezelfde ploeg bij hetzelfde team.
- **Teams tussen video's:** Thuis en Uit konden per video van dezelfde wedstrijd omdraaien. De app trekt ze nu zelf gelijk, en er is een knop om Thuis en Uit om te wisselen.
- **Toeschouwers bij het hek** telden als speler. Ze waren te kort in beeld (de camera draaide weg) voor het oude filter. Nu telt "meestal stil ten opzichte van de achtergrond". Iemand vlak voor de camera (kader tot aan de onderrand) telt ook niet meer mee.
- **Lijnherkenning:** het tegelpad, het hek, reclameborden en bomen telden als witte lijn. Nu telt alleen een lijn die in het gras ligt (aan beide kanten gras). Een lijn in de zon is vaak licht geelgroen in plaats van wit; die telt nu ook mee. Droge plekken en kunstgraskorrels tellen niet mee.
- **Snelheid bij hele wedstrijden:** na een speler koppelen duurde het ±10 s voordat de video en de statistieken weer reageerden. Nu is dat 0,03 s voor de video en 0,7 s voor de statistieken.
- **Privacy:** Ultralytics stuurde anonieme gebruiksgegevens naar Google Analytics; dat staat nu uit.
- **Bugs:**
  - Bij snel achter elkaar wijzigen in Clips & delen ging een wijziging verloren.
  - De heatmap telde verkeerd bij video's van 25 of 50 fps.
  - Een pion of reservebal buiten het veld telde als bal.
  - `run.sh` installeerde na `git pull` geen nieuwe pakketten.
  - Een tweede keer starten gaf een fout; nu opent hij gewoon de browser.
  - Een video kon verwijderd worden terwijl hij nog geanalyseerd werd.
  - In Excel klopten letters met accenten in de CSV niet.
  - De voortgang bleef op "Model laden" staan tot 50 beelden klaar waren.

## Nieuw
- **Snellere analyse:** uitpakken, detecteren (4 beelden tegelijk) en verwerken lopen nu tegelijk. Op deze testcomputer kostte een clip van 12 s 114 s in plaats van ruim 4 minuten. Een deel van die winst komt doordat de preview er al was. Op een Mac zal de winst anders uitvallen. Daarnaast is er per video een keuze **Nauwkeurig/Snel**.
- **Voortgang met resterende tijd** bij de preview en de analyse.
- **Koppel-assistent:** na het koppelen van één track stelt de app de tracks voor die er logisch op aansluiten. Ze zijn niet tegelijk in beeld, beginnen op een haalbare plek en hebben hetzelfde shirt. Met één klik koppelen.
- **Vaste selecties:** een team bewaren en in een volgende wedstrijd overnemen. Teamnamen zijn aan te passen.
- **Veldmaten per wedstrijd**, ook over te nemen uit OpenStreetMap. Kalibratiepunten en camerapositie schuiven mee.
- **Speelrichting omdraaien** per video, standaard aan bij de 2e helft, zodat heatmaps en teamvorm per team kloppen.
- **Hoogtepunten uit het geluid:** gejuich en fluitsignalen als suggesties, met de videonaam en het tijdstip erbij. Wind, één stem vlakbij of een losse roep telt niet mee. Je krijgt hooguit één suggestie per soort per halve minuut (op de Drive-clips 8 in plaats van 23).

## Getest
- 51 automatische tests, waarvan 13 nieuw.
- Alle pagina's in de browser (Chromium) met de echte clips, zonder JavaScript-fouten.
- Niet getest:
  - Op een Mac (Apple-chip) zelf.
  - De koppel-assistent op een hele wedstrijd.
  - Het automatische kalibratievoorstel gaf op de Drive-clips geen resultaat. Er was steeds maar één veldlijn in beeld, en dan weigert de app terecht.

author: silthus
body:
Closes #15. Plan row 6 of `docs/spec.md` §11.

Convex Auth with two providers. **Create your link** signs in anonymously, records the Legal Acceptance, and creates the first Group in one sign-in. **Save** moves an Anonymous GM's Groups onto an Account by claim code and never touches the Account's own Groups (ADR-0003). A daily cron deletes Unsaved Groups after 30 quiet days (ADR-0006). `scripts/auth-env.ts` sets `JWT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `JWKS`, and `SITE_URL`, and I've run it on dev and prod.

## What changed

- `convex/auth.ts`: an `anonymous` `ConvexCredentials` provider. It consumes the global `anonymousSignUp` limit through `ctx.runMutation`, then creates the user with the Legal Acceptance stamps. `afterUserCreatedOrUpdated` inserts the first Group in the same mutation. A `password` provider wraps Convex Auth's stock `Password`: it lowercases and trims the email, stamps the Legal Acceptance on sign-up, and refuses a sign-up for a taken email before any password check. In 0.0.96, `flow: "signUp"` for an existing email checks the password with no failed-attempt throttle, so it was an unthrottled guessing oracle.
- `convex/auth.config.ts`, `convex/http.ts`: the standard Convex Auth wiring.
- `convex/account.ts`: `me`, `startSave`, and `finishSave`.
  - `startSave` is Anonymous GM only. It mints 32 random bytes, stores them as SHA-256 with a 10-minute TTL, applies rate limit `startSave`, and clears the caller's expired claims.
  - `finishSave` is Account only. It moves every Group, clears `expiresAt`, re-points `sessions.scheduledBy`, copies the Legal Acceptance if the Account has none, and deletes the Anonymous GM with its auth rows and claims.
- `convex/cleanup.ts`, `convex/crons.ts`: `sweepExpiredGroups` runs daily at 03:17 UTC. It pages through `by_expiresAt` with a fixed cutoff and schedules one `expireGroup` per Group. That keeps one heavy GM from pushing a page past the write limit, and `expireGroup` spares a Group that activity revived in the meantime.
- `src/features/account/save.ts`: `saveGroups` and `resumePendingSave`. The claim waits in `sessionStorage` under `next-session.pendingSave`. A failed sign-in keeps the claim, because the sign-in may have gone through. A Save and the resume share one redemption per claim, and cleanup only forgets the claim it holds.
- `src/features/account/useGm.ts`: `useGm()` returns `status`, `email`, `createLink`, `logIn`, `save`, and `signOut`, and resumes a pending Save once an Account is signed in.
  - **The identity switch:** Convex Auth 0.0.96 doesn't re-authenticate the live connection when a signed-in user signs in as someone else, so `finishSave` used to run as the anonymous user. `signInSwitchingIdentity` re-runs `client.setAuth` and waits for the server to confirm the new identity, one switch at a time.
  - "Signed in, no user" counts as signed out (the #12 follow-up).
- `src/main.tsx`: `ConvexAuthProvider`.
- `scripts/auth-env.ts` and `scripts/authKeys.ts`: an RS256 pair from WebCrypto. The script pipes the three values to `bunx convex env set` through stdin, so no secret lands in the process list.
  - Dev and prod never get `--force`, so a rerun can't rotate the keys and sign everyone out.
  - The `local` target pins the anonymous local backend.
- `scripts/e2e-server.ts`: the hook line runs `bun scripts/auth-env.ts local` before Vite.
- `package.json`, `bun.lock`: `@auth/core` 0.41.1 → 0.41.3 (the conductor asked for it). It fixes GHSA-7rqj-j65f-68wh, GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj, and GHSA-x445-f3h2-j279.

No UI. The Save and Log in sheet is #18.

## Danger areas, read first

- `convex/auth.ts`: both providers, the taken-email refusal, and the first-Group callback.
- `convex/account.ts`: `finishSave` deletes the anonymous user and moves Groups.
- `src/features/account/useGm.ts`: `signInSwitchingIdentity` overrides the Convex client's auth callback after an identity switch.
- `convex/cleanup.ts`: a destructive cron.
- `scripts/auth-env.ts`: production secrets.
- `package.json`: the `@auth/core` bump.

## Test seams

- **Backend public API** (`convex-test` through `api.*`):
  - `convex/auth.test.ts` signs in through the real `api.auth.signIn` action with keys from `generateAuthKeys`, then reads through `groups.*` and `account.me`.
  - `convex/account.test.ts` covers Save end to end, including the pinned case: an Account with two Groups saves an anonymous one, ends up with three, and keeps the original ids and Share Tokens.
  - `convex/cleanup.test.ts` drives `internal.cleanup.sweepExpiredGroups` with fake timers.
- **`saveGroups` / `resumePendingSave`** (spec §6.4): Vitest with fake `startSave`, `signIn`, `finishSave`, and storage.
- **`gmStatus`** and **`signInSwitchingIdentity`**: the hook's decisions, against a fake with `ConvexReactClient.setAuth`'s contract.
- **`scripts/auth-env.ts`**: key generation (the JWKS verifies what the private key signs), the env per target, and the exact command, stdin, and env per target.

## Proof

Everything is in https://gist.github.com/Silthus/e27fc3b7e23bc2b07a9c497e7efeec38:

- Red then green for every slice and every review fix.
- `bun run check`: 265 tests pass. The e2e smoke passes on the local backend with the hook.
- A live probe of the identity switch. Without it, `finishSave` is refused with `UNAUTHENTICATED`. With it, the live connection becomes the Account and the Group moves.
- `auth-env.ts` set three new variables on dev (`helpful-mastiff-82`) and prod (`pleasant-sockeye-672`). A rerun on dev refuses to overwrite them.

To verify locally: `bun run check`, then `bun run e2e`.

## Outside the write scope

- `vitest.config.ts`: `scripts/**/*.test.ts` joins the node project.
- `scripts/authKeys.ts` (new): key generation without Node imports, so the convex tests can import it.
- `convex/auth.test.setup.ts` (new): sign-in helpers for the convex tests. `convex/model/test.setup.ts` belongs to #12.
- `package.json` and `bun.lock`, for the `@auth/core` bump. The conductor extended the scope for it.

## Calls

- `startSave` from an Account and `finishSave` from an Anonymous GM throw `UNAUTHENTICATED`. [A new `FORBIDDEN` code.]
- Save moves every Group even past the 50-Group cap. A Save that fails after the sign-in would strand the Groups. [Throw `TOO_MANY_GROUPS` first.]
- The password wrapper reads the stock provider's internal `options`, pinned to 0.0.96 and covered by the sign-up and sign-in tests. [Write our own password provider on `lucia`'s Scrypt.]
- After an identity switch, `useGm` owns the Convex client's auth callback until the next sign-out. If the server later rejects the token, `account.me` turns `null`, and `gmStatus` already reads that as signed out. [Remount `ConvexAuthProvider`, or reload after the sign-in.]
- `auth.config.ts` declares `process.env.CONVEX_SITE_URL` locally instead of adding Node types to the whole convex project.

## Follow-ups

- Password sign-up has no global rate limit, so Accounts can be minted without bound, each with non-expiring Groups. Add an `accountSignUp` limit to `convex/model/rateLimits.ts` (the ADR-0007 table).
- Auth failures (taken email, wrong password, short password) are plain `Error`s, which production redacts to "Server Error". The sheet in #18 needs typed codes such as `EMAIL_TAKEN` and `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` in `convex/model/errors.ts`.
- Convex Auth's default session lasts 30 days in absolute terms, so an active Anonymous GM loses its Groups' session after 30 days. Consider `session.totalDurationMs` of about 1 year with a 30-day `inactiveDurationMs`.
- ADR-0003's recovery holds only in the same tab within 10 minutes (`sessionStorage`). Name that window in the ADR, or move the claim to `localStorage` with a longer TTL.
- `sessions.scheduledBy` is written but nobody reads it. Removing it is a schema change.
- `LOCAL_BACKEND_ENV` in `scripts/auth-env.ts` repeats `scripts/e2e-server.ts`'s credential blanking.

author: marcinpalys
body:
Tasks: **A13**, **A14** (added to PLAN, Area A).

## Why
Real data from Marcin's laptop: the app showed **71% fatigue** while he felt fine. In those minutes blink rate and PERCLOS were `null` (eyes unreliable), so 65% of the weight dropped out and the score was built only from posture (avg ~15) + nods. That's a number that says nothing about fatigue. Separately, walking away for 2+ min reset the break timers but didn't count as a break in stats, didn't reset the Bateria trend or the stillness counter.

## How it works
- **A13:** `FatigueEstimator.update()` now returns `null` unless the face is reliable (≥ 70% frames, ≥ 12 fps) **and** there is a blink rate or PERCLOS (`eyesUsable()` in `core/fatigue.ts`). On `null` the smoothing resets, so a stale value doesn't come back. Everything downstream already handled `null` (stats skip the minute, Bateria redistributes the weight, no "fatigue" break). The live view shows "Za mało danych z oczu – nie zgadujemy" + a light/glasses hint instead of "Pojawi się, gdy będziesz w kadrze".
- **A14:** `BreakEngine` remembers a break earned by being away (`takeAwayBreak()`: ≥ 2 min = move, 20 s–2 min = eye). On a move break the analyzer runs the same reset as a clicked break (`resetAfterBreak()`: Bateria trend, fatigue, stillness) and calls the new `onAwayBreak` callback; `app.ts` logs `break-done` (`move:away`), clears the pending break and shows "Witaj z powrotem…". Eye-only (< 2 min) is not logged, so short disappearances don't inflate the stats.

## Verified
- `npm run typecheck` ✅ · `npm test` ✅ 64/64 (new: `test/fatigueReliability.test.ts` ×5, `test/awayBreak.test.ts` ×4; one existing test in `core.test.ts` got a null-check) · `npm run build` ✅
- `npm run demo`: fatigue is still computed (demo face is reliable): saved minute `fatigue 0, blink 15.1/min, perclos 3.8%`.
- `npm start` launches clean (models on GPU, no renderer errors). The away-from-desk path can't be simulated in demo mode; check by walking away 2–3 min.

## Heads-up
- Touches **Kacper's area** (`core/fatigue.ts`, `core/breakEngine.ts`, `analyzer.ts`, `test/core.test.ts`) and **one callback in `app.ts`** (integrator). Rebased on #76.
- Not addressed: when the face is "reliable" but the eye readings are implausible (e.g. 10 long blinks/min). That's MP6 / threshold tuning.
- Not addressed: an open break overlay doesn't auto-close after an away break (`overlays.ts`, area C).

author: kallanjones
body:
Delivers NFR-01 and US-03 in full. Supports US-06 and NFR-10.

**Merge #26 first.** This branch is built on `feature/quotation-terms` because both add a migration, and it targets `develop` directly. Until #26 merges, the diff also shows #26's commits. Once it merges, only the five commits below remain.

## What changed

**No line is priced at zero**
A costing line can no longer be created with a resolved price of zero, whether the price came from the catalogue, the rate card or was typed for the job. An unresolved price never reached a line before; a resolved price of zero now cannot either.

**No zero override (team decision, 3 October 2026)**
A rate typed on one quote (US-06) must be greater than zero. A refused override leaves the line at its card rate.

**No zero rate on the rate card**
`RatePrice` and `IPriceHistory.SetRateAsync` now refuse an amount of zero, the rule `MaterialPrice` already followed. A rate the client has not supplied still has no `RatePrice` row and reports as unresolved; it can no longer be set to zero instead.

## Schema

| Rule | How |
|---|---|
| A line's price is above zero | `CK_CostingLine_PricePositive` |
| An override is above zero | `CK_CostingLine_OverridePositive` |
| A rate is above zero | `CK_RatePrice_Positive`, replacing `CK_RatePrice_NotNegative` (`>= 0`) |

Migration: `RefuseZeroPricedLinesAndRates`.

## Tests

- `A_line_whose_price_never_resolved_blocks_the_calculation` keeps its purpose. It now builds the unresolved line with a plausible figure instead of zero, because a zero-priced line can no longer be created, and still asserts the calculation is refused.
- New: a line cannot be priced at zero, an override of zero is refused and the line keeps its rate, a rate of zero is refused in the domain, and a first rate of zero is refused by the price history service with the item left unresolved.

## Checks

- Builds with 0 warnings. 167 unit tests pass.
- SQLite stores decimals as text, so the three constraints were checked on SQL Server LocalDB: the migration applied, its idempotent script ran twice with no errors, and a zero value was refused.
- Merged locally with `feature/customers` and `feature/user-admin`: everything builds and all 214 tests pass.

## For whoever picks this up

- @MorganGibbon `ChangeLineRequest` in `CostingContracts.cs` refuses `UnitPrice < 0` only. It needs `<= 0`, or an override of zero reaches the domain and comes back as a 500 instead of a 400.
- @st10440432 The migration fails if a database already holds a rate of exactly zero. The seed creates none, but staging should be checked before this deploys.

Requested by Doc (@Dockery022).

Before: the jersey was tucked in and stopped at the belt. Skin poked through the jersey at the shoulders, armpits and sides. The cloth looked like plastic.

After:
- The jersey hangs untucked, outside the pants, covering the belt and dropping about 3 inches below it.
- The shoulders are a little broader, and the pants are a little fuller at the thighs and knees.
- No skin shows through the jersey or pants.
- The cloth is matte, with a fine thread weave and a polyester sheen, lit by a studio HDRI with ACES tone mapping.

How:
- **Fit** (`fitUniform()`, `JERSEY_FIT`): these are rest-pose edits, solved back through each vertex's skinning by a shared `moveRest()`. The player's positions are quantized integers, so `moveRest()` edits a float copy.
  - **Hem:** the lower torso is re-hung by its UV v, which flattens the old tucked folds. It drops to 7.5 cm below the belt, at the waist's widest radius plus 1.2 cm, interpolated around the body.
  - **Shoulders:** the shoulder caps push out 1.5 cm along their normals.
  - **Pants:** the thighs push out 1.2 cm and the knees 0.9 cm, with less on the inseam.
- **Clipping:**
  - `hideCovered()` drops skin that lies under the cloth. It also drops the upper-arm and deltoid skin inside each sleeve.
  - The jersey sits 6 mm out along its skinned normal.
  - The skin uses `polygonOffset`, so it draws behind coincident cloth.
- **Fabric:**
  - Roughness is 0.9 and metalness 0.
  - Sheen is 0.5.
  - A new weave normal map, `jersey-material/make_weave_map.py` → `maps/weave_normal.png`, gives threads about 0.8 mm wide.
- **Lighting:**
  - The environment is Poly Haven's CC0 "Studio Small 09" HDRI, read by `src/hdr.js`.
  - Tone mapping is ACES Filmic with exposure 0.8, so Cardinal Red stays #C9001F.

body:
## What

Scaffolds a production-ready Go HTTP service on [okapi](https://github.com/jkaninda/okapi) **v1.0.0**, Go 1.26.

### Layout

```
cmd/server/main.go     Entrypoint: env config (PORT, LOG_LEVEL via jkaninda/go-utils),
                       jkaninda/logger, okapi.OpenAPI docs with Scalar UI at /docs,
                       graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM (10s drain)
internal/routes/       Routes declared as data ([]okapi.RouteDefinition), grouped under
                       /api/v1, each with Summary, Request and Response types that feed
                       the generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec
internal/handlers/     Thin handlers: GET /healthz, GET /readyz and an items example
                       resource (list, get, create) using typed okapi.H handlers with
                       validation tags (required, minLength, maxLength)
internal/models/       Request/response types shared by handlers and routes
internal/store/        Concurrency-safe in-memory item store (RWMutex)
```

Plus: multi-stage **Dockerfile** (CGO disabled, static binary, non-root Alpine runtime), `.dockerignore`, `.gitignore`, **Makefile** (`build`, `test`, `vet`, `run`, `docker`, `clean`), README, and CI running `go vet ./...` + `go test -race ./...` on pushes and pull requests.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/v1/healthz` | Liveness probe |
| GET | `/api/v1/readyz` | Readiness probe |
| GET | `/api/v1/items` | List items |
| GET | `/api/v1/items/{id}` | Get one item (404 when unknown) |
| POST | `/api/v1/items` | Create item, 400 on validation failure |
| GET | `/docs` | Scalar API reference UI |
| GET | `/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1 spec |

### Testing

- `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass (handlers + routes covered via `net/http/httptest`: happy paths, validation failures, 404s, OpenAPI spec contents, Scalar UI).
- Binary smoke-tested end to end: probes, create/get/list round-trip, 400 on invalid body, docs and spec served, clean SIGTERM shutdown (exit 0).

### Note on the GitHub workflow

The token available to the agent lacks the `workflow` scope, so `.github/workflows/ci.yml` could not be pushed. The identical GitHub Actions workflow ships as `ci/github-actions.yml.txt`; a maintainer with a `workflow`-scoped token can activate it with:

```sh
mkdir -p .github/workflows && mv ci/github-actions.yml.txt .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

The Gitea workflow at `.gitea/workflows/ci.yml` is already active.

author: e-schultz
body: PIE-534: `ep0ch find` by query, view, subtree and dates, and `ep0ch export` to Markdown or JSON. ## What you can do now - `ep0ch find --query "type=chore (area=garden OR area=kitchen) updated >= -7d"`: the outline evaluates the saved views' grammar. `--view ` lists a view's members in the view's order, and `--under ` lists a subtree with the note itself included. These combine with each other and with words. - `--updated-after`, `--updated-before`, `--created-after` and `--created-before` only write the query clause: `--updated-after 2026-03-01` becomes `updated > 2026-03-01`. - `--ids` prints `((id))` a line, so `ep0ch show $(ep0ch find --ids --query type=errand)` works. `--json` prints block records. - `ep0ch export | --query … | --view … | --under … [--children] [--format md|json] [--out |-] [--split] [--resolve-links] [--manifest]`. ## Choices - **` - ` between header chips: the parser learns it.** We picked this over rebuilding with plain spaces. - `Seed order [type::errand] - [area::garden]` now gives both chips block scope, and the title is "Seed order". - Before, every chip but the last was an inline aside, and a chips-only line `[a::1] - [b::2]` had the title "-". - `PROPERTY_PARSER_VERSION` goes from 4 to 5 and `PROTOCOL` from 83 to 84. - We checked this on a private copy of a real outline. Among notes whose text was the same in the copy and the live file, the reparse changed no property scope. - **One header-line definition**, in outline-core's `header-line.ts`. The header line is the run of chips ending line 1, with blanks or ` - ` between them, hashtags allowed among them, and literal ranges respected. These all use it: - the parser's block scope for those chips; - every title: `firstLineWithoutPropertyTokens`, the tree index, publish's `stripPropertyTokens`, Detail's authored preview and the door's `titleLine`; - Detail's property table, which now says `header` for those chips; - export. The front matter mapping and its inverse (`noteFile` / `readNoteFile`) live in the same file, with round-trip tests. The hashtag value rule moved into `property-grammar.ts`, so the parser and the header line share one rule. - **Prose before the chips** is the common case: about 900 of roughly 1,900 first lines in the owner's outline. It stays as the body's first line, verbatim. When a note has no prose, the body starts with an empty line, so the inverse always knows which line was the prose. Nothing from the prose goes into front matter. - **Front matter:** - It starts with id, parent, created, updated, author and actor (when there is one), then the header chips in order. - Values are double-quoted strings, never dates. A repeated key becomes a list at its first place. - YAML keys that YAML would read as something else (`on`, `yes`, `null`) are quoted. - A chip whose key is an identity key stays in the body's first line. There are none in the owner's outline. - **One record shape**, outline-core's `block-record.ts`: - fields: title, header, body, text, properties (block scope, as lists), fields (line and inline), children, tasks with status, links (with every place each is written), backlinks, resources, created, updated, author, actor and revision; - one builder, which the host calls for `blocks.records` (at most 200 ids); - backlinks for a whole request in one pass over the outline. `store.queryBacklinks` and the batch share one context and one occurrence reader in `backlinks.ts`. - **The service evaluates every selection:** - `blocks.query` with `expression`, `text` and `subtreeRootId` for query, words and subtree. - `views.read`, paged, for a view. - `query.matches` now also takes `text` and `subtreeRootId`, so a view combined with words or `--under` is narrowed by the service. The door parses no query and no link. `--resolve-links` replaces at the spans the record carries. - **Deterministic output:** sorted JSON keys, outline order, ISO 8601 UTC timestamps with milliseconds, and file names `-.md` (whole ids if two notes would collide). The export time appears only in `manifest.json`, which `--manifest` writes. - **Export refuses a truncated selection** (more than 1000 matches) and writes nothing. - **Kitchen sink:** a fictional seed note "Seed order for the plot" that uses ` - ` between its chips, plus a "From a shell" section in the search section's note. Its test opens the section through `act`, then runs `find --query`, `show $(find --ids)` and `export` against the sink's scratch host. - **tv:** a new `ep0ch-tv query ""` source, with a README example. ## Verification - Root `bun run check`: green. - outline-core: `bun test` green (44). - outliner: `bun test` green (see the comment for counts). - door: `bun run test:parallel` green (see the comment for counts). - New tests: - `outline-core/test/header-line.test.ts` and `block-record.test.ts`; - `outliner/test/block-records.test.ts`: the parser, titles, the Detail table and preview, `blocks.records` over the socket, `query.matches` narrowing; - `door/test/find-export.test.ts`: selection, export md/json/split/resolve-links into temp dirs, refusals that show the command; - the door/service title parity probes with ` - `; - the tv `query` source; - the sink test. - Real terminal, against a scratch host in a tmux pane: `find --query 'type=errand updated >= -7d'`, `find --ids`, `show --width 60 $(find --ids --query tag=spring)`, and `export` as md and json. - Shape check on a private copy of a real outline, reporting counts only: - 431 notes exported as md; - all 431 bodies read back exactly; - 429 header lines read back in order, and 2 regrouped (a key repeated around another one). - Not tested: a physical keyboard. Nothing here is interactive. - A local review subagent did the architecture pass and a "Did you really?" pass. Its should-fixes are in: - view narrowing through `query.matches`; - 200-id record requests; - the reuse map and architecture map; - the service's display title for records; - links resolved by service spans; - one hashtag rule; - YAML key quoting; - truncation refused; - commands in refusals. Not done: the door's titles don't see code spans when they drop ` - `. The door has no code-span scanner, and the parity test leaves that case out. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01SPwEqHomk4QGpz2HgGhcdn --- Need help on this PR? author: vibgrate-team
body: ## Summary An unscored scan used to report DriftScore **0** and low risk — the same result as a fully current tree. A missing score now stays absent: - JSON (`vg scan --format json` and `.vibgrate/scan_result.json`) stores `"score": null` and null component fields. `riskLevel` is `none`, not `low`. - The text and Markdown summaries print **n/a** for the overall score, the risk level, and any component that was not measured. - A score that was actually computed is unchanged, including a real **0** (current runtime) and a runtime lag of 4 or more (health 0, reported as drift 100). - `--drift-budget` and a configured drift budget skip the comparison when the score is absent and do not fail the scan. author: jhweir
body:
## What

- The `paired with ad4m` label is now GitHub's `[!IMPORTANT]` purple, `8250DF`, matching the alert
  a pairing is written as. It was yellow, `FBCA04`.
- A comment beside the line says this is where the label's colour and description are defined, not
  the repository's label settings.

## Why

The paired check runs `gh label create --force` on every paired PR, and `--force` updates the one
existing label in place. So the purple set by hand in the repository settings reverted to the
script's yellow on the next run, which was #227's run right after.

Keeping the label defined in the workflow, rather than creating it only when it is missing, keeps
one source of truth. The label is part of the same mechanism as the comment, a change to it is a
reviewed one-line PR, and a fork or a fresh repository gets the right label without anyone setting
it up. A colour changed in the settings will still revert, and the comment says so.

## How

One line in `.github/actions/pairing-status/action.yml`, with the comment above it.

## Test plan

- [x] YAML parses; `prettier` clean.
- [ ] Not run on GitHub. The first paired run after this merges sets the label to purple. A paired
      run before then still sets it to yellow, so there is no point setting it by hand in the
      meantime.

body:
## Problem

oMLX reports server-measured prompt and generation rates in `usage.prompt_tokens_per_second` and `usage.generation_tokens_per_second`. These fields are not currently read into Activity, so the reported rates appear as unknown.

## Solution

Add compatibility with these oMLX usage extensions for streaming and non-streaming responses. Read each rate as a fallback when the corresponding TabbyAPI field is missing or null. Keep reported zeroes as zero and unreported rates as `-1`.

Existing TabbyAPI values retain priority over the fallback, and llama-server timings and vLLM metrics continue to override usage rates. Use the backend-provided rates directly without recalculating them from token counts.

## Tests

Passed: `make test-all`, `go vet ./...`, and `staticcheck ./internal/server`.

Also passed: `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/server -run 'OMLX|TabbyAPI|Timings|VLLM'`.

Checked a locally built binary against a fixture backend for JSON and SSE responses on both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`. Verified response-body preservation and rates recorded in Activity. This used fixtures rather than live oMLX inference.

author: visualdigitalagency
body:
Step A of the data plan: move virtual trading off NSE's live option-chain API (SEBI's May 2024 circular restricts real-time price data for paper-trading products) onto end-of-day prices, with live data only from a user's own connected broker.

**This PR only ingests. Nothing prices from it yet**, so app behaviour is unchanged. PRs B–D switch over after the owner has checked real files.

### What it does
- **`engine/eod.py`:** from `EOD_READY_IST` (18:30) on a trading day, the worker fetches NSE's UDiFF F&O bhavcopy (`BhavCopy_NSE_FO_0_0_0_YYYYMMDD_F_0000.csv.zip` from `nsearchives`, the same archive host the SPAN files come from).
  - It keeps stock options only: settlement price, close, previous close, OI, OI change and volume per contract. Spot and lot size come from the same file.
  - It saves one compact JSON per day under `engine/cache/eod/`, keeping the newest 5.
  - If the file isn't published yet, it retries every 15 minutes.
- **`eod.chain(symbol, expiry)`** returns a chain in **the same columns as `data_fetch.normalize_option_chain`**, so PR B can swap the source:
  - bid = ask = settlement, since the file has no order book;
  - IV is computed from the settlement price (`greeks_sr.implied_vol`, bisection over 1–300%);
  - a strike quoted on one side gets 0 on the other side, never NaN.
- **`greeks_sr.bs_price` / `implied_vol`:** new helpers.
- **`scripts/check_eod.py`:** run where the app runs to fetch a day and print SBIN's chain near the money. Compare it with NSE or your broker before approving PR B.

### Not verified against a real file
This session's network proxy blocks NSE (403), so the parser was built to NSE's published UDiFF column names (`TckrSymb`, `XpryDt`, `StrkPric`, `OptnTp`, `SttlmPric`, `UndrlygPric`, `NewBrdLotQty`, …) and tested against a sample file in that format. **Run `python scripts/check_eod.py` on the server before PR B.** If the format differs, `parse()` raises "No stock options in the bhavcopy" instead of saving bad data.

### Next (separate PRs, after this is checked)
- **B:** fills at the **next end-of-day settlement price** (no stale-price exploit); stop-losses, exits, RMS and auto-trade run daily on closing prices.
- **C:** screener and builder on end-of-day data, with "prices as of" labels.
- **D:** live prices only from a user's own connected Kite account, cached per user, never shared. Live-data users stay off the leaderboard, champions and prize draw.

### Tests
`tests/test_eod.py`: futures and index options filtered out; spot, lot and date read; same columns as the live chain; bid = ask = settlement; IV recovered within 0.2 of the pricing IV; one-sided strike filled with 0; unknown stock or expiry gives None; below-intrinsic IV gives 0; keep-5 pruning; `latest()`; fetch timing (before 18:30, weekend, unpublished, already saved); a file with no stock options is an error. All 41 backend files pass against local Postgres 16 + Redis; `ruff` clean.

author: kubowler99
body:
## Summary

Three slices of game expansion from the concept doc, plus one bug fix.

### 1. Content pack
- **Spawn table:** each spawn is picked from `spawner.enemyTable` in `game_config.json` (type, weight, unlock level, group size). This replaces the runner-only rule; runners keep their 30% share from level 3. Without a table, the spawner uses walkers only.
- **New enemies:**
  - **Brute** (level 5+): 80 health, slow, hits the wall for 12.
  - **Swarmling** (level 4+): 4 health, spawns in groups of 4.
- **Passive abilities:** they take a slot and change hero stats instead of firing.
  - **Arcane Might:** +10% damage per tier.
  - **Quickening:** 8% shorter cooldowns per tier (floor 0.4x).
  - `Hero:getStats()` combines passive stats, and active abilities read the damage and cooldown multipliers.
- **Orbiting Blades:** 2 blades circle the ability's slot on the wall and cut enemies they touch, at most once per enemy every 0.5s. Upgrades: blade count, speed, damage, size.
  - This adds a per-frame `ability:update(...)` hook in `combat_system` for abilities that don't fire on a cooldown.

### 2. Run arc
- **Bug fix:** the XP Boost card set `hero.xpMultiplier`, but nothing read it. `awardXP` now applies it.
- **Spitter** (level 6+): stops 260px short of the wall and attacks from range, shown with a projectile.
- **Elites** (level 8+, 8% of spawns): 4x health, 2x damage, 5x XP, larger and gold-tinted.
- **Bosses** at levels 10 and 20. Each spawns once at the top center, even at the concurrent limit, with a "BOSS INCOMING" / "FINAL BOSS" banner and a boss health bar.
- **Victory:** killing the final boss wins the run, and the end screen reads VICTORY!.
- Elites and bosses are off unless `game_config.json` sets them.

### 3. Meta progression
- **Gold:** each run earns 1 per kill, 5 per level reached, and 100 for winning.
- **Upgrades screen** (replaces the placeholder SETTINGS button): wall health, damage, cooldowns and XP gain, five levels each.
- **Hero select** before each run:
  - Arcane Wanderer (free): Arcane Bolt, +10% XP.
  - Frost Witch (300 gold): Frost Nova, 10% shorter cooldowns.
  - Ember Knight (500 gold): Orbiting Blades, +15% damage.
- Play Again keeps the hero. Definitions are in `data/meta.json`.

## Decisions to review
- **Ember Knight** uses Orbiting Blades and a flat +15% damage. The concept doc's Flame Slash and "+20% when below 50% HP" don't exist yet.
- **Frost Witch** uses Frost Nova and shorter cooldowns, instead of Frost Shard and a slow on hit.
- **Elites and bosses** change stats only. Elite slam/charge/summon and telegraphed boss attacks are not included.
- **Balance:** all the new numbers (enemy stats, boss health, gold rates, prices) are first guesses.

## Testing
- 1233 tests pass in normal order and over 10 shuffled runs.
- New specs cover the spawn table, every new enemy, passives, Orbiting Blades, elites, bosses, victory, meta progression, and the new scenes.
- **Not run in the Solar2D simulator.** Please check layouts (hero select, upgrades, boss bar, banner), blade visuals, the spitter projectile, and enemy tints and sizes.

author: yeongseon
body:
Closes #110

## 문제

Overview(`/`)가 History 분리(ADR 0013, #113/#114) 이후에도 활성 이슈 목록
아래에 전체 데이터셋을 다시 나열하는 중복된 "Datasets" 패널을 갖고 있었고,
상단 요약은 4개 pill뿐이라 "15개 중 몇 개에 문제가 있는지"를 한 문장으로
답하지 못했다. 활성 이슈 행에서도 그 데이터셋의 30일 이력을 보려면 History
페이지로 가는 링크가 없어 맥락이 끊겼다.

## 변경 내용

- `health_summary` 매크로: 헤드라인 문장("15개 중 N개에 문제가 있습니다.",
  문제가 0개면 다른 문구)과 상태 비율 막대(`--status-*-solid` 토큰, 장식용
  aria-hidden)를 추가하고, 기존 pill 4개는 막대 아래 접근성 범례로 유지했다.
  헤드라인과 막대 폭(%)은 `build_demo.py`의 `overview_context`에서 계산해
  템플릿은 그리기만 한다.
- `check_matrix(checks)` 매크로 신규: A/F/C/Q 4칸을 아이콘+줄임말로 그리고
  pass/warn/fail/unknown/not_applicable을 모두 처리한다. `not_applicable`은
  `--muted`/`--border` 같은 중립 토큰만 쓰고 `--status-*`는 쓰지 않아 상태처럼
  보이지 않는다. Overview의 데이터셋 × 체크 매트릭스와 `catalog.html`의 새
  Checks 열에서 같은 매크로를 재사용한다.
- `public_status.html`: 활성 이슈와 같은 데이터셋을 다시 나열하던 하단
  "Datasets" 패널을 데이터셋 × 체크 매트릭스(현재 health 심각도순, 기존과
  동일한 정렬)로 바꿨다. 활성 이슈 행마다 "최근 30일 중 비정상 N일" 한 줄과
  History 링크를 추가했는데, 이 수치는 History(#109)가 이미 계산하던
  `_dataset_abnormal_days`를 그대로 재사용한다(로직 중복 없음).
- `catalog.html`: Checks 열을 추가하고 각 행에 `check_matrix`를 재사용했다.
  필터용 `data-checks`(실패한 체크 이름 목록)는 그대로 둔 채 매트릭스 렌더링용
  `check_results`(네 체크의 CheckResult)를 별도로 추가했다.
- 구현 중 실제 브라우저에서 390px 전체 페이지가 가로로 스크롤되는 문제를
  발견했다: `<th>` 안에 넣은 `position:absolute` sr-only `<span>`이, 가장
  가까운 positioned 조상이 없어 containing block이 initial containing
  block(문서 루트)이 되면서 `.table-scroll`의 overflow 클리핑을 건너뛰었다.
  Checks 열 헤더의 확장 텍스트는 별도 span 대신 `<th aria-label="...">`로
  옮겨 해결했다(추가 박스를 만들지 않음).

## 검증

```
$ uv run --no-sources pytest
```
pypi.org는 되지만 files.pythonhosted.org가 막혀 있어 `uv sync`/`uv run`이
실패한다(이전 PR의 환경 메모와 동일). Homebrew Python 3.14 venv

author: mika-f
body: ## Summary Every layer the React CLI sends carries a full `EvaluatedTransform`, even when scale, rotation and anchor are at their defaults. In NEBULA (`examples/versus/bench/celesta/nebula.tsx`) that is 1,500 particles per frame. - **Rust**: `EvaluatedTransform` gets `#[serde(default)]`, so missing fields take the existing `Default` values (position 0,0 · scale 1,1 · rotation 0 · anchor 0.5,0.5). The generated TS type is unchanged; fields stay required. - **Bridge**: frame requests send `compactTransforms: true`. Component-resolution requests do not. - **CLI**: with that flag, `cli.ts` drops default-valued transform fields just before writing, recursing into groups. Layers returned by `renderAt` are untouched, so the web runtime and `debug.ts` keep full transforms. The flag is opt-in because many CLI tests assert full transforms (e.g. `transform.scale.x === 1`); without it the output is unchanged. ## Measurements Core i7-13700F, RTX 4070, Windows 11, release builds, interleaved with `main`. | | `main` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | JSON per NEBULA frame | 554 KiB | 458 KiB | | `JSON.stringify` (including the compacting copy) | 1.77 ms | 1.38 ms | | `preview-bench` Node time, ms/frame (3 runs) | 11.5 / 10.5 / 9.7 | 9.1 / 9.1 / 9.1 | | NEBULA export, s (5 runs) | 22.5 / 18.4 / 18.2 / 19.2 / 21.3 | 20.0 / 17.9 / 17.9 / 21.1 / 19.8 | Node time drops by about 1 ms/frame. The export difference is within run-to-run noise. Before/after MP4s have identical per-frame MD5s. Independent of mika-f/Celesta#121; the savings should add up. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm test` in `packages/react` (adds `compact-transforms.test.mjs`: compact with the flag, full without) - [x] `cargo test --release -p celesta-composition -p celesta-evaluator -p celesta-renderer -p celesta-react-bridge` (adds a test that omitted fields default) - [x] `cargo clippy` on the changed crates - [x] NEBULA export output frame-identical to `main` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Shrinks React CLI frame responses by omitting transform fields that match Rust defaults, cutting a NEBULA frame from 554 KiB to 458 KiB and preview Node time by about 1 ms/frame with frame-identical output. - Rust `EvaluatedTransform` gets `#[serde(default)]`; the generated TypeScript type stays unchanged. - Frame requests from the bridge carry `compactTransforms: true`; component-resolution requests do not. - The CLI then drops default-valued transform fields before writing, recursing into group layers. - Responses without the flag and layers from `renderAt` keep full transforms, so the web runtime, debug overlays, and existing CLI tests are unaffected. Written for commit 384e2e26a22a9d61a45ad78f61e731ddba413b95. Summary will update on new commits.

body:
## Summary

Remove the hardcoded employer stock ticker configuration and instead read it dynamically from imported E*TRADE files. The ticker is now extracted from the Benefit History workbook's Symbol column and the E*TRADE statement's holding row, then stored in the app's settings. This eliminates the need for manual configuration before importing data.

## Key Changes

- **Parser updates**: Modified `parseEtradeStatement()` to extract the ticker from the `<COMPANY> (<SYMBOL>)` holding row pattern instead of using a config constant. Enhanced `parseBenefitHistory()` to read the Symbol column from the workbook.

- **Dynamic ticker storage**: The ticker is now persisted in the `equitySymbol` setting via the `equitySymbol()` helper function in `repos.ts`. Import mappers (`mapBenefitHistory()` and `mapEtradeStatement()`) record the ticker when processing files.

- **Graceful fallback**: Before any E*TRADE import, the ticker is empty (`''`). The app handles this gracefully—no stock price is fetched from Finnhub, no price warning is shown, and the equity account is labeled "Employer stock" instead of a ticker.

- **UI updates**: Components now use the `useEquitySymbol()` hook to display the current ticker dynamically instead of importing the config constant. Account names and labels update based on the imported ticker.

- **Price refresh logic**: The Finnhub quote URL is now constructed dynamically with the current ticker. If no ticker has been imported yet, the stock price refresh is skipped entirely.

- **Configuration removal**: Deleted `EQUITY_SYMBOL` and `EQUITY_COMPANY` constants from `config.ts`, replacing them with `EQUITY_SYMBOL_SETTING` to reference the settings key.

## Implementation Details

- The E*TRADE statement parser now validates holding rows by checking that quantity × price ≈ market value, and prefers holdings named in the RSU table to handle statements with multiple positions.
- Benefit History parsing detects multiple conflicting symbols and reports them as a validation check.
- Import undo correctly restores the previous ticker by removing the setting when rolling back.
- Tests updated to set the ticker via settings before price refresh operations.

author: matteo-fontana
body:
## Summary
This PR restores the `conformal.multidim.jackplus()` function and `bikeMi` dataset that were available in version 1.1.1 but missing from 1.1.2. It also introduces new aggregation methods and improves the multi-split conformal inference implementation.

## Key Changes

### New Features
- **Restored `conformal.multidim.jackplus()`**: Implements multivariate jackknife+ prediction regions with two methods:
  - `method = "depth"` (default): Depth-based heuristic extension (no finite-sample guarantee)
  - `method = "max"`: Applies jackknife+ to scalar score `max_j |R_ij| / scale_j` with coverage guarantee of at least `1 - 2*alpha`
  - Includes optional `scale` parameter for component-wise scaling

- **Restored `bikeMi` dataset**: Daily bike trip data from Milan's Duomo district with meteorological covariates

- **Depth-based aggregation for multi-split**: New `aggregation` parameter in `conformal.multidim.msplit()`:
  - `"componentwise"` (default): Original aggregation method
  - `"depth"`: Depth-based aggregation from version 1.1.1, retains floor(2*tau*B) deepest vertices (requires at least 2)

- **Enhanced `conformal.multidim.msplit()`**:
  - `mad.train.fun` and `mad.predict.fun` parameters now passed through to split conformal
  - Scalar `training_size` recycled across all splits
  - Improved seed handling: with `seed = FALSE`, seeds drawn from current RNG stream (reproducible with `set.seed()`)

- **Improved `conformal.multidim.full()`**: Added `s_type` parameter for residual scaling ("st-dev" or "identity")

- **Enhanced plotting**: `plot_multidim()` now dispatches to appropriate function based on input type; `plot_multidim_full()` handles univariate responses

### Documentation Improvements
- Comprehensive documentation updates across all functions
- Clearer parameter descriptions and return value documentation
- Added detailed examples and cross-references
- Updated NEWS.md with version history and behavior changes

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test suite in `tests/testthat/test-methods.R` covering:
  - Split conformal score definitions
  - MAD function support
  - Multi-split, jackknife+, and full conformal methods
  - Depth aggregation validation
  - Seed reproducibility

### Internal Changes
- Improved `check.R` documentation for internal validation functions
- Enhanced `interval.build.R` documentation
- Updated `s_regression.R` documentation
- Improved `lm_multi()` and `mean_multi()` documentation
- Updated example files with better parameter choices

## Notable Implementation Details
- Jackknife+ uses parallel computation via `future.apply` with proper RNG handling
- Multi-split depth aggregation requires minimum 2 vertices to avoid degeneracy
- Seed behavior changed for reproducibility: `seed = 0` reproduces old behavior, `seed = FALSE` uses current RNG stream
- All functions properly restore RNG state on exit

body:
Part 1 of #1422 (the redesign follows in a separate PR). Spec and plan are included under `docs/superpowers/`.

## What was slow
- **P1, Agents tab during a crew run:**
  - The crew-integration effect depended on the `summaries` array, which is new on every 5 s poll, and reloaded on every `threads:changed`.
  - Each call ran about 6 + 3×workers **blocking** git commands in the main process (`execFileSync`), roughly 100–270 ms of stall per call, many times a minute.
- **P2, #1398:**
  - `threads:summaries` read the last message of every thread (about 1,850).
  - The Recap card fetched all rows to show one, on nearly every thread selection.
  - The team poll ran every 5 s whenever *any* project had a working thread.
- **P3:** `memo(AgentsPanel)` never skipped renders, because App passed new inline crew handlers on every render.
- **P4:** a panel-level `LaneHeartbeat` duplicated the app-level `ClaimedLanesHeartbeat` and wrote the store every 15 s.

## Changes
- **`threads:summaries` scoping:** it accepts `{ projectId?, threadIds? }`, filters **before** any message read, and caps `lastActivity.text` at 200 characters. With no argument the output is unchanged.
  - The Recap card passes `{ threadIds: [id] }`.
  - The team view passes `{ projectId }`.
  - The poll key (`panelRosterKey`) covers only the selected project.
- **Crew-integration effect:**
  - It is keyed on a derived `isCrewLead` boolean, and `threads:changed` reloads are throttled to 1 s.
  - A request-sequence guard drops stale results, now that responses can arrive out of order.
- **Async git in `crewIntegration`:** it uses `gitTryAsync`, `repoDefaultBranchAsync` and a new `listChangedPathsAsync`, which shares `diffBaseCandidates` with the sync `resolveDiffBase`. Same values, and it no longer blocks main.
- **App:** stable `useCallback` crew handlers, and the duplicate lane heartbeat is removed. Remote projects can't claim lanes, so the app-level beat covers everything.

## Verification
- `tsc` clean.
- Renderer 2679/2679. `vite build` OK.
- Electron 4106/4107 on the pre-fix HEAD. The one failure is an unrelated `claude.test.js` JSON-read race; it passes 3/3 alone.
- Crew-integration and worker-snapshot 33/33 after the final fixes.
- **New tests:**
  - scoped summaries read only the requested threads;
  - Recap and the team view request the narrowest scope;
  - no crew-integration rerun on a summaries-only change;
  - five pushes collapse into one reload;
  - an out-of-order integration result can't overwrite a newer one;
  - `crewIntegration` yields to the event loop with a live lead and worker.
- Per-task reviews and a final whole-branch review: ready to merge.
