author: chongfun
body:
## Bug

If the card had no books at its last scan, books copied onto it later stay hidden. The Library screen keeps showing its "no books, add EPUB files to /books" note on every boot.

The usual way to hit it is first-run setup: boot once on an empty card, then copy books on from a computer.

How it happens:
- The first boot writes `CATALOG.BIN` with a count of 0.
- On later boots, `load_catalog_cache` treats that as a hit and sets `status = LibraryScanStatus::Empty`. Nothing rescans.
- The folder listing does find the new book: `FolderListed` carries it and `rows()` shows it.
- But `ui/src/render.rs` checks `UiLibraryStatus::Empty` first and draws the "no books" note instead of the rows.
- A stale snapshot that is not empty does not have this problem: its rows show, and picking an unknown row goes Stale and rescans. An empty snapshot hides the one row whose pick would have triggered that rescan.

Found by a read-only audit of the library scan.

## Fix

`load_catalog_cache` treats a snapshot with no books as `CatalogFault::Missing`. The caller then queues `RefreshCatalog`, as on any cold boot. The bench label stays `miss`, which `bench.py` already treats as the ordinary cold path.

Cost: a card with no books at all rescans its empty shelf at boot instead of loading the snapshot.

## Test

`storage/tests/rescan_scenarios.rs`, `a_book_added_to_an_empty_card_while_off_is_listed`: wake and sleep a blank card, add `BOOKS/Dune.epub`, then wake and open the Library. The row is listed, the status is not `Empty`, and the catalog holds the book. On main the status stays `Empty`.

Checks run: `tools/check.sh fast`, `emulator`, `clippy-firmware` and `stack-frames`.

author: hjewkes
body:
Adds `isRepo(value)` to `@titan-design/github`: a non-throwing predicate for a bare `owner/name`. `checkRepo` now calls it, so the throwing and non-throwing forms share one grammar.

- Owner follows GitHub's rules: 1 to 39 alphanumerics and single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen.
- Name: `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, not all dots, no `..`.
- `owner/name.git` is refused. It names the same repo but compares unequal, so it would slip past a deny list (the old `isRepoKey` behavior; the old `isRepoSlug` accepted it).
- factory `isRepoSlug` is removed; registry.ts and cli.ts use `isRepo`. seats.ts uses `isRepo` and re-exports it as `isRepoKey` because commands.ts, tree-carry.ts, review.ts and config.ts import that name and are outside this task's file set. No caller outside factory imports either old name.

body:
Zes onderdelen. Elk is gebouwd door een bouwer, nagekeken door twee reviewers (correctheid en contract) en daarna verwerkt. Daarna samengevoegd en als geheel opnieuw getest.

## Wat erin zit
- **Sets en starter.** `npm start -- meditatie|dj|scene-kit` start de apps, opent Chrome met `?hub=` en zet de beginstand en de focus. Ctrl-C, SIGHUP of het venster sluiten ruimt op wat de set zelf startte. Zie `docs/SETS.md`.
- **Avondmap.** LPD8-pad 4 neemt de avond op in `~/Movies/varve-avonden/<datum-tijd>/`. `npm run herhaal -- <map>` speelt de avond terug en vergelijkt per app de staat-hash. Zie `docs/OPNAME.md`.
- **Geheugen.** De snapshots en de `truth:"hub"`-waarden blijven bewaard over een herstart, in `~/.varve-hub/staat.json`. `slew_s` geldt nu voor elke zet van de hub, behalve directe APC-bewegingen (PROTOCOL §12).
- **Altijd aan en netwerk (F5).** Nieuw zijn `--lan` (token, cookie, close-code 4003, mDNS), `installeer` (launchd/systemd) en `token`. Zie `docs/NETWERK.md` en PROTOCOL §13.
- **Generale repetitie.** `npm run repetitie` speelt één avond: de hub met de échte koppelingen in headless Chromium. In CI draait dezelfde avond met nep-apps die de echte manifesten gebruiken. Zie `docs/REPETITIE.md`.
- **av-kern.** De lease-koppeling staat als patch in `koppelingen/av-kern/`. Toepassen kan na 25 okt; av-kern zelf is niet aangeraakt.

## Afstemming bij het samenvoegen
- In `cli.js` en `hub.js` zijn sets, opname, geheugen en token samengevoegd. De PROTOCOL-secties van geheugen en netwerk zijn §12 en §13 geworden.
- `herhaal` wacht na de beginstand op de langste `slew_s`. Dat moest, omdat een cockpit-zet sinds het geheugen ook slewt.
- De repetitie wacht na het laden van een snapshot tot de slew klaar is.
- `sets-cli.test.js` gebruikt een eigen geheugenbestand. Zo leest of schrijft `npm test` nooit `~/.varve-hub/staat.json`.

## Getest
- `npx vitest run`: 648 geslaagd en 2 overgeslagen. De overgeslagen tests hangen af van root; als gewone gebruiker slagen ze ook. Gedraaid met een tijdelijke HOME, en daar kwam niets bij.
- De UI- en repetitietests slagen ook met chrome-headless-shell 1243, dezelfde browser als in CI.
- De echte repetitie tegen deze stand gaf dezelfde uitslag als vóór het samenvoegen: alles groen behalve de twee bekende hub-vragen (zie STATUS).

## Open (beslissing nodig, staat in STATUS.md)
- Na een paniek doet LPD8-K1 niets meer. De pickup volgt de eerste app met de rol, en waterschaal zet `volume` op 0. Dit staat als `it.fails` in de tests.
- Het tempo van waterschaal stapt per 0,5/min, waardoor hub en app het oneens blijven.
- Een macro op een keuze-parameter stuurt dubbele zets.

author: aaaxn
body:
Fixes #1292.

## Cause

`tree` in `safe.ts` picks the variables a match carries into its arms (`cv0`): q=1, used in more than one arm, not Data. Each arm binds them again, and `scope_move` renames their level. A later variable whose type names a carried one stayed outside the arms, at its type there. In the issue's file, `same : {x1 == x0}` reaches an arm whose `Box` needs `{x4 == x0}`, so the kernel rejects a program bend2 accepts. A live or `+` `same` fails the same way.

## Fix

- After `cv0`, the convoy also takes each variable the arms name, live or dead, whose type names one it carries. The scan runs in binding order, so a chain of such types is closed too.
- `convoy_bind` and the arm's application use the variable's own quantity instead of 1, so a dead `same` rides as `λ-x5` / `-x2` and a `+` one as `λ+x5` / `+x2`.
- A match built dry keeps its dead uses too, as dead arguments (`uses` still skips them, so live counts don't change). Without this, a match built again saw an inner match only through its live uses, and missed a dependent that is used only dead two matches down.
- `occurs(o, l)`: whether `o` names level `l`, live or dead.

The issue's term now goes out as the hand-fixed one in the report: `λx4 => λ-x5 => (.Box, (x4, (-x5, ())))` in each arm, applied to `x3 x1 -x2`.

## Checks

On `ea423f01`, against main `a950fd68`, Linux x86_64, kernel built from main's `bendtt.lean` (Lean 4.34.0):

- `tests/check/convoy_dependent.bend` covers six shapes: dead, live, nested in one arm, three deep with the dependent only in the innermost matches, a default arm, and a self-call. Each one fails `--verdict` on main when it is on its own. `pick_deep` also fails without the dry change. A law pins `main` at `21n`. The file prints `21n` when run, under `--checkup`, and from the JS and C builds.
- `--verdict` on all 1,554 existing test files gives the same exit code and output as main: 991 check, 560 fail, the same 3 mismatches (`conversion_shared_cells_once`, `model_false`, `model_no_base`). The new file checks.
- `-o` is byte-identical to main for every test file that checks (991), and for every `demos/` and `bench/` file that emits (57).
- A differential sweep over 162 generated convoy programs varied the quantity of `owner` and `same`, where the scrutinee sits, Type or Data, and flat, nested or default arms. Of the 81 bend2 accepts, 66 check on both main and this branch and 15 check only here. None checks on main and fails here.
- `bun gates/repo.ts`: PASS 50 / 50, the same as main. `safe.ts` grows from 21,624 to 21,896 ttok, under its 24,000 cap.
- `tsc`: 12 errors, the same as main.
- The cluster gates (`gates/test.ts`, `gates/perf.ts`, `gates/safe.ts`) weren't run. I ran `gates/safe_node.ts` locally over `tests/` instead.

## Limits

A dependent is found through its bend2 type (`b.T`). A binder with no known type is left out, as before. A scrutinee whose own type names a carried variable is unchanged.

Written with help from Claude Opus 5.5.

author: urriki1502
illyayalovyy
body:
Closes #46.

## What this does

Applications that manage their own copy — Claude Code, Codex, tmux, vim with
`set clipboard=unnamed` over SSH — copy by writing `OSC 52`. VTE 0.82 has no
handler for it (`VTE_OSC_XTERM_SET_XSELECTION` sits in the unhandled
fall-through list), so the copy did nothing at all. The daemon also forwarded
the sequence verbatim and appended it to the pane's scrollback log, so
clipboard text was being written to disk in plaintext.

**Daemon.** A stateful scanner lifts OSC 52 out of each PTY batch before
anything else sees it — the cell grid, every client, the log. Both `BEL` and
`ST` terminators, sequences split across any number of reads, base64 decoded
under a 1 MiB cap (hand-rolled decoder, so no new dependency and no Flatpak
cargo-sources churn). Completed writes surface on `FeedResult` beside
`new_cwd`/`new_title`. A write that can no longer be well-formed is abandoned
at the first impossible byte, so a never-terminated sequence cannot swallow a
pane's output.

**Protocol.** `ClipboardWrite { runtime_id, pane_id, target, data }` at tag 40,
gated on the new `OPT_CLIPBOARD_OSC52` capability so a client built before the
event existed never receives it.

**Client.** The push is applied through the same `gdk_clipboard_set_text`
UTF-8 path as `copy_to_clipboard` (#982). Two gates: the daemon sends the
event only to the client holding the workspace's write lease, and the pane's
own input state gates it again client-side, so a read-only mirror left behind
by a take-over cannot hijack the clipboard. "Let applications set the
clipboard" in Preferences → Terminal turns it off; it defaults on, including
for preference files written before the setting existed.

**Security.** The read/query form (`\e]52;c;?`) is recognised only so it can
be dropped — answering it would let anything able to print to a pane,
including a program on a remote host, exfiltrate the clipboard. Oversized and
undecodable payloads are dropped with a `warn!`. Empty writes are ignored
rather than clearing the clipboard.

## How to verify manually

1. `cargo build --workspace`, start the daemon, open a managed workspace.
2. In a pane: `printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf 'hello' | base64)"` — the
   clipboard now holds `hello`, and nothing is printed in the pane.
3. `grep -c $'\e]52' ~/.local/state/rttx/daemon/workspaces/*/scrollback/*.log`
   — the sequence no longer lands on disk.
4. Same thing in a workspace whose daemon is on a remote host over SSH: the
   text arrives on the *local* clipboard.
5. Take the workspace over from a second window: the demoted window stops
   writing the clipboard; the new owner writes it.

## Tests

- Pure-state (daemon, `screen.rs`/`pane.rs`): BEL and ST terminators, the
  sequence split at **every** byte boundary and byte-at-a-time, the `?` read
  form ignored, the 1 MiB cap (at the cap and over it), empty and undecodable
  payloads, an unterminated write releasing output, other OSC sequences
  untouched, base64 padding/malformed cases, and `pending_flush` plus the
  screen's raw bytes carrying no clipboard text.
- Protocol: capability gating and a frame round-trip of the push.
- Integration (daemon): a real shell `printf`-emits OSC 52 and the attached
  client gets exactly one `ClipboardWrite` and no OSC 52 bytes; the payload
  never reaches the scrollback log; only the write-lease holder is told, not a
  read-only client; a client without the capability gets no push; and the same
  write survives `attach-stdio`, the transport a remote (SSH) daemon uses.
- Client: pure-state decision tests in `terminal/mod.rs`; a GTK test under
  headless weston that proves the clipboard is ownable with a control write
  before asserting a write lands, and that a taken-over pane and a disabled
  preference leave it untouched; and a window-level test that dispatches the
  real push through `dispatch_managed_runtime_message` to the clipboard.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`,
  `bash .github/scripts/run-quality-tests.sh` and `./run_ui_tests.sh` (36
  AT-SPI tests) all pass; the runtime-behaviour gate reports both layers.

## One unrelated line each in two Cargo.toml files

CI's Fedora image now ships clippy 1.99, which added `assert_is_empty` to
`clippy::pedantic`; both crates deny pedantic, so the lint fails the Clippy
job on *any* pull request opened today (~150 pre-existing
`assert!(x.is_empty())` assertions). It is allowed here alongside the other
too-noisy pedantic lints so this PR can go green; nothing else in the repo
changes.

author: androidbot18
body:
Implements the client-side emulator shell described in `docs/TECHSPEC.md` (added in this PR).

## What's here

**Display model** — two independent RGB565 framebuffers. Primary is the Cardputer's built-in 240x135 at rotation 0; secondary is the TERM512's 240x320 panel memory rendered 320x240 at rotation 1. Geometry is taken from `area512_hal/captft/gfx/area512_display.cpp` rather than assumed. Rotation is applied during the RGB565 to RGBA expansion, and a test asserts the mapping is bijective so no pixel is dropped or duplicated.

**Keyboard** — the 56-key TCA8418 scan-code table is transcribed verbatim from `cardputer_lookup_key()` in `area512_hal/console/keyboard.cpp`. All 56 codes, kinds and legends match the firmware, verified by diffing the table against the source. The count is asserted at import time so a bad edit fails loudly.

Browser events resolve to the *base* scan code and emit modifier codes separately, which lets the firmware perform case conversion itself. That keeps the case-sensitive behaviour the spec calls for instead of duplicating it in JS. `Cmd` maps to the Cardputer `Ctrl` code, rollover caps at 6 keys (above the 3-key minimum), and auto-repeat is left to the firmware's own 450ms/55ms timing.

**UI** — desk and landscape layouts, pause, combined screenshot export, power-cycle, firmware picker with a guarded GitHub raw fetch, and local `.bin` loading. PWA manifest plus a service worker precache the app shell for offline use; firmware binaries are deliberately excluded.

## Verification

- 61 tests via `node --test`, all passing
- All 19 relative imports resolve (`tools/check-imports.py`)
- Every module passes `node --check`; JSON, SVG and HTML tags validated
- All 13 static assets serve with HTTP 200
- View modules are tested against a minimal DOM stub, so the suite needs no browser and no dependencies

## Status

The UI and input model are complete and tested. **The Xtensa LX7 emulation core (`src/core.js`) is not in this PR.** `main.js` imports it lazily through a guarded dynamic import and reports its absence in the status bar rather than failing silently, so the page is fully usable and debuggable today. The core only needs to write RGB565 into the two supplied framebuffers and forward scan codes — see the README for the two candidate approaches.

## Note on the display findings

Worth recording: in the CapTFT build the firmware *releases* the internal Cardputer display (`setBrightness(0)`, `sleep()`, `waitDisplay()`, `releaseBus()`) and drives the external panel exclusively at rotation 1. The emulator keeps both framebuffers live regardless, so single-screen `Area512Adv.bin` still works.

author: clintval
body:
Bumps bedspec to 4.0.0.

It is a major release because of #61:

- `record.territory()` returns a `Territory` instead of an iterator of spans. `for span in record.territory()` becomes `for span in record.spans()` wherever each piece or its strand matters.
- A custom record overrides `spans()` instead of `territory()`, which is now final; defining `territory()` raises a `TypeError` naming `spans()`.
- A `Bed12` is its blocks: its territory holds only its exons, and a query touching only an intron no longer finds it in `TreeDetector` or `TabixDetector`. To find a `Bed12` by its whole extent, add it as a `Bed6`.

It also adds `Territory` (#61), an immutable set of bases with `|`, `&`, `-`, `.length`, `contains` and `in`, and requires typeline 2.3.0 or newer (#62).

The release notes git-cliff writes list only commit subjects, so once the release exists I will add the breaking changes above to it.

## What
Adds **Update CMake** and **Dry run CMake** buttons to the PSX Bulk Migrate tab, backed by a new `git bulk-update-cmake` command in the vendored toolkit.

For each ticked title it runs psxrecomp's `tools/update_cmake.py` (the sibling psxrecomp checkout's copy if present, else the title's pinned `psxrecomp/` submodule) and commits `CMakeLists.txt` only. The Push checkbox is honoured; `--dry-run` only reports. As with `bulk-migrate-bundled`, no second copy of the logic lives here.

## Depends on
[RetroPortingToolKit/psxrecomp#487](https://github.com/RetroPortingToolKit/psxrecomp/pull/487) (adds `tools/update_cmake.py` and the `recomp-net-headers` managed block). Without it the command reports "no psxrecomp tools/update_cmake.py" per title.

## Why
psxrecomp's `main.cpp` includes `recomp_net/host_relay.h` unconditionally, so offline (`PSX_NETPLAY=OFF`) title builds fail without recomp-net's include dir on the path. This lets all titles pick up that CMake block in one go.

## Testing
- `bulk_update_cmake` against a scratch git repo with the sibling psxrecomp checkout: dry run, update + commit (only `CMakeLists.txt`), then "up to date".
- `cli.py`/`bulkops.py` compile. The ImGui change (`studio_main.cpp`) mirrors the existing `run_migrate` lambda but was **not built or run** here (no display / dependencies).

author: yukuhu
body:
## Summary

R4b of the 2026-10-03 codebase review: races and routing in the Cast, Android TV, webOS and Tizen adapters (AC1, AC3,
AC6, AC7, TV3, TV4, TV5). R4a (#186) covered Bluetooth, Sonos and UPnP.

**Cast and Android TV**
- **AC1, Cast connected too early:** a Cast receiver counts as connected once it has answered.
  - Before, the session reported CONNECTED and reset its backoff as soon as it had sent its status request. A
    receiver that hung up right after the connect was retried every second, for good. A Stop sent before the first
    answer "succeeded" without sending anything.
  - The attempt now stays pending until the first receiver status, as Android TV's does. Until then commands fail as
    "not connected".
  - The receiver has the command timeout (5 s) to answer. After that the connection is dropped and the backoff takes
    over, as for any lost connection.
- **AC3, slow reconnects:** Cast and Android TV devices reconnect as soon as they announce themselves over mDNS, as
  webOS, UPnP and Sonos already do. Before, they waited out a backoff of up to a minute after an outage.
  - Cast matches the receiver by its mDNS id or address, and Android TV by address.
  - Android TV skips this while "unpaired" verdicts that could be a reboot are still being counted. A booting Shield
    announces itself before it takes the certificate, so each early attempt would bring the permanent UNPAIRED latch
    closer.
- **AC6, wrong reason:** an Android TV whose pairing the device no longer accepts says it "must be paired again",
  instead of "is not connected".
- **AC7, double-clicked pairing code:**
  - Before, two submits of the code ran two checks on one pairing socket. The second failed after the first had
    paired, and the page showed that failure.
  - A second submit now gets the first one's answer, whether it arrives during the first or after it.
  - The Pair button is also disabled once the form is sent. So are the buttons of the forms that start a pairing.

**LG and Samsung TVs**
- **TV3, Samsung requests that could hang:** REST and DIAL requests to a Samsung TV have a deadline for the whole
  answer, not just the headers. A TV that stalls in the middle of an answer no longer holds its session, or a
  launch's request thread, for good.
- **TV4, LG pointer socket:** the d-pad's pointer socket is opened on the LG TV itself.
  - Before, the address in the TV's answer was used as it came: a device could make the server connect to any host.
  - A malformed answer gave the d-pad a 500. It now fails with "The TV offered an unusable pointer input socket".
- **TV5, LG over TLS (your ruling):** an LG TV is reached on `wss://host:3001` first. It falls back to `ws://host:3000`
  only when that fails, for older firmware. Before, the plain port came first, so the client key crossed the network
  in clear on every reconnect.
  - Now the key is encrypted whenever the TV answers on port 3001. The fallback still sends it in clear, as the ruling
    accepts.
  - A port 3001 that drops packets instead of refusing them costs up to twice the connect timeout (6 s) before port
    3000 is tried.

### Rulings I made
- **TV4 keeps the TV's port and path but always uses the TV's own host.** It does not refuse an answer that names
  another host. A TV added by name (`lgtv.fritz.box`) answers with its IP address, and refusing that would break its
  d-pad. Using the TV's own host keeps the request on the TV either way.
- **AC7 remembers the last answer only for the same code.** A different code after the attempt ended still gets "No
  pairing is in progress". Starting or cancelling a pairing forgets the remembered answer.
- **AC1 gives the receiver the command timeout to answer.** The final review found that a receiver which answers
  heartbeats but never its status would otherwise stay "connecting" for good.
- **The forms that start a pairing send once as well** (LG/Samsung prompt pairing, Android TV pairing). A double click
  there starts the pairing twice, and the prompt forms wait up to a minute. They use the same attribute the browser test
  covers. A page the browser restores with Back gets its buttons back.

### Deferred
- **A Cast receiver that keeps announcing itself and hangs up right away is retried as often as it announces.** An
  announcement resets the backoff, as it does for webOS, UPnP and Sonos.

## Linked issue

None.

## How it was tested

- **New unit tests:**
  - `CastSessionTest` (+2):
    - not connected before the receiver answers, and Stop fails then;
    - a receiver that never answers is dropped and tried again, with a request id on its status request.
  - `CastAdapterTest` (+1), `AndroidTvAdapterTest` (+1): with retries a minute apart, an announcement brings the
    device back within seconds.
  - `AndroidTvSessionTest` (+2):
    - announcements do not hurry the UNPAIRED latch;
    - an unpaired device asks to be paired again.
  - `PairingServiceTest` (+4):
    - a code submitted twice at once is checked once, and both submits get its answer;
    - a code submitted again after its answer gets the same answer, while another code does not;
    - an old attempt that ends late leaves the newer attempt's answer (Codex);
    - an attempt cancelled while its code is checked leaves no answer (Codex).
  - `TizenRestTest` (+1), `DialClientTest` (+1): a TV that stalls mid-answer fails within the request timeout.
  - `SsapConnectionTest` (+5):
    - the pointer socket goes to the TV whatever host it names;
    - a non-WebSocket socket address is refused with a reason;
    - a malformed one is refused with a reason;
    - the connection is TLS first;
    - the plain-port fallback.
- **New browser test:** `PairingCodeE2eTest` (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). The Pair button is disabled once the form is
  sent, and the code goes out once.
  - It reads `disabled` in the click's own task. Playwright waits out the held answer before it looks at the old page
    again.
- **Fakes:**
  - `FakeTizenServer.stallAnswers()`;
  - `FakeSsapServer.offerPointerSocket(…)`;
  - `FakeCodePairing` for the browser tests.
- **TDD:** each test failed for the reported reason before its fix. The Cast deadline test failed again with the timer
  removed.
  - The plain-port fallback test was the one exception: it passed before TV5, and it guards the fallback TV5 keeps.
  - The latch test failed against a `reconnectNow` without the guard.

- **Test count:** 3877, main's 3860 plus the 17 new tests. No other class changed its count. One setup-page test matched
  the pairing form's tag too exactly for the new `data-submit-once` attribute; it now allows the form's other
  attributes.
- **Final review** (Opus, of the seven fixes):
  - No Critical findings.
  - Important, all fixed:
    - the Cast attempt with no deadline (above);
    - `application.yaml` still said ws:// came first;
    - the guide over-promised what TLS first protects.
  - Minor findings fixed:
    - an `Error` in a pairing check no longer leaves a second submit waiting;
    - the double-submit test now holds the second submit while the first is checked;
    - the pairing forms, and a page restored with Back;
    - the browser test cleans up after a failure;
    - DIAL's cap leaves room for an error page;
    - Javadoc, one copy of the webOS options, a misnamed test.
  - The rest are noted above.
- **Codex and SonarCloud** (0fb425d3, 8719ed1e):
  - Codex: the remembered answer for a repeated code was one shared slot. An old attempt that ended late could
    overwrite a newer attempt's answer, or put one back after `cancel()`. Each attempt now keeps its own code and
    answer. Two new tests reproduced both cases before the change.
  - SonarCloud: S5778 in two tests is fixed.
- **Browser tests:** the full suite passed on the seven fix commits: 275 tests, 1 skipped as on main. The setup-page
  classes passed again after the review round.

## Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] `./gradlew build`

author: nikitacoeur
body:
Stacked on #145.

## What

Husonym talked to Presidio through two clients with different time limits and error behavior. There is now one, `backend/pkg/presidio`, for the three operations the product uses: analyze a text, anonymize a text, list the supported entities.

- **Written for what is used.** Value types hold only the fields sent and read. The client generated from an OpenAPI document, its generator and its runtime leave the dependencies.
- **Three errors a caller can act on:** Presidio did not answer (transport, time limit, 502/503/504); Presidio refused the request (with its message); the answer could not be used.
- **A 200 that lacks a required field is an error.** It could end in a nil dereference before.
- **One minute per call**, carried by the context; a caller that wants less sets a shorter deadline (the content scan keeps fifteen seconds). Answers are capped at 16 MiB.
- **Tests run over real HTTP** against answers recorded from Presidio 2.2.362 (image digests noted next to the fixtures). Other packages use a small fake instead of generated mocks.

## What a deployment or an API client sees

- `GetTransformPiiEntities` and `AnonymizeSingle` answer `unavailable` when Presidio does not answer, `invalid_argument` when it refuses the input with 400 or 422, `deadline_exceeded` when the caller ran out of time. They no longer quote Presidio's raw answer. Presidio's analyzer reports a refused input, such as a language without recognizers, as HTTP 500: that is answered as `internal` with Presidio's message.
- During a run, a value whose anonymization gets no answer from Presidio is retried for up to a minute before the run fails; it used to fail at once.
- The entity listing asks Presidio in `PRESIDIO_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` when it is set, instead of always English.
- A finding whose position falls outside the text fails the value instead of being dropped.
- At startup the API logs which Presidio features are on, and warns when an anonymizer is configured without an analyzer.
- The four `PRESIDIO_*` variables are documented.

## What does not change

- The license checks, where they were.
- What Presidio receives and returns for the same input, apart from empty fields no longer sent (checked against 2.2.362: identical answers).
- Variable names, the proto contract, the database.

## Tests

- The client over HTTP: each operation with recorded answers, each error kind, the time limit, a shorter caller deadline, cancellation, the size cap.
- The worker's retry on `unavailable`, and no retry on the other codes.
- Unit tests under the race detector, the API and worker integration suites, lint, and `go generate` leaving no diff.

author: yiliang114
body:
## What this PR does

Code Mode script output keeps its own evidence classification, while original nested tool results are preserved for Goal verification. Goal bookkeeping stays excluded from work evidence and useful computation remains available. For the new marked internal records, resumed model history, exports and ACP replay preserve the outer call/result view, and balanced completed turns retain their branch checkpoints.

## Why it's needed

A script can echo Goal metadata, discard a real tool result or emit an invented file/test claim. Previously, the wrapper output could be treated as an external fact, while aggregate recording could omit the original nested result. This existing defect was confirmed during the review of #13033 and is corrected independently here. Keeping the original records also requires downstream readers to distinguish internal evidence from model-emitted calls, so exports, replay and checkpoint validation remain compatible.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a Goal with Code Mode, silently read a known fixture, echo Goal metadata, swallow a missing-file error and emit an invented file/test claim. Original reads and errors must retain their Goal owner and enter the verifier window as external facts; script claims remain script output and Goal bookkeeping is excluded.
2. Compute `6 * 7` without a nested tool and confirm that `42` remains available as script output. Check direct execution, bridged execution and older recordings.
3. Exercise permission denial and the terminal Goal proposal barrier. Resume the session: the provider should receive paired outer calls/results without orphan internal responses, and reopening a managed log should retain the original nested records.
4. Export and replay a complete session containing the new marked internal work results and Goal bookkeeping. The visible transcript should contain the announced outer calls and ordinary direct calls, including ordinary Goal results; internal evidence must not add fabricated calls, completeness errors or unannounced ACP completions. A same-name direct file write should keep its own path and line counts. A completed Code Mode turn with these marked records should create and recover its checkpoint, while a genuine unmatched ordinary result should remain invalid.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Original evidence repair, at `2013078bdc`: the real Exec/Goal/file/recorder regression was red on the aggregate baseline because original nested results were absent; retained native input replay also showed Goal echoes and script literals classified as external facts. After correction, 1012 tests in 12 focused suites passed. Independent built-CLI headless recording and fresh-process resume retained the original evidence and paired outer history. These are historical results for that commit, including [headless verification](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13324#issuecomment-5971687721) and [fresh-process resume](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13324#issuecomment-5973797017).

Reader compatibility, `3044e3a0dc` → `16c3553015`: independent production-reader reproduction showed two fabricated export calls and two unannounced ACP completions, incorrect direct-write statistics, and an incomplete document for a partial internal display. Actual Code Mode execution and recording separately showed missing checkpoints for balanced completed turns. The five new regressions failed before repair. At the current candidate, 635 tests in 12 focused suites pass (328 core, 145 ACP, 162 CLI), together with full build, typecheck, bundle, changed-file ESLint and formatting. The commit hook preserved all reviewed source hashes. Two consecutive clean self-audits and independent correctness/simplicity reviews cover the unchanged repair.

Independent post-fix verification at the unchanged `16c3553015` passed the four production reader probes and controls. A fresh native headless Goal run retained five original internal records and projected seven outer calls without orphan ACP completions; export remained complete and Goal bookkeeping stayed outside external work evidence. Actual Code Mode execution, recorder and checkpoint recovery passed for direct reads, ordinary Code Mode and a real Goal permit; orphan, colliding-ID and missing-outer-result controls remained invalid as expected. A native ACP text control created and forked its actual persisted checkpoint. Source and all 1,370 shipped files matched the verified build. Supplementary native ACP Code Mode execution found a separate pre-existing unmarked producer failure, tracked in #13378; this PR does not claim to fix that legacy entry.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment

Node 22.22.0 on macOS. The earlier global-CLI baseline attempt could not exercise Code Mode. Native verification uses the newly built local CLI and owned deterministic loopback providers; no real model provider is used. Module-boundary fallbacks and native runs are identified separately in the reports.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: final Goal acceptance still depends on the verifier model's semantic judgement. Deterministic verification checks recording, classification and protocol behavior; it does not establish resistance to every forged claim.
- Not validated / out of scope: active-Goal continuation, full native ACP/managed or legacy restore, UI branch/fork operations, TUI, native cancellation, disabled-recording restoration, and local Windows/Linux execution. Unit coverage includes scheduler cancellation, managed record retention and API-history restoration. Default tool deferral remains in #13033; non-Code-Mode aggregate provenance is tracked in #13360. Ordinary native ACP Code Mode still writes unmarked nested results and loses checkpoints through an unchanged recording entry (#13378); that separately owned defect is outside the new marked-result compatibility repair.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: updated readers accept older recordings. Older binaries do not recognize the new internal-result subtype, so restoring newly recorded sessions requires an updated reader. Missing original results in historical transcripts cannot be recreated by this change.

Design: [English](https://github.com/yiliang114/qwen-code/blob/16c355301554341e04f504d6c7199ceee1a19b8f/docs/design/goal-code-mode-evidence.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/yiliang114/qwen-code/blob/16c355301554341e04f504d6c7199ceee1a19b8f/docs/design/goal-code-mode-evidence.zh-CN.md). Both versions describe the same contract, constraints and acceptance criteria.

## Linked Issues

Related to #13033; separate follow-ups #13360 and #13378.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

Code Mode 脚本输出采用独立证据分类，原始内部工具结果则保留给 Goal 验证。Goal 元数据继续排除在工作证据之外，普通计算仍可使用。针对新的已标记内部记录，恢复给模型的历史、导出和 ACP 回放保留外层调用与结果视图，配对完整的已完成回合保留分支检查点。

## 为什么需要

脚本可以回显 Goal 元数据、丢弃真实工具结果，或输出编造的文件与测试声明。原先包装输出可能被当作外部事实，聚合记录又可能遗漏原始内部结果。本问题在审查 #13033 时确认属于既有缺陷，在此独立修复。保留原始记录也要求下游读取器区分内部证据和模型发出的调用，确保导出、回放和检查点校验兼容。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在 Code Mode 下启动 Goal，静默读取已知文件、回显 Goal 元数据、吞掉文件不存在错误，并编造文件与测试声明。原始读取与错误必须保留 Goal 归属，以外部事实进入验证窗口；脚本声明属于脚本输出，Goal 元数据被排除。
2. 不调用内部工具，计算 `6 * 7`，确认 `42` 仍以脚本输出保留。检查直接执行、bridge 包装执行及旧记录的行为。
3. 验证权限拒绝和终止 Goal 提案屏障。恢复会话后，提供方应收到配对的外层调用与结果，没有孤立内部响应；受管理日志重新打开后应保留原始内部记录。
4. 导出并回放包含新标记内部工作结果和 Goal 元数据的完整会话。可见历史应保留已宣布的外层调用及普通直接调用，包括普通 Goal 结果；内部证据不能产生虚构调用、完整性错误或未宣布的 ACP 完成消息。同名直接文件写入应保留自己的路径与行数。包含这些已标记结果的 Code Mode 完成回合应能创建并恢复检查点，真正未配对的普通结果仍应被拒绝。

### 修复前后证据

原始证据修复，在 `2013078bdc`：真实 Exec、Goal、文件工具与记录器的回归检查在聚合基线失败，缺少原始内部结果；对保留的原生输入回放也显示 Goal 回显和脚本字面量被分类为外部事实。修复后，12 个聚焦文件共 1012 个测试通过。独立的打包 CLI headless 记录和新进程恢复保留了原始证据以及配对的外层历史。以上是该提交的历史结果，包括 [headless 验证](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13324#issuecomment-5971687721) 和 [新进程恢复](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/13324#issuecomment-5973797017)。

body: ## Thinking Path > - two-bot-next is the Together We Own Discord bot, written in Rust, running as one always-on container > - Its staging database is migrated by a staging-migrate workflow whose plan step should read the pending set without any write path, and whose apply step should stay human-gated > - Today one `migrate` job serves both modes through one reviewed environment, and the role plan knows three groups (migrator, runtime, reader); there is no least-privilege identity a plan run can borrow, so planning needs the migrator group itself > - A plan identity with SELECT on bot tables, the admission lane and the SQLx ledger — and nothing else — lets the plan step inspect everything it needs while being unable to change data or schema > - This pull request adds that fourth group, `two_bot_migrator_ro`, to the plan, the verifier, the docs and the acceptance tests, and splits the workflow into a `plan` job (no-reviewer plan environment, always runs) and an `apply` job (reviewed apply environment, mode=apply only, after a green plan) > - The benefit is that a plan dispatch reads without any write path or reviewer click, while apply keeps its human gate bound to the reviewed plan ## Linked Issues or Issue Description No public issue exists. Problem: every migration-plan read currently needs the migrator group (or a superuser), which carries full DDL/DML, and plan/apply share one job and one environment. Expected: a dedicated read-only group plus a plan job that always runs reviewer-free and an apply job that stays gated. Single-file dispatch-only policy is preserved. ## What Changed - `sql/database_roles.sql`: creates the `two_bot_migrator_ro` NOLOGIN group in the creation/refusal guard; grants it CONNECT plus USAGE on `public` and `web_v1`; grants it SELECT on `table`, `admission` and `ledger` matrix objects only; revokes it everywhere else alongside the existing groups, including default privileges - `sql/verify_database_roles.sql`: expects the fourth group, requires its schema USAGE, requires its table SELECTs and rejects any other privilege, membership, attribute or grant option for it - `docs/database-roles.md`: documents the fourth group, its least-privilege shape and the four-login deployment binding - `crates/core/src/database_roles.rs`: offline render test pins the new group in both phases - `crates/core/tests/database_roles.rs`: fourth isolated group name (longest-name-first replacement to avoid the `two_bot_migrator` prefix hazard); new read-only probes (ledger/table reads, 16 denials, least-privilege login `SET ROLE` fence denied with 42501); six read-only drift inject/restore cases - `.github/workflows/staging-migrate.yml`: `migrate` job split into `plan` (environment `staging-migrate-plan`, main-only, fixed `--plan`) and `apply` (environment `staging-migrate-apply`, main-only plus mode=apply, `needs: plan`, fixed `--apply`); per-job routed runners; `shell: bash` plus `set -o pipefail` kept on both Run steps - `scripts/ci/test_workflows.py`: job inventory and `staging_migrate_errors` rewritten for the two-job/two-env policy with fail-closed mutations (missing apply, dropped needs, always-run apply, swapped environments, per-job env/if/runner widening, per-job deploy steps) - `docs/runbook.md`: staging-migrate section documents the plan/apply jobs, environments and the create-both-before-dispatch prerequisite ## Verification - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0 - `python3 -m unittest scripts.ci.test_workflows scripts.ci.test_console_lints scripts.test_job_inputs scripts.test_container_inputs`: all pass (13 + 3 + 70) - End-to-end SQL validation against disposable `agent-testdb` scratch databases (mirrors the acceptance test, which hosted CI compiles and runs): clean full plan twice with zero verifier findings; read-only reads succeed; 16 denial probes denied; least-privilege login is not a migrator member and its `SET ROLE` into the migrator group fails with 42501; six drift cases detected then restored clean; runtime/reader/migrator-only spot checks still hold; scratch databases and roles dropped - Did not run the Rust acceptance test locally: this worker has no C toolchain for ring/rustls, so hosted CI is the compiler - Did not dispatch `staging-migrate`: the plan/apply environments do not exist yet and creation is an admin step outside agent execution - CI green on the exact head is still pending; review should wait for it ## Risks - Low. Role half is additive only: no existing grant is changed, and the verifier's new expectations are satisfied by the plan's new grants (proven by the zero-finding validation above). Workflow half keeps the reviewed dispatch shape, pipefail hardening and single-file policy; apply gains a `needs: plan` gate it did not have. New environments must be created before dispatch or the jobs fail instead of running. Rollback: revert this squash-merge. ## Model Used Anthropic Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) via Claude Code, with shell, file and GitHub tools. The pipefail hardening this stacks on was reviewed in PR #406. ## Checklist - [x] I wrote a thinking path that runs from the project to this change - [x] I named the model used, with its version - [x] I searched for duplicate or related PRs and linked them above - [x] I ran the tests locally and they pass - [x] I added or updated tests where applicable - [x] I updated the documentation this change touches - [x] No secret, token or credential is in the diff, the title, the body or the branch name - [x] No internal ticket id, instance link or private host is in the title, body, commits or branch name - [ ] CI is green on the exact head before I ask for review --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: vitalyvorobyev
body:
Roadmap Track M, step M5.

## What

**vm-primitives** — new `edge::LevelCrossing1D` (`level1d.rs`), reusable, owns its scratch, no per-call allocation:
- `end_levels(&mut self, s, count: NonZeroUsize) -> (f32, f32)` — medians of the first/last `count` samples, `np.median` semantics (mean of the two middles for even counts).
- `crossings(&mut self, s, level, polarity) -> &[f32]` — linear-interpolated crossings with `baseline.py`'s equality rules (rising `a <= L < b`, falling `a >= L > b`).
- `half_contrast(&mut self, s, seed, &HalfContrastConfig) -> LevelOutcome` — `refine.half_contrast`: flank medians at `[near, far]` either side, level = their mean, nearest crossing (a change of `s >= level`, either polarity) within `near`, iterate until it moves by `tol` or `max_iter`; a result more than `near` from the seed or an empty flank is `NoCrossing`. The crossing search only scans the segments that can lie within the window (equivalence with a full scan is a seeded unit test, ties included).
- Types: `HalfContrastConfig`, `LevelEdge { x, before, after, level, iterations }`, `LevelOutcome::{Found, LowContrast { before, after }, NoCrossing }`.
- `Edge1DDetector::smooth_in_ref` — the detector's own Gaussian (radius from the derivative setting), which both level methods read.

**measure**
- `Locate::MidpointCrossing { endpoint_samples, min_contrast }` — checks in CaliperBench's order: contrast (`LowContrast`), polarity from the levels vs `polarity` and the first `StrongestInOrder` entry (`WrongPolarity`), crossing nearest `(n − 1)/2`, ties to the first (`NoCrossing`). One edge, `amplitude = |after − before|`.
- `Locate::HalfContrast { flank_near_px, flank_far_px, tol_px, max_iter, min_contrast }` — seeds from `GradientPeak { Parabolic3 }` + the normal threshold/polarity/obliquity/select; each refined; refined edges not strictly increasing → `IncompleteSequence`. Pixel distances are converted with the profile spacing.
- `RejectReason::{LowContrast, NoCrossing}` (appended, so existing discriminants are unchanged); with `OffImage::Fill` a partly filled profile that found nothing still reports `OffImage`.
- `Caliper::levels() -> &[LevelEdge]` for the last call.
- `select_edges` now hands back candidates (profile position kept) so a selected edge can be refined.

**Python** — `vm.Locate.midpoint_crossing(endpoint_samples=3, min_contrast=0.05)`, `vm.Locate.half_contrast(flank_px=(3, 8), tol_px=0.01, max_iter=5, min_contrast=0.0)`, `Caliper.levels()`, `vm.LevelEdge`, reasons `"low_contrast"` / `"no_crossing"`; stub and tests. The Tauri command maps the new reasons.

**Docs** — `measure.md` "Locating the edge" (the three methods and when to use each), ADR-0008's edge-location paragraph rewritten, CHANGELOG, M5 row removed from the roadmap, crate READMEs, vm-python coverage/not-bound list, backlog binding note.

## Verification
- `tests/caliper_bits.rs` unchanged and green: defaults are bit-identical.
- Unit tests: exact medians (odd/even/clamped count), crossing equality cases, half-contrast seed independence (port of `test_half_contrast_does_not_depend_on_where_the_search_starts`), convergence on pixel-integrated steps at 4 phases from 5 seeds, shading the end levels miss, every failure outcome; caliper tests for the midpoint (CaliperBench's step, a hand-computed profile → 4.75, the tie rule, the check order) and half-contrast (bar, shading, staircase → `IncompleteSequence`, `LowContrast`, `NoCrossing`).
- Cross-check against CaliperBench's own `predict(method="midpoint_crossing")` (local, not committed; M7 brings the golden fixture): 800 randomized strips (oblique blurred steps, shading, noise, 1–5 lines across, 10–200 samples, every polarity): every status and rejection reason identical, worst position difference **4.3e-6 px**.

## Benchmarks
Interleaved A/B against a worktree at `origin/main` (`7cda808`), alternating base/new, 3 rounds each, Apple M4 Pro (shared machine). Medians of the three rounds:

| Bench | base | new |
|---|---|---|
| `caliper_rect_pos_1280x1024` | 1.414 µs | 1.401 µs |
| `metrology_model_apply_96_calipers` | 214.6 µs | 215.0 µs |
| `caliper_strip_40px_81s_parabolic` | 514 ns | 523 ns |
| `caliper_strip_400px_801s_w15_a15` | 34.34 µs | 34.38 µs |
| `caliper_strip_40px_81s_midpoint` | — | 481 ns |
| `caliper_strip_40px_81s_half_contrast` | — | 789 ns |

The small parabolic strip reads about 1.5 % (≈ 8 ns) slower in every round; the other default paths are flat. Half-contrast adds one smoothing pass and two flank-and-crossing refinements to the parabolic strip's work.

## Gates
`cargo fmt`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, `check-invariants.py`, vm-python `pytest` (91 passed), `lab/frontend/src-tauri` `cargo test`.

author: maulepilot117
body:
## Summary

Release F, unit **U32** (`docs/plans/2026-09-10-release-f-backup-assurance-impl.md`): the backup assurance schema and the policy/exception store. Observation only. Nothing outside `backend/internal/store/` changes, and no code path that creates a Velero object is added.

- **Migration `000022_create_backup_assurance`** creates four tables exactly as Design Decisions §1 specifies: `backup_assurance_policies`, `backup_assurance_exceptions`, `backup_assurance_deliveries` and `backup_assurance_collector_lease`. The partial UNIQUE index `idx_backup_assurance_exceptions_open_unique` allows at most one open row per `(cluster_id, subject_kind, subject_namespace, subject_name, subject_uid, condition)`. That index is the cross-replica correctness guarantee. The down migration drops all four tables.
- **`NOTES.txt`** gets a 000022 section covering:
  - rollback destroys open-exception state, so each still-true condition is re-notified exactly once;
  - no Velero CRD and no `nc_*` table is touched;
  - deleting a policy cascades to its exceptions and their deliveries;
  - the 90-day retention.
- **`store.BackupAssuranceStore`**:
  - policy CRUD (`InsertPolicy`, `UpdatePolicy`, `DeletePolicy`, `GetPolicy`, `ListPolicies`), scoped by cluster, with optimistic revisions;
  - `ListOpenExceptions`;
  - `ListExceptions`, filtered by state and namespace restriction, paged, and returning the pre-paging total;
  - `ObserveException`, which only moves open to open and is monotonic in `observedAt`;
  - `PruneResolved`, which refuses a non-positive retention;
  - `WithTx`, for U32b's composite transitions.

  `NewBackupAssuranceStore(nil)` returns nil, so callers must nil-check it (U34c wires it).

Decisions applied:
- **O-2:** install creates no default policy. The migration seeds nothing and a test asserts it.
- **O-3:** resolved exceptions are kept for 90 days, via the constant `store.BackupAssuranceExceptionRetention` and a NOTES.txt sentence.

## Deviations from the plan

- **Plan finding C2 is out of date.** Migration 000021 (#2 pre-existing defect, merged after the plan was written) already added `cluster_id` and `resource_uid` to the notification dedup key. The plan's rationale for durable exception state still holds: duration mismatch, no delivery signal, and resolution needing prior state. U32 changes no code because of this. Later units should not cite C2 as a current defect.
- **`AssuranceExceptionQuery` is defined here.** The plan names the type but not its fields. Fields: `State` (`""` means all), `RestrictNamespaces` plus `Namespaces` (an empty list matches nothing, and cluster-scoped rows are included only when `""` is listed), `Limit` (default 50, max 500) and `Offset`. U35's handler filters further with SSAR and must recompute counts after filtering, as the plan requires.
- **Policy scope cannot be changed after creation.** `UpdatePolicy` rewrites thresholds and switches only; a different scope means a new policy. The plan's `SET …` left this open.
- **Extra Go-side validation and sentinels beyond the plan's list.** `validatePolicy` checks scope shape, `treatPartialAs`, whole seconds and the int32 range, and returns `ErrAssurancePolicyInvalid`. A CHECK violation also maps to `ErrAssurancePolicyInvalid`. `ObserveException` returns `ErrAssuranceExceptionNotOpen` and `ErrAssuranceObservationInvalid`. The numeric floors stay with the DB CHECKs, which remain the single owner.
- **Extra tests.** All eleven named tests are present, plus hermetic enum/validation tests, a `ListExceptions` filter/paging table and a `WithTx` rollback test.

## Code review (ce-code-review, full depth)

Reviewers: correctness, project-standards, testing, maintainability, data-migration, reliability, learnings, plus an independent cross-model adversarial pass. The pass used Codex (requested gpt-6-luna at xhigh; served model unverified). Verdict on the first commit: *Ready with fixes*, no P0/P1. Every finding and residual risk was handled in `0e1d4242`:

| Finding | Source | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `validatePolicy` checked only the upper int32 bound, so a huge negative duration could wrap into a valid-looking threshold (P3, validator-confirmed) | correctness, testing, reliability | **Fixed.** Both bounds are checked (`fitsInt32Seconds`). Added negative-wrap and grace-underflow test cases. |
| The global `PruneResolved` test could delete other suites' rows in the shared DB (P3) | adversarial (Codex) | **Fixed.** The test runs on a throwaway `migrationScratchDB`, and its oracle is now exact (`n == 1`). |
| A delayed replica could overwrite a newer observation with stale severity/detail | adversarial (Codex), reliability | **Fixed.** `ObserveException` updates only when `last_observed_at <= observedAt`. A stale observation of an open row is dropped with a nil error. Tested. |
| A nil `lastSuccessAt` erased a recorded success | reliability | **Fixed.** `COALESCE($4, last_success_at)`. Tested. |
| A bad severity or malformed detail surfaced as an unclassified pg error; empty non-nil detail was not defaulted | maintainability, reliability | **Fixed.** Added severity constants plus validation and a `json.Valid` check, returning `ErrAssuranceObservationInvalid` before any DB call. `len(detail) == 0` becomes `'{}'`. Tested. |
| `WithTx` rollback on `context.WithoutCancel` had no deadline | reliability | **Fixed.** The rollback context is detached from cancellation and bounded to 5s. |
| Testing gaps: `WithTx` panic path; namespace restriction with `""` | testing | **Fixed.** Added a panic-rollback test and a cluster-scoped-inclusion case. Commit-failure injection is not practical against a real pool and is left untested. |
| No CHECK tying `state='resolved'` to `resolved_at IS NOT NULL`; exception `cluster_id` not constrained to the policy's cluster | correctness (residual) | **Not changed (latent).** U32 must ship the §1 DDL verbatim, and adding constraints would change the mandated schema. No U32 path writes exceptions: U32b's resolve UPDATE sets `resolved_at`, and U32b/U33 write the policy's cluster. Recommend U32b assert both in its transition tests. |
| A policy delete cascades away open-exception history | data-migration (residual) | **By design (plan §1 iii).** Documented in NOTES.txt. Confirmation and audit belong to U35's admin handler. |
| `docs/solutions/postgres-test-harness-conventions.md` table audit should list the Release F tables | learnings | **Deferred.** Updating it would exceed the five-file unit cap. Follow-up after merge. |

## Verification

Run locally on Windows (no gcc, so `-race` is CI-only) against a throwaway `postgres:17-alpine`:

```
cd backend && go vet ./...                         -> clean
KUBECENTER_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<fresh db> go test ./... -count=1   -> EXIT=0, 36 packages ok
KUBECENTER_TEST_REQUIRE_DATABASE=1 go test ./internal/store/ -run 'Assurance|Policy_|Exception_|ValidatePolicy' -v
  -> 15/15 PASS (incl. both 000022 migration round-trip tests on scratch DBs)
go test ./internal/store/ (no DB env)              -> ok (DB tests skip)
```

Two harness behaviours showed up locally that this PR does not cause:
- `TestESOHistory_PageSQL_KeysetUnderGenericPlan` starts failing on a shared test database after several repeated runs. `eso_sync_history` residue changes the planner's index choice. It passes on a fresh database.
- The first `go test ./...` against an empty database can hit a cross-package `pg_advisory_lock` deadlock while several packages migrate at once. A re-run passes.

No frontend files changed, so `bun run check` was not run.

Parte de #390 (PR 7a: gestión de compras, diálogo de ítem, buscador, stock/sugerida y lista de compras). Recepción de mercadería (7b) y solicitud de pago (7c) van aparte.

Plan, desvíos, prueba de runtime y auditoría: `docs/manuales-implementacion/operaciones/plan-errores-de-red-en-gestion-compras.md`.

## Qué cambia
- **Arranque y recargas**: monedas/formas de pago/sucursales y el pedido se cortan y avisan («Reintentar» / «Actualizar»); sin datos no se guarda la cabecera. Una recarga fallida tras una acción avisa que la acción se registró.
- **Ítem en edición**: si las distribuciones no cargan no se inicializa como alta (el merge pisaba las reales): Guardar bloqueado + «Reintentar distribuciones». «Distribuir» no abre el diálogo vacío.
- **Stock y sugerida**: «—» si no se obtienen; la sugerida no se calcula con un 0 inventado.
- **Cotización**: al cambiar de moneda se vacía mientras consulta y, si no responde, queda vacía con aviso (antes quedaba la de la moneda anterior). El refresco manual conserva el valor si falla.
- **Buscador**: 10 s, sin duplicar la espera con la búsqueda por filtros, sin cachear fallos; la búsqueda al escribir no muere con un error.
- **Lista de compras**: avisa, conserva las filas y no cachea el fallo de sucursales recepcionadas.

## Prueba
Central local `:8081` (replicación apagada y verificada) congelado con `kill -STOP`, desktop con `ng serve -c web`; sin guardar nada. Todos los casos dieron lo esperado (tabla en el plan). Errores GraphQL (`null`) verificados por código. `npm run check` OK en cada fase.

Ensayo de release: entra el bloque de calidad interna completo (puntos 19 del
roadmap) más las cuatro features que lo precedieron.

## Features

- **#67 · filtro por color** y panel de filtros rehecho en grupos plegables (el

- **#68 · disfraces y calzado**: categorías nuevas con foto propia y **dos

  al carrito".
- **#70 · "Eliminar mis datos"** en Ajustes: borra la clave de esa cuenta y
  cierra sesión. Las preferencias del dispositivo y las claves de otras cuentas
  sobreviven.

## Calidad interna (bloque de 5 ramas, tests primero)

- **#71 · red de pruebas antes de tocar nada**: de 487 a 531 tests, cero cambios
  en código de producción. Se cubrió el despachador de `main.js`, que no tenía
  NINGUNA prueba, y por fin `main.js` se carga en los tests.
- **#72 · fix**: la reseña se guardaba con fecha inválida (hallazgo de #71).
- **#73 · refactor de `data.js` / `state.js`**, con los invariantes de precio y
  depósito intactos.
- **#74 · guardarraíl del despachador**: sin él no se podía extraer ningún
  helper de marcado sin cegar el inventario de acciones.

author: fingolfin
body:
When searching in the full symmetric group on the domain, PartitionBacktrack changed the base of the stabilizer chain of S_n for every point fixed in the R-base. Instead count the points not yet fixed, and build the permutation at a leaf from the discrete partitions. For a transitive group of order 1296000 on 1125 points, ConjugatorPermGroup in S_1125 drops from 22.5 to 1.2 seconds and NormalizerPermGroup from 79 to 5.2 seconds.

Heiko Theißen added this in 1997. It was switched off in 1998 and the code commented out in 2001 as "too hopeless". Two flaws of the old code would explain that: it counted the moved points of the group even if the domain was larger, and it counted a point again that was fixed already. Either ends the R-base before the partition is discrete. Guard against both, and raise an error if a partition at a leaf is not discrete, as a partial map could lose a solution silently. Also handle leaves of an empty R-base, and pass the property as a function rather than a list.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5.5)

Stage 2: Kapitel 1, Gården, in greybox, from the deck to the forest's edge (plan §3.4).

**Open it with `?dev`.** Without `?dev` the page still shows the test course: no chapter is released, and `RELEASED_CHAPTER` is untouched.

## What you play

1. **The deck:** steps like cliffs, and the gap where Pappa has lifted a board.
2. **The ladybird:** Använd turns its lever (*Vänd*). It flies to the hose, and Elof slides down it.
3. **Under the deck:** the lace on a nail. One swing over flat ground, where a miss costs nothing, and one over the drain gully.
4. **The dandelion:** the ghost can nearly be caught (*Ta!*), and drops five candies.
5. **The lawn:** the birch's roots and a boulder.
6. **Under the birch:** the dew rain.
7. **Pappa's shavings:** one curl pulled down as a step, one pushed across the gap at the top.
8. **Moa:** *Ropa på Moa*, and her paper plane carries him over the hedge to the forest's edge. Up and down steer towards the candy.

Then the card: *Kapitel 1 klart!*, with the candy in rows of ten and *Spela igen*.

It is ground, candy and rules only: it looks like the test course. What it looks like comes with the look-dev and the characters.

## What is new for it

- **Bubbles** for what is said (`ChapterData.beats`): the game has no voices. Four lines so far, all in `src/content/sv.ts`.
- **Rides that can't fail** (`ChapterData.rides`): an arc from one place to another, steered up and down inside its corridor.
- **A hose that waits for a flag** (`Climb.needs`), a glint over each thing Använd can act on, and the end card.
- **The list of courses** (`src/content/chapters/index.ts`): `?course=testbana`, `?course=garden`, and `?dev`.
- **The robot is shared** between the courses (`tests/robot/robot.ts`).

## Tests

10 new ones. The robot plays the chapter at 30, 60 and 144 Hz with no bubble and no knock, and leaves at most six candies; on *Lugnt* it is played by running and Använd, with Hoppa only on the lace. The browser test opens `?dev` and reads the first bubble.

The prologue before it; the swing chain (C1); the lost things; the dew bells; memory 1; the ghost as helper and its bubbles; the family as giants; stickers and Moa's map. The chapter takes the robot about two minutes, and the plan asks for 18 to 22 for Elof.

body:
## Description

Picks up #2208 by @Sh4pe on `v2`, the way @BeastyBlacksmith suggested there: the bins follow the axis scale, so on a log axis they are spaced evenly in the log. This covers `histogram`, `stephist`, `scatterhist` and `histogram2d`.

`_make_hist` bins the log of the values and maps the edges back, so the counts and `normalize` work as before, with densities per unit of the value. `bins` given as edges are still in the values' units. Values the axis cannot show, zero and below, are left out along with their weights, as NaNs already were.

Two more things kept log axes from working:
- `histogram(x; xscale = :log10)` drew no axes and the bars filled the frame, because the bar recipe widened the bin range linearly, down below zero. It widens in the axis scale now, which is the same on a linear axis.
- `histogram2d` passed linear bin centers to the heatmap, which works out the cells in the log, so the cells came out as thin slivers. The centers are taken in the axis scale now.

A NaN together with `weights` threw a `DimensionMismatch`, since the NaN was dropped but not its weight. That goes through the same filtering now.

On linear axes the edges and counts are exactly as before, and the reference images are untouched. With `permute` the scale is read the same way as in the rest of the bar code, which #5825 makes follow `permute`.

## Attribution
- [ ] I am listed in the appropriate version of `.zenodo.json` for [PRs against v2](https://github.com/JuliaPlots/Plots.jl/blob/v2/.zenodo.json) or [PRs against master](https://github.com/JuliaPlots/Plots.jl/blob/master/.zenodo.json) (see https://github.com/JuliaPlots/Plots.jl/issues/3503)

## Things to consider
- [x] Does it work on log scales? That is the change
- [x] Does it work in layouts? Not affected
- [x] Does it work in recipes? Yes, all the histogram recipes go through `_make_hist`
- [x] Does it work with multiple series in one call? Not affected
- [x] PR includes or updates tests? `test_recipes.jl` checks the log spaced bins in 1D and 2D, finite limits, the density, and dropping values with their weights. They fail without the change
- [x] PR includes or updates documentation? `NEWS.md`

author: kakkoidev
body:
## Summary
Audit fixes. Each fix has a regression test that fails on the old code.

- **Order validation:** orders are re-checked against the live world before they are applied. This stops double-spending, negative resources and multiple missions per fleet.
- **Resource exploits:**
  - Ship-cost overflow made ships free; batch size is now capped.
  - Negative transport cargo created resources; cargo capacity was never checked.
  - Fuel was burned before the cargo check, so a rejected launch still paid.
- **Determinism:**
  - The fuel-paying planet was picked in map order; it now uses slot order.
  - Agent observations are now sorted deep copies instead of live world objects.
- **Spec fixes:**
  - Capture needs a frigate or cruiser; a lone scout could take a colony.
  - Exiled empires can recolonize with zero-cost launches.
  - `TurnResult` returns only the current turn's events and has JSON tags for the browser.
- **Robustness:**
  - `serve` no longer exits when a client disconnects mid-page.
  - `agame new` refuses to overwrite an existing run.
  - World saves are atomic, and event-log write errors are reported.
  - The OpenAI adapter handles a malformed endpoint, fenced JSON and oversized bodies.
  - Autopilot no longer re-issues a colonize order that can't launch.
- **Coverage:**

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| world | 59% | 92% |
| agent | 58% | 92% |
| engine | 0% | 95% |
| run | 36% | 84% |
| media | 0% | 88% |
| cmd/agame | 0% | 51% |

Known gaps (combat rounds, docked ships defending, stranded fleets, trade between empires) are recorded as skipped tests with reasons.

author: ruckth
body:
A successfully sent reply now moves its guest turn to Done automatically when no staff task or handoff remains. New guest messages reopen the chat; unresolved handoffs, failed or uncertain delivery, and explicit follow-ups stay visible. Staff send once instead of sending and then clicking Resolve, and the selected transcript remains visible as its queue changes.

All five channels share correlated lifecycle transitions. Guest-message IDs and staff request IDs prevent stale replies, alerts, failures and watchdogs from overriding newer work. Drafts stay attached to the guest turn they cover and require review after a new message. No reply needed checks the current turn transactionally, including legacy chats. Undo creates a review task; Keep with staff preserves deliberate ownership.

Generated AI answers require explicit outcome evidence. Missing markers and staff promises stay Needs you; optional contact guidance does not create a false handoff. Outcome normalization and staff notification use one classifier. Follow-up save errors remain visible inside the dialog with the entered task preserved.

Validation:
- `pnpm verify`: all typechecks, ESLint without warnings, 990 tests across 101 files, production build (147 routes).
- Independent Standards and Spec reviews report no remaining blockers. Added public-action and UI regressions for AI outcome evidence, draft/new-message races, guarded manual completion, legacy IDs, and accessible follow-up failures.
- Real development app checks for all eight plan cases, actual Web staff sends/retries/task completion, Undo and No reply needed; 17 local screenshots, including a 390px mobile viewport. AI/provider outcomes and failures were simulated; no external guest messages were sent. Temporary fixtures were removed.
- Development backfill: previewed 368 sessions, reviewed a dry-run batch with changes, migration completed. Production migration has not run; rollout commands are documented in `docs/plans/automatic-inbox-lifecycle.md`.

Interactive plan: `public/prototypes/inbox-lifecycle-plan.html`.

author: webtecnica
body:
Closes #2190

## O problema

Depois da #2189 quem ouve o áudio do cliente é a **escada** (`lib/messaging/media/escada-de-transcricao.ts`): serviço da instalação (`TRANSCRIPTION_API_KEY`) → chave OpenAI → modelo de conversa da organização (quando declara áudio) → nada, com motivo. Uma organização sem chave OpenAI, com Gemini, transcreve pelo Gemini.

Mas a **tela** seguia anunciando outro caminho: o ponto `transcricao_de_audio` em `lib/ai/pontos/registro.ts` vinha com `fixo: { provider: "openai", modelId: "whisper-1" }` e a razão dizendo "exige uma chave desse serviço". Dois caminhos anunciados para o mesmo áudio — e a régua tela×motor só cobria imagem/modelo, então passava em verde.

## O que mudou

- `lib/ai/pontos/registro.ts` — o ponto deixa de fixar provider/modelo e passa a declarar `fixo.escada: "transcricao"`; a razão passa a descrever os três degraus e o motivo quando nenhum existe.
- `lib/messaging/media/escada-de-transcricao.ts` — cada degrau ganha `anuncio` (o que a rota anuncia) e `motivo` (por que **este** áudio vai para **aquele** degrau); `decidirTranscricao` passa a ser exportada para a tela rodar a mesma escada.
- `app/api/v1/ai/providers/route.ts` — roda a escada com os dados que já estão na requisição (credenciais ativas da org + knobs do `.env` do processo) e entrega a decisão ao resolvedor; some o override de `modeloDeTranscricaoEmVigor` na rota e o `porQue` fixo da origem passa a preferir o motivo escolhido.
- `lib/ai/pontos/resolver.ts` — o degrau 0 ganha o ramo `fixo.escada`, que devolve o anúncio do degrau resolvido (ou `"—"` com motivo, quando a escada não veio: o resolvedor é puro, não inventa `whisper-1`); `DecisaoDeBinding` ganha `motivo`.
- i18n — a razão nova entra em `lib/i18n/dicionario.ts` (es), `traducoes/en.json` e `traducoes/zh-CN.json`; a antiga sai dos três.
- `tests/unit/a-tela-e-o-motor-concordam-sobre-imagem.test.ts` — a régua tela×motor passa a cobrir a escada de transcrição: o motor tem que devolver exatamente o degrau que a tela anuncia, a razão não pode citar um serviço fixo, o registro não pode voltar a fixar provider/modelo no ponto, e o valor tem que depender da escada (mudou degrau → muda anúncio).
- `tests/unit/painel-de-provedores-anuncia-o-modelo-de-transcricao.test.ts` — mesma pergunta, do lado da rota: os três degraus anunciados (serviço da instalação, chave OpenAI com `whisper-1`/`gpt-transcribe`, modelo de conversa da org).

## O que medi

- **Régua alvo, VERMELHO antes do fix** (só os testes novos, motor antigo): `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/a-tela-e-o-motor-concordam-sobre-imagem.test.ts` → **5 falhas / 24 testes** (19 verdes), exit 1.
- **Mesmo gate, VERDE depois do fix**: **24/24 verdes**, exit 0.
- **Irmãos** (12 arquivos ligados a pontos/escada/provedores/i18n, incluindo a régua alvo): **143/143 verdes**, exit 0.
- **typecheck**: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.typecheck.json` → exit 0, saída vazia.
- **eslint** nos 7 arquivos tocados → exit 0.
- Todos os gates rodaram fora do cgroup do gateway: espera por irmão (`pgrep vitest|tsc --noEmit`) + `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=5G --collect`, com `timeout` por comando.

## O que NÃO medi

- **Suíte inteira** (`pnpm test:unit`) e **`pnpm cercas`**: não rodei — fora do orçamento do lote. Cobrei apenas os 12 arquivos do recorte de pontos/escada/provedores/i18n.
- **`test:e2e` / playwright**: não rodei (sem Docker no meu caminho).
- **Comportamento em runtime**: não subi stack local; a rota chama `decidirTranscricao`, que é pura (sem I/O), mas a chamada em si em produção não foi medida.
- **Demais textos do cartão** do ponto além da razão, e traduções de en/zh foram escritas por mim sem revisão de falante nativo.

## Como reproduzir

```bash
# vermelho (testes novos + motor antigo)
git stash -- lib/ app/            # mantém só os testes
pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/a-tela-e-o-motor-concordam-sobre-imagem.test.ts   # 5 falhas
git stash pop
pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/a-tela-e-o-motor-concordam-sobre-imagem.test.ts   # 24/24
```

author: iseekyan
body:
Adds an opt-in training-side W4A8 forward for MoE routed experts that follows the operand contract of the rollout's DeepGEMM FP8 x MXFP4 MoE path (vLLM `DeepGemmFP4Experts`, `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`).

**Numerics**
- Activations: dynamic per-token, K-group 128 E4M3. Scale = `ceil_ue8m0(max(amax/448, 1e-10))`, with amax also floored at 1e-10 and the exponent rounded up by bit math. This matches vLLM's per-token-group quant kernels byte for byte on CPU transcriptions. All-zero groups get scale 2^-33, and an amax of 448·2^k gets exactly 2^k. vLLM's 1e-10 floor is used rather than the 1e-4 clamp in DeepGEMM's own test cast.
- Weights: MXFP4 bytes from `quantize_mxfp4` on the BF16 master. These are the same bytes the QAT exporter streams to the rollout, and a test checks this against the exporter.
- GEMM: DeepGEMM on CUDA, raising if DeepGEMM is unavailable rather than falling back. The CPU reference multiplies the identical dequantized operands in FP32.
- Expert MLP: BF16 FC1 output, SwiGLU in FP32 rounded once to BF16, A8 requantization, BF16 FC2 output, router weight applied after FC2 in FP32.
- Backward: straight-through on both operands into the BF16 master weights. No saturation mask is needed because both scale rules cannot saturate.

**Surface**
- `QATSpec(activation_bits=8)` is accepted only with `format="mxfp4"`.
- Qwen3 MoE switches its `Experts` to the W4A8 forward. It honours `ignore_patterns` and rejects fp8 padding, `moe_act` recompute and expert LoRA.
- `apply_qat_to_chunks` rejects `activation_bits` for models that do not wire W4A8 experts, so those models cannot silently train weight-only.
- With the default configuration, the model construction, state dict, forward and gradients are byte-identical to main, and the new module is not imported. This was checked in separate processes against main.

**Tests**: 25 new CPU tests, all of which fail on main. Eight mutations of the numerics (scale floor, UE8M0 rounding, exponent off-by-one, saturation, router-weight position, SwiGLU rounding, STE operand, weight bytes) are each caught. Two Blackwell GPU tests (DeepGEMM vs. reference, installed vLLM quant op vs. ours) are included and marked; they have not been run yet.

**Not in this PR**
- DeepSeek V4.1 wiring and SITU.
- FP32 top-k combine: the dispatcher still sums BF16 per-expert outputs.
- Batch-invariant mode.
- A W4A8 rollout configuration: the existing four-arm example is a W4A16 rollout and does not match this contract.
- Weight-only MXFP4 QAT does not currently reach TE `GroupedLinear` expert weights (`weight0..N-1`). This predates this change and is tracked separately.

## Review follow-up (`44a0d386`, `51c704c4`)

- Live-kernel evidence on GB200 (vendored DeepGEMM `m_grouped_fp8_fp4_gemm_nt_contiguous`): the training-side W4A8 expert forward is **bitwise identical** to vLLM's `DeepGemmFP4Experts.apply` for top-k 1 and top-k 8.
- Top-k combine now accumulates in FP32 (FMA) on the W4A8 path, matching vLLM. With BF16 accumulation, 58% of output elements differed by 1 BF16 ulp at Qwen3-30B dimensions (H2048/I768, top-k 8); with FP32 accumulation the difference is zero. A test at those dimensions fails on the previous head and passes now.
- Scale handling aligned with vLLM (all-zero MXFP4 blocks), unsupported K dimensions (including after ETP split) rejected at enable time, and a real tiny `Qwen3MoEModel` built via `build_model` runs a training step on CPU.
- Default path unchanged: loss and all gradients of a tiny Qwen3MoE model (QAT off and weight-only MXFP4), and a standalone MoE layer forward/backward, are identical across main and this branch.
- Preconditions for bitwise equality: unfused permute (W4A8 with fused permute or DeepEP is rejected at `build_model`), vLLM's default E8M0 scale setting, and router weights taken from the training-side output. The EP>1 all-to-all combine path has not been run on multiple GPUs.
- The unrelated formatting commit was removed; the diff contains only this feature.

## Final (`edb328ca`) — after two review rounds (advisory, no blockers)

- EP>1 is rejected at enable time (and therefore by `build_model`) until the expert-parallel combine has multi-GPU validation; use EP=1.
- One weighting contract: router weights are applied only during the FP32 top-k combine. The unused "weight after FC2" branch was removed; W4A8 `Experts` now raises if given router probabilities.
- The MoE-layer bitwise test now recomputes expected unweighted expert rows independently from the inputs and master weights; a double-weighting mutation makes it fail (the previous test still passed under that mutation).
- Targeted suite: 193 passed, 4 skipped (Blackwell-only); the remaining failures are identical to main (missing Transformer Engine / environment). GPU tests only had call-signature updates in this commit and were not re-run on GPU.

Limitations: GPU parity tests skip when DeepGEMM/Blackwell are unavailable; DeepEP rejection is enforced at build but has no EP>1 branch test (EP>1 is rejected outright); no matching W4A8 rollout recipe is included.
