author: miguelfiguera
body:
## Issue

Agent CLIs fill their context window with raw tool output (long `git log`, test runs, build logs), and there was no way to see what an agent is actually holding in its context. This branch adds context mode — tool output is offloaded to a local, searchable store and the model receives a pointer or summary instead — plus a `/context` window to inspect each live agent's context. Work in progress (step 3).

## Summary

- Add context mode: offload large shell output to a local SQLite + FTS5 store and hand the model a pointer or computed summary
- Connect context mode to Claude Code and the Cursor CLI through pre-tool-use and session-start hooks
- Add the `polakapi ctx`, `polakapi ctx-hook` and `polakapi ctx-mcp` subcommands
- Add a `/context` window showing what each running agent holds in its context
- Add Context Mode settings and a project action to delete stored context data
- Add close all and reload all to the project actions menu
- Bump version to 0.15.0

## Changes

### Backend

- New `ctx` module (`src-tauri/src/ctx/`): router (bypass / summarize / index), chunking that keeps code blocks intact, summarizer for logs and test output (keeps both sides of a failed assertion), SQLite + FTS5 store, storage paths with promotion into the project's `.polakapi/`, and per-session stores keyed by the CLI session so resumed sessions find them
- Rerouted commands run in the user's shell with capped output, cut on character boundaries; output is still returned when the store cannot be written
- `polakapi ctx` CLI (search / read) and `polakapi ctx-mcp` stdio MCP server exposing the `ctx_*` tools
- `polakapi ctx-hook` handler for Claude Code (`PreToolUse` / `Bash`, `hookSpecificOutput`) and Cursor (`preToolUse` / `Shell`, top-level `updated_input`); hooks act only inside polakapi terminals and under their own CLI, carry no permission decision, and are removed when switched off
- Hook installer keeps `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.cursor/hooks.json` in step with the toggles, recognises existing hooks by shape, and preserves a symlinked settings file
- Context mode is applied to a CLI started from a plain shell pane; hook diagnostics log only the program seen and are size-capped
- New `agent_context` module reading Claude Code and Codex transcripts and process lists off the main thread, with regex search over full entry bodies and context window sizes matched by model version
- `Db::cli_session_id_for_pty` and `db::agent_session` to link a pane to its transcript; `memory::tree_maps` extracted so the process walk is shared
- New `pty_activity` to report which panes still have running commands before batch close / reload
- `regex` crate added

### Frontend

- `/context` window (`context.html`, `agents-flow/context-window.ts`, `agent-context/`): agents grouped by project, per-category breakdown, entry list with on-demand bodies, sorting and search; stale answers are ignored once the view moves on
- Context Mode section in Settings with per-CLI toggles and an accurate description of what it does today
- Project actions menu: close all, reload all (with a running-commands warning), and delete stored context mode data
- Split layout preserved when reloading all terminals

### Tests

- 10 frontend test files added or updated: context formatting, context mode preferences / info / settings section, project data, terminal batch operations, terminal manager, project pane, and window capabilities
- Rust unit tests across the new `ctx`, `agent_context`, hooks and `pty_activity` code

### Other

- New `context` window capability and Vite entry
- `docs/context-mode-plan.md` with the analysis, architecture and implementation plan, including verified Cursor CLI hook behavior
- Version bumped to 0.15.0 in `package.json`, `tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added Context Mode for offloading, summarizing, searching, and retrieving agent tool output, with configurable CLI support, storage, and size thresholds.
  * Added a `/context` view for monitoring running agents, reviewing context usage and process stats, and searching or sorting transcript entries.
  * Added project settings to manage Context Mode and clear stored context data.
  * Added terminal actions to reload or close all panes, with a confirmation when panes are running commands.
* **Improvements**
  * Reloading panes now preserves their layout, titles, directories, CLI selection, and startup commands.
  * Added clearer context-mode information and status feedback.

author: corruptmemory
body:
The two open items from PR #5's review: chunked request bodies (refused with 501 today, though Caddy and cloudflared forward unknown-length bodies chunked), and slow clients pinning memory. Spec: `docs/plans/2026-10-03-chunked-and-slow-clients-design.md`; plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-03-chunked-and-slow-clients-implementation.md`.

## Summary

- **Chunked request bodies.**
  - **Decoding** (`parse_chunked`): in place, inside the read buffer. A write cursor trails the read cursor, chunk data moves down, and framing is skipped. The grammar is strict: CRLF only; chunk sizes are bounded to 15 significant hex digits before any arithmetic; extensions and trailers are validated, then discarded. Handlers see one contiguous `req.body`.
  - **Framing rules** (`finish_headers`):
    - 400 for any of: Transfer-Encoding with Content-Length; Transfer-Encoding on HTTP/1.0; a final coding other than `chunked`; `chunked` listed twice.
    - 501 when another coding comes before `chunked`.
    - A chunked body that fills the read buffer is 413 and is timed as BODY.
- **Minimum drain rate** (`MIN_SEND_RATE`, 16 KB/s). While a response tail is queued, the client must take bytes at this average rate once the `WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` grace has passed. Both WRITE checks count the bytes the peer actually takes: what is left of our tail plus the kernel's unsent and unacknowledged bytes (`TIOCOUTQ`). A reader at or above the floor is never cut.
- **Per-worker pending budget** (`MAX_PENDING_PER_WORKER`, 64 MB).
  - Every tail is reserved once and charged to its worker's pool. It is refunded in `release_pending`, the one place every tail ends.
  - A refusal closes the connection. Refusals are reported as one `log_error` line per worker per second, so a client cannot flood the error log.
  - The once-a-second sweep now always runs.
- **First-request deadline.** A connection that has sent nothing (state NEW) gets `HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) from accept, then a silent close, as nginx does. If header timeouts are off, it falls back to the idle limit.
- **Cleanup.** The dead `CACHE_LINE_SIZE` parameter and the stray `channel.jai` were deleted earlier, in PR #5.

## Spec deviations

1. **Budget charge.** It is recorded in `pending_charge` rather than refunded from `pending.allocated`, because tests append to `pending` directly.
2. **Test connections.** `standalone_connection` (tests) shares one accounting pool, `standalone_pool`, because the writer tests `free()` connections one by one.
3. **File placement.** `Tail_Refusal`, `tail_refusal` and `reserve_tail` live in `connection.jai`, beside the refund.
4. **§4.1 amended after the final review (I1).** The rate floor's deadline now moves forward with the bytes the peer takes, instead of being fixed when the tail is queued.

## Final review

A fresh Opus reviewer ran a 200,000-message fuzz of the decoder and a real-TCP `TIOCOUTQ` probe. A read-only Codex pass read the Jai reference first.

**Fixed, test first:**
- **I1 (Important).** WRITE progress was measured by our own flushes. Those happen only at an edge-triggered EPOLLOUT, which on a full socket comes after about a third of the kernel's send buffer drains (2.4–2.8 MB on loopback). So the 30 s stall check cut readers above the floor, and the original fixed deadline had the same blind spot. Pinned by `test_kernel_drain_counts_as_progress`, over loopback TCP.
- **M1 (re-graded Important).** With `HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 0`, a silent NEW connection was never reaped; on master it was reaped as IDLE at 60 s. Pinned by `test_new_connection_limit_falls_back_to_idle`.

**Deferred minors, for your call:**
- `WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 0` also zeroes the floor's grace. This is now documented next to the parameter.
- `reserve_tail` does not assert its empty-queue precondition. No caller violates it.
- No `#assert` stops a `WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` near `S64_MAX` from overflowing `start + grace` in `drain_deadline`.
- Two test gaps: no fake-worker test where many small chunks fill the buffer, and the logging test uses one refusal rather than two.
- NEW's 10 s close can race Go's transport (Caddy) on a dialed-but-unused pooled connection, which could produce a rare 502. Low confidence.
- From Codex: Transfer-Encoding with a >18-digit Content-Length answers 413 instead of rule 2's 400. Both refuse and close.

## PR review

Two independent passes over the whole PR: the `/code-review` agent (15 leads, each then checked against the code) and a read-only Codex pass that read the Jai reference first. Both came back clean on crashes, arithmetic overflow, request smuggling and budget accounting. Codex traced the `body_end <= parse_offset` invariant and both charge/refund paths independently.

**Design rationale corrected (finding 1, with 4).** Spec §4.2 justified refuse-not-evict by saying the rate floor makes an attacker's share of the budget turn over within about 94 s. It does not: a drained tail's refund goes straight back to the same connection's next pipelined response in the same `handle_client` call, and the floor is per tail, so a reader at about 11 KB/s per 1 MB tail keeps its share. Holding one worker's whole budget costs about 0.7 MB/s of real download. The floor bounds pinned memory (about 94 s of the attacker's download rate), not fairness. Refuse stays for now, because nothing in the library answers with 1 MB tails yet. The static-file plan decides eviction, together with zero-copy static bodies, which would not be charged at all. Amended in spec §4.2; module.jai's `MIN_SEND_RATE` comment no longer says a slow reader "frees its slot".

**Fixed in this PR, test first (`9539e3b`):**
- **Stray empty lines (finding 3; older than this PR).** A CRLF after a request (RFC 9112 §2.2 says to ignore it) stayed buffered and turned an idle connection into a HEADER wait, closed with an unsolicited 408 ten seconds later. `skip_empty_lines` now consumes empty lines when nothing else is buffered, and the request clock starts in `dispatch_buffered` where a partial request is first parsed, not at the read, so empty lines start nothing, even behind a stalled response. Pinned by `test_trailing_empty_line_leaves_connection_idle`, `test_empty_lines_do_not_start_a_request` and `test_empty_line_behind_a_stalled_response`.
- **First-request clock (findings 2, 6, 7).** A connection's first request has its BODY wait timed from accept as well as its HEADER wait. This is now documented in module.jai, README and spec §4.3. The test `attach()` stamps `request_start_ms` as accept does, so fake-worker tests start NEW. Pinned through the real read path by `test_first_request_timed_from_accept`.
- **`drain_deadline` sentinel (finding 9).** "No floor" returned 0, which `now >= deadline` satisfies. It now returns `NO_DRAIN_DEADLINE`.

**Declined:** setting `TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT` at accept so EPOLLOUT edges come often enough to make our own flushes the progress measure. The kernel stops accepting writes once unsent bytes reach the threshold, so the buffering moves into our heap tails. With `MAX_PENDING_BYTES` at 1 MB, responses over about 1 MB would be refused even for fast readers; today the kernel takes about 2.4 MB up front on loopback. Worth revisiting with zero-copy static bodies.

**Deferred from the PR review:** the decoded request keeps its `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header (Go's net/http strips it); chunk-size and trailer lines are rescanned from their start on every read, quadratic in their length (capped at 4096, and header lines already behave this way); NEW is still inferred from `bytes_used == 0 && request_start_ms != 0` rather than an explicit flag (now covered end to end by the tests above); every chunk is copied byte by byte, single-chunk bodies included; `hex_value` duplicates helpers.jai's `hex_digit`; `is_field_line` duplicates the header loop's validation; `check_timeouts` recomputes `timeout_state` and `write_too_slow`.

## Review focus

Five inputs the spec implies, each pinned by a test:

| Input

<!-- What changed and why. "Fixes #123" closes the issue on merge. -->
## Summary

Everything going into **3.0.0-alpha.5**: the Alias Command Guide gets its own page in the app plus a practice quiz, Telephony can pull in VATSIM-Radar's virtual airline list, and every page in `docs/` was checked against the code and consolidated. The version is bumped to `3.0.0-alpha.5`, and `## Unreleased` in the ChangeLog is now the `3.0.0-alpha.5` section.

## Info: Alias Command Guide

- **Its own Info page.** Info has a second featured card that opens the whole guide inside FE-Buddy, colour-coded by part, built from the same `AliasGuideContent` as the export, with the export button at the top. On What's New, the card no longer exports the guide. It links to Info ▸ Alias Command Guide with **View the guide →** instead.
- **Commands never wrap.** The Syntax and Example columns are as wide as their longest command, and a syntax is split into lines only between its parts. The web page, the Markdown and the app all match. The new `CommandTablePanel` stacks each row when the window is too narrow. The `<wbr>` that let Chrome/Edge break a command even with nowrap is gone.
- **Easier to scan.** Short points in bold with nested bullets under them, and each example command on a line of its own. The content comes from the hand-edited export (lead links to FE-Buddy, no facility name, no About section, footer reads *Page updated on …*). The web page's source is indented like an outline.
- **New: Export Alias Command Practice.** Produces `FE-Buddy Alias Command Practice.html`, a self-contained quiz on 44 real charts, procedures, airways and ISR cards (AIRAC 2610). The controller types the command and it's marked green or red. A wrong answer is lined up part by part against the closest right one to say what's missing or out of place, then the page shows the right command and how it's built. Questions can be filtered by section, and the page keeps score and lets you retry the ones you missed.

## AIRAC Service

- **Telephony ▸ Virtual Airlines: Include the VATSIM-Radar Virtual Airline List** (off by default). When ticked, every run downloads VATSIM-Radar's `custom-data/airlines.json` (cached in `%APPDATA%\FE-Buddy\Telephony`). Its roughly 250 virtual airlines are written after the user's own, each with a `--VA--` card, sorted and deduplicated. Entries that can't be valid 3LDs are skipped and named in the run output. Entries identical to one of the user's are written once, as the user's.
  - On the tab: adding a VA that exactly matches one on the list is rejected with a warning. One that differs at all is added with a note and gets its own card. User VAs already on the list are flagged.
- **Upload to vNAS** card text fixed: a ticked alias file goes into `vNAS_Alias.txt` *ahead of* your custom alias files, so yours win. Four code comments had the same mistake and are fixed too.

## Docs

- Merged: Users README → Getting Started; developer README + Getting Started → Developer guide; Core-Structure + WPF README → `Code-Structure.md`; Settings-Blocks + UserConfig-Reference → `Settings-Reference.md`; Release-Checklist → `RELEASING.md`; MSI-VERSION-NUMBERING → `VERSIONING.md`.
- Removed: the planning Archive, `Developer_Notes.md`, the 2.x Manual HTML, and the root `FE-Buddy_3.0_Whats_New.md`.
- Fixed statements the code contradicted (tab status dots, card names, DAT Include default, airway file groups, CI/CodeQL rules, failed-cycle behaviour, 2.x tools missing from 3.0, and more). The User Guide, FAQ and GitHub Token Guide keep their paths because the app links to them.
- Comments in `build.ps1`, the installer, CI and `Push-InstallerCounter.ps1` that pointed at deleted pages now point at `VERSIONING.md` / `Architecture.md`.

## Tests

- New: `VatsimRadarAirlineParserTests`, `VatsimRadarVirtualAirlinesTests`, `AliasPracticeContentTests` (every chart answer checked against `ChartRecallCodes`, every Data Display procedure against the alias writers' naming), `AliasPracticeWriterTests`, `CommandTablePanelTests`, `AliasGuideViewModelTests`.
- Extended: Telephony downloader/loader/builder/service/settings/view-model, AliasGuide writer/inline, Info and What's New view models.

author: pxldi
body:
Before: you could pick up loose rocks, sticks and flint, but there was nothing to make from them. Vanilla wooden and stone tools were the only way forward.

After: right-click while holding loose rocks (2 or more) or flint to open a 5x5 knapping grid. Strike out cells until the stone matches a head: axe, knife, shovel, hoe, hammer, spear or pickaxe. Then craft head + stick + twine into a stone tool. A tool's durability depends on what it was knapped from (igneous extrusive ×1.2, sedimentary ×0.8, flint ×1.5), and its tooltip names the rock. A knife cuts grass and ferns for plant fibre and straw. Fibre twists into twine, and twine weaves into fibre cloth. Logs need an axe: an axe breaks them, and log + axe gives 2 planks. Config switches, all on by default, remove the vanilla wooden and stone tool, log-to-planks, campfire and furnace recipes. Leaves sometimes drop sticks, and gravel drops more flint.

How:
- **Knapping:** knapping is its own recipe type with a 5x5 bit-mask pattern that can be mirrored left to right. The menu syncs the grid through data slots and strikes a cell when the client sends a button click.
- **Opening cost:** the material is taken on the first strike.
- **Stone tools:** tools are assembled by a shapeless recipe. The recipe copies `knapped_from` and sets `max_damage`.
- **Planks:** log + axe planks use a shapeless recipe that leaves the axe in the grid with 1 damage.
- **Vanilla removals:** each vanilla recipe is regenerated under its vanilla id, with a `strataindustria:config` condition so it only loads while its switch is off.
- **Assets:** sounds are pitched variants of the vanilla stone dig samples, each with a subtitle. Textures come from the texture generator, and the GUI follows the vanilla panel style.

Defaults picked:
- The stone spear is the vanilla `minecraft:stone_spear`, assembled from a knapped head with a base durability of 60. It handles like the vanilla spear; it is not thrown.
- Plain right-click with loose rocks or flint opens knapping. Sneak + right-click places the rock on the ground.
- Copper gear recipe changes come with the copper work, as does the saw.

author: oddurs
body:
The site now serves the component metadata in the form coding agents read. Everything is generated at build from `@rockaway/react/meta.json` and `docs/`, and none of it is hand-written. This is the site half of cairn 0048 (criteria 1 and 2). The MCP server (criteria 3 and 4) is a package of its own, and I propose it as a follow-up item.

## What is served

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `/llms.txt` | What rockaway is, then a link to every document and component twin, with its one-line summary, in llmstxt.org's shape |
| `/llms-full.txt` | Every twin, in one file |
| `/components/<slug>.md` | A component's twin: summary, description, import line, when and when not to use (with links to the alternative's twin), related components, anatomy with prop tables, variants, states, accessibility and keys, tokens, and every snapshot as a `text` block |
| `/<doc>.md` | A document from `docs/`, as written, with its relative links sent to GitHub |
| `/meta.json` | The metadata itself |

- **Code.** The generation is in `apps/site/src/lib/llms.ts`, as pure functions. The endpoints are thin, and `src/lib/llms-site.ts` gathers their inputs.
- **Docs.** A document's title and description come from `docs.ts` (0107), so `llms.txt` describes each document the way its page does.
- **Base path.** URLs are absolute and placed by `SITE_URL` and `SITE_BASE`. The base is read from `astro:config/server`, not `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, because in a module that runs on the server a `BASE_URL` in the environment overrides the latter. Vitest sets `BASE_URL=/`, so the first version linked to `/components/...` when built at `/rockaway/`. `href()` in `.astro` pages may have the same blind spot under test; nothing exercises it yet.

## Coordination with 0147 (#128)

- **Paths.** A twin sits beside its page: `/components/key-hint.md` next to `/components/key-hint/`, with the same kebab slug. The two routes do not collide.
- **One `slugOf`.** This PR has a `slugOf` in `llms.ts`, and #128 has one in `lib/components.ts`. Whichever lands second should import the other's, so there is only one.
- **A link from page to twin.** Once both land, each component page could add `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` pointing at its twin.

## Tests

- **`test/llms.test.ts`.** For every component in the metadata, checks that its twin:
  - carries every snapshot character for character;
  - names every prop, anatomy part, variant value, state, key binding and token;
  - links each component it names to that component's twin;
  - keeps every table row as wide as its header, even when a prop type contains `|`.

  It also checks that `llms.txt` has llmstxt.org's shape and lists every component and document, and that `llms-full.txt` contains every twin.
- **`test/site.test.ts`.** Under both bases, fetches the built `llms.txt`, follows every link in it on the built site, and checks the Button twin's snapshots.

Local runs: site build (astro check clean), `pnpm --filter site test` (110 tests), lint, and `cairn check`.

author: kadirnar
body:
Part of #107 (triage item A21a).

## Problem
`NativeSupertonicRuntime.fine_tuning_loss` defaulted to `total_steps=5` (`voicehub/architectures/supertonic/runtime.py:462`). Every inference entry point uses 8 denoising steps: `infer_batch`, `synthesize`, `SupertonicForTextToSpeech._generate`, and upstream `py/example_onnx.py` (`--total-step` default 8).

## Root cause
The vector estimator is conditioned on `total_step`, and the flow-step objective interpolates at `current_step / total_steps`. With the default of 5, fine-tuning trained the estimator on the points `k/5` with `total_step=5` conditioning. Default 8-step inference never visits those points. A fine-tune that relies on the default was therefore optimising a schedule the model is not sampled with.

## Fix
- Change the `fine_tuning_loss` default to `total_steps=8`, the same as the inference defaults.
- Add a sentence to the docstring explaining why.

Callers that pass `total_steps` explicitly are unaffected. Inference code is untouched.

## Tests
- New CPU-only test `test_fine_tuning_default_schedule_matches_inference`. It calls `fine_tuning_loss` without `total_steps` and with `current_step=[0, 7]`, then checks through a forward pre-hook that the estimator receives `total_step == 8`.
  - On the base branch it fails: `current_step` 7 is rejected as out of `[0, 5)`.
  - With this change it passes.
- All tests that mention supertonic: 194 passed (576 subtests).
- pre-commit is clean.

## Evidence
- This change does not affect inference outputs. Only the training objective's default changes, and `infer_batch`, `synthesize` and `generate` are untouched, so no parity re-run is needed.
- The docs example (`total_steps=5` in `docs/models/providers/supertonic.md`) passes the value explicitly as an inference argument, so it is left unchanged.

### Commits
- 04657761 fix(supertonic): default fine-tuning schedule to the 8 inference steps

Verified together with every open parity PR on top of main: full CPU suite 3075 passed, 0 failed; pre-commit clean.

author: leewardbound
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"leewardbound"} -->
_Requested by **Lee**_

## Markdown
Chat messages (yours, the bot's, replies and messages from other bots, queued and steering messages), KB articles, skill bodies and bot instructions render as Markdown through one `Markdown` component (react-markdown + remark-gfm: tables, task lists, strikethrough). Raw HTML is shown as text, links to other sites open in a new tab, and fenced code blocks are highlighted with the existing highlight.js setup from `CodeView`.

## Files in the chat
- Images a tool returned (`image_ref` items: `penpot_render`, screenshots) show as thumbnails under the tool's card instead of as JSON inside it.
- Files a bot made (`ergo_attachments_create`, `orca_attach`, exports) have no `message_sequence`, so the transcript never showed them. They now appear where the bot made them (placed by creation time), and the list refreshes as new messages stream in.
- Images you pick or paste preview in the composer, and files you send stay visible with your message until the worker stores it.

## Bot icons and colors
New optional `bot.yaml` keys `icon` (an emoji) and `color` (a palette name or hex), validated in `definition.py` and returned by the bots API. They show as a badge before the name in the sidebar and on the bot page. Without them, the badge uses the first letter and a color picked from the name. The sidebar no longer shows "in <parent>". Docs are in `docs/bots.md` and `docs/ergonaut.md`. ergo-bots PR: boundcorp/ergo-bots#33.

## Thin scrollbars
Thin scrollbars in theme colors (`scrollbar-width`/`scrollbar-color` plus `::-webkit-scrollbar`). The sidebar's appears only on hover.

## Paged long chats
`GET /api/sessions/{id}` returns the newest 50 messages and the calls that touch them, plus `first_line` and `has_more`. `?before=<line>` returns the page before that line. `SessionSource` reads only the requested range of sequences. The event stream reads messages, and calls that reach the client's newest line (plus any running or awaiting approval), so it no longer reloads the whole chat on every change. A "See more" button at the top loads the older page and keeps the scroll position. Reloads after sending keep the older pages already loaded. Detecting when a queued turn has finished now compares the last call's id instead of the call count, so loading older pages can't end it early.

## Testing
- New tests for icon and color parsing and validation, and for paging (three pages, with calls attached to the right page). The bots API test now includes the new fields.
- Ergonaut suite: 79 passed. Library suite: the only failures are the knowledge/embedding tests, which make real OpenAI calls (I ran with a dummy key), and a leftover-table error in `test_bot_pages`. Neither touches these changes.
- `npm run build` passes. I checked Markdown in a live chat and in bot instructions in the browser, against the running Ergonaut.

author: joshuamschmidt
body:
## What

Two sources, both downloaded file by file with `curl` from `odelaneau/shapeit` at pinned commit `c34d4db3e99a2f7e23deb727671ae260901a5886`:

- **`genetic_maps_shapeit_b38`** is SHAPEIT5's GRCh38 genetic map. It sits directly after `genetic_maps_decode2019` in `SOURCES` and goes under the same `genetic_maps/` prefix, at `genetic_maps/shapeit/c34d4db/b38/`, so all genetic maps are found together. Its keys are `map_chr1` … `map_chr22`, `map_chrX` (non-PAR), `map_chrX_par1` and `map_chrX_par2`, 25 files.
- **`shapeit_chunks_b38`** is SHAPEIT5's UKB-derived phasing chunks. They are chunk boundaries, not a map, so they get their own prefix: `shapeit/c34d4db/chunks/b38/`. Its keys are `chunks_20cM_<contig>` and `chunks_4cM_<contig>` for chr1–22 and chrX, plus `chunks_readme`, 47 files.

The `genetic_maps_decode2019` comment now notes that genetic maps are kept together as `genetic_maps_*` and points to the SHAPEIT map. It also records that the two formats are not interchangeable: deCODE's per-chromosome files are `pposition rrate gposition` and SHAPEIT5's are `pos chr cM`.

## Why

The popgen-phasing pipeline (SHAPEIT5 `phase_common` → `ligate` → `phase_rare`) uses the map for `--map`. It uses the chunks as static chunk boundaries, which cpg-flow needs because `expected_outputs` are fixed at planning time. The chunks are in cM, so they don't depend on the cohort, and pinning the commit keeps the boundaries stable across freezes. deCODE 2019 (#112) is a different map for a different tool (`plink2 --cm-map`). A map-sensitivity comparison in phasing may later use both.

## Provenance

- `odelaneau/shapeit` is the author's replacement for `odelaneau/shapeit5`. GitHub has blocked the old repo since 2026-05, so its URLs return 403 or an HTML page.
- The maps and the chr1–22 chunk files have the same git blob SHAs as the v5.1.1 release's `resources/` (commit `990ed0d`), which I checked against a full-history mirror. The maps also match `odelaneau/GLIMPSE`'s `maps/genetic_maps.b38`.
- The chrX chunk files are new in `odelaneau/shapeit`. They span all of chrX, PARs included, so a consumer phasing the PARs separately clips them to the PAR boundaries.

## Checks

- `import references` passes. `transfers()` gives 25 and 47 per-file `curl` commands to the expected destinations.
- A sample of the pinned raw URLs return HTTP 200: the `chr1` and `chrX_par2` maps, `20cM/chunks_chrX.txt`, `4cM/chunks_chr22.txt` and the README. `chr20.b38.gmap.gz` decompresses to the expected `pos chr cM` header.
- pre-commit (flake8 etc.) passes.

author: mgoldsborough
body:
Workspace → General's instructions now save when the editor loses focus, on the autosave pattern (`web/AGENTS.md`, "Forms save as they change"). The Save and Reset buttons are gone.

**When it saves:**
- **On blur only.** Not on a pause in typing: the instructions reach every conversation in the workspace, and a half-written one would too.
- **Enter is a newline,** and Escape doesn't revert, so a stray key can't discard a long edit.
- **A save shows a notice with Undo.** The page status sits in the header beside the workspace ID.

**Refusals:** over 8,192 characters, the save is refused on the field without being sent, and the text is kept. A server refusal shows its reason, with Retry and Revert.

**Each save names its workspace** (`callTool(…, { workspaceId })`), and the editor is keyed by the workspace. Saves queue, so one could run after the reader switches workspaces, and `callTool` alone would send it to whichever workspace is active by then.

**Supporting changes:**
- The hook gains `textareaProps`, which saves on blur only.
- `web/AGENTS.md` gains the textarea rule and the workspace-scoped rule.
- The settings guide says when the instructions save.

**Tests:** `WorkspaceInstructions.autosave.test.tsx` covers saving on blur with the workspace ID, Enter not saving, the length limit, a server refusal, and the read-only view.

`bun run verify` and `bun run test:integration` pass.

author: echoes675
body:
Closes FHQ-243 and FHQ-242 — two production defects, both of which lose a reminder the family set.

## FHQ-243: a reminder configured but never added was silently discarded

Reported from production. The audit line added two tickets ago answered it in one query, which is the first time that line has earned its place:

```
Event bc08e0e9-… reminders written as explicitly-none; previously inherits-default.
```

One write on that event, no member change beforehand, v1.2.2 live, and the event was not recurring. So at save time the Reminders tab held **inheritance off, zero reminders** — the family configured a reminder, the Add button was never pressed, and everything downstream behaved correctly on a tab nobody realised was empty. The event went from inheriting to explicitly silenced.

An earlier fix made the pending value read as an offer (`Add 45 minutes before`) rather than as a set reminder. That was not enough.

### The fix

`ReminderPickerModel` now routes every form control through one `Set<T>` that flips `IsFormTouched` on an **effective** change, and exposes `CommitPendingFormReminder()`. `EventModal.SaveEvent` calls it once, after validation and **before** the scope branch reads `HasChanged`, so the series warning and `RemindersToWrite` both see the commit. It commits via `TryAdd`, so `HasChanged`/`ToEventReminders` remain the only gate on the wire — and the server's audit line needed no change, since it already describes `request.Reminders`.

**The dirty-tracking is the entire safety property.** The form shows `30 · Minutes · Notification` from the moment it appears, so committing unconditionally would invent a reminder for anyone turning inheritance off *because they want silence*. That is why this option was rejected before, and why it is safe now.

Three conditions beyond "touched" guard it, two of which were added during implementation rather than specified:

- **The list must be empty.** Without this, opening an event that already has reminders, poking a pill and saving would add a *second* one. With a visible list nothing is being lost, and the Add button stays the offer it says it is. The principle: the commit exists to prevent silence the family did not ask for.
- **The pending value must not be one `Remove` took away this visit.** A blanket "Add or Remove was used" flag was implemented first and was wrong: turning inheritance off on a calendar *with* defaults, removing the pre-filled reminder and configuring a different one would leave the family silent — the original defect again. Removing one and configuring another is a **replacement**; only handing back the exact reminder they removed undoes their choice. This is also what keeps the existing `A reminder added and taken away again says nothing about the event's reminders` scenario honest.
- Not inheriting, which the picker already enforces.

**"Touched then changed back" counts as touched**, documented in the model's remarks: someone who dials 45 and settles on 30 has engaged with the form and is configuring a reminder. Someone who wants silence does not touch it at all. Assigning a control the value it already holds, and an input the clamps rejected, are both *not* touches.

The all-day form's controls are included — it reads "1 day before at 09:00 · Notification" before anyone touches it, which is the identical hazard.

## FHQ-242: an all-in-series reminder edit never reached the local occurrences

`PatchSeriesMasterFieldsOnlyAsync` builds a **transient** `CalendarEvent` to carry the write. Google's returned reminders land on it via `ApplyRemindersGoogleReturned`, and it is never saved — the method receives `seriesRows`, the real occurrence entities, and never gives them the new reminders.

Fixed by `ApplySeriesRemindersAsync`, called from **both** branches of `PatchSeriesMasterAsync`. The ticket named only the fields-only branch; the timing-change branch builds the same throwaway and had the same hole. It copies `master.Reminders` — non-null only when the write carried reminders and Google's response mentioned them, so strictly what Google returned — onto every row in `seriesRows`.

### The ticket's diagnosis was too broad, and was corrected with evidence

Throwaway probe tests were run **before** any change. `CalendarSyncService:369` already does `localEvent.Reminders = evt.Reminders ?? localEvent.Reminders`, and `reminders` is among the fields the events list requests — so a probe arranged the Google-honest way passed *before* the fix. "Google is correct and the local occurrences are stale" is not true in general.

The hole that is real is narrower:

- **Rows outside `SyncState.SyncWindowStart/End`.** That window is written only `if (isFullSync)`, and `isFullSync` requires no sync token, so it records the *last full sync's* window while incremental syncs persist what Google sends with no window filter. A long-lived calendar accumulates rows beyond it, and the window can stop covering today — so the occurrence the family just edited can be the stale one. That is the production-visible symptom.
- Any instance whose list item says nothing about reminders.

**`ThisAndFollowing` was traced and deliberately left alone.** `SplitSeriesAsync` discards the entity Google's answer lands on in the same way, but the forward series has no local rows at that point — they are deleted and re-inserted from Google's own fetch — and the truncated original's surviving rows were never written to. The worst case is a freshly inserted row with `Reminders == null`, an honest "never synced" that the next sync fills in, rather than a stale wrong value.

**`RecordOutbound` is kept.** Both now happen and nothing is lost: the hash only suppresses Google's echo of our own write, which can no longer teach the rows anything they do not already hold. Dropping it would turn our own write into an inbound change for sync to re-apply. Pinned by a test.

## Both fixes were verified by mutation

Neither test was trusted to fail. Neutering `CommitPendingFormReminder` turned **8 red**; neutering `ApplySeriesRemindersAsync`'s guard turned **3 red**, including *"Expected edited.Reminders!.SameAs(googleStores) to be True because the occurrence the family edited is the one the modal re-opens on"*. Both restored and re-run green.

## E2E

Both scenarios are in `EventReminders.feature`, deliberately — a sibling branch was rewriting `RemindersView.feature` and `DayRollover.feature` at the time, and this is the better home anyway since both defects are about what the modal writes. The rebase onto that branch's merge was conflict-free as a result.

- **FHQ-243**: configure a reminder without pressing Add, save, reopen — **one** reminder, 2 hours. The count is half the assertion: the calendar's usual reminder that was taken away must not come back with it.
- **The over-reach guard** is the existing `An event taken off its calendar's reminders without adding one is left with none`, which passes *because* the form is untouched. Its comment now says it is that guard rather than duplicating it.
- **FHQ-242**: a reminder added to every occurrence of a repeating event survives a re-open. **This pins the product behaviour but cannot isolate the fix**, and the feature file says so: the Simulator reports a master's reminders on every expanded instance, as Google does, so the window re-fetch carries them and a fresh run has one sync window. The out-of-window case is unit-test territory. Nothing of this shape existed before — the only recurring-reminder scenario asserted the warning and never that the change landed.

## One unrelated commit, carried because it blocked the gate

The suite's last clock-dependent scenario failed two gates in one night — the second time blocking this production fix. "Fired, but not yet happened" was thought to require seeding relative to now. It does not: an event **tomorrow** with a reminder **48 hours before** puts that reminder **yesterday**, so both halves hold at every hour. The row files under Tomorro

body:
Landing page for the House of Wellness Brickell campaign, at **`/house-of-wellness`** — the page the Facebook lead form links to.

## What's in it

**The page** (`app/house-of-wellness/page.tsx`)
Full project page in Spanish: hero, the wellness concept, amenities, residences, payment plan, location (with map), gallery, booking, and a 12-question FAQ.

Built to the SEO/AIO rules in `CLAUDE.md`: keyword-rich metadata, canonical on the `www` host, `openGraph` + `twitter` cards, JSON-LD (`RealEstateAgent`, `Residence`, `Offer`, `ItemList`, `FAQPage`), a visible FAQ that mirrors the `FAQPage`, one `<h1>`, descriptive `alt` text throughout, mobile-responsive, and an entry in `app/sitemap.ts`.

Renderings are read from `public/house-of-wellness/` at request time, so dropping more files in adds them to the gallery with no code change.

**Booking** (`app/house-of-wellness/booking-form.tsx`)
Uses the CRM's own calendar, not an external scheduler: `GET /api/appointments/slots` for Catherine's real availability, `POST /api/appointments/book` to create the contact, the appointment, the task and the notifications. It also captures `utm_*` and `fbclid` from the URL and saves them on the contact, so the leads this campaign brought in can actually be counted.

**Nurture** (`app/api/admin/seed-house-of-wellness`)
A 15-touch, 30-day sequence across WhatsApp/SMS, email and agent call tasks. It removes the "I can't buy in the US" blocker first, makes the 10% reservation concrete ($41,990, not $419,900), explains the rental terms and the real monthly costs honestly, and drives one single action — booking the appointment.

It triggers on the tag **`House of Wellness`**, which is exactly the Facebook form's `utm_campaign` and `utm_content`, so ad leads enrol themselves through the existing webhook → `applyTagAndEnroll` → `CONTACT_TAGGED` path. `POST` to the route to seed it (and re-run it any time to refresh the copy and backfill).

**`/api/appointments/book`** now accepts an optional `source` / `sourceDetail` plus a fixed allowlist of campaign tags, so bookings from the page land in the same sequence as Facebook leads. Default behaviour for `/book` is unchanged.

## Two claims deliberately left off the page

This page is linked from a paid ad, so both are omitted until confirmed:

- **The delivery date.** Our project data says Q1 2029; public listings say Q1 2030. The FAQ says the developer confirms the date at reservation and it goes in writing in the contract.
- **"40% projected appreciation"** and **"the lowest price per square foot in Brickell."** A projected return and an unverifiable superlative in a paid-ad landing page are not worth the exposure. The page leads with the facts instead ($419,900, $41,990 to reserve).

Both are one edit away if Catherine confirms them.

Prices come from the developer's own current brochure ($419,900 studios / $41,990 reservation), which supersedes the $400,000 figure in `data/preconstruction/colombia-event-2026.json`. The 1- and 2-bedroom prices from that older list are **not** published — the page shows the sizes and routes to the appointment for the current list.

## Still needed

- 10 more renderings were sent but did not arrive as files on disk; only 5 are in `public/house-of-wellness/`. Re-sending them is all that's needed — the gallery picks them up automatically.
- A purpose-made 1200×630 social card. The page currently uses `hero-brickell.jpg`, which Facebook will crop.

author: lex00
body:
One working tree is written by several principals at once (people through hud, the coding agent, the steward, builders), and until now chant's working-tree writes were plain read-modify-write: two `records amend` calls on one record could each read it and the second would drop the first's change, and two concurrent `records new` could allocate the same id. This change gives those writes a concurrency model and records it as ws-089.

What changed:

Every chant write to the working tree (`records new`, `amend`, `review` and `close`, `points ask` and `answer`, `box listing set`, and `work evidence` through `amend`) now holds a write lock from its first read to its last write. The lock is the directory `chant-write.lock` in the working tree's git directory (per linked worktree, so builders in their own worktrees never wait on each other), taken with `mkdir`, with an `owner.json` naming the holder. A holder whose process has exited or whose `expiresAt` passed is broken by the next writer. A writer waits up to `CHANT_WRITE_LOCK_WAIT_MS` (15s by default) and is then refused with `write-lock-timeout`, naming the holder. Record files are now replaced through a temporary file and a rename. Writes inside one process (two requests to `chant serve mcp`) also serialise, through AsyncLocalStorage, while a write inside a write (work evidence's amend) is re-entrant. Ledger writes on `chant/lifecycle` were already compare-and-set on the ref and are unchanged.

`records amend`, `review` and `close` take `--expect <digest>`, the read contract's digest the caller read the record at. When the record has another digest the write is refused with `record-conflict`, and the failure document carries `conflict: {id, path, expected, digest, lastWrite}`, so the caller re-reads and retries from `digest`. Every write result now carries `digest`, the record's digest after the write, so a caller can chain its next `--expect` without a read. Reviews and seals stay outside the digest, so a verdict landing between a read and an amendment is kept rather than reported as a conflict.

`records --json` prints `lastWrite: {verb, by, agent, at} | null` beside `worktree`, from a write journal (`chant-writes.json` in the git directory) keyed by the file's SHA-256, so it is only shown while the file still holds what that write left. The journal is a cache; losing it only nulls `lastWrite`.

`chant workspace lock [acquire --holder <name> [--ttl <duration>] | release --token <token>]` lets a tool hold the lock across several chant calls for a batch (hud#819): each write of the batch runs with `CHANT_WRITE_LOCK=<token>` and goes ahead without waiting, everyone else waits, and a batch whose lock expired gets `write-lock-not-held`. Its document follows the new `write-lock.schema.json`; `lock` alone never prints the token.

New reason codes `record-conflict`, `write-lock-timeout` and `write-lock-not-held` are in the closed list, the output schemas, the read-contract page and the boundary roster. The writer conformance suite gains the concurrent case: when a writer performs `records amend`, three amendments of one record are made at once through it from one digest, exactly one must be written, the other two must be chant's `record-conflict` refusal returned unchanged, and each retry from the named digest must be written. A writer that retries blindly without `--expect` is caught. `WriteParams["records amend"]` takes an optional `expect`, which `writeArgv` passes as `--expect`.

Docs: the read contract's new "Concurrent writers" section (what is serialised, what merges, what conflicts, batches), `records` CLI page, writer conformance page, and ws-089 written through `chant workspace records new`.

How it was verified: core tsc; `write-lock.test.ts` (lock placement incl. linked worktrees, in-process serialisation and re-entrancy, stale and expired locks broken, timeout naming the holder, batch tokens, the journal); `records-concurrent.test.ts`, which runs two people's amends and an agent's (`CHANT_AGENT`) against one record at once and checks exactly one wins per digest, the others get a conflict naming the winner, and their retries land with nothing lost; `records-concurrent.e2e.test.ts`, the same across three CLI processes plus a batch held with `lock acquire`; the writer conformance e2e with the new case; the core unit project; docs-check and the prose lint.

Closes #3173

## Summary

The board kept polling WMATA about once a minute even when nobody could see it: minimized, in a background tab, or with the phone locked.

**`index.html`:**
- **Pause rule:** while `document.hidden`, the poll loop and the timetable refresh are skipped. The exception is when the locked train means leaving within 15 minutes, which keeps polling at the normal cadence so the heads-up and Go alerts fire on fresh data.

author: apachler
body:
## Summary

**Nightly retention** (`workers/gateway/src/retention.ts` `pruneOperational`, called from `runScheduled`; each window is a named constant with its reason; deletes run in bounded 5000-row batches through `pruneBounded`, which the firehose-position prune now uses too):

- `aprs_outbox`: queued items older than 1 hour are deleted, and `GET /outbox` never hands them to the box. A box that comes back after an outage does not send stale WX beacons, radio answers or status announcements to APRS-IS. Sent and failed items are deleted after 7 days. No outbox kind needs a longer window: nothing retries through the outbox, and a Mailbox message is queued again each time its station is heard.
- `box_commands`: deleted after 7 days, whatever their state.
- `bbs_messages`: bulletins (`type = 'B'`) past `expires_at` are deleted. A bulletin stored without an expiry lives `BULLETIN_LIFETIME_SEC` (30 days) from `posted_at`. Inbound FBB bulletins, federated mirrors and ACSFED carrier bulletins now get that lifetime when they are stored. Personal mail and NTS traffic are not pruned by age.
- `bbs_forward_log`: entries are deleted after 30 days, unless their message is still in the forwarding pool. Deleting such an entry would offer the message to the partner again.
- `watch_alerts`: unseen alerts are also deleted after 30 days.
- `stations`: stations not heard for 365 days are deleted, unless a living cache, a registered station (`account_stations`) or a MeshCom node names them. Those rows supply the position of the cache, station or node.

**Mailbox** (`mailbox.ts` `deliverMailbox`): the delivery read is limited to the heard calls and their base calls (`to_call IN (…)`, 90 addressees per statement). Mail waiting for stations that are not on the air no longer fills the 500-row read.

**Weather** (`wx.ts` `readingTime`): a PWS `dateutc` is used only when it falls within [now − 1 day, now + 5 min]. Any other value stores the arrival time.

**Live WebSocket**: `/ws?region=` accepts only `LIVE_REGION` (`global`, or the parameter left out) on the Worker, Node and Bun, through the shared `liveRegionOf`. Any other value gets a 400. `RoomsCore` deletes a room once it is empty, on leave or on sweep.

## Testing

- New `servers/node/test/retention.test.ts`: outbox serving and pruning, box commands, bulletin lifetime and pruning, the forward log, unseen alerts, and stations with each kind of reference.
- `mailbox.test.ts`: a heard station gets its mail with 600 messages waiting for others. This test fails on `dev`.
- `wx.test.ts`: the `readingTime` window.

author: kadirnar
body:
Part of #107 (triage item A21b).

## Problem
`voicehub/models/supertonic/source/SOURCE.json` says the vendored tree is `supertone-inc/supertonic@7e2804f`, but `source/supertonic/helper.py` had been edited by hand. Lines 235-248 trim each chunk with `round()`, and line 256 concatenates on `axis=-1`. Upstream `py/helper.py` at that revision does neither, so the provenance record was wrong. Anyone using the vendored copy as the upstream reference would compare against code that upstream never shipped.

## Root cause
Commit 253b9d43 ("Refactor inference runtimes across TTS models") applied VoiceHub's per-chunk trimming fix inside the vendored upstream file. The file was exact before that commit (blob `ff9e4dac`). Nothing at runtime imports the vendored file. VoiceHub's own chunk joining lives in `voicehub/architectures/supertonic/runtime.py` and uses `int()` truncation, so the patched copy also no longer matched VoiceHub's behaviour.

## Fix
- Restore `source/supertonic/helper.py` to the exact bytes of upstream `py/helper.py@7e2804f`.
- In `SOURCE.json` under `architecture_source.vendored_files`, record:
  - the upstream git blob id of every vendored file (each can be checked with `git rev-parse 7e2804f:py/<file>`);
  - the upstream directory (`py`);
  - the import rewrite `supertonic -> voicehub.models.supertonic.source.supertonic`. `scripts/vendor_tts_sources.py` applies this rewrite, and it is the only change in `example_pypi.py`;
  - the two `__init__.py` files that VoiceHub adds.
- Record the deliberate multi-chunk joining deviation (trim each chunk before joining, instead of upstream's trim of the joined result) in `voicehub_port.deviations`. It previously existed only as the hand patch.

No runtime code changes.

## Tests
New CPU-only test, no network: `test_vendored_source_matches_the_recorded_upstream_revision` in `tests/test_native_supertonic_runtime.py`. It checks that the vendored tree contains only the recorded files plus the VoiceHub-added package files. For each file it undoes the recorded import rewrite and any CRLF line endings from a Windows checkout, then compares the git blob id with the recorded one.
- On the base branch the test fails (the manifest has no record yet). With the new manifest but the old `helper.py`, it fails for `supertonic/helper.py` only (`5a1aba0b... != ff9e4dac...`).
- With the fix, all supertonic tests, the documentation-site tests and the other tests that mention supertonic pass. pre-commit is clean.

## Evidence
- No module under `voicehub` imports `voicehub.models.supertonic.source.supertonic`, and importing the supertonic inference, modeling, training and runtime modules loads none of it. Synthesis output therefore cannot change, so no parity re-run was needed.
- I ran the vendoring script's transforms on upstream `py/@7e2804f`. After the fix, `helper.py` is byte-identical to the script's output; before the fix it was not.

### Commits
- 0620444d fix(supertonic): restore vendored helper.py to pinned upstream revision
- 1993cbdf style(supertonic): apply pre-commit formatting

Verified together with every open parity PR on top of main: full CPU suite 3075 passed, 0 failed; pre-commit clean.

author: silas-asamoah
body:
## Summary

Stormlog can now aggregate any window of vLLM `/metrics` scrapes for one engine, and decide from it the incident signals that metrics alone can decide. This is the first of #218's PRs. #219's online triggers and #218's diagnoser both build on it, so they cannot disagree about what a window shows.

- **Windows of scrapes.** `stormlog.infer.scrape_window` aggregates exactly the scrapes a caller gives it, for one `engine` label:
  - a gauge's statistics and the share of samples at or above a value;
  - a counter's increase, summed from consecutive-scrape deltas, with rate bounds;
  - a histogram's share above a value, and the bucket holding a quantile, as bounds between bucket boundaries.

  Differencing consecutive scrapes catches a counter that went backwards between two interior scrapes, which a first-to-last comparison cannot. A window lasts from the first scrape's sample-interval midpoint to the last's. When nothing can be said, the result is `None` with a reason, never a zero.
- **One implementation for windows and case blocks.** #215's delta primitives move into the new module, and `vllm_report` calls them. The report's output and its reason names are unchanged.
- **The diagnosis vocabulary and threshold table.** `diagnosis_vocabulary` holds the closed set of finding kinds, the components each may be located at, and the causes. `diagnosis_thresholds` is one versioned table (`diagnosis_thresholds_v1`) that triggers and the diagnoser both read.
- **Online signals.** `evaluate_signal(kind, scrapes, config)` decides three kinds from a window:
  - queue saturation, from the median waiting count;
  - KV preemption pressure, from the preemption increase;
  - prefix-cache loss, from the hit ratio against a reference the caller supplies, once enough prompt tokens were queried.

  Each result carries the threshold, the table version and whether the caller overrode it. A window that cannot decide gives no verdict and says why. Every other kind answers what it needs: `requires_hook`, `requires_trace` or `requires_client`. Metrics cover every client's traffic, so a signal over its threshold means a mechanism is suspected, never a diagnosis.

Documented in `docs/vllm_telemetry.md` (Windows of scrapes) and a new `docs/inference_diagnosis.md`, which is in the toctree.

## Design decisions for review

- **The caller chooses the window.** The module never picks scrapes by time. It aggregates the ones it is given, in the order given, so a trigger, a case block and an incident window all use the same rules.
- **One engine per figure.** Nothing is summed across engines.
  - A family that more than one label set matches (`waiting_by_reason` without a `reason`) is `ambiguous_series`.
  - A window whose scrapes hold several engines needs one named (`engine_required`). This is checked for the whole window, not per family, so a signal that divides one family by another cannot read each from a different engine.
- **Order is by stamp and by sample midpoint.** Scrapes must be in strictly increasing stamp order (`scrapes_out_of_order`, `duplicate_scrape_time`). A later stamp whose sample midpoint is no later (a quick scrape inside a slow one's interval) is also out of order, because which one sampled first is unknown. Midpoints are compared over the successful scrapes only: a failed scrape sampled nothing, so only its stamp takes part.
- **Only a failed first or last scrape spoils a window.** Either one shortens the window the caller chose (`scrape_failed`). An interior failure is counted in `WindowCheck.failed`: gauges use the samples they have, and counters are differenced across the failure.
- **A series is the same series throughout.** The matched label set is compared for every consecutive pair, so a series whose labels change (another model name, say) is never differenced across the change (`series_labels_changed`). A gauge, like a counter, is one exporter's: `gauge_window` refuses samples from both sides of a restart (`engine_restart`), and a family that is not a gauge (`not_a_gauge`), so the diagnoser can call it directly.
- **Each histogram step must itself be a histogram.** Its cumulative counts must never fall as the boundary rises, none may exceed the step's count, and its `+Inf` bucket must equal that count. Otherwise the window is `histogram_inconsistent`. Two scrapes can each be valid and still differ by a step that is not a histogram, and that step's shares would fall outside 0 to 1. The check sits in the window layer, so #215's pair delta is unchanged.
- **Placement is labelled.** Records written before scrapes carried `completed_at_ns` bound the sample interval by `observed_at_ns + duration_ms`. That misses the fetch thread's start delay, so such windows say `placement: approximate`. (#218's PR 1 adds the completion stamp.)
- **The prefix-cache ratio needs volume.** vLLM counts every prompt token of a new request as a query, so one short, unseen prompt alone has a hit ratio of 0. Below `prefix_cache_loss.min_queried_tokens` (2,048 tokens, provisional like the rest) the signal gives no verdict (`too_few_queried_tokens`). The key is in `diagnosis_thresholds_v1` now, so #219 reads it from the first version it consumes.
- **Overrides are checked.** A threshold override with a key the table lacks, or a value that is not a finite number (a string or a boolean included), is refused with `ValueError`: a NaN would never be exceeded and a misspelt key never read, both silently. A prefix-cache reference outside 0 to 1 is refused, and so is a `min_scrapes` below 2, which would decide on one sample. A histogram share above NaN is refused as a quantile outside 0 to 1 is.
- **A verdict says what it rests on.** Each signal's `detail` carries the window's successful `scrapes` and the `failed_scrapes` inside it, so a caller need not count again.
- **Thresholds are provisional.** They will be read from the first real joined runs in #218's GPU validation.

## Validation

- **Tests.** 60 new test functions (96 cases) across three files, and two cases added to the scrape record's tests, against synthetic scrapes written in vLLM 0.30.0's exposition format (`tests/vllm_scrape_helpers.py`):
  - **Windows:** midpoint durations and bounds; failed, short, out-of-order and restarted windows; a missing engine.
  - **Gauges:** statistics; non-finite samples counted, not averaged; ambiguity and engine selection.
  - **Counters:** consecutive deltas with rate bounds; an interior reset caught when the ends agree; a recreated series; a case delta matching #215's on real vLLM scrapes.
  - **Histograms:** exact shares at boundaries and bounded shares between them; the overflow bucket; changed boundaries; a bucket that went backwards.
  - **Signals:** each signal, each threshold override, and each kind that metrics cannot decide.
  - **`test_infer_scrape_window_review.py`:** every review finding below, and the composed path a trigger takes: each of the three metric signals, over each window the layer refuses (a failed first or last scrape, out of order, one instant, inverted midpoints, a restarted exporter, families on two engines), gives no verdict.
- **The move changes nothing.** Fable compared the `analyze_inference_events` JSON between `release/dev` and this branch on 34 artifacts (six real #215 live runs and 28 #263 cases), and it was byte-identical. Those artifacts exercise `counter_reset` (×37), `counter_recreated`, `engine_restart`, `non_finite_sample`, `series_missing` and `unresolved`. Codex Astra independently found identical reports and text on 35 analysis-test reports and five archived real #215 scrape pairs.
- **Property checks (Astra).** 2,000 share-bound and 1,200 quantile-bound checks over valid histograms. 52 insufficient-window checks, each confirming no verdict, the table version and the override echo.
- **Review fixes.** Fable's and Codex Astra's code reviews found no P0 or P1. Each finding was reproduced and fixed in its own commit on top of the two feature co

author: qwadratic
body:
Deploys pushed from GitHub Actions instead of the minute timer, as Ivan asked (VM side only; `release.yml` is the coordinator's part).

## What is in it
- `infra/ops` (TypeScript, no runtime deps, `node server.ts`): `POST /ops/deploy` and `GET /ops/deploy/status` on 127.0.0.1:8788.
  - The public API forwards `/ops/*` there. Keeping it a separate service means the webhook survives the switch from the placeholder to `apps/api`.
  - Checks on `POST /ops/deploy`:
    - HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body in `X-Deploy-Signature`, compared timing-safe;
    - `ts` window of −300/+60 s;
    - replay → 409;
    - the sha must be on `origin/main` after a fetch;
    - rate limit 6/min per IP and 30/h overall;
    - body ≤ 1 KiB.
  - It never logs bodies or signatures, answers 202, and writes `deploy-request.json`.
- `apprentice-deploy-request.path` → `apprentice-deploy --request`, so the webhook needs no sudo.
  - Same build, health check, rollback and failed-sha logic as before.
  - Progress goes to `deploy-status.json`: queued, running, ok, failed or rolled_back.
- The deploy health check also requires `/ops/deploy/status` through port 8000, so an API that stops forwarding `/ops/*` is rolled back. The README contract for `apps/api` says so.
- sudoers may restart `apprentice-ops`. `check.sh` tests the webhook. The README covers the signing snippet for the workflow and secret rotation.

## Verified on the VM (installed from this branch)
- `check.sh`: 31/31 pass, including:
  - status is public;
  - unsigned and wrongly signed requests → 401;
  - a correctly signed request passes HMAC (→ 422, because the branch sha is not on `main`);
  - replay → 409.
- Signed request for `12d2b06`, which is on `main` but has no `infra/ops`: 202 → the path unit ran the deploy → the health check failed → rolled back to the branch. Status `rolled_back` with a message; all services active.
- Stale `ts` → 401 `timestamp_out_of_window`.
- `DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` was generated on the VM into `/etc/apprentice/env` (0600) and set as an Actions secret through stdin.
- `DEBUG_ENDPOINTS` cleared.

## Not verified yet
A successful deploy through the webhook: every commit on `main` lacks `infra/ops`, so the first success will be the Actions-driven deploy of this merge. The minute timer is stopped, not disabled, until then.

body:
## Task
Closes #215 (T-BUILD-WILDCARD-SOURCES-001). Ordered by the user, see D-011 in #137. It is implemented by the cloud session; the PC Claude does the MSBuild and live check through the D-012 gate.

## What and why
Almost every domain PR adds a line to the same two hand-kept lists:
- 55 `<Compile Include>` items in `VikingAI.csproj`;
- the single-line harness list in `tools/Test-Logic.ps1`.

As a result, parallel PRs conflict on every merge.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `VikingAI/VikingAI.csproj` | One `<Compile Include="**\*.cs" Exclude="bin\**;obj\**" />`, plus commented `<Compile Remove>` lines for sources kept out of the plugin (today only `WorldStatePersistence.cs`). Nothing else in the csproj changed: Jötunn imports, the ProfilerModule workaround, deploy, references. |
| `tools/Test-ProjectIntegrity.ps1` | Mirrors the glob instead of reading per-file entries. The csproj `Remove` lines replace the script's `$notInPlugin` map, so there is one source of truth. It still fails on MSB4067 text and on C# > 7.3 in no-Unity sources. It now also fails on per-file Compile items (for example when Visual Studio expands the glob) and on stale `Remove` entries. |
| `tools/Test-Logic.ps1` | Runs every `tools/Test-*.ps1` except a one-per-line exclusion table: itself, the integrity and Memory CI steps, and the game/MCP-driven `HumanoidRuntime` and `ValheimMcp`. A stale exclusion fails. The order is deterministic. |
| `tools/Test-WorldStatePersistence.ps1` | It no longer compiled (CS1529) after its harness gained `using` lines in #194. Nobody noticed because it was not in CI. Auto-discovery found it, so it now hoists `using` like the other runners. |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` | Explain how to add sources, exclusions and harnesses, and how to resolve conflicts: take main's version. |

After this, adding a domain file and its harness touches **no shared list**.

## Tests / evidence
Run in this cloud container with **real pwsh 7.4.6 + .NET SDK 8**, plus CI on windows-latest.
- **MSBuild evaluation:** `dotnet msbuild VikingAI.csproj -getItem:Compile` gives **55 items, identical** to the old explicit list. This checks evaluation only, not a full plugin build.

author: katrinsharp
body:
## Why

In this release, every waitpoint a run can wait at belongs either to an **approval** (an agent turn gate or a tool gate) or to **the runtime itself** (a flow's agent step waiting on its child turn). Packs can't create waitpoints of their own. A run waiting for an approval continues through `POST /v1/approvals/{approvalId}/complete`, which checks the reviewer's role and records the decision.

`POST /v1/runs/{runId}/resume` completed any waitpoint by id, so it could stand in for both owners and skip what they do. The route has no use of its own in this release, so it now declines.

## Changes

- **`@kindgi/api`:**
  - `POST /v1/runs/{runId}/resume` answers `422 run-resume-not-supported` and reads or completes nothing. The authorization middleware is unchanged.
  - The new code is mapped in `errors.ts`.
  - The operation's spec says the route isn't available and points to the approvals route.
  - `openapi.json` and the Python client are regenerated (`runs.resume` now documents the refusal).
- **`@kindgi/cli`:**
  - `runs resume` joins `UNWIRED_COMMANDS`, so `--help` and the generated reference leave it out.
  - A new `UNWIRED_REASONS` map gives the message the CLI prints instead of the generic "not yet wired". The command never calls the runtime.

## Tests

- **API:** the route answers 422 for an approval waitpoint, a runtime child waitpoint, and no waitpoint, with nothing completed or resumed. Full API suite: 712 passed.
- **CLI:** `kindgi runs resume … --value='{"decided":"approve"}'` exits 2 with the reason and never calls the client. The unwired list still matches its call sites. Full CLI suite: 724 passed.
- **Pre-commit:** the API drift, `openapi.json` freshness, SDK wire-type coverage and Python client checks pass.

author: kadirnar
body:
Part of #107 (triage item A21c).

## Problem
`MossTTSProcessor.build_training_record` builds the assistant turn as `<|audio_start|> … <|audio_end|> <|im_end|>`. The trailing `\n` after `<|im_end|>` that the official finetuning data contains is missing. This affects the Delay, Local and Local v1.5 variants. As a result VoiceHub training sequences are one token shorter than upstream, and the model is never trained to predict the newline after `<|im_end|>`.

## Root cause
Upstream finetuning (`moss_tts_{delay,local,local_v1.5}/finetuning/dataset.py::_pack_record`) calls the processor with `mode="computing_loss"`. The processor renders the assistant message with the checkpoint's `chat_template.jinja`, and in every pinned MOSS-TTS checkpoint that template closes each message with `<|im_end|>\n`. `_get_unified_codes` fills the trailing rows with audio pad codes, so `\n` (id 198) is a supervised text target. `_assistant_target` (`voicehub/architectures/mosstts/processing.py:559-565` and `:573-579`) stopped at `<|im_end|>`.

## Fix
Both `_assistant_target` branches now append `self.tokenizer.encode_ids("\n")` after `<|im_end|>`. `processing.py:357` already encodes the newline the same way for the prompt. The new rows are text-only, with pad audio, so their audio labels are masked as before. The realtime path and inference prompts are unchanged.

## Tests
- New: `TrainingTargetTests.test_assistant_turn_ends_with_im_end_newline` checks delay, local and local_v1_5 with the tiny CPU config. Text labels must end `[audio_end, im_end, "\n"]`, and the audio labels of the newline row must be masked. It fails on the base (3/3 subtests) and passes with the fix.
- `tests/test_native_mosstts*.py`: 28 passed, 26 subtests passed.

## Evidence
I ran the upstream repo's own SFT dataset packing (`_pack_record` + `collate_fn`) at OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS @58b20a0. It used the real checkpoint tokenizer, chat template and config for all four pinned checkpoints. I compared it with VoiceHub `build_training_record` on identical random codes, with and without a reference. This was tokenizer-only: no weights, no GPU.

| Checkpoint | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MOSS-TTS (delay) | 100 vs 101 rows, tail differs | input_ids + labels **bit-exact** |
| MOSS-TTS-v1.5 (delay) | 100 vs 101 rows, tail differs | input_ids + labels **bit-exact** |
| MOSS-TTS-Local-Transformer | 69 vs 70 rows, tail differs | assistant tail exact |
| MOSS-TTS-Local-Transformer-v1.5 | tail differs | assistant tail exact |

Two remaining differences in the Local checkpoints come from other causes and are out of scope here:
- **Local v1:** upstream's generation prompt (used for `prompt_length`) includes `<|audio_start|>`, so upstream does not supervise that one label. VoiceHub does.
- **Local v1.5:** upstream tokenises the user text differently in the chat-template training path than in its direct generation path (for example `".\n"` becomes one token). VoiceHub follows the generation path.

Inference is unaffected: generation prompts and decoding are unchanged.

### Commits
- ca69c0ba fix(mosstts): end training assistant turn with <|im_end|> newline

Verified together with every open parity PR on top of main: full CPU suite 3075 passed, 0 failed; pre-commit clean.

author: aureliolo
body:
Tauri's NSIS template registers only `UninstallString`, the uninstaller with its window. winget's silent uninstall runs `QuietUninstallString` and falls back to that, so `winget uninstall --silent` opens the uninstaller and waits on it (seen in the winget check on #195, against v0.1.0). An NSIS hook registers `"uninstall.exe" /S` as the quiet uninstall.

The Windows install check reads the registered quiet uninstall, requires it to be exactly that command, runs it, waits for NSIS's uninstaller (which carries on from a copy in %TEMP% after the command returns) and checks the Apps entry is gone.

author: satcomwarrior
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Custom URL validation using `String.trim()` fails to remove C0 control characters (such as `\x01`), which can lead to normalization evasion bypasses where malicious schemes like `javascript:` are improperly parsed.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could potentially bypass protocol allowlists and trigger Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) or SSRF by prepending control characters to disallowed schemes.
🔧 Fix: Replaced `input.trim()` with an aggressive regex `.replace(/^[\s\x00-\x1F]+|[\s\x00-\x1F]+$/g, "")` to correctly strip all C0 control characters and whitespace before validation.
✅ Verification: Tested against malicious inputs including `\x01javascript:alert(1)` and confirmed they are successfully rejected. Run `npm test` to verify URL normalization functionality remains intact.

author: aquilaxk
body:
## Summary
Implements Phase 1-B of the Next-Gen Architecture Plan to harden session tokens, OAuth flows, and login endpoints against spoofing, session replay, login CSRF, pre-account hijacking, and brute-force attacks.

Resolves #269.

### Key Changes
1. **JWT & Session Security**:
   - Enforce fail-closed boot and signing in production when `JWT_SECRET` is not configured, eliminating ephemeral per-instance random secrets.
   - Attach standard `iss` (`easyconvert`), `aud` (`easyconvert-api`), and cryptographically secure `jti` (UUID) claims to issued tokens.
   - Implement distributed instant session revocation: Redis-backed `jti` denylist and user `sessionVersion` tracking.
   - Automatically revoke the session token's `jti` upon `POST /api/auth/logout`.
2. **OAuth 2.0 PKCE & State Cookie CSRF Protection**:
   - Generate cryptographically secure RFC 7636 PKCE `code_verifier` and `code_challenge` (S256).
   - Persist OAuth state, `nonce`, and PKCE parameters in Redis with a 10-minute TTL.
   - Bind state to an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie (`easyconvert_oauth_state`) to eliminate login CSRF.
   - Resolve canonical application origin (`APP_ORIGIN` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`) to prevent Host header poisoning on callback URLs.
   - Require `email_verified: true` from identity provider and protect against pre-account hijacking when linking with existing accounts.
3. **Login Brute-Force Rate Limiting**:
   - Implement distributed failed attempt tracking in Redis/memory per IP (limit: 10 attempts) and email (limit: 5 attempts) within 5-minute rolling windows.
   - Return standard RFC 9457 Problem Details with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After` headers when rate limited.
   - Clear failed attempt counters upon successful authentication.

### Deterministic Verification
- `npm run guard:anti-cheat`: 0 un-baselined violations (132 locked baseline).
- `npm run lint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `npm test`: 133 test files passed (1,715 passed, 34 skipped, 0 failed).
- `npm run build`: All 41 Next.js routes compiled and optimized cleanly.

author: jumanji144
body:
A rare bug with the jdk has recently been filed again: https://github.com/adoptium/adoptium-support/issues/1538, which reports the already seen behavior in JDK-8352077: `unhandled instruction`. The original issue was closed with no reproduction. I have managed to write a reproduction with the new data. It seems that it is caused by a missing null check in the `BreakpointInfo::set` path, which calls into: `incr_number_of_breakpoints` which calls `build_method_counters`. Which has multiple ways to return `nullptr` if either the oom flag is already set or the allocation fails, which is done via allocate_no_exception since it runs on a VMThread, therefore it cant actually call a GC or raise the metadata limit. Therefore incr_number_of_breakpoints, never increases the number (since method counters is nullptr). Compilation is then paused, because the method cannot increase it's invocation counter, then after a purge caused by a gc pass, the mark is unset. After that it can correctly create it's counter, but since it never captured the breakpoints, the breakpoint is 0. The method then can be picked up by a compiler thread since `number_of_breakpoints` is now 0 and a counter is real it falsely passes `Method::is_not_compilable`. Then it copies the bytecode containing the `breakpoint` instruction, and doesn't invoke the clean function since the breakpoint count reports '0'. This causes a crash in the `ciBytecodeStream` since `ciBytecodeStream::next_wide_or_table` assumes the only special bytecodes can be `wide` or a type of switch, and bytecode is a special length instruction. This also explains why this happens so rarely. For this to happen the following need to happen in succession: - The debugger must try to set breakpoints - The method must never have been run - Metadata space needs to be at the limit and not resized when its setting the breakpoints and set the oom flag - Class unloading must purge the flag afterwards - The method must get compiled hot while the breakpoint is still installed 3 of the 5 conditions already happen when debugging with jdwp normally, from platforms like intellij, the others are race / resource conditions that seem happen very rarely. For the fix i propose to check the method counter allocation before actually requesting a breakpoint set. Here done by checking if method counters are not null before sending the vm request. I also had to expand the user facing method to make sure the OOM error code is propagated properly (JVMTI_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY is a universal jvmti error code, so it can be returned by jvmti functions). I have added a test for the bug, so it is reproducible. The original repro fails 10/10 on GA and passes with the fix 10/10 on release and fastdebug, and the JVMTI/JDWP/JDI/jdb suites pass cleanly. I would also provide a alternative, which i didnt touch on here since it would require changing the reads of it aswell: Set a new flag in MethodFlags::_statusfor 'has_breakpoints', so even if counters fail to allocate, it can bail out any downstream compilations of the method. This is would also address that SetBreakpoint now returns OOM even if that is not true, because the flag is only cleared when the class is unloaded I would also humbly request that the original issue to be re-opened or a new issue to be created for this - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with the [OpenJDK Interim AI Policy](https://openjdk.org/legal/ai). --------- ### Progress - \[x\] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - \[x\] Commit message must refer to an issue - \[ \] Change must be properly reviewed (2 reviews required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer), 1 [Author](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#author)) ### Error  ⚠️ OCA signatory status must be verified ### Issue * [JDK-8352077](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8352077): Fatal error: unhandled bytecode (**Bug** - P4) ⚠️ Issue is not open. ### Reviewing
