author: alirezaabedinii
body:
## Why

- **#4**: the notebook depends on Google Drive paths (`… (Unzipped Files)`) and cached files that only existed on my Drive, and nothing documented which dataset it uses. That is why image loading fails on a fresh setup.
- **#2**: asks how this implementation relates to Chen et al. (2019). The docs didn't cover that, and some details in `src/` were wrong.
- While testing, I found that the dashboard server could not return a caption at all.

## Changes

- **Notebook:** updated to the final thesis version (November 2022).
  - Adds the cells that save the tokenizer, encoder and generator, an upload cell and a configurable `best_caps`.
  - Adds a setup cell at the top: dataset links (COCO 2017 val), path setup and the one-off first-run steps.
- **`src/`:** aligned with the code that actually ran.
  - Embeddings are learned (`embedding_dim = 2048`); GloVe was never used.
  - Discriminator: embedding copied from the generator and frozen.
  - `metrics.compute_bleu` reproduces the notebook's BLEU exactly.
  - `train.py` now has the full GAN loop, including discriminator updates.
- **Dashboard server:**
  - Resizes uploads to 299×299. InceptionV3 rejects 150×150, so every upload failed before.
  - Answers the CORS preflight that browsers send.
  - Runs requests on threads, so an idle browser connection can no longer block it.
  - Returns 400/500 instead of dropping the connection.
- **Docs:**
  - README: Dataset section.
  - The demo now says it shows the best-scoring captions.
  - ARCHITECTURE.md: corrected model details and a new *Relation to the paper* section.
  - BLEU caveat: it's computed on characters (NLTK on raw strings), so it isn't comparable to the word-level BLEU-4 in papers.

## Testing

Run in an isolated TensorFlow 2.11 environment against the trained weights (`final_model_V4.h5`, kept out of git).

- **End-to-end: 26/26 checks pass.**
  - `build_generator()` matches the deployed model: 11,208,219 parameters, and its weights load.
  - The rebuilt tokenizer equals the training tokenizer.
  - On the notebook's own test images, the captions match the notebook's printed output word for word.
  - The discriminator, RL environment and data utilities work.
  - A small GAN/SCST training run updates the generator, and the notebook passes nbformat validation.
- **Server:** live HTTP checks of GET, the CORS preflight (204), image POSTs (captions match the notebook), a garbage upload (400), and that the server stays up afterwards.
- **Browser:** uploading through the page's file input in a real browser returns a caption, and a second upload works too.

Addresses #4 and #2.

author: eulerfx
body:
## Capability

Coauthor target implementation evidence, physical placement and native Pulumi construction instead of maintaining three matching inventories. A deployment can select an `InfrastructureTargetImplementation` directly; the existing facility/profile IR is derived from the selected evidence. `PulumiDeploymentProjection<TContext>` associates each placement group with one native factory or an existing resource and delegates traversal to the existing graph interpreter.

### Concrete example

Previously, adding an application's state database meant registering its target facility, selecting that facility and physical database in a deployment manifest, and registering a matching factory separately. Now a projection group selects the database implementation and physical identity beside `.Create(...)`. An application with an existing native database can use `.UseExisting(native => native.Database)`; a separate Pulumi-only monitoring resource needs no Cohesive declaration. Tests exercise that existing-resource case and verify separate/inline authoring produces identical canonical fingerprints.

## Authority and boundaries

The existing definition, facility, capability and deployment IRs remain semantic authorities. This is a human authoring surface and native adapter extension, not another wire format. Callbacks/native objects never enter IR. Native SDK configuration, outputs, children and ownership remain native. Exact-manifest validation, coverage, dependencies and association checks reuse `PulumiGraphProjection`; no second traversal was introduced. Capability assertions do not establish runtime readiness.

Evaluated and extended existing target/deployment builders and the Pulumi graph interpreter. Reusable target catalogs remain supported. The existing Azure attachments still check physical identity. Aspire-first convenience is a subsequent adapter deliverable using these semantics, not included here.

No temporary package versions or source copies are introduced. [Ari #199](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/ari/pull/199) adopts public alpha.124 and completes stack unification. The temporary external source override has been removed; public-only restore and 428 consumer tests passed. Its exact-head CI and dev proposal preview passed; the reported resource/property differences match the baseline. It is ready for review.

Published as alpha.124 from exact merge `8cc2b872f3f5da5375a95b01e04d6b7bafa226f9` through [release run 37164274268](https://github.com/cohesivesystems/cohesive/actions/runs/37164274268). Version-availability guard, 33 packaged Pulumi/manifest consumer tests, and public NuGet publication passed.

## Validation

- 129 infrastructure tests passed.
- 17 Pulumi adapter tests passed, including existing resources alongside unmodeled native resources, deferred construction, canonical fingerprint equivalence, conflicting evidence/kind rejection, missing factories, immutable authoring and wrong-manifest rejection.
- Ari consumer: 243 Azure tests passed against this source. All 18 native mock profiles exactly match baseline resource types/names/providers/inputs (80–82 registrations each).
- No cloud apply or runtime qualification. Mock equality is not live plan equality.

## Critical files for review

- `src/Cohesive.Infra/Authoring/InfrastructureTargetImplementation.cs`: authoring-only implementation evidence and kind boundary.
- `src/Cohesive.Infra/Authoring/InfrastructureTargetDeployments.cs`: selection deduplication and materialization into existing canonical manifests.
- `src/adapters/Cohesive.Adapters.Pulumi/PulumiDeploymentProjection.cs`: placement/factory association, immutable authoring and exact-plan execution boundary.
- `src/Cohesive.Adapters.Pulumi.Tests/PulumiDeploymentProjectionTests.cs`: partial-adoption and canonical-equivalence regression scenarios.

author: vynnyss
body:
> **Baseado em #4** (branch empilhada sobre `feat/vendor-lmp`). Enquanto #4 não for mergeado, o diff deste PR inclui o commit dele; o commit próprio deste PR é o último ("Interaction spike…").

## O que muda
A ferramenta **Animation Sculptor** aparece no toolbar em Pose Mode. Com ela ativa, passar o mouse sobre um ponto da trail o realça (anel + texto no header) e **arrastar um key point move a pose daquele controle naquele frame** — 1 gesto = 1 passo de undo; Esc/botão direito cancela restaurando as F-Curves bit a bit. Resultado do spike registrado no ADR 0010: **opção 3 (WorkSpaceTool + Gizmo + modal) confirmada**, sem fallback.

**Achado importante (docs corrigidos):** a fórmula planejada `P(f) = M_arm · M_pose · M_basis⁻¹` está errada para bones com `use_local_location = False` — exatamente os controles IK do Rigify (`hand_ik`, `foot_ik`). O espaço de `location` agora vem do próprio Blender (`Object.convert_space` LOCAL→POSE) em `anim/spaces.py`.

Escopo do spike: só grab de *key point* de controle de translação. Ctrl+LMB (tempo) e arrasto de in-between (arco) são recusados com mensagem — vêm nos próximos PRs.

## Como testar (para o mantenedor)
1. `python scripts/dev.py test all` e `python scripts/dev.py validate`.
2. (Opcional, abre uma janela do Blender por ~20 s, não mexa no mouse) `python scripts/dev.py test ui` → esperado `18 passed, 0 failed`; screenshots em `.blender_test_profile/ui/shots/`.
3. Manual: abrir `tests/assets/local/attack_test.blend`, `rig` em Pose Mode, selecionar `hand_ik.R`.
4. No toolbar (esquerda), escolher a ferramenta **Animation Sculptor** (ícone abaixo do Transform). As trails ligam sozinhas.
5. Passar o mouse sobre o losango do frame 18 (impact): anel branco + header "Animation Sculptor · hand_ik.R · frame 18 (key)".
6. Arrastar: a mão segue o mouse no plano da vista (header mostra Δ em metros; Shift = precisão). Soltar: a trail recalcula e passa pelo novo ponto. Dope Sheet: nenhuma key nova.
7. Ctrl+Z: desfaz o gesto inteiro de uma vez. Ctrl+Shift+Z: refaz.
8. Arrastar de novo e apertar Esc no meio: tudo volta como estava.
9. Clicar fora da trail seleciona bones normalmente; arrastar no vazio faz box select.
10. Recusas: Ctrl+arrastar um ponto ou arrastar um in-between ⇒ aviso no status bar, nada muda.

## Testes automatizados
- unit: passou (8)
- blender: passou (47 locais; Windows, Blender 5.2.1). Novo `test_sculpt_gesture.py` (23): grab move o controle exatamente pelo Δ de mundo (< 0,1 mm) em `hand_ik.L`, `foot_ik.R`, `torso`; só a key do frame muda; Δ=0 é identidade; eixo travado; recusas (driver, NLA, frame sem key); `location_space` correto em IK/FK/torso.
- ui (novo, local, precisa de display): `dev.py test ui` — 18 checagens com eventos simulados: hover pega o key point, press inicia o modal, engine das trails suspenso no arrasto, **ponto termina sob o cursor (erro 0,00 px)**, trail recalculada = rig, **1 Ctrl+Z restaura exatamente**, redo, Esc bit a bit, Ctrl+LMB chega ao operador.
- validate: passou
- Custo por mouse move (parte do operador): **0,19 ms** (meta < 16 ms). Custo do frame inteiro (reavaliação do Rigify + redesenho) ainda não medido.

## Docs atualizados
- ADR 0010 (resultado do spike), decisions/README, design/motion-sculpt-model.md (`P(f)`), architecture.md, reference/editable-motion-trails.md, reference/open-source-provenance.md, development/blender-5.2-notes.md, development/setup.md, testing/blender-tests.md, testing/strategy.md, current-state.md, agenda.md.

## Fora do escopo / limitações conhecidas
- Preview analítico da trail durante o arrasto ainda não existe: durante o gesto a trail antiga fica como "fantasma" e o rig se move ao vivo; a trail nova aparece ao soltar (próximos PRs).
- O acesso às F-Curves do spike está em `interaction/sculpt_tool.py`; vai para `anim/action_io` + `core/` no próximo PR (registrado como dívida técnica).
- Sem soft grab, arc drag, retime, spacing (PRs seguintes).

author: jaredwray
body:
**Please check if the PR fulfills these requirements**
- [x] Followed the [Contributing](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](../blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) guidelines.
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes/features) with 100% code coverage.

**What kind of change does this PR introduce?** (Bug fix, feature, docs update, ...)

Bug fixes and security hardening, with docs. These are the remaining pre-GA fixes, after [jaredwray/keyv#2185](https://github.com/jaredwray/keyv/pull/2185) and [jaredwray/keyv#2186](https://github.com/jaredwray/keyv/pull/2186), one per commit. (A fifth commit added notes on migrating pre-release ciphertext and a sixth reverts it: the encryption adapters haven't been released, so there is nothing to migrate.)

**1. `encrypt-node`: accept only authenticated ciphers and text-safe encodings**

`KeyvEncryptNode` accepted any algorithm Node's `getCipherInfo()` knows and any `BufferEncoding`:

- 32 of the algorithm names it accepted failed on the first `encrypt()`: ECB and other ciphers without an IV, `aes-256-xts`, `chacha20` treated as AEAD, OCB without a tag length, and more.
- `utf8` and `ascii` output never decrypted, and `utf16le` failed whenever the ciphertext length was odd.
- 77 accepted algorithms (CBC, CFB, CTR, OFB) are unauthenticated: anyone who can write to the store can change values, or read them by watching for decryption errors (a padding oracle).

It now takes an allowlist: `aes-128/192/256-gcm`, `aes-128/192/256-ccm` and `chacha20-poly1305` (`NodeAlgorithm`), and `base64`, `base64url` or `hex` (`NodeEncoding`). Anything else throws when the adapter is created. Every cipher sets a 16-byte tag length, so a truncated tag is rejected. The output format is unchanged, and a test decrypts values written by the previous code. Compatibility between encrypt-node and encrypt-web was never a goal, so the cross-compatibility sections are gone from both READMEs, the encryption overview and encrypt-web's class comment.

**2. `encrypt-web`: accept only AES-GCM**

`KeyvEncryptWeb` also offered AES-CBC, with the same tampering problem. It now accepts only `aes-128/192/256-gcm` (`WebAlgorithm`). The lookup uses a `Map`, so names like `constructor` no longer pass the check and fail later. The output format is unchanged, and a test decrypts values written by the previous code.

**3. `keyv`: bridge `setMany()` reports the writes a store rejects**

`KeyvBridgeAdapter.setMany()` returned `true` for every entry. With a native `setMany` it dropped the store's result, and without one it ignored each `set()` result, so `keyv.setMany()` reported success for writes a legacy store rejected while `keyv.set()` returned `false`. It now maps the store's result back to the entries: one boolean per live entry, one for the batch, or nothing (v5 typed `setMany` as `Promise<void>`), which still counts as success. Only an explicit `false` marks a failed write.

**4. `keyv`: the JSON serializer keeps own `__proto__` keys**

`prepare()` copied objects into a plain `{}`, so an own `__proto__` key (as `JSON.parse` creates from a request body) hit the prototype setter and was dropped. v5's `@keyv/serialize` kept it. The copy now has no prototype. Reading back is unchanged and safe: `JSON.parse` defines `__proto__` as an own property and never sets a prototype.

**Verification**

- Each fix's new tests fail on `main` and pass here.
- `pnpm test` passes in `core/keyv` (370 tests), `encryption/encrypt-node` (26) and `encryption/encrypt-web` (22), with lint clean and every branch of the changed source files covered.
- With the rebuilt `keyv`, these also pass: bigmap, test-suite, the three compression adapters, both serializers, sqlite, redis (against local Redis), and the website's docs and skill validation.
- `tsc --noEmit` on encrypt-node reports no errors. encrypt-web's one `CryptoKey` type error exists on `main` too, and both packages build.

author: zechengz
body:
## Summary
- The stale-file check (`file_version.ts`) hashed with `node:crypto` and returned `Buffer`, so a browser app importing the agent adapters (Vercel, OpenAI Agents) failed to build: `"createHash" is not exported by "__vite-browser-external"`.
- It now hashes with Web Crypto and returns a copy of the bytes as `Uint8Array`, as Python returns `bytes`; the stamp is unchanged (unpadded base64url sha256), pinned to the same value on both hosts.
- A read that a write overtook fetches again, so it never shows bytes older than that write (both hosts).
- `decode` keeps a UTF-8 BOM, as Python's does, so an edit no longer drops it.
- eslint refuses `node:*`, `Buffer` and `process` in the modules the Vercel and OpenAI adapters load.
- `integ-e2b` runs the e2b suite on the python host only: E2B's sandbox proxy closes its connection to envd mid-stream now and then, and only the JS SDK's traffic trips it (reproduced with the bare JS SDK, no mirage involved).

## Test plan
- [x] Vite build of a plain browser page using `mirageTools` over OPFS: failed before, builds after; shell/read/edit/write work and an edit after an outside change is refused
- [x] New tests (overtaken reads, copied bytes, BOM edit) fail with their fix reverted; the eslint rule flags a `node:crypto` import and `Buffer`
- [x] `vitest` agents (236 passed), `tsc --noEmit`; `pytest tests/agents`, `mypy`
- [x] TS runtime runner runs no e2b case with a sandbox set

author: philliphoff
body:
The S-102, S-104 and S-111 rule packs reported false positives on NOAA's production tiles. I audited each finding against the real files:

| File | Rule | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| S-102 `102US005SEAFL262247` (EPSG:32610) | S102-R-3.2 `IssueDate '20260902'` | **False positive, fixed.** ISO 8601 basic format is what S-100 Part 10c uses. |
| S-102 `102US005SEAFL262247` | S102-R-4.1 / R-4.2 origin and extent outside ±90/±180 | **False positive, fixed.** UTM grid values are metres. |
| S-111 CBOFS `..._US4VA1BF` | S111-R-3.1 `SurfaceCurrentDepth -4.5` | **False positive, fixed.** The value is signed on an upward axis, so below the sea surface is negative. |
| S-111 CBOFS `..._US4VA1BF` | S111-R-4.2, 9 errors | **Real data issue, kept.** The tiles contain literal `360.0` directions, which break their own Group_F closure `[0, 360)`. The same happens in LEOFS, NGOFS2 and WCOFS. The message reported "worst observed: 0°"; it now reports 360°. |
| S-104 pilot (EPSG:4326) | none | Clean, but S104-R-4.2 had the same projected-CRS bug. Fixed. |

## Changes
- **Core:** two new shared helpers.
  - `Iso8601Text` recognises basic and extended ISO 8601 dates, times and date-times.
  - `GridGeoreferencing` checks grid positions according to the CRS: degree ranges for geographic CRSs, UTM easting/northing bounds for projected ones, and conversion to WGS 84 when a transform is available. It skips CRSs it can't classify.
- **`ValidationContext`:** new optional `CrsTransformFactory`. `S102DatasetProcessor` and `S104DatasetProcessor` pass their ProjNet factory in, so a finding's bounding box is converted to WGS 84 instead of holding metres in a box that claims degrees.
- **S-102:**
  - R-3.2 accepts basic-format dates.
  - New **S102-R-3.3** checks `issueTime`. `S102Dataset.IssueTime` is now read from the file.
  - R-4.1 and R-4.2 check according to the CRS.
- **S-104:** R-4.2 checks according to the CRS.
- **S-111:** R-3.1 checks only that the magnitude is at most 1500 m, and R-4.2 reports the real worst direction. `SurfaceCurrentDepth` doc comments corrected.
- **Docs:** READMEs updated.

## Testing
- Unit tests for both helpers.
- S-102 tests for basic-format dates and times, projected coverages with and without ProjNet, and degrees written into a UTM file.
- S-102 end-to-end test on the repo's real NOAA UTM file `102US004MI1CI262227.h5`.
- S-104 tests for projected grids.
- S-111 tests for the negative depth and the 360° message.
- Solution build: 0 warnings. DocFX with `--warningsAsErrors`: clean. Core, S-104, S-111, Pipelines and CLI test projects pass.
- `s100 validate` on NOAA S3 data:
  - 9 S-102 tiles from 4 regions: clean.
  - 4 S-104 pilot tiles: clean.
  - 5 S-111 OFS tiles: only the genuine 360° findings remain; SFBOFS is clean.

author: oneilltomhq
body:
## What

- `nodes::display::ao` / `GtaoNode`: a port of three's GTAONode. Radius, thickness, scale and distanceExponent uniforms; samples baked into the shader (3 or 5 slices); the 5×5 magic-square noise; temporal rotations and offsets; `resolutionScale` with the centre-depth `textureGather`; the white clear and quad render in `updateBefore`.
- `builtinAOContext`: `PassNode::set_context_ao(node)` puts an AO node in a pass's context, `SetupContext.ambient_occlusion` carries it into material setup, and Basic, Lambert, Phong, Toon, Standard and Physical multiply their ambient occlusion by it. Nested passes inherit the outer context (three's flow-context merge); the GTAO pre-pass lifts it so it cannot read the AO it feeds.
- `examples/webgpu_postprocessing_ao.rs`: the page, in the viewer (key 87). Not graded: three keeps the page in its own e2e exception list, so there is no reference screenshot.
- Plumbing: `textureGather` on a depth texture binds a non-filtering sampler; `textureLoad` honours the texture's wrapping via per-axis polyfills; `tsl::depth_texture_gather`, `get_screen_position_from_clip`, `unpack_rgb_to_normal`; `Renderer::frame_id`; `TraaNode::set_use_subpixel_correction`; `Texture::wrapping`.

## Gates

- `tests/nodes_display_wgsl.rs`: `gtao_matches_three` and `gtao_screen_position_from_clip_matches_three`, structural fingerprints against three's dump (`webgpu_postprocessing_ao_m18_gtao.wgsl`). All 18 display gates pass.
- `tests/gtao_frames.rs` (GPU, listed in `tests/gpu_only`): a white box on a white floor; the contact is darker than the open floor at full res, at half res (gather path), with 8 samples + temporal filtering, and the Standard beauty through the AO context darkens at the contact and not in the open.
- Lib tests, clippy (0 warnings), `cargo doc` with `-D warnings`, `nodes_mx_library` (the `NodeBuilder` texture arms moved into `#[inline(never)]` helpers so the debug node depth did not shrink), headless viewer run of the page (40 frames, steady frames build nothing).
- e2e grader: the debug run aborts in `steady_frame_builds_nothing` with a stack overflow on `main` as well as here; the release run is reported in a comment below.

## Not ported

Normal reconstruction from depth, logarithmic depth, `distanceFallOff`, SSAONode / `aoOnly`, per-pass sample counts. See `docs/nodes.md` §64 and `docs/webgpu_postprocessing_ao-progress.md`.

author: erwinkn
body:
The original failures in [37154736842](https://github.com/erwinkn/coffre/actions/runs/37154736842/attempts/1) and [37159332960](https://github.com/erwinkn/coffre/actions/runs/37159332960/attempts/1) each have one compose startup. Packed conformance creates its database via SQL and does not start compose. Port 55432 falls within Linux’s default outgoing source-port range. An established outgoing socket, with no listener, reproduced Docker’s exact bind failure on a disposable port. The historical logs do not identify their socket owner.

Reserve 55432 with `sudo sysctl -w`, preserving existing reservations, as the first step of the shared CI preparation action after checkout and before package downloads. Serialize cold starts across worktrees with a kernel advisory lock; reuse an initializing container and use `--no-recreate`. Wait out an already-allocated socket before asking Docker to bind, and require a published port before readiness. Unrelated startup failures surface immediately. Startup and lock waits have 120-second budgets.
